title: Break up the 497-module src/sase import cycle
close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: valid root-cause analysis, but a 497-module cycle break is an epic with its own design phase, not a ready task bead. Cut for queue size; re-propose as a plan if the selection imprecision is worth paying for.
description: src/sase has a single import cycle spanning 497 modules, which the epic plan for sase-fp (Test suite Tier 1 -- two-speed verification with diff-scoped test selection) identified as the root cause of static import-graph-based test selection being unsound: any module inside the cycle transitively 'imports' every other module in the cycle, so a change anywhere in it selects far more tests than the change actually touches (or, if broken apart naively, could miss tests). Breaking the cycle into smaller, real dependency components would let static selection be both cheaper and more precise. Proposed by epic sase-fp's land phase (sase-fp.8.3); named directly in the epic plan plans:202608/test_suite_tier1.md.

notes.author: uc
notes.text: Backlog triage 2026-08-06 (master 25285417d): NOT closed because it is invalid. Epic sase-fp's plan (plans:202608/test_suite_tier1.md) correctly names the single 497-module import cycle in src/sase as the reason static import-graph selection is imprecise — anything inside the cycle transitively imports everything else in it. It lost its slot on shape rather than merit: it is sized large, it is the only bead in this backlog that would restructure the package layout, and 'break it apart naively' is explicitly called out as capable of making selection MISS tests, so it needs a design and a staged migration rather than a task worker. The right next step if the owner wants it is /sase_plan, not 'sase bead work'. Note the payoff is bounded by what the two-speed lane already achieves — worth measuring the current escalation and selection rates first (just selection-health) to decide whether the imprecision is actually costing enough to justify an epic.

plus_one_evidence.note: Epic sase-g3 measured the cost of this import cycle directly, and it survives the epic's own mitigation. 'just selection-backtest' replays real commits and compares the diff-scoped selection against per-test coverage ground truth; with --include-descendant-baseline over the last 100 commits at 625b5cac40fb, closure-only recall is perfect on 29 of 31 usable commits but still blind-spots on two AFTER phase compensate's no-baseline-depth-boost (depth+1) is active: 9a366e0d6c5a 'fix(ace): resolve Artifacts project scope through project refs' at 57.1% recall (missed 9 of 21 ground-truth test files) and 840cdff10664 'fix(commit-finalizer): break async-wait deadlock in finalizer passes' at 85.7% (missed 1 of 7). Both fit the widely-executed-but-shallowly-imported shape this bead names as root cause. The sharpest case is src/sase/ace/tui/_app_layout.py, where 42 of 91 covering test files stay outside the depth-3 closure. Phase compensate measured and REJECTED the obvious workaround: directory-mirror expansion of tests/ace/tui/** is 831 files = 35.7% of the suite, above the 0.25 escalation ratio, so it degenerates into a full run. Depth is therefore exhausted as a lever short of breaking the cycle. Proposed by sase-g3.3/sase-g3.5, corroborated at land time by sase-g3.land.

title: Full-run failure recorder must drop xdist worker-crash node IDs
close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: test-selection / test-lane cost, caching, measurement, retention, or metric-hygiene follow-up from epic sase-fp — not a correctness defect. Cut to bring the ready task queue from 30 to 7.
description: FullRunFailureRecorder (tests/_test_selection_health.py and its pytest plugin) records pytest node IDs from failure reports without validating that they resolve to a real repo test path. When an xdist worker crashes, pytest can emit a CollectReport whose nodeid is the bare worker ID (e.g. 'gw22') rather than a test path. The selection-health store at HEAD holds exactly such a 'gw22' entry, which find_false_negatives then treated as an excluded test file and reported as a false negative -- corrupting the metric with a non-test artifact. FullRunFailureRecorder should filter out (or the correlator should ignore) any recorded node ID that does not resolve to an actual repo test path. Proposed by epic sase-fp's land phase (sase-fp.8.3); discovered during sase-fp.8.2 (Change-scoped false-negative correlation).

title: Diff-scoped selection soundness — measure the blind spot now, stop degrading silently, and stop depending on a CI artifact
description: The reliability of `just check`'s diff-scoped test lane becomes a measured property rather than an assumed one: a backtest over real historical commits reports selection recall against per-test coverage ground truth today instead of waiting weeks for organic samples, a missing or stale coverage-contexts baseline provokes a named and measured compensating action instead of silently narrowing the selection, an agent can see what the scoped lane actually did on the success path, and a workspace can obtain a baseline from a local full run instead of depending solely on a 14-day CI artifact.

notes.author: sase-g3.5
notes.text:
LAND READING (sase-g3.5, combined tree at 8b8acb433588): selection-health — 42 scoped runs, 70 full-lane runs recorded in the durable host-local store; correlatable sample (post-schema-2) is 79 of 112 total records, 33 excluded for predating schema 2 (10 scoped, 23 full-lane). escalation 47.6%, median selected 37 files (1.6% of 2331), 76,691 worker-seconds avoided. 1 false negative surfaced (tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_prompt_codeblock_highlight.py::test_codeblock_band_replaces_cursor_line_fill_but_not_cursor, full-run head fa8fc69e46c4, workspace sase_11) but its triggering diff only touched src/sase/agents_sync/** — unrelated to prompt-codeblock rendering — matching the ACE-TUI load-sensitive flake family already tracked on sase-ct/sase-e2, not a genuine selection miss.

selection-backtest — default mode (baseline must be an ancestor, faithful replay) over the last 50 commits: only 5 have usable ground truth against the current cached baseline (6b0976bcb6e5), because that baseline is itself only 10 commits old; nowhere near 30. With --include-descendant-baseline (accepts the reverse, pessimistically-widened direction) and --limit 100: 32 of 100 commits have usable ground truth (5 faithful + 27 widened/approximate). closure-only recall: median 100%, mean 98.2%, perfect on 30/32 (11 by escalation); 2 blind-spot commits (9a366e0d6c5a 57.1% missed 9/21, 840cdff10664 85.7% missed 1/7). closure+contexts recall: perfect 100% on all 32, 0 blind spots.

Honest reading: the >=30-varied-changes exit criterion IS now met by backtest evidence, but only in the widened/approximate --include-descendant-baseline mode (27 of the 32 usable commits are pessimistic reads, not faithful replay — the faithful-only reading is still just 5). It is NOT met by live correlation: the correlatable sample is 79 records and only 1 true scoped-to-full-run pair has been found, so live correlation alone remains far short of 30 and should not be blurred with the backtest reading. The backtest also confirms the contexts baseline is still what makes recall airtight — even after phase compensate (depth+1 when no baseline), closure-only still blind-spots on 2/32 backtested commits, while closure+contexts is 0/32.

notes.author: sase-g3.5
notes.text: LAND READING RECONFIRMED (sase-g3.5) at the true final combined tree 625b5cac40fb, two commits past the earlier reading at 8b8acb433588; the honest reading is unchanged. selection-health: 42 scoped runs / 70 full-lane runs, escalation 47.6%, median selected 37 files (1.6% of 2331), p90 180 (7.7%), median duration 49.7s, 76,691 worker-seconds avoided; 33 pre-schema-2 records excluded from correlation, leaving a correlatable sample of 79; contexts baseline present in 20 of 42 scoped runs. selection-backtest against the newest cached baseline 6b0976bcb6e5: strict ancestor-only --limit 50 yields just 6 usable commits (38 skipped baseline-not-ancestor because that baseline is itself only ~10 commits old), closure-only mean recall 92.9% / worst 57.1%, 1 blind-spot commit. With --include-descendant-baseline --limit 100: 31 usable commits (6 faithful + 25 pessimistically widened), closure-only median 100% / mean 98.2% / worst 57.1%, perfect on 29/31 (11 by escalation), 2 blind-spot commits (9a366e0d6c5a 57.1% missed 9/21; 840cdff10664 85.7% missed 1/7), 10 missed files total; closure+contexts 100% on all 31 with 0 blind spots. HONEST READING: the >=30-varied-changes exit criterion is met by BACKTEST evidence only, and only in the widened/approximate mode (25 of the 31 usable commits are pessimistic reads; the faithful-ancestor-only reading is 6). It is NOT met by live correlation — 79 correlatable records have produced exactly 1 scoped/full pair, and that one pair is the ACE-TUI flake already tracked on sase-ct/sase-e2, not a selection miss. The two readings must not be blurred. The backtest also confirms the contexts baseline, not the closure, is what makes recall airtight: even with phase compensate active (no-baseline-depth-boost), closure-only still blind-spots on 2/31 commits while closure+contexts blind-spots on 0/31. VERIFICATION: just check-full green on 625b5cac40fb (all 12 gates incl. the full suite, no flakes this run) and just symvision clean. The plan is marked status: done. Six PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP entries are collected on sase-g3.5 awaiting /sase_new_task triage; this land agent was instructed not to create beads and not to close this epic.

notes.author: sase-g3.land
notes.text: LAND INTEGRATION (sase-g3.land): reviewed the six non-epic commits landed since the epic's first commit 2ef98cb3e — 9a366e0d6 (ace artifacts project scope), 48a34b4a1 and 8b8acb433 (agents-sync), d9c13549f and b08862001 (sdd plan-header validation), 625b5cac4 (axe workspace lock). Two integration facts are worth recording: d9c13549f resolved phase compensate's PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP about tests/test_plan_display.py::test_malformed_header_block_leaves_authored_metadata_visible failing on a clean tree (that test now asserts validation_ok is False deliberately), and 9a366e0d6 is one of the two commits the backtest still blind-spots on at 57.1% closure-only recall, which was corroborated onto sase-fy rather than treated as an epic defect.

notes.author: sase-g3.land
notes.text: LAND DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (sase-g3.land): verifying phase visible's summary line against a real escalated run surfaced a defect this epic introduced, plus a pre-existing miscount it turned into a decision input. select_tests consults contexts only inside the 'not forces_full_suite' branch, so a rule-forced escalation left the manifest's default-shaped contexts block (baseline: null) — which phase visible's new success-path line rendered as 'contexts baseline missing' and tools/select_tests --explain rendered as 'no baseline cached (run just refresh-contexts-baseline)'. Both are false: an escalated run executed every test and never looked at the cache. Escalations are 21 of 44 recorded scoped runs (47.7%), so nearly half of all just check runs showed an agent a false claim and a remedy it did not need. The same conflation drove just selection-health's 'runs without one: 23 of 44 (static closure alone)'. Measured against the real host store: escalated with null baseline 21, genuinely scoped with a baseline 21, genuinely scoped without one 2. The lane's true closure-only exposure is 2 of 23 consulted runs (8.7%), not ~52% — an order of magnitude, and it is the number phase compensate cited ('a baseline is absent in 20 of 39 recorded scoped runs, so escalating would send half the lane to the full suite') to justify keeping no-baseline-depth-boost out of FULL_SUITE_RULES. FIX: ContextSelection gained an explicit 'consulted' flag (manifest schema 3 -> 4) set False on the forced-full-suite path; context_line, manifest_summary_line, and selection-health now report 'not consulted' distinctly and count baseline availability over consulted runs only, with a shared contexts_consulted() helper inferring the flag for pre-schema-4 records so the 30-day store reads correctly. DECISION NOT REVISITED: depth+1 stays the compensating action. The corrected frequency does make escalation affordable, but absence is persistent rather than occasional exactly where it matters — an offline workspace, or one idle past the artifact's 14-day retention — so escalating would hand those a permanently full lane, and depth+1 recovers a measured 91% of the closure blind spot for roughly double the selected files against 3,650 worker-seconds. The rationale in docs/development.md, tests/_test_selection_rules.py, and the rule's own test docstring was rewritten to state the corrected numbers rather than the inflated ones.

notes.author: sase-g3.land
notes.text:
CLOSE NOTE (sase-g3.land; the epic was auto-closed at commit time by sase commit's SASE_BEAD footer, so this is the close record).

VERIFIED (step 1). Read every child bead and note, then confirmed each deliverable in the source rather than trusting the reports. sase-g3.1: tools/selection_backtest and just selection-backtest exist, replay into a reusable detached worktree, report recall twice (closure-only and closure+contexts), itemise every skip reason, and --execute is opt-in and absent from check and check-full. sase-g3.2: manifest_summary_line in tests/_test_selection_report.py plus tools/print_scoped_summary, wired into the Justfile check recipe as a separate step after tools/run_silent returns, with tests pinning step order and that check-full prints nothing. sase-g3.3: RULE_NO_BASELINE_DEPTH_BOOST fires when contexts are unusable, is deliberately not in FULL_SUITE_RULES, and effective_depth is on the manifest; contexts are consulted before the closure so baseline status can set the depth. sase-g3.4: tools/install_coverage_contexts with dirty-src and partial-run guards (both overridable), atomic staging, shared prune_baselines, and COVERAGE_CORE=ctrace pinned for the cov-contexts lane. 217 targeted selection tests pass; just selection-health runs clean against the real host store (44 scoped / 71 full-lane runs, 47.7% escalation, median 38 files = 1.6% of 2331, 80,237 worker-seconds avoided, 1 false negative which is the known ACE-TUI load flake).

INTEGRATED (step 2). See the LAND INTEGRATION note above: the six non-epic commits since 2ef98cb3e touch no selection code and need no integration; d9c13549f independently resolved phase compensate's clean-tree test_plan_display failure.

FIXED AT LANDING. See the LAND DEFECT note above. Verifying phase visible's summary line against a real escalated run found that a rule-forced escalation recorded contexts as a *missing* baseline rather than an unconsulted one, which made nearly half of all just check runs show a false claim and a remedy the agent did not need, and inflated just selection-health's closure-only exposure from 2-of-23 to 23-of-44. Fixed in b3a54e5 with an explicit consulted flag (manifest schema 3 -> 4), back-compatible reading for the 30-day store, and the corrected numbers written into the rationale. The depth+1 decision was re-examined against the corrected figure and deliberately kept.

FOLLOW-UP TRIAGE (all seven collected proposals resolved). (1) selection_backtest silently empty outside the venv -- FIXED in the same commit; run_backtest now refuses with a named error when coverage is not importable, verified end to end with the system python. (2) Contexts baselines ranked by mtime so the thin local baseline displaces the fuller CI one -- NEW TASK sase-g9 (medium, ready). Re-measured at land time: 6b0976bcb.sqlite holds 14,349 contexts / 46,364 line_bits against 96183d71b.sqlite's 58,770 / 597,959 over a near-identical file count, and resolve_baseline prefers the thin one. Root-caused further than the proposal did: that database was recorded ~30 minutes before sase-g3.4 pinned COVERAGE_CORE=ctrace, so it is a pre-fix artifact and future local baselines will be comparable -- but the ranking weakness itself survives and needs a breadth signal, which is a design decision rather than a mechanical change. (3) Third flaky ACE-TUI test -- +1 on sase-ct. (4) Load-sensitive flakes across four phases -- folded into the same sase-ct +1 and a +1 on sase-e2. (5) Residual closure-only blind spots survive depth+1 -- +1 on sase-fy. (6) Directory-mirror rejected for the _app_layout shape -- folded into the sase-fy +1. (7) Depth-3 cost re-measurement -- +1 on sase-fu with the backtest's recall-for-cost numbers. Nothing was declined. One earlier proposal (tests/test_plan_display.py failing on a clean tree) needed no bead: d9c13549f fixed it and it no longer reproduces.

VERIFICATION. just check-full green on the combined tree at b08862001 plus this fix -- all 12 gates including the full suite, exit 0, no flakes this run. just symvision clean. The plan file plans:202608/selection_soundness.md is marked status: done.

HONEST READING CARRIED FORWARD. sase-g3.5's reading stands and is not revised: the >=30-varied-changes exit criterion is met by BACKTEST evidence only, and only in the widened --include-descendant-baseline mode; the faithful-ancestor-only reading is 6 commits. It is NOT met by live correlation -- 79 correlatable records have produced exactly one scoped/full pair and that pair is a flake. The two must not be blurred. The backtest also confirms the contexts baseline, not the closure, is what makes recall airtight: with compensate active, closure-only still blind-spots on 2 of 31 commits while closure+contexts blind-spots on 0.

title: Historical backtest of selection recall against coverage ground truth
description: backtest: add a `tools/selection_backtest` harness (plus a `just selection-backtest` recipe) that replays the last N real commits, computes the selection each diff would have produced, and reports recall against per-test coverage-context ground truth — so the epic's unmet exit criterion is answerable now rather than after weeks of organic sample growth.

notes.author: sase-g3.1
notes.text: Added tools/selection_backtest + just selection-backtest: replays the last N commits in a reusable detached worktree (never the invoking checkout), rebuilds the import graph as of each commit, and compares selection against per-test coverage ground truth. Verified: 44 targeted tests (tests/test_test_selection_backtest.py + tests/test_justfile_lint.py) pass; just lint clean (ruff, mypy 2758 files, symvision, toobig, keep-sorted); full suite 25859 passed / 7 skipped in 345s. Measured at 6b0976bcb (--limit 150 --include-descendant-baseline, baseline 96183d71b), 65 commits with usable ground truth: closure-only median 100.0%/mean 96.2%/worst 23.5% with 13/65 blind-spot commits and 118 missed files; closure+contexts 100% by construction, so the reported gap is the useful number. Report states its own limits: only 1 of 65 is a faithful baseline-ancestor replay (strict >=30 criterion NOT met), core-identity-changed cannot fire historically so recall is under-reported, and --execute on one commit showed its 4 missed files all pass (proxy miss, not a true false negative).

title: Make the scoped lane's selection and degradation visible on the success path
description: visible: `tools/run_silent` discards captured output on success, so a passing `just check` shows only `✓ test (scoped)` and hides how many tests ran, whether the run escalated, and whether the contexts baseline was missing; surface a one-line scoped summary that survives the success path.

notes.author: sase-g3.2
notes.text: Implemented: manifest_summary_line() in tests/_test_selection_report.py renders the scoped lane's one-line summary (selected count/share or escalation, rules fired, contexts baseline status) from the persisted JSON manifest; tools/print_scoped_summary is the CLI wrapper wired into the Justfile check recipe as a separate step immediately after 'tools/run_silent "test (scoped)"' returns, outside run_silent's captured region, so it survives the success path. Verified: 33 new/updated unit+CLI tests pass (tests/test_test_selection_report.py, tests/test_print_scoped_summary_tool.py, tests/test_justfile_lint.py incl. two new tests pinning step order and that check-full prints nothing); all 11 just-check lint gates pass; end-to-end against the real manifest written by this diff's own (Justfile-triggered) escalated test-scoped run, tools/print_scoped_summary correctly printed 'scoped: escalated to the full suite (rules: justfile, selection-tooling); contexts baseline missing'. The escalated full-suite run had 5 failures (fakey/test_retry_pipeline_e2e.py x3, ace/tui/test_prompt_catalog.py, test_bead/test_cli_work_contention_regressions.py) that all pass individually in isolation -- pre-existing load-sensitive flakes already covered by the epic's out-of-scope flake family (sase-e2, sase-ct), not caused by this change.

description: compensate: `context-baseline-missing` and `context-baseline-stale` are recorded but are absent from `FULL_SUITE_RULES` and widen nothing, so roughly half of scoped runs narrow silently; choose and implement a compensating action on the backtest's measured recall evidence, and record it as a named rule.

notes.text: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: cached contexts baselines are ranked by mtime alone, so a thin local baseline displaces a fuller CI one — 6b0976bcb.sqlite on athena has 14,349 contexts / 7.3 MB against 96183d71b.sqlite's 58,770 / 49 MB, and resolve_baseline prefers the thin one; rank or reject on recorded coverage breadth, not recency.

notes.author: sase-g3.3
notes.text: Chose depth+1 (epic plan candidate 1) on measured evidence and shipped it as the named rule no-baseline-depth-boost: when the contexts baseline is missing or stale, the closure walks one extra hop instead of escalating; the rule is deliberately NOT in FULL_SUITE_RULES (a baseline is absent in 20 of 39 recorded scoped runs, so escalating would send half the lane to the full suite). select_tests now consults contexts before the closure so baseline status can set the depth, and the manifest gained effective_depth (schema 2 -> 3). MEASURED with just selection-backtest --limit 150 --include-descendant-baseline --baseline 96183d71b at 4651ed199, 63 commits with usable ground truth (3 faithful ancestor replays, 60 approximate descendant ones), closure-only arm: mean recall 96.0% -> 99.2%, p10 85.3% -> 100%, worst 23.5% -> 81.3%, blind-spot commits 13 -> 5, missed test files 116 -> 11 (91% of the blind spot recovered). Re-running the backtest AFTER the change reproduces those numbers through the real code path with no-baseline-depth-boost in the closure arm's rules and the union arm (baseline present) unchanged at 6.4% median / 23 escalations, confirming the boost applies only when there is no usable baseline. COST: selection size roughly doubles when no baseline is cached (median 6.4% -> 8.8% of the suite, p90 11.9% -> 21.2%; src/sase/agent_lanes.py 110 -> 255 files, 1117 -> 2514 tests, 57s -> 164s serial on athena), replayed escalation rate 23/63 -> 28/63 on whole-commit historical diffs; contract-set-only changes (the median scoped run, 34 files) are unaffected because they seed no closure. ACCEPTANCE on the plan's sharpest case: a real edit inside src/sase/ace/tui/_app_layout.py's compose body with contexts forced absent recovers 27 of the 69 previously missed covering test files (recall 24.2% -> 53.8% of 91) at 14.2% of the suite, still scoped. Candidate 2 (directory-mirror) measured and REJECTED: tests/ace/tui/** alone is 831 files = 35.7% of the suite, above the 0.25 ratio, so it degenerates into a full run. VERIFIED: 160 targeted tests pass (selection engine, contexts, select_tests CLI, backtest, health, scoped summary); five new tests pin the rule, its composition with the rename/delete hop, and that it never forces the full suite; just lint clean; just check-full green apart from two failures unrelated to this change - tests/test_plan_display.py::test_malformed_header_block_leaves_authored_metadata_visible reproduces on a stashed clean tree, and tests/ace/tui/test_agent_bulk_kill_edit.py::test_bulk_waiting_agents_mount_forced_artifact_prompts passes in isolation and in an earlier full run (known load-sensitive flake family). docs/development.md documents the rule and the before/after table. Changes are staged in the working tree, not committed.

title: Reject a malformed plan-header block at validation time instead of mid-launch
description: A plan whose provenance header block is malformed is rejected the first time anything validates it — `sase plan validate`, `sase plan propose`, and the tale/epic approval gate — with a diagnostic that names the offending section and its line, so an approved epic can never reach `sase bead work` and abort at its archive step; and if the archive boundary is ever reached with a malformed document anyway, it fails with that same actionable diagnostic instead of a bare `validation:` exception from the Rust binding.

notes.author: sase-g4.land
notes.text:
LAND VERIFICATION (sase-g4.land, 2026-08-06, master be25ef5b4): the epic is complete and its goal is met. All five phases closed; every child note read and confirmed against source, commits, and live behaviour.

VERIFIED IN SOURCE AND AT RUNTIME
- sase-g4.1 (core-diagnostic): crates/sase_core/src/plan/validate.rs:483 validate_header_block() pushes one error diagnostic, code 'header-invalid', empty field_path, line from the offending bullet, message = parser reason + HEADER_BLOCK_REMEDY (validate.rs:20-22). It is called at validate.rs:381 inside the same pass as the frontmatter checks, so it does not short-circuit them. Landed as 508d5d9 on sase-core master, released as 0.18.4 by 34da143. Wire untouched.
- sase-g4.2 (links-parity): src/sase/sdd/_link_validation.py:85-97 emits an error issue with code 'header-invalid' and the parser's reason on an INVALID disposition, then skips the parent-target check. This matches plan_links_refresh.py:217-223, so the two commands now agree. Commit fa8fc69e4.
- sase-g4.3 (core-adopt): pyproject.toml:46 is 'sase-core-rs>=0.18.4,<0.19.0'; 'just install' builds and installs 0.18.4 clean. PLAN_HEADER_BLOCK_NOTE (src/sase/main/plan_explain.py:6-13) now states the rule ('a validation error, not a style choice') and restates the canonical link-shaped and list-shaped forms, matching the Rust message. Commit d9c13549f.
- sase-g4.4 (archive-guard): src/sase/sdd/plan_archive.py:118-134 calls validate_plan_for_commit(content, path=source) BEFORE project_plan_header_sections(), with a comment recording why the reorder is sound. Nothing is written on the failing path. Commit b08862001.
- All seven tests the phase notes name exist and pass. Ran the epic's targeted files together (test_plan_links_validate_handler.py, test_plan_gates.py, test_bead/test_cli_work_from_plan.py, sdd/test_plan_archive.py, test_plan_validate.py, test_plan_display.py, test_sase_core_rs_telemetry_smoke_tool.py): 115 passed.

LIVE END-TO-END on a fresh malformed plan (trailing text after the PARENT link): 'sase plan validate' exits 1 and prints '<path>:7: error [header-invalid] plan header block is invalid: unexpected trailing text in PARENT plan header section. SASE owns the plan header block: ...' -- path, line, code, reason, and remedy, which is exactly what the original failure lacked. 'sase bead work <plan> --dry-run' now fails at up-front validation instead of printing a green archive preview, which is the specific regression that produced this epic.

CORPUS RESCAN at be25ef5b4: sase/repos/plans is 3456 files -> 3138 canonical / 318 missing / 0 INVALID; ~/.sase/plans is 1199 files -> 41 canonical / 1158 missing / 0 INVALID. title: Diagnose the race between agents-sync publication and workspace-prep clean/reset against the shared agents sidecar clone
description: Root-cause the race that emptied the sase agents-repo owner manifest from 1389 hoods to 1 hood in a single publication: agents-repo commit 5f244a229 (2026-08-06 09:11:53, 1389 hoods) -> 6ad0b6e2a (2026-08-06 09:16:12, 1 hood, 'tv' only), with the commit's diff losing the manifest entries plus 1390 lines of the browsing README. 6ad0b6e2a is the exact fetched_sha recorded in five stale incoming-cache items that misclassified this machine's own 24 legacy-v1 runs as an unknown-user import (surfaced as a green unknown-user badge in ACE). The agents-repo reflog shows a whole-tree 'reset: moving to HEAD' + 'checkout: moving from main to main' one second before that commit (2026-08-06 09:16:11) -- the signature of vcs_clean_workspace (git reset --hard HEAD + git clean -fd) followed by a branch checkout, i.e. a workspace-preparation pass running against the agents sidecar clone at ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/repos/agents, which all 24 sase_<N> workspaces share. The 1391 hood directories under users/bbugyi200/machines/athena/hoods/ survived intact -- only the manifest.json that references them was truncated, meaning publication_planning.plan_hoods's read_owner_manifest() must have seen a missing or freshly-reset manifest.json (v2_manifest_io.read_owner_manifest returns an empty V2OwnerManifest when the file is not present) and then republished from that empty base for a single targeted hood ('tv'), overwriting the real manifest. The precise interleaving that made the file unreadable at that instant -- whether the clean/reset briefly deleted manifest.json while a concurrent publish read it, or checkout raced a write, or something else entirely -- is not diagnosed. Discovered and surfaced via plan sase/repos/plans/202608/unknown_user_legacy_hood_ownership.md, whose Fix 3/Fix 4 (landed in that plan's implementation) harden publication_planning.plan_hoods to raise AgentsSyncFormatError instead of silently republishing from an empty manifest when on-disk hood directories exist, and add a 'sase agent sync --repair-manifest' command to reconstruct lost manifest entries from intact on-disk snapshots -- but those are containment/repair, not a fix for the underlying race. A related precedent exists: sase-ab.1 (closed) solved an analogous problem for the *beads* sidecar, teaching workspace-preparation to protect or publish local-only bead-store commits before a clean+hard checkout discards them; that fix's shape (protect-before-clean) may be a useful starting point but does not itself cover the agents sidecar's manifest.json, since sase-ab.1 was scoped to bead-store commit protection only. Scope: reproduce or trace the concurrent-workspace-preparation-vs-agents-sync-publication interleaving against the shared agents sidecar clone, and land whichever fix shape avoids the corruption at its source (e.g. per-workspace clones instead of a shared one, a lock that workspace-prep's clean/reset respects, or protecting/publishing local-only agents-sidecar commits before a hard reset the way sase-ab.1 did for beads).

notes.author: sase-g5
notes.text:
Root-caused the manifest collapse to an uncoordinated workspace-preparation pass over the machine-shared agents sidecar clone, and landed a lock fix at the source.

DIAGNOSIS. The actor is 'sase repo open agents'. repo_handler_open -> workspace_handler_list.prepare_opened_checkout -> axe.runner_workspace.prepare_workspace runs run_sase_hg_clean (vcs_clean_workspace = git reset --hard HEAD + git clean -fd) then provider.checkout(default parent) against the resolved checkout. For the agents sidecar that checkout is ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/repos/agents -- one clone shared by all 24 workspaces (confirmed 'agents sidecar 24/24' in sase repo list), unlike the per-workspace sidecars under sase/repos/. Confirmed on the live clone: reflog has 'reset: moving to HEAD' + 'checkout: moving from main to main' at 2026-08-06 09:16:11, one second before the truncating commit 6ad0b6e2a at 09:16:12; a second bare 'checkout: moving from main to main' at 09:19:44 pairs with the repo-open audit record (sase repo log --repo agents: last_opened_at 2026-08-06T13:19:45Z, agent u0, workspace #11) -- 47 opens by 44 distinct agents against that one clone.

THE INTERLEAVING. Every agents-sync mutator serializes on <git_dir>/sase-agents-sync.lock (git_sync._sync_project, commit_publication, incoming_integration, publication_repair, v1_retirement, status, commit_finalizer_git). prepare_workspace was the one actor that took no lock. agents-sync stages its whole regenerated payload in the worktree before commit_agents_payload_if_dirty commits it, so at that instant manifest.json was dirty-tracked. git reset --hard rewrites a dirty tracked file by unlinking it before recreating it; v2_manifest_io.read_owner_manifest returns an empty V2OwnerManifest for a non-existent path, and publication_planning.plan_hoods seeds its entry map from that read. A targeted single-hood publication ('tv') that read inside the unlink window therefore republished from an empty base, emitting the 1-hood manifest while all 1391 hood directories stayed on disk. git clean -fd compounds this by deleting untracked staged payload.

FIX. src/sase/axe/runner_workspace.py: prepare_workspace now runs its clean/checkout/sync pass (extracted to _prepare_workspace_locked) inside _agents_sidecar_sync_guard, which takes the same sase-agents-sync.lock when _agents_sidecar_clone_root identifies the target as the machine-shared <sase_projects_dir>/<key>/repos/agents clone, and returns False with a named diagnostic when the lock is busy. Every other workspace, including a workspace-scoped sase/repos/agents clone, is unaffected. This is the sase-ab.1 protect-before-clean shape applied to the agents sidecar; no commits are at risk here (reset --hard HEAD drops none and payload is regenerated every pass), so a lock is sufficient and no rescue ref is needed.

TESTS. New tests/test_axe_runner_workspace_agents_lock.py: a busy sync lock blocks the clean entirely (run_sase_hg_clean not called, returns False); the lock is provably held across the clean and released afterward; a workspace-scoped agents clone stays unguarded. Verified red before the fix (2 of 3 fail) and green after.

VERIFIED. just install; just check -- all lint gates green (fmt, ruff, mypy, pyscripts, symvision, toobig, SASE validation, committed plans) and 25968 passed / 1 failed. The single failure, tests/test_plan_display.py::test_malformed_header_block_leaves_authored_metadata_visible, reproduces on a clean stashed tree, is unrelated to this change, and is already fixed on origin/master by d9c13549f (sase-g4.3), which rewrites that exact fixture to assert validation_ok is False; this workspace checkout (9a366e0d6, 10:00) predates it while carrying the newer sase-core-rs wheel. No task bead filed for it.

SCOPE NOTE. The plan's Fix 3 (plan_hoods raising instead of republishing from an empty manifest) and Fix 4 (sase agent sync --repair-manifest) are not on master yet and are deliberately untouched here -- they are that plan's containment/repair work, this bead is the source fix.

notes.text: Root-caused: prepare_workspace's git reset --hard + clean -fd + checkout ran unlocked against the machine-shared agents sidecar clone while agents-sync had its regenerated payload staged in the worktree; the reset unlinked manifest.json, read_owner_manifest returned empty, and plan_hoods republished a 1-hood manifest. Fixed by wrapping that pass in the same sase-agents-sync.lock guard. New tests/test_axe_runner_workspace_agents_lock.py verified red before / green after; just check lint gates green.

title: Diff-scoped selection emits deleted test files, so just test-scoped fails with pytest exit 4
description:
Discovered on 2026-08-06 while splitting tests/test_commit_artifacts.py into focused modules (the original file was git rm'd and replaced by tests/test_commit_result_marker.py, tests/test_commit_marker_repo_metadata.py, tests/test_commit_sdd_result_marker.py, tests/test_commit_pr_body.py).

REPRODUCTION: delete or rename any tests/test_*.py file, then run 'just check' (or 'just test-scoped'). Every whole-repo lint gate passes, then the scoped lane fails:

  selected 40 of 2337 test files (rules: contract-set-always, rename-or-delete)
  ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_commit_artifacts.py
  collected 0 items / no tests ran
  error: recipe `test-scoped` failed on line 346 with exit code 4

'.venv/bin/python tools/select_tests --explain' confirms the cause: the deleted path is seeded from the change set and emitted verbatim ('tests/test_commit_artifacts.py  <- seed tests/test_commit_artifacts.py at hop 0'). Nothing filters selected test paths down to those that still exist in the working tree, so pytest aborts on the missing path before running anything. Because pytest exits 4 with zero tests collected, the whole scoped lane is skipped, not just the deleted file — an agent who deletes a test file gets no scoped test signal at all.

IMPACT: 'just check' cannot pass for any change that deletes or renames a test file, which is exactly the shape of the module-split refactors this repo does often. Workaround today is to hand-filter the selection ('tools/select_tests | grep -v <deleted path>') and run pytest directly, or to fall back to 'just check-full'.

SCOPE: filter selected test files to paths that exist on disk before handing them to pytest (or drop deleted paths at the seed/emission boundary), keeping the rename-or-delete rule's escalation behavior intact so the tests that imported the removed module are still selected. Add regression coverage for a change set that deletes a test file. Note that touching tests/_test_selection*.py or tools/select_tests trips RULE_SELECTION_TOOLING, so verify with 'just check-full'.

notes.author: sase-g7
notes.text: Fixed: tests/_test_selection.py now filters the selected test set to paths still present in graph.paths (built from the current working tree via discover_python_files), so a deleted/renamed-away test path from change_set.paths is dropped before reaching pytest instead of being emitted verbatim. The closure and rename-or-delete depth-boost were already unaffected since importers only ever resolve to on-disk modules. Added regression test test_deleted_test_file_is_not_selected in tests/test_test_selection.py (git rm a test file, assert it's excluded from selection.selected while RULE_RENAME_OR_DELETE still fires). Verified with the targeted test_test_selection.py suite (63 passed) and just check-full (all lint gates + full test suite green).

notes.author: sase-g7
notes.text: Filtered selected test paths against graph.paths (current working tree) in tests/_test_selection.py to drop deleted/renamed-away test files before handing selection to pytest, preventing exit-4 collection failures. Added regression test test_deleted_test_file_is_not_selected. Verified via targeted suite (63 passed) and just check-full (all lint gates + full suite green).

description:

  git commit failed: fatal: could not parse HEAD

then passed on a re-run of the same tree, so it is a flake, not a regression.

The message is the assertion text in the test module's own commit_at() helper (completion.rs:3114-3118), which shells out to 'git -C <repo> commit --quiet --allow-empty -m <subject>' with GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE pinned. init_git_repo() (completion.rs:3083-3089) creates each repo with 'git init --quiet' plus user.name/user.email/core.abbrev config. This particular test is the heaviest fixture builder in the module: it creates ARTIFACT_REF_COMMIT_MAX_ROWS/ARTIFACT_REF_COMMIT_SCAN_LIMIT repos under one tempdir and commits ARTIFACT_REF_COMMIT_SCAN_LIMIT times into each, then adds a sidecar repo.

'fatal: could not parse HEAD' from 'git commit' means git resolved HEAD to a ref it could not read as a commit -- a partially written or truncated ref file, not a simply unborn HEAD (an unborn HEAD is the normal root-commit case and succeeds). Candidate causes worth checking: a ref write that lost a race with another cargo-test thread sharing the tempdir root, or a resource shortfall (ENOSPC / inode exhaustion) on the runner leaving a zero-length .git/refs entry -- the same class of runner resource problem that sase-fq.8 chased for the Python artifact-ref parity test, though the failing syscall and the failing test are different.

Scope: make the fixture deterministic against whatever the race is (e.g. assert on the ref after init, or serialize/retry the repo construction), or prove the cause and fix it at its source. Do not simply retry the whole test in CI.

Repo: sase-core (../sase-core via 'sase repo open sase-core), not this repo.

title: Rank cached coverage-contexts baselines by recorded breadth, not file mtime
description:
resolve_baseline (tests/_test_selection_contexts.py) sorts cached baselines by file mtime and then takes the first ancestor of HEAD, so the most recently *written* database wins regardless of how much ground truth it actually holds. Its own docstring says it picks 'the most recent ancestor of HEAD', which mtime only approximates -- that held while every baseline arrived the same way, as a CI artifact, and stopped holding when epic sase-g3 phase 'baseline' (commit 2ef98cb3e) added tools/install_coverage_contexts as a second, local supply route.

OBSERVED on athena at b08862001, both baselines ancestors of HEAD:
  6b0976bcb.sqlite  7.3 MB  14,349 contexts   46,364 line_bits  (local, mtime 09:10, distance 12)
  96183d71b.sqlite   49 MB  58,770 contexts  597,959 line_bits  (CI,    mtime 00:32, distance 27)
resolve_baseline returns the 7.3 MB one. It holds 4x fewer contexts and 13x fewer (file, test) attribution pairs over a near-identical file count (2,643 vs 2,638), so selections resolving it get materially less ground truth while reporting a healthy 'context-selection' rule.

IMPACT, measured at land time: with the thin baseline preferred, a strict 'just selection-backtest --limit 50' found only 6 of 50 commits with usable ground truth (38 skipped baseline-not-ancestor), where the same harness measuring against 96183d71b at --limit 150 got 63.

WHY THE THIN DATABASE EXISTS: it was recorded at 09:10, about 30 minutes before sase-g3.4 pinned COVERAGE_CORE=ctrace for the cov-contexts lane (2ef98cb3e, 09:39). On Python 3.14 coverage's default sysmon core stops monitoring a location once seen, so only the first test to execute a line is credited. Later local runs will be ctrace-recorded and comparable to CI's. That fix removes the mechanism that produced this particular artifact but not the ranking weakness itself: any thin or truncated database that lands with a fresh mtime still displaces a fuller one, and the installer's existing dirty-src and partial-run guards did not catch this one because the run was complete, just thinly attributed.

SCOPE: give resolve_baseline a quality signal instead of trusting mtime -- e.g. record context/line_bits counts in a sidecar at install and fetch time and rank on (breadth, then commit distance), and/or have tools/install_coverage_contexts refuse a database whose attribution density is far below an already-cached one. Picking the threshold needs measurement, which is why this is not a mechanical change. While fixing, also reconcile resolve_baseline's docstring with its behaviour: ranking ancestors by commit distance rather than file mtime is what it already claims to do. An immediate host-local mitigation is to delete or re-record the thin ~/.sase/test-selection/contexts/6b0976bcb*.sqlite; it is a regenerable cache entry, but it degrades every scoped run on athena until it ages out.

Proposed by sase-g3.3 and re-raised by sase-g3.5; evidence above re-measured at land time by sase-g3.land.

notes.author: sase-g9
notes.text: resolve_baseline now ranks cached baselines by recorded breadth then commit distance instead of file mtime, and its docstring says so. Breadth = (contexts, line_bits attribution pairs, measured files) counted straight from SQLite (read-only URI, ~17ms warm on the 49MB CI database) and memoized in a <sha>.sqlite.breadth.json sidecar keyed on the database's size+mtime_ns, so a re-recorded SHA is re-measured; both producers (tools/install_coverage_contexts, tools/fetch_coverage_contexts) write it at install/fetch time, prune_baselines removes it with its database, and cached_baselines re-measures lazily for databases already on disk. Ranking: ancestors of HEAD sorted by commit distance, then the nearest one holding >= 75% (BREADTH_TOLERANCE) of the best candidate's attribution pairs wins; unmeasurable databases count 0 and never displace a readable one; with nothing measurable the old distance ordering stands unchanged. tools/install_coverage_contexts gained a third guard refusing a database whose density (pairs per measured file) is under 50% (MIN_DENSITY_RATIO) of the densest already cached, overridable with --allow-thin, never firing when the cache holds no measurable reference. VERIFIED on athena's real cache at HEAD 5da193482: the two baselines measure 6b0976bcb = 14,349/46,364/2,643 (density 17.5, distance 28) and 96183d71b = 58,770/597,959/2,638 (density 226.7, distance 43), and resolve_baseline now returns 96183d71b -- the 13x-better-attributed CI artifact -- where it previously returned the newer, nearer, thin local one. The thin database was left in place rather than deleted: it is now correctly deprioritized, and the installer would refuse to re-cache one like it (17.5/226.7 = 8%, well under the 50% floor). 12 new tests across tests/test_test_selection_contexts.py and tests/test_install_coverage_contexts_tool.py cover measurement, unreadable databases, sidecar reuse and invalidation, prune cleanup, thin-vs-broad and comparable-breadth ranking, the density refusal and its override, and the empty-cache exemption. docs/development.md's coverage-context section updated with the new ranking, the sidecar, the third guard, and the measured evidence. just check passed clean (exit 0; the selection-tooling rule escalated it to the full suite: 26,054 tests), plus bare mypy across 2,762 files.

notes.author: sase-g9
notes.text: Breadth-aware baseline ranking verified: just check green (full 26,054-test suite via selection-tooling escalation), 12 new tests, real athena cache now resolves 96183d71b (597,959 pairs) over the thin local 6b0976bcb (46,364).

title: A leading unknown plan-header key is silently ignored instead of diagnosed
close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: defence-in-depth, dead code, or misleading-but-harmless output with no currently-reproducing user-visible failure. Cut to bring the ready task queue from 30 to 7.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-g4.1 (epic sase-g4). Not caused by that epic: this is pre-existing parser behaviour that the epic's new header-invalid validation rule made visible, because the rule only fires when the parser reports a problem.

sdd_plan_header_block_problem() -> first_header_candidate() (crates/sase_core/src/plan/artifact_link.rs:907) requires the block to START with a KNOWN section key. A bolded-key bullet whose key is unknown, appearing first, is therefore not recognized as the start of a header block at all: the whole block is classified MISSING and no diagnostic is emitted. The same unknown key placed after a known one is correctly rejected.

Reproduced at master be25ef5b4 with sase-core-rs 0.18.4 installed:

  leading unknown key      -> disposition=MISSING, reason=None
  unknown key after known  -> disposition=INVALID, reason='unknown `NOPE` section inside plan header block'

(both documents identical apart from bullet order; probe used sase.sdd.plan_header_block.parse_plan_header_block on a tale document whose bullets were '- **NOPE:** [x](x.md)' and '- **PARENT:** [p](p.md)').

Impact is small but real: it is exactly the shape a hand-authoring agent produces (a made-up section name at the top of the block), and it is the one case where sase-g4's new rule does not catch a hand-authored header block. The plan text a user sees looks like a provenance block and is silently treated as prose.

Scope: decide the intended contract and implement it. Diagnosing a leading bolded-key bullet that looks like a header section but names an unknown key would close the gap; the risk to weigh is false positives on ordinary prose bullets that happen to start with a bolded word followed by a link, so the detection needs to be narrow (bolded key immediately followed by ':' and a single Markdown link, at the document's leading-block position). Whichever way it lands, pin it with a Rust test.

Repo: sase-core (open with 'sase repo open sase-core'). If the decision is to diagnose it, the fix also needs a floor bump here once released.

title: write_sdd_files projects plan header sections before validating, so a malformed header raises a bare ValueError
close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: defence-in-depth, dead code, or misleading-but-harmless output with no currently-reproducing user-visible failure. Cut to bring the ready task queue from 30 to 7.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-g4.4 (epic sase-g4). Not caused by that epic: this is the same pre-existing defect shape sase-g4.4 fixed at the archive boundary, at a second boundary the epic's phase description did not name.

src/sase/sdd/_write.py::write_sdd_files calls project_plan_header_sections() at line 85 and only then calls validate_plan_for_commit() at line 95. project_plan_header_sections() upserts the PARENT/PROMPT/BEAD sections, and the Rust binding refuses to update a document whose existing header block is invalid, so a malformed source escapes as a bare 'validation: <reason>' ValueError with no path, no line, no code, and no remedy -- precisely the failure mode that produced epic sase-g4 in the first place.

sase-g4.4 fixed the identical ordering in src/sase/sdd/plan_archive.py::archive_plan_file (commit b08862001): validate_plan_for_commit() now runs before projection, so the caller gets the actionable header-invalid diagnostic (path, line, code, reason, remedy) and nothing is written. The comment at plan_archive.py:112-117 records why the reorder is safe -- projection only rewrites derived header sections into canonical form, so a document that fails validation before projection would fail identically after it.

Live caller: src/sase/axe/run_agent_exec_plan_accept.py:461.

Reachability note: after sase-g4, the approval gate rejects a malformed plan before this path runs for approved plans, so this is defence in depth rather than a currently-reproducing user-visible failure. It is worth closing because it is the last known instance of the shape, and any future non-approval caller of write_sdd_files reintroduces the bad error.

Scope: apply the same reorder in _write.py (validate the pre-projection content, passing the source path), and add a test asserting that a malformed header block raises the actionable diagnostic and that no SDD file was written. Mirror tests/sdd/test_plan_archive.py::test_archive_rejects_malformed_header_before_writing_destination.

title: Approval-time plan archive has failed silently since 2026-07-31 on a bogus project directory
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-g4.5 and named in epic sase-g4's plan as an explicit out-of-scope follow-up. Not caused by sase-g4: separate root cause, and it did not cause the launch failure that produced that epic (the launch's own archive would have raised regardless).

Every approval-time plan archive raises and is swallowed into a warning. Re-confirmed at master be25ef5b4 on 2026-08-06: ~/.sase/logs/tui.log now holds 62 'Failed to archive approved plan' warnings and 124 lines of the underlying error, most recently 2026-08-06 09:45:22. The error is always:

  ValueError: No workspace plugin detected a workflow type for '/home/bryan/.sase/projects/.sase'. Install the appropriate workspace plugin.

raised from get_workspace_directory. Note the path: '/home/bryan/.sase/projects/.sase' is not a project directory -- the ProjectSpec key is missing from it, so something is resolving a project directory from an empty or unset key and handing the result to the workspace-plugin lookup. That resolution bug is the thing to fix; the plugin message is a symptom.

Both call sites swallow it:
  - src/sase/plan_approval_actions.py:462
  - src/sase/_notification_plan_background.py:54

Consequence: approved plans have not been archived at approval time since 2026-07-31. Plans that reach the archive by another route (a subsequent 'sase bead work <plan>' launch) are still archived, which is why this stayed invisible for a week.

Scope: find why the project directory resolves without its key, fix it at the source, and decide whether these two call sites should keep swallowing the failure -- a silent warning is what let this run for a week. Pin the fix with a test that exercises the approval archive path with a real project key. Sizing is medium because the root cause is not yet identified and the swallow-vs-surface decision touches two approval surfaces.

Do NOT fold this into sase-g4's error-quality work: sase-g4 made the header-invalid failure actionable, but the exception here is a different failure at a different layer.

notes.author: sase-g4.land
notes.text:
CONCRETE INSTANCE, recorded while landing epic sase-g4: this defect swallowed epic sase-g4's OWN plan.

~/.sase/logs/tui.log:19760 records 'Failed to archive approved plan /home/bryan/.sase/interaction_requests/plan/680cb0bf-d691-412a-b36f-fa9f192f24f7/plan.md' at 2026-08-06 09:04:48 -- 25 seconds before bead sase-g4 was created at 09:05:13 -- with the same 'No workspace plugin detected a workflow type for /home/bryan/.sase/projects/.sase' ValueError.

The observable consequence: /home/bryan/.sase/plans/202608/plan_header_validation.md exists only machine-locally. There is no 202608/plan_header_validation.md in the committed plans store and no 'Archive approved plan plan_header_validation' commit in its git log, while every other recent epic's plan resolves into sase/repos/plans/202608/ (checked sase-fp, sase-fq, sase-fr, sase-g3). The file also carries no create_time or bead_id frontmatter, which archive_plan_file stamps -- independent confirmation it never went through the archive.

This gives the fix a precise, reproducible target and shows the real cost: an epic's plan of record can be silently absent from the committed store while the epic itself completes and closes normally. It also shows the failure is intermittent rather than total -- the same log window contains successful 'Archive approved plan selection_soundness' and 'Archive approved plan artifact_ref_scratch_failure' commits -- so whatever makes the project directory resolve to '/home/bryan/.sase/projects/.sase' is state- or timing-dependent, not unconditional. Worth reproducing both outcomes before fixing.

The sase-g4 land agent did NOT hand-archive the plan: doing so would mean committing to the plans sidecar without being asked, and would destroy this evidence. It marked status: done on the machine-local copy only.

notes.author: sase-gc
notes.text:
Root cause found and fixed: approval-time archiving resolved the project by calling os.path.basename() on action_data['project_dir'], which is the agent WORKSPACE dir written by plan gates with a trailing slash. Confirmed against real data: all 208 plan interaction_requests on this machine that carry project_dir have a trailing slash, so basename returned '' and get_project_file_path('') produced '/home/bryan/.sase/projects/.sase' -- exactly the path in the 62 swallowed warnings. Even without the slash the basename ('sase_10') is a workspace name, never a ProjectSpec key, so this path could never have worked for gh_ projects. The other 362 requests carry no project_dir at all and hit an early 'return None' with no log: that is the second, fully silent signature recorded in the +1 evidence.

Fix: new src/sase/_plan_archive_approval.py holds one shared archive implementation used by both approval surfaces (plan_approval_actions.py and ace/tui/.../_notification_plan_background.py, which had drifted duplicates). It resolves the project through resolve_plan_action_project_name (renamed from the private _plan_action_project_name in _plan_approval_artifacts.py), which prefers agent_project_file and resolves project_dir through the workspace provider with the numbered suffix stripped. Verified against the real action_data of a failed request: it resolves 'gh_sase-org__sase' both with and without agent_project_file, and get_workspace_directory on that name returns /home/bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase/ instead of raising.

Swallow-vs-surface decision: archiving stays best-effort (an approval must never fail because its plan could not be filed), but failure is no longer log-only. report_plan_archive_failure logs at ERROR and posts a plan-archive notification naming the plan, the exception, and the consequence. The silent 'no project_dir' early return is gone -- that path now reports too.

Tests: new tests/test_plan_approval_archive_project_resolution.py pins both surfaces (parametrized gate/tui) on a real project key, on a trailing-slash workspace dir, on unresolvable action data being reported rather than silent, on lower-level failures being reported, and on the notification's contents. Four existing tests whose synthetic fixtures name no project were updated to patch the failure report, since their assertions count notifications.

Verification: just check green (all lint gates + scoped tests). just check-full: 26050 passed, 1 failed -- tests/test_bead/test_cli_work_contention_regressions.py::test_concurrent_bead_mutations_wait_past_the_old_lock_timeout, which passes in isolation (6s vs 38s under load) and is the already-fixed sase-e2 flake; this workspace predates that fix (still has the 12s SASE_BEAD_MUTATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT), so no new bead was filed. Files are changed but not committed, per the launch instructions.

Not done deliberately: the 27 plans in ~/.sase/plans/202608/ that exist only machine-locally were left alone -- backfilling them would mean committing to the plans sidecar unasked, which the two prior notes explicitly preserved as evidence. That backfill is a separate owner decision.

notes.author: sase-gc
notes.text: Verified: shared archive helper resolves project via resolve_plan_action_project_name (agent_project_file, then workspace-provider lookup of project_dir with numbered suffix stripped); confirmed against real failing action data that it resolves gh_sase-org__sase instead of raising. Archive failures now log at ERROR and post a plan-archive notification instead of being swallowed. just check green; just check-full 26050 passed with only the known sase-e2 lock-timeout flake.

plus_one_evidence.note:
SECOND CONCRETE INSTANCE PLUS A SCALE MEASUREMENT AND A SECOND FAILURE SIGNATURE (sase-gg.land, 2026-08-06). This defect also swallowed epic sase-gg's own plan, and the blast radius is much wider than one plan.

SCALE: 27 of the plan files in ~/.sase/plans/202608/ are absent from the sase--plans sidecar remote. Measured by diffing 'git ls-tree -r origin/main --name-only 202608/' (excluding prompts/) against 'ls ~/.sase/plans/202608/*.md', with origin/main confirmed current at eb0985fca3f8a63b4d33fab47d79385d5801b120 via git ls-remote. 7 of the 27 are epic-tier plans: agents_sync_owner_manifest_forward_compat, ci_green_restore, family_model_lanes, modernize_quote_and_podcasts, plan_header_validation (the instance already recorded here), pr_branch_commit_laundering, priority_property. So this is not a rare intermittent miss — a quarter of this month's plan-of-record corpus exists only machine-locally.

SECOND SIGNATURE — SILENT, WITH NO WARNING AT ALL: the existing note's mechanism (a 'Failed to archive approved plan' warning at approval, then rescue by the 'sase bead work' launch route) is confirmed by the logs but does NOT explain this case. Correlating ~/.sase/logs/tui.log against the sidecar log, every archive-failure warning today has a matching launch-route rescue commit minutes later: 09:30:11 -> 'Add SDD files for agent_page_bead_links' 09:30, 09:42:10 -> run_pytest_main_env_leaks 09:42, 09:45:22 -> unknown_user_legacy_hood_ownership 09:45, 13:08:09 -> sdd_store_agents_sidecar_degradation 13:08, 13:28:29 -> family_member_roster 13:28. Epic sase-gg's plan was approved and its bead created at 12:26:13, inside the 09:45:22-to-13:08:09 gap where tui.log records NO archive warning at all, and grepping the 12:20-12:49 window for plan/archive/approve returns nothing. Yet 202608/ci_green_restore.md never reached the sidecar and, like plan_header_validation.md, carries no create_time or bead_id frontmatter — so archive_plan_file never ran on it. There is therefore a second path that loses a plan without logging anything, which the current 62-warning count understates. Whoever fixes this should account for both: the logged ValueError and this silent one. The second swallow site named in the description, src/sase/_notification_plan_background.py:54, is the natural first suspect since this plan was approved from an agent-proposed notification gate.

ALSO NOTE: the rescue route is real but incomplete. It fires on 'sase bead work <plan>' launch, and epic sase-gg WAS launched — five phase agents ran off this plan — so a launch alone is not sufficient to get an epic plan into the sidecar.

Following the precedent set in the existing note, I did NOT hand-archive the plan: committing to the plans sidecar unasked would destroy the evidence. I marked status: done on the machine-local ~/.sase/plans/202608/ci_green_restore.md only, as the land instructions require.

NOT caused by epic sase-gg: sase-gg only touched test files in this repo (tests/_rust_extension_module_helpers.py and 15 call sites, tests/ace/tui/test_app_title.py, tests/ace/tui/test_artifacts_files_detail.py) plus an upstream sase-core PR, none of which can affect plan archival.

title: sase bead work --dry-run prints a green Archived line it never attempted
close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: defence-in-depth, dead code, or misleading-but-harmless output with no currently-reproducing user-visible failure. Cut to bring the ready task queue from 30 to 7.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-g4.5 and named in epic sase-g4's plan as an explicit out-of-scope follow-up. Not caused by sase-g4.

src/sase/bead/cli_work_from_plan.py:203-207 prints

  ✓ Archived        <destination> (preview; no files written)

during --dry-run. That line is rendered from plan_archive_destination(), which only computes a path; archive_plan_file() is never called on the dry-run path. The preview therefore reports success for a step it did not exercise.

This is the misleading output that hid epic sase-g4's defect: a --dry-run of the malformed selection_soundness.md plan exited 0 and printed that green line for the exact step that then failed the real launch. sase-g4 made that specific failure impossible before the archive is reached (the up-front validation now rejects a malformed header block, verified: 'sase bead work <malformed> --dry-run' now fails at validation), but the preview line still claims more than it checked for any other archive-time failure -- a write permission problem, a full disk, a projection failure from some other cause.

Scope: make the dry-run line honest. Options to weigh: reword it so it states only what was computed (the destination), or give archive_plan_file a genuine no-write dry-run mode that runs formatting, validation, and projection against a temp target and reports the real outcome. The second is more work but is the only version that actually previews the archive. Pin whichever lands with a test on the dry-run rendering.

description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-fq.8.3 (epic sase-fq.8) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; independently verified from the run pages by the sase-fq.8 land agent, and NOT caused by that epic.

WHAT HAPPENS: a hosted-runner incident makes a whole master CI run read as red with zero code signal, because jobs fail in GitHub's own 'Set up job' step before any repo step executes. Two consecutive master runs, both verified directly:

- Run 31114984919 (sha 7cbfc3449): published-core-minimum-smoke, perf-floors and coverage-contexts each failed with 'Set up job' as the only failing step. Annotations: 'The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts' (published-core-minimum-smoke), 'Failed to resolve action download info' and 'Service Unavailable' (build-core). build-core, lint and visual-test were green and the three test legs ran the full suite, so the run's actual code signal was fine.
- Run 31116699976 (sha 628708a71): build-core itself died the same way ('Failed to resolve action download info', 'Service Unavailable'), which skipped docs-build, coverage-contexts, test, lint, visual-test and perf-floors -- all reported '- <job> in 0s'. Zero tests ran on that run at all.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the specific thing that made epic sase-fq hard to land. Its exit criterion was 'every job in the sase CI workflow passes on master', and for two rounds the only way to tell a platform outage from a real regression was to open each failed job and check whether 'Set up job' was the failing step. Any gate, agent, or human reading run conclusion == failure gets a false regression signal, and re-running is currently a manual decision made after that inspection.

CURRENT STATE: .github/workflows/ci.yml has timeout-minutes on every job (line 23 comment explains why) but no retry, no continue-on-error, and nothing that classifies a setup-phase failure differently from a test failure. Nothing in the repo reruns a job.

SCOPE (a decision, then one of two implementations):
1. Retry: make the setup-phase failures retryable -- e.g. a workflow_run-triggered rerun-failed-jobs job that reruns only jobs whose failure is confined to 'Set up job', bounded to one retry, or an action-level retry wrapper. Note build-core is the fan-out root, so retrying it is worth more than retrying any leaf.
2. Classification: leave the run red but make the redness legible -- a job-summary or annotation step that names which failed jobs executed zero repo steps, so 'platform failure' is distinguishable from 'tests failed' without opening each job.

Option 2 is strictly cheaper and already unblocks the reader; option 1 also unblocks automation. Pick deliberately and pin whichever lands with a test in tests/test_github_actions_ci.py, which is already the workflow-shape contract surface and is in tests/contract_manifest.txt.

OUT OF SCOPE: the 3.12-leg sase_core_rs NameError storm (bead sase-fs) and the ACE parallel flakes (bead sase-ct), which are real test failures on the same runs and tracked separately.

FOURTH AND FIFTH CONSECUTIVE OCCURRENCE, blocking a second epic's landing (sase-gg.land, 2026-08-06 ~18:50Z). Independently verified from the run pages.

- Master CI run 31123018619 (sha baebfcd21): visual-test and test (3.13) both failed with 'The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts' as the only annotation. Every job that DID acquire a runner was green — build-core, published-core-minimum-smoke, perf-floors, lint, coverage-contexts, test (3.12), test (3.14). WHAT THIS ADDS: (1) The failure mode has widened beyond the CI workflow — the Publish and Deploy Docs workflows are hitting the identical runner-acquisition failure, so a classification/retry fix scoped only to .github/workflows/ci.yml would leave two workflows still emitting false red. (2) It is not confined to this repo: sase-org/sase-core PR #89's CI run 31120460060 lost BOTH jobs to the same annotation, and a manual rerun sat queued for 6+ minutes. (3) Concrete landing cost, second epic running: epic sase-gg's exit criterion is 'confirm a full CI run is green'. Its verify phase (sase-gg.5) was left holding on a CI monitor and closed without ever recording verification evidence; the land agent had to substitute local runs plus per-job annotation inspection to distinguish platform failure from regression. That is exactly the manual inspection this bead proposes to remove, and it has now cost two consecutive epics.

title: An SDD land phase cannot execute a "close the parent epic" deliverable, and nothing stops a plan from authoring one
close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: real and recurring, but a land agent already absorbs the cost every time, so it is workflow friction rather than a defect that loses work. Cut for queue size.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-fq.8.3 (epic sase-fq.8) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; independently verified by the sase-fq.8 land agent against the actual prompt sources.

THE DEFECT: an epic plan can author a phase whose deliverable is 'close the parent epic', and that phase can never complete it. Three independent mechanisms make it impossible:

1. The parent-close descendant guard. 'sase bead close <parent>' is rejected while any descendant is unclosed -- and the descendant doing the closing is itself unclosed at the moment it tries. Documented at sase/memory/sase_beads.md:91-93.
2. The phase-worker prompt (xprompt bd/work_phase_bead, src/sase/default_config.yml) and sase/memory/sase_beads.md:95 both tell phase workers never to close a parent epic; the land agent does that.
3. Only the land agent's prompt (xprompt bd/land_epic, src/sase/default_config.yml:950) actually carries the close-the-epic instruction, plus the symvision and plan-file-status steps that follow it.

So the phase's own guidance ('if the close is rejected, a phase bead is still open -- finish or reopen it instead') is circular: the still-open bead IS the phase attempting the close. The phase must either force the close, which its plan forbids, or leave its headline deliverable undone.

VERIFIED RECURRENCE -- four times, three different epics, in bead notes:
- sase-fq.8.3 ('Close out epic sase-fq'): could not close sase-fq because in_progress child epic sase-fq.8 existed; left it to sase-fq.8's land agent.
- sase-fr.9.3 ('Close epic sase-fr and retire its plan'): 'sase bead close sase-fr is rejected by the descendant-close guard because immediate parent epic sase-fr.9 ... is still open'.
- sase-fp.8.3 ('Land epic sase-fp'): 'functionally the land phase for the grandparent epic'.
- sase-bd.9.5 ('Close the epic'): 'I was instructed not to close my parent epic, so sase-bd closes once sase-bd.9 does'.
The pattern is specifically the child-epic shape: a follow-up epic is created under an epic to finish it, and the follow-up's land phase inherits 'close the grandparent' as a deliverable.

WHY IT MATTERS: every occurrence costs a landing round trip and leaves an epic in_progress after all its work is done, which is exactly the state that makes the next agent unsure whether the epic is finished. It also burns land-agent budget re-deriving why the close failed.

SCOPE -- pick one of two remediations:
A. Authoring side (cheapest). src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_plan.md says nothing about the land agent existing; it does not tell a plan author that closing the epic, running symvision, and marking the plan file done are the LAND agent's job and must not be authored as a phase. Add that rule, and consider a plan-validate check that rejects a phase whose description names closing its own parent or an ancestor epic. Note plan validation now lives in sase-core (see epic sase-g4), so the validation half is cross-repo; the skill-text half is local and is the minimum useful fix.
B. Tooling side. Give 'sase bead close' a deferred handoff -- 'close this ancestor once my own bead closes' -- so a phase can record the intent and the runtime executes it at the right moment. This also covers the child-epic chain (close sase-fq once sase-fq.8 closes) that today needs a human or a second land agent.

A alone stops new plans from being authored wrong; B alone makes the existing shape work. Doing A is recommended first because it is local and prevents recurrence; B is the larger change and should be sized on its own if triage wants it.

NOT CAUSED BY epic sase-fq/sase-fq.8: the mechanism predates it (sase-bd.9.5 hit it first) and is a property of the plan-authoring guidance and the bead-close guard, neither of which that epic touched.

notes.author: uc
notes.text: Backlog triage 2026-08-06 (master 25285417d): NOT closed because it is invalid. The four recurrences cited (sase-fq.8.3, sase-fr.9.3, sase-fp.8.3, sase-bd.9.5) are documented in bead notes and the three blocking mechanisms are real. It lost its slot because every occurrence so far ended with the epic closed correctly by the next land agent or the owner — the cost is a landing round trip and an epic that reads in_progress for a while, not lost or corrupted state. Worth noting for whoever picks this up later: remediation A (teach src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_plan.md that closing the epic, running symvision, and marking the plan done are the LAND agent's job and must never be authored as a phase) is a local skill-text edit and would prevent recurrence on its own; remediation B (a deferred close handoff in 'sase bead close') is the larger change. If A is wanted as a standalone, it is small enough to just do rather than re-triage — but note that editing a bundled skill source is a memory-adjacent change that needs the owner's explicit go-ahead.

title: Restore a green CI signal on sase master
