title: Ratchet the sase-core-rs window at the release boundary instead of on feature PRs
description: A feature agent can call a newly landed sase-core binding or behavior without editing pyproject.toml, uv.lock, or a version literal, and without waiting on a core release; the published-floor invariant is enforced once, mechanically, on the pending sase release instead of ~1.2 times a day by a dedicated agent.

notes.author: toobig-2a.split_file.src.sase.dev_update.prebuild.0
notes.text: DISCOVERED ISSUE: The full-suite escalation for an unrelated dev_update/prebuild.py refactor independently found tests/test_contract_manifest.py::{test_contract_manifest_matches_marker_selection,test_contract_set_manifest_entry_budget_has_no_hidden_headroom} failing deterministically. collect_contract_files now includes tests/test_probe_core_floor_tool.py, added by this epic's phase sase-ij.7, but tests/contract_manifest.txt still omits it and the 36-entry budget was not re-curated; the current selected set has 37 entries. This is causally linked to the active core-window-ratchet epic rather than the prebuild split.

notes.author: sase-ib.land
notes.text: DISCOVERED ISSUE: tests/test_contract_manifest.py fails deterministically on master (ee9603d31), blocking `just check` / `just check-full` for every agent. Phase sase-ij.7 (f43d6e4fe) added tests/test_probe_core_floor_tool.py with `pytestmark = pytest.mark.contract` but did not run `just refresh-contract-manifest` or update the entry budget. Two failures: (1) test_contract_manifest_matches_marker_selection -- marker selection now yields 37 files including tests/test_probe_core_floor_tool.py while tests/contract_manifest.txt still lists 36 without it; (2) test_contract_set_manifest_entry_budget_has_no_hidden_headroom -- refreshing the manifest alone then trips the 36-entry _MANIFEST_ENTRY_BUDGET cap, whose failure message requires re-curating the contract set by value per second and updating the cap plus its measured-cost comment per plans/202608/test_suite_tier1.md. Reproduced by sase-ib.land at ee9603d31 with a clean tree (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_contract_manifest.py -q -p no:randomly` -> 2 failed, 1 passed); first reported by phase sase-ib.7 as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP. Left unfixed while landing epic sase-ib because the budget bump is a deliberate curation decision this epic owns, not a mechanical refresh.

notes.author: sase-in

Read all 8 phase notes and confirmed each deliverable in the current tree, not just in the phase reports. sase-ij.1: tests/test_sase_core_rs_telemetry_smoke_tool.py derives the expected minimum from pyproject.toml (no 0.21.3 literal remains) plus a tmp_path parse case. sase-ij.2: tools/ratchet_core_window (735 lines) selects the newest complete non-yanked PyPI release via wheel-tag/sdist superset checks, routes the upper bound through one ceiling_specifier_for_floor(), refuses downgrades, returns EXIT_OK when already matching (idempotent), and supports --check/--report-only with bounded pyproject/uv.lock diff guards; ran it live: 'sase-core-rs floor already matches newest complete published release 0.23.0', exit 0. sase-ij.3: ci.yml release-core-floor-smoke is gated on head.ref == release-please--branches--master, installs the exact declared floor, asserts it, and runs bindings + validate + five smokes + the contract set; publish.yml install-smoke-core-floor pins the floor exactly and publish needs it. sase-ij.4/.5: publish.yml sync-release-metadata runs tools/ratchet_core_window in apply mode before uv lock and treats exit 2 as applied. sase-ij.6: published-core-minimum-smoke is gone with zero remaining references repo-wide, all three Justfile warnings (_setup:99, rust-install:790, rust-dev-install:850) now say the ahead direction is normal and needs no action, and docs/rust_backend.md documents ownership plus the by-hand recipes. sase-ij.7: tools/probe_core_floor is wired into check and check-full right after SASE validation with --advisory; ran it live -- silent, exit 0 (verdict ok now that the floor is 0.23.0, which supersedes the phase's blocked_unpublished acceptance check for parse_merge_summary). sase-ij.8: verified in the sase-core checkout opened via sase repo open -- release-plz.yml has release-plz-merge with author/head-branch/title/body guards, a 300s check-registration poll, gh pr checks --watch --fail-fast, and gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch.

EPIC-CAUSED WORK FINISHED (both DISCOVERED ISSUE notes on this bead). tests/test_contract_manifest.py was failing deterministically for every agent. Refreshed tests/contract_manifest.txt to add tests/test_probe_core_floor_tool.py (sase-ij.7 marked it @pytest.mark.contract but never regenerated the manifest) and re-curated the entry budget from 36 to 39. The three entries over the old cap are tools/-script guards -- test_ratchet_core_window_tool.py and test_probe_core_floor_tool.py from this epic, plus test_sase_core_rs_glossary_line_break_smoke_tool.py from epic sase-ik's 12af4fefe, which also added a manifest line without touching the cap. They earn their place on value per second, not on kind: a tools/ script is not a node in the import graph, so a change touching only one contributes no seeds, RULE_CONTRACT_SET_ONLY fires, and the contract set is the only thing that runs. Measured the 39-entry set at 26.7s summed node time / 33.4s wall (contended host) via the same --durations aggregate the retired oracle read -- inside the plan's 30s serial budget, and the three additions cost ~0.3s combined. Also de-duplicated a hardcoded '36-entry' string out of the diagnostic and made the diagnostic self-test derive its expected filename from the cap. Result: tests/test_contract_manifest.py 3 passed.

RESIDUAL CONSCRIPTION FIXED (also epic work). sase-ij.6 rewrote the three Justfile warnings the plan named, but tools/validate_sase_core_rs_version's EXIT_AHEAD remediation still printed 'Bump sase's sase-core-rs constraint in pyproject.toml...' to stderr -- and rust-install/rust-dev-install call that tool immediately before printing the new 'no action is needed' note, so an agent whose checkout ran ahead got both messages, contradicting each other. Replaced it with the ratchet-era guidance and updated tests/test_validate_sase_core_rs_version_tool.py to assert the new text and that 'Bump' is absent. 11 passed. There are now zero manual floor-bump instructions anywhere in the repo outside CHANGELOG history.

INTEGRATION (step 2). Reviewed every commit since 755987ff5, plus the 5 that landed on origin/master during this landing. 12af4fefe (sase-ik glossary) added smoke_sase_core_rs_glossary_line_break to both the doomed published-core-minimum-smoke job and the new release-core-floor-smoke; sase-ij.6's removal correctly preserved it in the release lane. 9fddbbe77 (sase-in) rewrote sase_core_dir resolution to ignore env vars inherited from other numbered workspaces; the probe_core_floor call sites pass {{ sase_core_dir }} so they inherit the fix with no change needed. 8ed11bb80 (sase-i8.8) manually raised the floor to 0.23.0 at 07:46 on 2026-08-10, before sase-ij.6 landed the docs that retire that habit -- harmless and now moot, since the ratchet reports master's declared floor already equals its own choice. ee9603d31 (sase-ib.7) added just test-cost to check-full; the probe still runs in both lanes and the ~0.3s of new contract tests do not approach any cost budget. 354d8c19f, 6d131aa7b, b9008c535, eb66c3f27, f42a68c07, 8658abee6, 59ea423c6, 46fbdc07a, f21c8d850, 2f71b6bc4, 4f54489af, dfadc7cb4, 884951057, e9e414e2f, 92b82819c, 31ff3a3ff touch subsystems this epic does not, and none duplicates or conflicts with it.

FOLLOW-UP DISPOSITIONS (step 3). (a) 'fmt-md-check fails on sase/memory/build_and_run.md', proposed 4x by sase-ij.1/.2/.3/.7 -- RESOLVED by 0c2d5dd71; fmt (markdown) is green. No task filed. (b) 'init memory --check failed on the chezmoi memory README', sase-ij.6 -- RESOLVED by 5e7f6fb1c; just validate reports ok on all five checks. No task filed. (c) 'validate-committed-plans fails tale-size-missing on 202608/new_task_recent_task_sweep.md', sase-ij.6 -- RESOLVED by b9008c535; 3551 files, 0 errors. No task filed. (d) 'unrelated full-suite ACE/TUI failures', proposed by sase-ij.2 and sase-ij.5 -- these are the sase-ct parallel-only flake class, not this epic. Corroborated with a +1 on sase-ct (now +49) and a DISCOVERED ISSUE note on the active epic sase-h8 that is chartered to retire it, naming all six nodes and flagging test_agent_group_revival_e2e.py and test_family_member_relaunch.py as apparently new families. No new task filed: /sase_new_task's duplicate test matches sase-ct exactly.

FINAL STATE. just check-full at 0968318b1 with these 4 files changed: every lint gate green (fmt py/md, keep-sorted, ruff, mypy, pyscripts, test waits, changelog, patch/stitch, symvision, toobig), SASE validation green, committed plans green, cost lane 8 failed / 28315 passed / 10 skipped in 350.83s. None of the 8 is attributable to this epic and all were proven pre-existing by re-running the exact node IDs on a stashed clean tree (1 failed, 7 passed). Two belong to task sase-iq (deterministic; I recorded a +1 with the root cause -- 354d8c19f deliberately added TEST_COST_MODE to HEALTH_RECORDING_MODES and left tests/test_run_pytest_main.py:250 asserting the opposite, so the TEST is the stale half, and the file is in the contract manifest so it breaks just check for every agent -- plus a supplementary note on the second node, test_main_ace_page_group_isolation_uses_manifest_without_recorders, which inherits RECORD_ENV from the cost lane's parent process). title: Revisit true single-cargo-build packaging for the dev-update Rust install
close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-10: deprioritized out of the top seven, on the bead's own assessment. It closes with 'Lower priority now that the sase-i9.4 prebuild cache usually removes the compile from the interactive path entirely; this only helps runs that miss the cache.' The shipped plan-B fallback (per-artifact CARGO_TARGET_DIR isolation) already stops the two builds from invalidating each other, so the remaining cost is a duplicate sase_core compile plus a second target directory on cache-miss runs only. Worth revisiting if a maturin release lands that can reuse a feature-unified build, or if prebuild-cache hit rates turn out to be poor (see sase-io).
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-i9.2 (epic sase-i9, 'Build the Rust core and LSP in one feature-unified cargo invocation') as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP. That phase's plan A was to collapse the two dev-update Rust builds into one cargo invocation whose feature-unified dependency graph both artifacts share, so sase_core compiles once per update instead of twice. Measured evidence recorded on sase-i9.2: a feature-unified 'cargo build --profile

-p sase_core_py -p sase_xprompt_lsp --features sase_core_py/extension-module' took 188.15s, and the following 'maturin develop' still rebuilt for 99.20s instead of only packaging. maturin 1.14 reruns 'cargo rustc' after the shared build, so the shared cache did not carry over. The phase therefore shipped the plan-B fallback documented in plans:202608/fast_dev_update.md: per-artifact CARGO_TARGET_DIR isolation ('/target/uv-tool-py' and 'target/uv-tool-lsp', Justfile recipes rust-dev-install / rust-dev-install-uv-tool). That stops the two builds from invalidating each other's cached units but still compiles sase_core twice on a core change, and costs a second target directory of disk. Scope: find out whether a newer maturin, 'maturin build --skip-auditwheel'/'--frozen', a hand-packaged wheel built from the shared target dir, or a maturin flag can make the packaging step reuse the feature-unified build's artifacts, and if so replace the target-dir isolation. Re-measure cold and warm 'just rust-dev-install-uv-tool' against the numbers above and against docs/rust_backend.md before switching. Lower priority now that the sase-i9.4 prebuild cache usually removes the compile from the interactive path entirely; this only helps runs that miss the cache.

title: Justfile sase_core_dir trusts workspace-scoped env vars, so agent-shell rust installs can target the wrong sase-core checkout
description:
Recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on epic sase-i9 (by sase-ia.land) and given its concrete mechanism by phase sase-i9.5. Landing sase-i9 confirmed the mechanism is pre-existing and broader than dev-update, so it is filed here rather than fixed inside that epic.

MECHANISM (Justfile:24):
  sase_core_dir := env_var_or_default("SASE_CORE_DIR", env_var_or_default("SASE_LINKED_REPO_SASE_CORE_DIR", env_var_or_default("SASE_SIBLING_REPO_SASE_CORE_DIR", env_var_or_default("SASE_SIBLING_REPO_CORE_DIR", fallback_sase_core_dir))))
Every SASE-launched agent process exports SASE_LINKED_REPO_SASE_CORE_DIR and SASE_SIBLING_REPO_SASE_CORE_DIR pointing at its own ephemeral workspace clone. Re-confirmed 2026-08-09 in workspace sase_10 by dumping env: both resolve to
  /home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_10/sase/repos/linked/sase-core
So any 'just rust-install', 'just rust-install-uv-tool', 'just rust-dev-install', or 'just rust-dev-install-uv-tool' invoked from an agent shell builds sase_core_rs from that workspace clone even when cwd is correctly set to the real host checkout, because those two variables outrank the relative-path default. The env vars are not workspace-aware and predate the sase-i9 recipes (Justfile history: f72bdec19 -> 80d0ce218 -> b0f316ab7 -> 1114961b4), so 'just install' and every other recipe that reads sase_core_dir share the exposure.

OBSERVED IMPACT (2026-08-09): the host uv-tool venv's editable sase_core_rs.pth was written pointing into a numbered agent workspace clone
  .../workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_10/sase/repos/linked/sase-core/crates/sase_core_py/python
and broke silently once that workspace rebuilt/cleaned its target dir and the abi3 .so disappeared. Every host command reaching require_rust_extension() then failed with 'sase_core_rs is not importable in this environment but is a hard runtime dependency of sase' -- 'sase memory init --check', 'sase repo list', 'sase project list' -- while 'sase version' and 'sase bead ...' kept working, so the breakage was invisible until a Rust-backed command ran. Because the post-commit 'sase init' hook is one of those commands, commit 495eaedd3 left AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md/QWEN.md/OPENCODE.md and sase/memory/{README,glossary}.md stale and turned 'just check-full' red at the 'SASE validation' -> 'init memory --check' gate for every agent on master until they were regenerated (bfa34ffc8).

A later real ',U' in ~/.sase/logs/dev_update.jsonl (2026-08-09T12:48:31-04:00) shows the sase-core-rs package plan entry's git_root pointing at that same ephemeral workspace path even though the reconcile command's cwd was the host source root, reproducing the class after the first incident.

CURRENT STATE: the host is healthy again -- the .pth now reads /home/bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase-core/crates/sase_core_py/python, the abi3 .so is present, and 'sase_core_rs' imports as 0.21.3 in the uv-tool venv (verified 2026-08-09 while landing sase-i9). The gap itself is still open.

SCOPE (pick one or both; the choice is a design decision, which is why sase-i9's land agent did not guard it inline):
  1. Make the resolution authoritative rather than ambient: have recipes that install into a venv derive the core checkout from that install's own source root (SASE_LINKED_REPO_SASE_CORE_PRIMARY_DIR is already exported alongside the workspace path and holds the host checkout), or refuse to write an editable extension into a venv whose owning source root does not match.
  2. Scrub SASE_LINKED_REPO_SASE_CORE_DIR / SASE_SIBLING_REPO_SASE_CORE_DIR (and the legacy SASE_SIBLING_REPO_CORE_DIR) when just runs with cwd outside the workspace that exported them.
Also consider making the dev-update rust_health_check verify the .pth target still resolves to a loadable extension, not just that the import happens to work at install time, so a later workspace recycle is caught.

Verification for whoever takes this must not be done by running the real rust install from an agent shell without the guard in place -- that is the exact action that corrupted the host venv.

title: Confirm the dev-update prebuild cache actually hits on a real ,U and report the before/after timings

description:
Epic sase-i9 ('Make dev-install SASE updates fast') closed with its headline claim measured only in parts. Its plan (plans:202608/fast_dev_update.md, 'verify' phase, item 1) asked for a median cargo-seconds comparison of core-changed and core-unchanged runs before vs after, plus the prebuild hit rate. That comparison is still not possible: no real ',U' has run since the prebuild cache landed.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN (verified on the host 2026-08-09 while landing sase-i9):
  - The background producer works end to end. ~/.sase/cache/rust-prebuild/ holds a mirror clone checked out at an incoming upstream sase-core commit (443f1aa), two completed stamped sets (retention 2, so pruning works), and last-result.json recording {"hit": true, "set_key": "27b89954466b3b1fc3b90d17"}. That set's stamp.json carries all six provenance fields (core_commit, cargo_lock_sha256, rustc 1.97.1, profile dev-update, python_abi cpython-314-x86_64-linux-gnu, target_interpreter .../uv/tools/sase/bin/python3) plus sha256 digests for both artifacts, and the 13M sase_core_rs.abi3.so and 12M sase-xprompt-lsp are present.
  - The producer's and consumer's checkout resolution agree in production: the live runtime inventory reports the editable sase-core-rs record with source_root == git_root == /home/bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase-core, which is what the producer receives as --source-root and what _rust_prebuild_core_root passes as --core-root.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN:
  - _consume_prebuild has never installed a stamped set during a real update. ~/.sase/logs/dev_update.jsonl contains only two timed records, both schema 2 (2026-08-09T12:48:31-04:00, rust_dev_install 399.4s; 2026-08-09T14:44:41-04:00, rust_dev_install 157.8s), i.e. both from before the prebuild commit bumped the journal to schema 3. Neither carries a rust_prebuild field.
  - So 'tools/dev_update_timings' cannot yet show the epic's before/after or the hit rate, and nobody has seen the ',U completes in seconds' outcome the epic promised.

SCOPE (small): after the host has run at least one real ',U' that advances sase-core, read ~/.sase/logs/dev_update.jsonl for the schema-3 record, confirm rust_prebuild.hit is true (or record the exact miss reason), run 'tools/dev_update_timings', and post the numbers against the baselines already recorded on sase-i9.1 and sase-i9.2. If the record shows a miss, diagnose the reason field (stamp-missing / commit-mismatch / lockfile-mismatch / rustc-mismatch / profile-mismatch / abi-mismatch / interpreter-mismatch / digest-mismatch / copy-failure / health-check-failed / disabled) and fix the mismatch. This is a read-then-report check, not a rebuild; do not invoke the rust install recipes from an agent shell (see sase-in).

title: Split the suite-cost subprocess bucket into deliberate process-boundary tests and avoidable CLI round-trips
close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-10: valid but deprioritized out of the top seven. Confirmed the flat buckets still exist (tests/_test_cost.py:44-45 'subprocess_popen'/'subprocess_run'; a single subprocess_run budget in tests/perf/baselines/test_cost_budgets.json). This is test-harness metric granularity: it makes an exceeded budget harder to diagnose, but nothing is currently broken or red because of it, and the budget still catches regressions in aggregate. Reopen with a +1 when the subprocess_run budget is actually exceeded and the flat bucket blocks diagnosing which population grew.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-ib.4 (epic sase-ib) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP and forwarded by sase-ib.land while closing that epic.

PROBLEM: the cost harness attributes every subprocess call in the suite to two flat buckets. tests/_test_cost_plugin.py::_patch_subprocess wraps subprocess.run and subprocess.Popen wholesale and records them as the causes 'subprocess_run' and 'subprocess_popen' (labelled in tests/_test_cost.py). Those buckets mix two populations with opposite meanings: deliberate process-boundary coverage (git invocations, nested pytest runs, generated-gate execution, argv/exit-code/signal tests) that must stay a real subprocess, and avoidable CLI round-trips where a test spawns the sase CLI only to assert on stdout and an exit code. sase-ib.4 converted a batch of the second kind to in-process calls but never established the named set of the first kind that its own plan asked for, so the single 'subprocess_run' budget in tests/perf/baselines/test_cost_budgets.json (limit 300.0s) cannot distinguish 'someone added a legitimate process-boundary test' from 'someone reintroduced an avoidable CLI round-trip'. The metric is therefore too coarse to act on: it can only be exceeded, never diagnosed.

SCOPE: decide and implement the classification (a pytest marker on deliberate process-boundary tests is the obvious candidate, since the plugin already sees the running node), attribute the two populations to separate causes in tests/_test_cost.py and tests/_test_cost_plugin.py, split the committed budget accordingly in tests/perf/baselines/test_cost_budgets.json, and document the rule in docs/perf_runbook.md so a new test's author knows which bucket they are landing in. Record the named deliberate set that sase-ib.4's plan called for.

VERIFY: 'just test-cost' produces the two separate causes with numbers that sum to today's combined bucket, and 'tools/check_test_cost_budgets' fails when an avoidable CLI round-trip is reintroduced into a hot file while the deliberate set is unchanged.

title: test_main_cost_mode_arms_only_the_cost_recorder fails on master (HEALTH_PLUGIN_MODULE leaks into cost-mode command)
description:
Discovered while verifying the fix for task bead sase-ii (tests/ace/tui/test_tasks_pane_store.py mtime-cache regression) by running `just check`; the diff-scoped test lane failed on an unrelated node:

tests/test_run_pytest_main.py::test_main_cost_mode_arms_only_the_cost_recorder

Failure:
    assert runner.HEALTH_PLUGIN_MODULE not in command
AssertionError: assert 'tests._test_selection_health_plugin' not in ['.../.venv/bin/python', '-m', 'pytest', '-n', '2', '--dist=worksteal', ...]

Reproduction: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest 'tests/test_run_pytest_main.py::test_main_cost_mode_arms_only_the_cost_recorder' -q`

Confirmed via git stash / rerun / stash pop that this fails identically on a clean master checkout (354d8c19f) with no changes applied, so it is unrelated to the sase-ii fix.

Scope: tools/run_pytest's cost-mode arg assembly (the `main(["cost", ...])` path, look near HEALTH_PLUGIN_MODULE/TEST_COST_PLUGIN_MODULE wiring in tools/run_pytest) is including the test-selection-health plugin module (tests._test_selection_health_plugin) when arming cost-recording mode, but the test expects cost mode to arm only the cost recorder, not the health plugin. Fix by excluding HEALTH_PLUGIN_MODULE from the assembled command when in cost mode (or updating the test if the health plugin's presence in cost mode is now intentional and the assertion is stale).

title: bead_task_triage never reconciles gates for a project key that left the enabled inventory, leaving 11 live zombie TaskTriage notifications
close_reason: Let's punt on this for now.
description:
ROOT CAUSE: _reconcile() in src/sase/scripts/sase_chop_bead_task_triage.py only iterates projects returned by _enabled_project_stores() (line 473). Its lane state, however, is keyed by project and is read/written wholesale (_read_state/_write_state). A project key that leaves the enabled inventory — renamed, deregistered, or disabled — keeps its gates/generations/fingerprints/kinds entries forever, and its pending gate bundles are never inspected, never cancelled, and their notifications never settle. The chop cannot cancel them because it never visits that project again.

EVIDENCE (this host, 2026-08-10): ~/.sase/axe/lumberjacks/checks/bead_task_triage.json still holds a project entry 'gh_sase-org__sase-2', which is not in ~/.sase/projects/ and not in 'sase project list' (only actstat, bob-cli, and sase are registered). Of the 12 currently pending task_triage gate bundles in ~/.sase/interaction_requests/task_triage, 11 belong to that dead key and have been pending since 2026-08-02: sase-cl, sase-ct, sase-cu, sase-dn, sase-dy, sase-e5, sase-ec, sase-ed, sase-ee, sase-ef (all created 08-02 14:40) and sase-cb (08-02 15:15). Each request.json records producer {"chop": "bead_task_triage", "project": "gh_sase-org__sase-2"} and names a live notification id, e.g. bead-task-triage-sase-cl-1c7fbbb5b5e5-g1 -> 49d096cf-ca8b-4675-9ae7-adcd7bfefcef. Only one pending gate (sase-cj under gh_sase-org__sase) is legitimate. The beads themselves are duplicated across both keys in the state file, so the same bead was gated twice under two keys.

IMPACT: violates the chop's own documented invariant that a live task bead has at most one pending gate (docs/axe.md, docs/notifications.md). The user gets task-triage notifications that can never be cleared by the owning chop and that reference a project that no longer exists. The state file also grows without bound: it currently carries a stale gh_bobs-org__bob-cli entry and ~180 sase entries.

SCOPE: teach the reconciler to handle project keys present in lane state but absent from the current enabled inventory — cancel their pending gates with a distinct reason and drop their state entries — while failing closed when the inventory read itself fails (_enabled_project_stores already returns early on error, and a partial inventory must not be treated as 'these projects are gone'). Decide and document what a temporarily *disabled* project should do (cancel vs retain). Include a one-time cleanup of the 11 gates and notifications listed above. Add regression tests alongside tests/test_axe_chop_bead_task_triage.py.

CONTEXT: found while diagnosing a separate, confirmed defect in the same chop — it re-raises a gate for a task bead whose launch is still in flight — which is covered by its own tale plan proposed 2026-08-10. Do not conflate the two: different trigger, different fix.

title: Symvision epic-symbol bead lookup can transiently miss an existing in-progress bead
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: one preventive gate and one unreproduced transient, closed in favor of live defects.
description: During unrelated runner-slot queue work on 2026-08-10, mandatory `just check` passed fmt, ruff, mypy, pyscripts, test-waits, changelog, and patch/stitch terminology, then failed at lint (symvision): `Error: --epic-symbol 'sase-i8(MergeSummary)': bead 'sase-i8' not found. Remove this --epic-symbol entry.` The failure is not a stale whitelist entry: immediately afterward `SASE_SYMVISION_BEAD_STATUS_ONLY=1 tools/sase_bead show sase-i8` resolved the in-progress epic, and the exact Symvision invocation from the Justfile with `BD_COMMAND=tools/sase_bead` passed with `All public/private classes/functions are used properly!`. Investigate why the Symvision epic-symbol bead status lookup can transiently miss a bead that the same wrapper can resolve, and make the lint gate deterministic or emit a retryable diagnostic. This blocks clean unrelated `just check` runs when it recurs.

Independent of the race, a dozen further +1s with fresh flake evidence landed on sase-ct between 14:31Z and 14:59Z (same recurring ACE/TUI node class), so `ready` is the correct current status on its own merits regardless of how the reopen was triggered. title: The /sase_plan skill still classifies plan authoring as large/xlarge work after that guidance was deleted from the sizes memory
close_reason: Displaced from the owner's seven by sase-it, which reopened mid-triage; confirmed live but non-blocking
description:
Found by sase-il.7's land agent while integrating changes that landed during epic sase-il.7 (core-owned tale size semantics).

THE INCONSISTENCY: src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_plan.md step 2 says 'Authoring a tale plan is `large` work; authoring an epic plan is `xlarge` work.' Commit 24dde3775 (tale 202608/drop_plan_authoring_size_paragraph.md) deleted the equivalent paragraph from src/sase/main/init_memory/templates/memory-sase-sizes.template.md and the regenerated sase/memory/sase_sizes.md, because the project owner judged that claim 'not useful, not clear, and not accurate'. That plan explicitly scoped the skill line out ('Do not change it') and asked for it to be reported so the owner could decide whether it deserves its own task bead. This bead is that report.

WHY IT MATTERS: epic sase-il made sase/memory/sase_sizes.md the single source of size truth, and epic sase-il.7 finished that by cutting the size taxonomy out of the sase-core schema descriptions so they only point at the note. The skill is now the last place that carries a size claim the canonical note deliberately does not, and step 1 of that same skill tells the agent to read the note first -- so an agent gets the deleted guidance from the skill immediately after being pointed at the note that dropped it.

SCOPE: this needs the owner's decision at triage, not a mechanical edit. Either delete the sentence (matching the deletion request that motivated 24dde3775) or restate whatever rule is actually wanted -- the sizes note owns size meanings, so a pointer is the only duplication-free option. sase_plan.md is a generated-skill source: after editing it, follow sase/memory/generated_skills.md and redeploy the skill rather than editing a deployed copy.

notes.author: sase-j3.land
notes.text:
Verified all 8 phases against the shipped code, not just the bead notes, and read every phase commit (e01584098, 4d8be52cf, 21c83218f, 64ddea98a, ba77762e6, de530b340, 0ccd7f844, aae179e86, d4b913bb9).

WHAT I CONFIRMED IN THE SOURCE. target: ace.snippet_config_path exists in default_config.yml, sase.schema.json, and _state_init_late.py; snippet discovery lives in the Textual-free src/sase/xprompt/snippet_targets.py with modals/snippet_config_location_modal.py deleted and no compatibility alias anywhere (grepped .py/.pyi/.md); resolve_snippet_save_target implements all six rules and pipes through write_targets.resolve_xprompt_write_target; snippet_collision is pure and built on resolution_after_save. model: PromptStackState carries snippet_item/snippet_index/has_snippet_pane/agent_items/agent_count/append_snippet_pane/remove_snippet_pane/retarget_snippet_pane/snippet_is_dirty, and texts/join/editor_markdown/is_effectively_empty are agent-only, so no launch, stash, or save-as payload can contain the snippet body. name: snippet_name_modal.py builds every verdict row from the plan's table and loads bodies through asyncio.to_thread. pane: the gt binding is in _PROMPT_G_PREFIX_BINDINGS, and _prompt_input_bar_snippet_pane.py implements open/retarget/close with PromptFocusRestore(item_id, cursor, vim_mode) and the dirty-discard ConfirmActionModal guard. save: snippet_save_confirm_modal.py renders draft/existing/diff with the changed-on-disk reload branch, and both gx and gt route through the single save_snippet() coroutine, so the write, last-used location, live publish, and post-write commit/scoped-chezmoi-apply chain cannot drift. visual: the separator title bar, the .prompt-pane.snippet-target $primary CSS, and the snippet subtitles are all present. docs: the gt row is in the help popup and both docs/ace.md keymap tables, and ace.snippet_config_path is documented in docs/configuration.md.

EPIC WORK I FINISHED HERE. Phase sase-j3.6 recorded a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP that its fourth planned PNG golden -- the save confirmation showing a diff -- could not be pinned because sase-j3.5's modal did not exist in its workspace. That is epic scope, not a follow-up, so I completed it: new tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_snippet_save.py and golden snippet_save_confirm_diff_120x40.png, rendering the real unified diff, the [Diff] tab strip, and the overwrite verdict. All four of the visual phase's planned goldens now exist.

INTEGRATION. Compared the epic's 56 touched files against all 13 non-epic commits that landed between 2026-08-10 14:49 and 18:44. Only four overlaps exist (5f6d8ea64 and 63f9f15d6 on docs/ace.md, 5f6d8ea64 on default_config.yml, 83e3d3c27 on docs/configuration.md, c69d16378 on styles.tcss) and every one of them predates the epic commit that touched the same file, so each phase already rebased onto it. Semantically: no other code computes a snippet destination or writes ace.snippets outside snippet_targets.py, snippet_config_yaml.py, and the two save paths, so nothing duplicates or conflicts with what this epic added; the = keymap (sase-j2.1) is app-level and does not collide with the prompt-bar g table; the opt-in global-state leak detector (sase-j7.2) has nothing to catch here, since none of the epic's new modules introduce module-level mutable state; and _editor_helper_snippets.py reads the merged config, so it needs no change.

VERIFICATION. just install, then just check-full on this tree: every lint gate (fmt python/markdown, keep-sorted, ruff, mypy, pyscripts, test waits, changelog, patch/stitch terminology, symvision, toobig), SASE validation, committed-plans validation, and the full pytest cost lane all pass. Full just test-visual: 652 passed, 1 skipped -- one more than sase-j3.8's 651, which is exactly the golden added above. check-full stops only at its final gate, the flake baseline, on two nodes that are not this epic's.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UPS, ALL RESOLVED. (1) sase-j3.5 and sase-j3.8 both proposed the logs-pane scroll-extremes flake: filed as new task sase-jb (large, ready). I read the durable selection-health record store directly rather than trusting the summary -- the node has two qualifying full-run failures with disjoint change sets (head e01584098 carrying only sase-j7.2's leak-detector test files, head ba77762e6 carrying only sase-j3.5's snippet-save files), and neither touches logs-pane code, so it is not attributable to this epic. (2) sase-j3.8 also proposed the plus-one presentation flake: task sase-j6 already tracked it, so I recorded a +1 with independent evidence instead of a duplicate -- that node has three disjoint-change-set failures, the earliest (head 012e1a88b, models_panel_rendering.py) predating any sase-j3 commit. Both nodes are also recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on in-progress epic sase-h8.10, which owns clearing the nodes that fail sase-h8's flake-gate exit criterion. (3) sase-j3.6's PNG-golden proposal was epic work and is done, as described above. Nothing was declined.

ONE GAP I FOUND AND DID NOT FIX, filed as task sase-jc (medium, ready): resolve_snippet_save_target accepts any writable .yml path, but sase's config loader only merges ~/.config/sase/sase.yml, its sase_*.yml overlays, and the project sase/sase.yml. So ace.snippet_config_path: 'snippets.yml' is accepted with no fallback_reason, the snippet is written and published live for the session, and it silently disappears on the next start -- a near-miss with the documented 'sase_snippets.yml' example, which does load. I left it for the owner because there are two defensible fixes (reject non-loadable destinations with a fallback_reason, or teach the loader to read the configured file) and because narrowing the resolver would intersect sase-j3.8's deliberate out-of-discovery picker work in d4b913bb9. This is a plan-faithful implementation of rules the plan did not include, not a phase that failed to do its job.

title: flake-baseline gate never clears a renamed or deleted test's node ID
description: tools/selection_health --fail-on-new-flake (reproducible_flake_nodeids, tests/_test_selection_health.py:183) flags a node ID as a reproducible flake whenever it fails across two disjoint change sets with no independent interleaved pass. When a flaky test is renamed or deleted, its old node ID can never appear in a passing run again -- there is no test left to run under that ID -- so it stays flagged as a reproducible flake forever, regardless of commit ordering, until someone manually bumps the baseline's effective-after cutoff past every one of its historical failures. This defect was masked by the cutoff bump landed for tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt as part of the sase-ct retirement (commit 83bb8a6f7), which incidentally cleared the concrete instance below, but the underlying mechanism gap remains and will silently recur the next time a flaky test is renamed. Concrete instance: tests/test_run_pytest_main.py::test_main_cost_mode_arms_only_the_cost_recorder was renamed to test_main_cost_mode_arms_cost_and_health_recorders by commit 1417de7db; the old node ID had a 14:33Z failure recorded against it and could never pass again under that name. notes.author: sase-ns.6.6.6.land
notes.text: DISCOVERED ISSUE: residual ambient config readers reach load_merged_config() through Python's process-shared default asyncio ThreadPoolExecutor, which outlives any single ACE app/test. Measured by epic sase-ns.6.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.6.1 (bead sase-mv's probe, re-run post-fix on master): `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -n 2 -p tests._config_reader_probe --sase-detect-config-readers tests/ace/tui tests/test_config_cache.py tests/test_config_cache_token.py tests/test_config_cache_selector.py tests/test_config_cache_teardown.py tests/test_config_cache_isolation.py tests/test_llm_override_indicator.py` -> 9621 passed, 4207 ambient reads, 181 records, 150 poisoning, 33 cross-test threads. Two real families: 22 records via sase.ace.tui.widgets.llm_override_indicator's run_worker(thread=True) default-resolution path, and 117 via ordinary awaited asyncio.to_thread(prepare_loaded_agents_worker_boundary, ...) in src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_loading_disk.py (both async_load and artifact_delta_load) calling get_max_running_agents() -> load_merged_config() from _loading_compute.py:404. The remaining 11 are a probe self-artifact: tests/_config_reader_probe.py keys _remember_thread_locked purely by native thread_ident and never clears stale entries, so OS thread-id reuse misattributes short-lived test threads to an unrelated earlier test. IMPACT: this is process-global state leaking between tests by the mechanism this epic owns -- the readers are correctly-awaited application code, not leaked background workers, so it cannot be fixed by draining a thread. The fix belongs at the executor-sharing root (a per-app custom executor for AcePage tests, or an explicit decision to stop gating on ambient reads). Re-measure with the probe command above first: the mix has shifted since sase-mv's step-1 probe, where llm_override_indicator was the majority contributor and is now 22/139. Recorded here rather than as a task bead because epic sase-ns.6.6.6's plan routed sase-j7-owned root causes to this bead.

title: Make sase-github fork-aware across numbered workspaces and PR lifecycle
close_reason: No fork-based external contribution in flight; large design work on a hypothetical topology
description: External-contributor research found that sase-github pushes Patch branches to origin, then runs context-sensitive gh pr view/create/merge commands without explicit base/head repository coordinates. Core ensure_git_clone_at clones a primary checkout into numbered workspaces while retaining only origin; a local reproduction confirmed an upstream remote and remote.upstream.gh-resolved=base on the primary disappear in the numbered clone. On a contributor-owned fork this can push correctly to the fork but target PR operations at the fork, and primary-only gh repo set-default configuration does not survive. Scope: detect and persist fork-parent/base/head metadata, make all PR lifecycle operations explicit and fork-aware in every numbered workspace, cover creation/view/close/submit behavior and non-fork regressions, and document the external-contributor topology. Preserve the permission boundary: origin is the contributor fork, upstream code writes must not be required. Full evidence and proposed workaround are in the attached research artifact.

notes.author: yb
notes.text: Backlog triage (owner-requested seven-bead cut, 2026-08-12): verified at HEAD 62951abcb that sase-github is still fork-blind (the only fork reference in the plugin is workspace_plugin.py:1276 is_fork on a repo listing). The gap is real, but it costs nothing until an actual contributor-fork topology is in use, and remediation is a large change across the whole PR lifecycle in every numbered workspace. The research artifact attached to this bead keeps the evidence and the proposed workaround. Reopen with a +1 the first time a fork-based contribution actually mis-targets a PR.

title: ace.snippet_config_path accepts a destination sase never loads back, so those snippets silently vanish on restart
close_reason: Backlog cut to seven (owner-requested, 2026-08-12): needs an owner design decision, and the trigger is a misconfiguration rather than a default path. The analysis is sound -- resolve_snippet_save_target accepts any writable .yml/.yaml destination, while the config loader only merges ~/.config/sase/sase.yml, the ~/.config/sase/sase_*.yml overlays, and the project sase/sase.yml -- so a configured ace.snippet_config_path outside that set is written and never read back. But it fires only when someone sets that field to a non-loadable path (the docs example, sase_snippets.yml, loads correctly), it was never reproduced end to end, and the bead itself says the two remediations are a judgment call the owner should make, not something to hand an agent. My read if you want a default: option (a) -- reject the non-loadable destination in resolve_snippet_save_target and fall back with a fallback_reason, since the trigger-name panel already renders that field for exactly this purpose -- plus one sentence in docs/configuration.md stating the constraint. Re-file with that decision attached, or with a +1 if a real snippet loss is observed.
description:
Found by the sase-j3 land agent while verifying epic sase-j3 (snippet target mode) on master d4b913bb9. Not a plan violation: sase-j3.1 implemented resolve_snippet_save_target() exactly as the approved plan specified. The gap is that the specified rules never check whether sase will read the file back.

WHAT HAPPENS: src/sase/xprompt/snippet_targets.py::resolve_snippet_save_target accepts any configured path whose suffix is .yml/.yaml and whose _writability_reason() is None. But sase's config loader only merges three sources: ~/.config/sase/sase.yml, the ~/.config/sase/sase_*.yml overlays discovered by src/sase/config/loading.py::get_overlay_paths (glob 'sase_*.yml'), and the project sase/sase.yml. src/sase/xprompt/snippet_targets.py::load_snippet_config_locations enumerates exactly that set, so any configured destination outside it is writable but never loaded.

REPRODUCTION (by inspection; not yet run end-to-end): set ace.snippet_config_path to 'snippets.yml'. Rule 2 resolves it to ~/.config/sase/snippets.yml. The parent is writable and the suffix is fine, so it is accepted with source='configured' and fallback_reason=None. gt writes the ace.snippets entry there and _publish_saved_snippet() makes the trigger expand immediately, so the loop looks correct for the rest of the session. On the next ACE start the file is not an overlay ('snippets.yml' does not match 'sase_*.yml') and is not merged, so the snippet is gone with no diagnostic. Any absolute path outside ~/.config/sase/ and the project config has the same shape. Note the near-miss: the docs/configuration.md example uses 'sase_snippets.yml', which does load; dropping the 'sase_' prefix silently does not.

WHY IT NEEDS A DECISION RATHER THAN A DRIVE-BY FIX -- there are two defensible remediations:
  (a) Reject a non-loadable destination in resolve_snippet_save_target and fall back to the default with a fallback_reason. The plumbing already exists: the trigger-name panel renders fallback_reason precisely so a user learns why their preference was not honored. Cheapest and consistent with rule 4.
  (b) Teach the config loader to also read the configured snippet file, honoring the user's choice end-to-end. Larger, but it is what a user setting the field probably expects.
Whichever is chosen, docs/configuration.md's ace.snippet_config_path section needs to state the constraint explicitly.

CARE REQUIRED: sase-j3.8 (commit d4b913bb9) deliberately made UnifiedXPromptSaveModal include a resolved snippet target that is outside the discovered locations. Option (a) narrows what the resolver can return, so re-check that work and its tests in tests/ace/tui/modals/test_unified_xprompt_save_modal.py and tests/ace/tui/actions/test_prompt_save_xprompt_targets.py rather than assuming it becomes dead code.

title: sase stitch list lists repos, not stitches, and overlaps sase repo list
close_reason: Obsolete: commit 3306e093c removed the wart
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-j8.1 (epic sase-j8, epic plan sase/repos/plans/202608/stitch_rename.md documents it under 'Known design wart to flag, not fix').

After epic sase-j8 renamed the `sase vcs` command tree to `sase stitch` (commit 83e3d3c27), `sase stitch list` renders the repository *constellation* — primary, linked, and sidecar repos with branch, dirty state, commit counts, and activity — not stitches. Reproduce with `sase stitch --help` and `sase stitch list`; the help text itself reads 'Inspect the repository constellation ... or show their cross-repository stitch timeline.'

Two consequences:
1. The subcommand name is now misleading: 'list' under 'stitch' lists repos.
2. It overlaps the already-existing `sase repo list`, which also enumerates the project's primary, sidecar, linked, and external repos.
3. Bare `sase stitch` still defaults to `sase stitch list` through the central `_default_list_subcommands()` convention (src/sase/main/parser.py), so the bare command shows repos rather than the stitch timeline that the Stitch name implies.

Proposed remediation (needs a design decision, hence the size): move repo-constellation listing under `sase repo` — either by folding its columns into `sase repo list` or by adding a distinct `sase repo stats`-style subcommand — and repoint bare `sase stitch` at `sase stitch log` (the commit/stitch timeline). Keep `sase stitch list` and `sase vcs list` accepted as deprecated aliases so existing invocations and agent muscle memory keep working, following the alias precedent already established by sase-j8.1 (parser_stitch.py's aliases=['vcs'], the parser_vcs.py/vcs_handler.py facade shims, and _COMMAND_REGISTRARS carrying both keys).

Relevant code: src/sase/main/parser_stitch.py, src/sase/main/stitch_handler.py, src/sase/main/parser.py (_COMMAND_REGISTRARS, _COMPACT_ROOT_COMMANDS, _default_list_subcommands), src/sase/vcs_list/ (the engine, deliberately not renamed), src/sase/main/parser_repo.py, docs/vcs.md, docs/cli.md.

Note the concurrent tale sase/repos/plans/202608/stitch_create_migration.md is adding `sase stitch create`; whoever works this should land after or coordinate with it, since both reshape the `sase stitch` subcommand set.

description: Phase sase-hn.8.2 (commit 50f8961ac) renamed the dismissed_bundle_summaries column meta_changespec to meta_patch but left SCHEMA_VERSION at 1. notes.author: sase-jo.5
notes.text: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: Design/implementation mismatch in the origin taxonomy. plans:202608/stitch_origin_badges.md specifies a closed 3-value taxonomy (stitch/auto/manual) driven by SASE_TYPE= footer precedence rules (TYPE=stitch -> stitch; TYPE=<other> -> auto; legacy AGENT=/BEAD=/PLAN=-only -> stitch; otherwise -> manual). The core phase (sase-jo.1, closed) instead implemented a simpler 2-value CommitOriginWire enum in sase-core (crates/sase_core/src/vcs_log/origin.rs): Manual/Sase, classified purely by "does parse_commit_footer find any tag at all" - no TYPE= precedence, no auto/manual split. The Python wire (sase-jo.3, closed) mirrors this 2-value type (sase.core.vcs_log_wire.CommitOrigin = Literal["manual","sase"]). This filter phase (sase-jo.5) implemented origin:manual/origin:sase filtering against the actual 2-value wire since that is what exists and type-checks; it does not implement the 3-value grammar the design doc describes. The still-open render phase (sase-jo.4) and docs phase (sase-jo.6) will hit the same mismatch - the design's glyph/legend table and detail-panel wording assume 3 values (including an auto-vs-stitch distinction and reading the TYPE value for auto, e.g. "auto . sase init"), which the current wire cannot produce. The still-open invariant phase (sase-jo.2) stamps SASE_TYPE=stitch specifically, but classify_commit_origin() never reads TYPE, so that stamp does not affect classification. Epic land agent should decide: (a) update the plan doc + render/docs phases to match the shipped 2-value reality, or (b) file a task bead to redo the core classifier to implement the originally-specified 3-value TYPE= precedence taxonomy before render/docs land.

title: Artifact reference contract
description: Artifact references stop being xprompts and become a first-class, versioned ref contract: five builtin kinds (`@stitch`, `@patch`, `@bead`, `@agent`, `@file`) plus artifact-repo document kinds (`@plan`, `@research`, ...) configured inline or with `use: <provider>` from an installed plugin. Every ref expands deterministically, is recorded per occurrence against the agent that used it, publishes as a numbered Markdown reference link, writes a `Referenced By` table back into the cited artifact, and gets a generated "Artifacts" sub-tab in ACE.

title: sase repo open mis-resolves primary_dir/workspace for auto_clone linked repos (sase-core)
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: single-surface CLI/doc papercuts with narrow blast radius, closed in favor of cross-agent correctness and gate-blocking work.
description:
Reproduction (from workspace sase_11, host project gh_sase-org__sase, cwd = the
workspace root):

  $ sase repo open sase-core -r "..."
  Current directory belongs to a different project's workspace; pass -w/--workspace.

cwd IS that project's workspace 11, so this message is wrong on its face.

  $ sase repo open sase-core -r "..." -w 11
  Primary workspace directory does not exist: /home/bryan/projects/git/sase-core

  $ sase repo open sase-core -r "..." -p gh_sase-org__sase -w 11
  Primary workspace directory does not exist: /home/bryan/projects/git/sase-core

But the agent process's own SASE_LINKED_REPOS_JSON env var reports, for the same
linked repo entry (name: sase-core, auto_clone: true):
  primary_dir: /home/bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase-core
  workspace_dir: /home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_11/sase/repos/linked/sase-core

i.e. github (with the sase-org segment), not git. The CLI's own computed
primary_dir ("/home/bryan/projects/git/sase-core") disagrees with the env-exported
value, and is also missing the org path segment. This matches the resolution
described in the closed bead sase-in, which confirms
SASE_LINKED_REPO_SASE_CORE_PRIMARY_DIR=/home/bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase-core
is the authoritative primary dir - sase-in's fix was scoped to the Justfile's
sase_core_dir recipe var, not to `sase repo open`'s own resolution, so this
appears to be an unfixed sibling bug in a different code path.

Impact: the auditable `sase repo open` entry point cannot be used for this linked
repo from this workspace at all - every invocation errors before doing anything.
It does not block actual repo access: the workspace_dir
(.../sase_11/sase/repos/linked/sase-core) is already a valid, up-to-date,
auto-cloned checkout on disk (confirmed via `git status` / `git log` inside it),
so an agent can just use that path directly, but that skips the `sase repo log`
audit trail the skill relies on.

Discovered while implementing sase/repos/plans/202608/sase_core_ci_parity_gate.md
in workspace sase_11 on 2026-08-12.

notes.author: yd
notes.text: RELATED: sase-in — closed bead that fixed the same primary_dir/workspace-dir ambient-env-var confusion for sase-core, but scoped to the Justfile's sase_core_dir recipe variable. Confirms SASE_LINKED_REPO_SASE_CORE_PRIMARY_DIR=/home/bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase-core is authoritative; this bead is about sase repo open's own (different) resolution path still getting it wrong.

notes.author: sase-jx.5.1
notes.text:
Repaired the chop-overrun classifier's timestamp and per-run contract in sase-core (commit 46ce1fe, pushed to origin/master).

Fixed: sampled_blocking_ms now parses/validates started_at unconditionally for every otherwise-known-status run (completed/running/action) before deriving blocking_ms, instead of only for status=="running". A completed run with valid duration_ms but an unparsable started_at is now dropped as unsampled rather than classified off duration_ms alone; excluded statuses remain unaffected (already unsampled). Verified with a new test covering success/running/skipped/action_succeeded all given "not-a-timestamp".

Extended: ChopOverrunWire gained run_ratios: Vec<Option<f64>>, one entry per raw request.runs entry in order (None = unsampled, Some(ratio) = that run's own blocking/interval ratio). Existing summary fields (level, sampled_runs, over_runs, worst_ratio, worst_blocking_ms, latest_ratio) are unchanged. CHOP_OVERRUN_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 1 -> 2 (no versioned shape changed under the old number). Verified with tests proving [skipped, over-success] -> run_ratios [None, Some(...)] with level="over" and latest_ratio pointing at the older sampled run, and a case locating an older overrun by raw index after a healthy newest run.

Updated PyO3 bindings in sase_core_py: round-trip test (chop_overrun_binding_returns_exact_plain_python_shape) now pins the 8-key shape including run_ratios; structural-error test's schema-mismatch fixture uses CHOP_OVERRUN_SCHEMA_VERSION + 1 instead of a stale hardcoded literal so it still asserts a real mismatch after the bump.

Verification: cargo fmt --all, then `just check` (fmt-check, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test --workspace including sase_core_py's abi3-py312 binding tests via the repo's PYO3_PYTHON resolution) — all green, exit 0. title: Memory notes xprompts.md and glossary.md still document the removed %name/%n and %tribe/%t directives
description:
Discovered on 2026-08-12 while planning a chop change that needed to name a launched agent from a prompt. The Directives table in sase/memory/xprompts.md lists '%name:<n>' (alias %n) as the agent-name directive and '%tribe:<name>' (alias %t) as the tribe directive, and the 'Agent Tribe' entry in sase/memory/glossary.md likewise says tribes are assigned with '%tribe:<name>' (alias %t). Both directives were removed from SASE and now fail closed.

ROOT CAUSE: src/sase/xprompt/_directive_types.py lists 'name' and 'tribe' in _DEPRECATED_DIRECTIVE_MESSAGES, and _DIRECTIVE_ALIASES still maps 'n' -> 'name' and 't' -> 'tribe', so the short spellings resolve to the deprecated canonical names. _directive_collect.py raises DirectiveError for any deprecated directive. The memory notes were never updated when the directives were retired.

REPRODUCTION (this workspace, master 56d6bd772):
  .venv/bin/python -c "from sase.xprompt._directive_extract import extract_prompt_directives as e; e('%n:foo.@ x', process_references=lambda s: s)"
    -> DirectiveError: The '%name'/'%n' directive has been renamed; use %id/%i, and %id(<id>, clan=<clan>) to join a clan.
  Same call with '%t:mytribe x'
    -> DirectiveError: The '%tribe'/'%t' directive has been removed; use %id(tribe=<tribe>) or the #tribe xprompt for an auto-named agent, %id(<id>, tribe=<tribe>) for an explicitly named agent, or %clan(<clan>, tribe=<tribe>) for a clan.
  '%i:ci_fix.sase.@ x' parses fine and yields name='ci_fix.sase.@'.

IMPACT: any agent that follows these notes when authoring a prompt writes a directive that raises DirectiveError at launch. The notes are Tier 2 (xprompts.md) and Tier 1 always-loaded (glossary.md), so the wrong spelling is in front of every agent working on prompts or agent naming.

SCOPE: update the Directives table in sase/memory/xprompts.md to '%id:<n>' / alias '%i' and to drop the removed %tribe row in favor of the '%id(tribe=<tribe>)' / '#tribe:<tribe>' / '%clan(<clan>, tribe=<tribe>)' forms; update the 'Agent Tribe' glossary entry the same way; check the rest of both notes for other uses of the retired spellings. Memory-file edits require the user's explicit permission, which launching this task supplies; finish by running 'sase memory init' to regenerate AGENTS.md, the provider instruction shims, and the memory README, as the repo instructions require.

Fixed in bugyi-chops 3676814 (released 0.5.1, pushed, plugin updated, axe healthy): the dry-run check sits at the point of action so the preview still reports which repo would be gated. just check green (163 tests, 91% coverage, ruff/mypy/build/twine). FOLLOW-UPS. sase-jz.1's PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP (track uv.lock or change the install recipe) was already resolved inside the epic by a33d21d, which tracks uv.lock; no task filed. title: Clone SDD sidecars from a local primary checkout before the remote
close_reason: Backlog cut to seven (owner-requested, 2026-08-12): accepted cost, not a defect. Sidecar materialization cloning from the recorded remote instead of a matching local primary checkout is a latency optimization on the first @research ref in a fresh workspace -- the approved lazy-materialization plan explicitly accepted this cost, and the correctness properties it must not break (remote URL normalization, strict failure diagnostics, workspace isolation) make it a medium change for a one-time network clone. Nothing is broken or blocked. Re-file with a +1 if sidecar clone latency actually shows up on the agent launch path in practice.
description: While implementing lazy document sidecar materialization, the approved plan accepted the current cost: ensure_sdd_kind_clone -> ensure_sidecar_sdd_clone clones missing sidecar roles from the recorded remote URL even when a matching local primary checkout already has that sidecar clone. The first @research ref in a fresh workspace therefore pays a full network clone on the launch path, and the same source choice affects sase repo path <role> --ensure plus existing plans/beads workspace prep. Scope: teach sidecar materialization to prefer a verified matching local primary checkout as the clone source or fallback, preserve remote URL normalization and strict failure diagnostics, and cover plans, beads, and custom document sidecars without weakening workspace isolation.

notes.author: sase-k2.land
notes.text:

- filters: external_mirror/filters.py glob engine, config.py legacy fold for exclude_labels/pr_authors, schema + default_config.yml with the four release-please/release-plz head-ref exclusions, CLI Filtered column (main/patch_sync.py:109), TUI remote-only chip (_patch_list_banner.py), doctor check config.external_mirror, docs.

No hardcoded lumberjack_state_dir('checks') or ensure_lumberjack_dirs_fn remains anywhere in src/.
- bug_status: issues.py close/reopen with the documented guards, beads_closed/beads_reopened on MirrorReport and in sase bead sync-external, --dry-run lists 'would close'/'would reopen'.
- patch_status: ACTION_REFRESH end to end, guarded to pr_origin external with an under-lock re-ownership check, active-to-archive move, refreshed counter.
- perf: external_pr_import_batch holds both ProjectSpec locks once per pass over an incrementally updated in-memory index.

LIVE STATE. The external_mirror lane is running clean: 4 cycles / 2884s uptime against its 900s interval, 0 errors, and every external_pr_mirror[sase] record on 2026-08-12 (14:10 through 15:04) is status no_op with fetched=200 unmirrored=32 created=0 repaired=0 refreshed=0 errors=0 -- no timeouts, and the 32 release-please PRs are filtered rather than adopted. The checks lane is back to a healthy 320s average against its 300s interval. ('sase patch sync-external --project sase --dry-run' reports pull_requests_unsupported from a workspace venv because no plugins are installed there; the chop records are the real evidence.)

FIXED AT LANDING (step 2), two conflicts with work that landed alongside the epic:
1. Core binding floor. sase-k2.5 bumped EXTERNAL_PR_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION 1 -> 2 (0567ce03b, 13:29). Two minutes later 688eec2bd, from unrelated epic sase-jx, ratcheted pyproject.toml to sase-core-rs>=0.26.4 with uv.lock pinned to exactly 0.26.4 -- and 0.26.4 ships EXTERNAL_PR_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1 and rejects any other value, while schema 2 first published in 0.26.5. Any environment resolving from the lockfile rather than a linked sase-core checkout would have failed every PR mirror pass; core/rust.py is strict with no Python fallback. Raised the floor to >=0.26.5,<0.27.0 and refreshed uv.lock.
2. Undocumented refresh behavior. docs/axe.md's external_pr_mirror counter list omitted 'refreshed' and neither it nor docs/change_spec.md described that an adopted external Patch now follows its PR to merged/closed and moves into the archive. Documented both, including the pr_origin guard, the under-lock ownership recheck, and why the daily full scan became load-bearing.
Also confirmed already-integrated: sase-k2.4 routes its mirrored-bead closes through settle_closed_task_bead_gates, matching 875f67b74; the (mtime_ns, size) Patch snapshot cache from 2d92ef6a9 invalidates correctly against the new batch writer; no AXE overrun code enumerates lane names.

ARCHIVE REPAIRED. gh_sase-org__sase-archive.sase had re-accumulated 50 duplicate blocks (25 release-please names x3) between sase-k2.1's repair at 12:32 and 12:58, written by the then-deployed build. It now reads 289 raw NAME: lines / 289 parsed Patches / 289 unique names at 0.53 MB, down from the 33.8 MB and 3375-vs-289 split the plan measured. project.duplicate_patch_blocks is OK.

VERIFICATION RUN. 'just check-full' passed every lint gate (fmt, ruff, mypy, symvision, toobig, keep-sorted), SASE and committed-plans validation, and the entire pytest test-cost lane with its suite-cost budgets. It failed only at the final 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' gate, which named 7 nodes over tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt -- all already tracked, none epic-caused, and no node failed live in the run. The same gate blocked sase-k3.6 and sase-k0.4.land on clean trees today.

- sase-k2.1 'flake baseline gate exceeds current baseline' -- duplicate of ready bead sase-jq, which already names all six nodes (five test_core_vcs_log plus test_contract_manifest_matches_marker_selection). Corroborated with a +1 carrying this landing's reproduction rather than filing again.

Confirmed the mechanism first: issues.py:326-328 seeds upstream_states for every newly created ref, so an issue already closed at first sight records 'closed' on the creating pass and no transition ever fires; that bead stays open permanently.
- plan-directed deferral, the perf phase's 'fetch_limit=200 deserves its own task bead' -- filed as sase-kl (large, ready), with live evidence that the limit is saturated (fetched=200, ~296 PRs on the repo) and the new note that refresh makes the up-to-24h staleness matter more than adoption delay did.

notes.author: sase-k3.land
notes.text:
LANDED epic sase-k3 (sase-k3.land, 2026-08-12). Phase sase-k3.6 did the re-measurement and follow-up filing but was forbidden by its prompt from closing the parent; this close carries the verification, the integration work that phase could not do, and the disposition of every outstanding proposal.

== 1. VERIFIED ==
All six phases closed done. Read every child note and confirmed each against the source at HEAD 67d846327, not against the reports:
- k3.1 telemetry: _startup_telemetry.py records one tui_startup.jsonl row per session (agents_ready/axe_ready/visible_ready/all_surfaces_ready + tier/artifact_source/record_count); env-overridable loader-stage threshold; docs/perf_runbook.md capture recipe. Present and wired into startup.py.
- k3.2 imports: toast_log.py has no module-scope sase.axe import; patch/_loading.py uses the sys.modules-guarded _is_mock() (validation.py:58-66) with no module-level unittest.mock. tests/ace/tui/test_lazy_imports.py guards both.
- k3.3 badges: _loading_diff_badges.py implements the deferred coalesced pass; both loader call sites pass classify_diff_badges=False (_agent_loader_normalization.py:86,118 and _loading_compute_merge.py:186); carry_over_diff_badges is wired into _loading_apply.py:399.
- k3.4 repair: freshness threaded end to end (_loading_state.py -> agent_loader.py -> _agent_loader_artifacts.py -> wire) defaulting to 'cached', with the deferred post-paint revalidating reconcile in _loading_refresh_polling.py. Rust side confirmed in the linked sase-core checkout (AgentArtifactIndexQueryWire.freshness, index.rs:83/442).
- k3.5 axe: count_hook_and_agent_runners_global() loads the archive once via find_all_patches_cached; _startup_visible_surface_ready() gates the stopwatch on the initially visible tab.
The epic's five commits are e4391c373, 59967cc06, 2d92ef6a9, 8f9c5c3ff, 14fcbc21a. I did not re-run the A/B; sase-k3.6's numbers stand as recorded, including the honest finding that the plan's <2s p50 / <2.5s p95 target was MISSED by 1.28s / 1.08s while the epic still bought p50 -28% and p95 -43%.

== 2. INTEGRATED ==
Reviewed all 14 non-epic commits landed since the epic's first commit (e4391c373, 12:15) through HEAD. Only two files overlap the epic's 33: ace/patch/__init__.py and ace/tui/actions/patch/_loading.py, both additive and non-conflicting (duplicate-block exports from d4139e96e; external-mirror glob filters from 6b139a0d4). No post-epic commit added a call to anything the epic optimized, and none introduced competing Patch caching. The mtime+size-keyed PatchSnapshotCache self-invalidates, so the new ProjectSpec writers (32ccc9eb7, 0567ce03b, d4139e96e) cannot serve stale runner counts.

Two integration items were real and are handled:

(a) FIXED IN THIS LANDING. count_all_runners_global() in ace/patch/validation.py was still 'count_hook_runners_global() + count_agent_runners_global()' -- two independent uncached full-archive parses, which is exactly the defect phase k3.5 created count_hook_and_agent_runners_global() to remove, and that helper's own docstring names this caller shape. k3.5 migrated the AXE status collector but left this one. It is not cosmetic: axe/runner_pool.py calls it at 8 sites for per-tick admission control, twice inside an fcntl LOCK_EX critical section (reserve_slot, is_at_limit), so the second parse was pure latency inside a cross-process lock, and the two separate parses could observe different on-disk states (a torn read). Now routed through the shared cached snapshot; arithmetic unchanged. Added tests/test_patch_runner_counters.py pinning one cached load / zero uncached loads, equality with the old expression, and the 2/3 hook/agent split. Existing callers patch at the import site (sase.axe.runner_pool.count_all_runners_global), so no test churn.

(b) ALREADY FIXED UPSTREAM, corroborated. Phase k3.4 depends on a core API first published in sase-core-rs 0.26.5 (61cc793, shipped by release commit d2a418d which bumps Cargo.toml 0.26.4->0.26.5 despite its 'release v0.26.4' subject), but commit 688eec2bd had pinned the floor to '>=0.26.4,<0.27.0' 21 minutes before k3.4 landed. Because AgentArtifactIndexQueryWire.freshness is #[serde(default)] with no deny_unknown_fields, 0.26.4 would silently drop it and revalidate on every startup -- no error, just the silent loss of the epic's largest win. origin/master b4c6038e6 has since raised the floor to >=0.26.5, which covers this wire too. Recorded as an independent +1 on task sase-km (the missing floor-gate), with the specific finding that sase-km's proposed round-trip-assertion remedy would NOT catch this instance and that grepping *_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION misses it because this wire never bumped a schema version. NOTE: this workspace is 2 commits behind origin/master (abc8a9ea8, b4c6038e6); the floor fix is upstream, not here.
Checked and found NOT to be a defect: pyproject's floor lagging the sase-core checkout is the designed dev state -- tools/validate_sase_core_rs_version's own remediation text and the Justfile both say tools/ratchet_core_window owns the published window at release time.

== 3. FOLLOW-UP DISPOSITION ==
Every PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP across all six children, plus k3.6's six named ones:
- k3.1 #1 (stale symvision --epic-symbol sase-js whitelist breaking just lint): ALREADY RESOLVED. Was filed as task sase-kc (closed) and fixed by commit c30bcb012. Confirmed zero --epic-symbol entries remain in the Justfile, and no sase-k3 whitelist was ever added.
- k3.1 #2 and k3.5 #1 (test_multi_prompt_launcher_xprompt_groups.py::test_launcher_qualifies_research_swarm_per_dispatch, order-dependent full-lane flake): recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on in-progress epic sase-j7, whose scope is precisely this class (process-global state leaking between tests) and whose phase sase-j7.5 owns the flake baseline. Deliberately NOT filed against sase-ct: its close reason retires it as an umbrella and forbids +1, directing narrow records elsewhere. Honest status recorded there: four observations 2026-08-08 (closed sase-hj called it a tracked flake) through 2026-08-12, but no live reproduction in either of the two most recent full lanes (k3.6's check-full, or my escalated check) -- intermittent, not deterministic.
- k3.6 #1 (the unattributed agents-loader 'disk' stage): FILED as task sase-kn (large, ready) via /sase_new_task. No semantic duplicate; sase-kf is import-only (process_start->on_mount) and k3.6 explicitly flagged the overlap question, so the two were kept disjoint. Cross-noted RELATED to sase-kf, sase-kj, sase-kh, sase-ki. This is the single largest remaining startup cost at p50 2.250s of a 3.284s visible_ready.
- k3.6's named follow-ups 1-5: already filed ready as sase-kf, sase-kg, sase-kh, sase-ki, sase-kj. Verified present.
- k3.6's named follow-up 6 (plans-sidecar AA merge conflict / sase repo open plans failure): DECLINED, per the plan's own 'file only if it reproduces on a clean workspace' condition. Independently re-checked in this workspace today: git -C sase/repos/plans diff --diff-filter=U is empty and sase repo open plans succeeded. Prior-agent local state, not a defect.

== 4. VERIFICATION ==
just install, then just check on the landing tree: all 15 gates green (fmt python+markdown, keep-sorted, ruff, mypy, pyscripts, test waits, changelog, patch/stitch terminology, symvision, toobig, SASE validation, committed plans, test scoped). The scoped lane escalated to the full suite (rule: core-identity-changed) and passed. No flake-baseline failures in this run.

CARRIED FORWARD: the working tree holds the item (a) change (src/sase/ace/patch/validation.py + tests/test_patch_runner_counters.py) uncommitted for the commit finalizer.

notes.author: sase-k3.6
notes.text:
Landed epic sase-k3. Re-measured the full budget in a real terminal (tmux, workspace .venv, live ~/.sase state) against the phase `telemetry` baseline, filed the named follow-ups, and did NOT close the parent epic (my launch prompt forbids it; the re-measured budget and corrections below are what an epic close should carry).

== METHOD ==
A/B between commit 59967cc06 (phase `telemetry` baseline: startup telemetry + the `imports` fix landed, `badges`/`repair`/`axe` not yet) and master 1f388edee, both run from the same workspace .venv against the same live ~/.sase state and the same locally-built sase_core_rs 0.26.5. Per run: one detached tmux window running `python -m sase ace`, per-run SASE_TUI_STARTUP_PATH / SASE_TUI_AGENT_LOADS_PATH / SASE_TUI_TRACE_PATH, SASE_TUI_LOADER_LOG_THRESHOLD_SECONDS=0.01, quit with `q` once the telemetry record landed. n=8 before, n=9 after; blocks interleaved (after, before, after) to bound load drift. 33 agent rows, 532 index rows, initial_tab=agents on every run.

HOST CAVEAT: athena was at loadavg ~30 on 64 cores throughout, with several sibling-epic agents running. Per the plan's own convention, absolute numbers are inflated (it estimated 15-40%); the A/B deltas are the portable result. Loadavg drifted only 35.0 -> 34.1 (15-min) across the whole capture, and the after-block was captured both before and after the before-block, so drift does not explain the deltas.
CORE CAVEAT: sase-core's `record_json`-removal from refresh_stale_rows is present in BOTH arms (it is unconditional), so the baseline arm is slightly faster than a true pre-epic tree. That biases against the epic, not for it.

== THE BUDGET, BEFORE AND AFTER (seconds, warm) ==

  (import; unchanged, as expected)

visible_ready and all_surfaces_ready are identical in every run because initial_tab is `agents` and Agents is the slower surface — exactly what phase `axe` predicted when it moved the stopwatch to the visible surface.

== TARGET: MISSED, AND BY HOW MUCH ==
The plan's target was warm Agents-tab time-to-interactive under 2 s with p95 under 2.5 s on athena. Measured: p50 3.284 s, p95 3.575 s. That misses by 1.28 s at p50 and 1.08 s at p95. Applying the plan's own 15-40% busy-host inflation allowance deflates p50 to roughly 2.0-2.8 s — at or above the target, still not under it. A projection that does not survive measurement is a finding: the epic bought a real ~1.3 s at p50 and ~2.8 s at p95, and did not reach the stated number.

Separately, the plan's phase-`repair` check "warm cached selection plus decode stays under 250 ms" measured 0.280-0.295 s warm — marginally over, on a busy host.

== WHAT EACH PHASE ACTUALLY BOUGHT ==
`telemetry` (sase-k3.1): the instrument this entire report is built on. Without tui_startup.jsonl there would be no before/after here at all, only component sums. Recording visible_ready from day one is what let phase `axe` move the stopwatch without invalidating the baseline. Highest-leverage phase in the epic.

`imports` (sase-k3.2): small and real. `python -X importtime -c "import sase.ace.tui.app"`, best of 3: pre-epic 875f67b74 = 2383 modules / 1.325 s self-time; master = 2375 modules / 1.300 s. Net -8 modules; the self-time delta is inside run-to-run noise, and process_start->on_mount is unchanged at p50 0.66-0.67 s. Both defects are gone at HEAD (verified: importing sase.logs.toast_log pulls no sase.axe module; importing sase.ace.tui.actions.patch._loading does not import unittest.mock), and tests/ace/tui/test_lazy_imports.py guards them.

`repair` (sase-k3.4): by far the largest win, and the plan UNDER-projected it by ~4-5x. Direct component A/B on today's live index (6,775 rows, 4,706 hidden, 103 MB), same process, same host: Tier-1 loader query with freshness="revalidate" = 1.861 s; with freshness="cached" = 0.464 s first call, 0.280/0.295 s warm. That is ~1.5-1.6 s removed from the loader, against a projected 0.26-0.39 s. It also accounts for essentially the whole measured visible_ready delta.

`badges` (sase-k3.3): removed from the critical path as designed; its cost is now a deferred, visible-rows-only background pass. Measured across the 9 master sessions (span agents.diff_badge_classification, source=apply): 11-12 candidates, 417 ms min / 643 ms p50 / 1035 ms max. Reported separately, per the plan: that ~0.6 s is new user-visible badge-settle latency, paid once per session (carry-over keeps refreshes from re-paying it), not a saving. I could not isolate the loader-side badge saving from the repair saving in this A/B because both phases are in the same "after" arm.

`axe` (sase-k3.5): structurally correct, magnitude does NOT reproduce — see corrections.

== CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD ==
1. Badge cost is ~0.4 s, not the ~0.8 s the adjudicating research pass asserted. This is the plan's own re-measurement and I did not re-derive it independently; nothing in this phase contradicts it.

2. AXE's cost is a double ProjectSpec parse, not log tails / chop history / run snapshots. The ATTRIBUTION is confirmed and the summary/detail split the research prescribed was correctly not built. The MAGNITUDE does not reproduce on today's state, and this is a new correction: the plan measured find_all_patches() at 0.222 s warm and the double parse at ~0.41 s of a 0.543 s collect. Today the whole ProjectSpec archive is 339 patches in 16 .sase files totalling 1.1 MB and parses in 0.027 s. Measured at master vs the baseline commit, same host, same state:
     get_axe_status() warm:          0.075-0.087 s -> 0.022-0.026 s   (-0.053 s)
     collect_axe_status_data() warm: 0.136-0.178 s -> 0.075-0.088 s   (-0.07 s)
     count_hook_runners_global() (still uncached, by design): 0.027 s
     count_hook_and_agent_runners_global() (shared cached): 0.002 s
   So the real win is ~0.05-0.07 s per collect, about 1/6 of the projection — consistent with the 0.16 s axe_ready p50 delta. It is still worth having: it is paid on every 10 s refresh tick, not just startup, and it removes a cost that grows with archive size. Do not re-derive the 0.4 s figure from the plan; the archive it was measured against is not the archive that exists now.

3. New: the plan's budget model does not account for what is left. See the PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note on this bead — the `disk` stage is still p50 2.250 s, of which the Tier-1 cached query is only ~0.3 s.

== PRODUCTION LOADER LOG: NO CONCLUSION AVAILABLE ==
~/.sase/logs/tui_agent_loads.jsonl (+.1), 8,173 records. Pre-epic (<16:15Z) `disk` p50: startup 2.663 s (n=462), auto_refresh 2.628 s (n=6,393) — reproduces the plan's recorded 2.663 / 2.637 exactly. Post-epic there are only 3 startup and 20 auto_refresh records, and the log is censored at >=2.0 s so these are percentiles of already-slow loads. Not enough data to claim anything; re-check after a few days of normal use. (My capture runs redirected this log per-run, so they are not in the production file.)
