title: Reduce the sase.ace import graph: 780 modules and ~0.42s of self-time for one 'import sase.ace.tui.app'
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: epic sase-k3 already took the ACE first-paint win these follow-ups refine.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k3.6 (land phase of epic sase-k3, ACE startup critical path); named as follow-up 1 in plans:202608/ace_startup_critical_path.md.

After epic sase-k3 removed persisted diff-badge classification, hidden-row repair, and a double ProjectSpec parse from ACE first paint, Python import is the largest single remaining fixed cost in startup and the one this epic explicitly did not attack.

Measured on athena in workspace sase_11 at master 1f388edee, best of 3 'python -X importtime -c "import sase.ace.tui.app"' runs (host at loadavg ~30/64 cores, so absolute times are inflated):

  modules imported: 2375
  sum of self-times: 1.300 s
  sase.* share: 1661 modules / 0.991 s
  sase.ace.* share: 780 modules / 0.415 s

The same measurement on the pre-epic tree (875f67b74) was 2383 modules / 1.325 s, so phase sase-k3.2's two import-defect fixes removed 8 net modules and a self-time delta inside run-to-run noise. Real-terminal startup telemetry puts process-start-to-on_mount at p50 0.669 s across 9 master sessions, essentially unchanged by the epic.

There is no single slow import: 1,661 sase modules average ~0.6 ms each. The remediation is structural (lazy/deferred imports at the ACE package boundary, splitting eagerly-imported subpackages, or a lazy module proxy), which is why the plan sizes this as an epic with its own design phase rather than a task worker.

Scope requirements from the proposing plan:
- Treat 'python -X importtime' module counts and self-times before/after as the acceptance evidence; do not accept intuition or projections.
- Pair it with a real-terminal capture of process_start_to_on_mount_seconds from ~/.sase/logs/tui_startup.jsonl (see docs/perf_runbook.md, 'Startup telemetry capture') so the import win is confirmed end to end and not just in a synthetic import.
- Keep the subprocess import-graph guard tests added by sase-k3.2 (tests/ace/tui/test_lazy_imports.py) as the pattern for locking in each removal.

The right next step is /sase_plan, not a direct implementation.

title: Route all artifact marker writes through an atomic-replace helper, then add the directory-mtime gate to index revalidation
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: epic sase-k3 already took the ACE first-paint win these follow-ups refine.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k3.6 (land phase of epic sase-k3, ACE startup critical path); named as follow-up 2 in plans:202608/ace_startup_critical_path.md.

Epic sase-k3 phase sase-k3.4 gave ACE's Tier-1 artifact-index query a 'cached' freshness policy so startup and auto-refresh skip hidden-row repair and per-row marker revalidation, and left one coalesced revalidating reconcile running after first paint on a long cadence. That reconcile still recomputes MarkerSignatures for every row: ~13 syscalls per artifact directory (8 marker stats, one read_dir, plus a stat per prompt_step_*.json).

Research report __b proposed gating each row on a single directory mtime, turning that into 1 syscall per row. The sase-k3 plan measured that gate to be UNSOUND at HEAD and deliberately did not land it: an in-place open(path, "w") rewrite of an existing marker does not move the parent directory's mtime, and SASE has such writers.

Confirmed at master 1f388edee:
- src/sase/axe/runner_artifacts.py:276 — write_done_marker writes done.json through a plain open(done_path, "w").
- src/sase/axe/run_agent_helpers_artifacts.py — read-modify-write helpers update agent_meta.json in place.
- Atomic helpers already exist to model on, e.g. src/sase/axe/agent_meta.py:16 write_agent_meta_atomic.

The plan re-counted against the live tree: 1,535 of 6,740 artifact directories (22.8%) already hold a marker newer than their own directory — 1,501 agent_meta.json, 51 done.json, 31 prompt_step_*.json, 30 workflow_state.json, 1 waiting.json. So the gate would silently skip revalidating nearly a quarter of the tree today.

Scope:
1. Route every artifact marker write (done.json, agent_meta.json, workflow_state.json, waiting.json, prompt_step_*.json) through an atomic write-temp-then-os.replace helper, so a marker mutation always moves its parent directory's mtime.
2. Only then add the directory-mtime gate to the revalidating path in sase-core (crates/sase_core, agent_scan/index.rs refresh_stale_rows / select_records), turning the background reconcile from ~4,700 x ~13 syscalls into ~4,700 x 1.

MANDATORY test, called out explicitly by the proposing plan: rewriting an existing marker in place must still trigger repair. That is the assertion that would have caught the unsoundness, and it must ship with the gate.

Work in sase-core through /sase_repo (sase repo open sase-core) and read that repo's AGENTS.md first: release-plz owns versions, do not hand-edit Cargo.toml versions or the sase-core-rs pin in pyproject.toml, and verify with sase-core's own 'just check'.

title: Prune or archive hidden agent-artifact index rows: 4,706 of 6,775 rows are hidden and nothing ever removes them
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k3.6 (land phase of epic sase-k3, ACE startup critical path); named as follow-up 3 in plans:202608/ace_startup_critical_path.md.

The agent-artifact index's 'hidden' flag is set on dismissal and hidden rows are never pruned short of a full rebuild. Re-counted on athena at master 1f388edee against the live ~/.sase state:

  sqlite3 ~/.sase/agent_artifact_index.sqlite
  agent_artifacts: total=6775  hidden=4706  (69.5% hidden)
  file size: 103.0 MB

The plan measured hidden rows accumulating at roughly 46/day, which is the mechanism by which ACE startup was getting worse every week.

Epic sase-k3 phase sase-k3.4 removed the read-path cost: ACE's Tier-1 startup and auto-refresh queries now use freshness='cached', which skips repair_stale_rows_for_query and per-row marker revalidation entirely, so hidden-row count no longer drives the syscall count on the startup query. That fixed the slope on the hot path but not the underlying growth.

Hidden rows still cost:
- the coalesced revalidating reconcile that sase-k3.4 left running after first paint (it stat-walks every row's artifact directory);
- the index's 103 MB on-disk footprint and its page-cache pressure;
- every remaining revalidating caller (bead pages, family attach candidates, agents/cli_index.py, agents_sync, sdd).

Scope: decide and implement a retention policy for hidden rows — prune outright, move to a cold/archive table, or age them out — including what still needs to resolve a dismissed agent by artifact dir, whether an existing rebuild path can serve as the recovery mechanism, and how the policy runs (lifecycle hook, maintenance chop, or an explicit command).

The index schema and query live in sase-core (crates/sase_core/src/agent_scan/index.rs); work there through /sase_repo (sase repo open sase-core) and read that repo's AGENTS.md first. Do not hand-edit the sase-core-rs pin in pyproject.toml.

That removed ~0.40 s from first paint but did not remove the work — it relocated it, and it is still redone once per process.

Measured on athena at master 1f388edee across 9 real-terminal sessions (~/.sase/perf/tui_trace.jsonl, span agents.diff_badge_classification, source=apply):

  candidates: 11-12 visible rows per session
  duration: min 417 ms, p50 643 ms, max 1035 ms

That is the new user-visible badge-settle latency the deferral introduced, paid once per ACE session. Persisted diffs are immutable, so this is parsed once per process today when it could be parsed once per machine.

Scope: store the diff-badge signature (the identity the classification is valid for) and its result on the artifact row in the Rust core, so ACE reads a stored badge instead of re-reading diff bytes. The proposing plan is explicit that this belongs in the core rather than as a third frontend-side cache — sase already has DiffBadgeResultCache (in-process, sase-k3.3) and diff_has_real_edits' (path, mtime_ns, size) cache in src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_diff_badge.py.

Input to the schema design, per the plan: phase sase-k3.3 was asked to confirm or refute the research's suspicion that the byte volume concentrates in the linked-commit branch (_classify_linked_commit_diffs -> agent_commit_diffs). Its close note reports the linked-commit branch is NOT where the volume concentrates, but qualifies that dedup through the shared DiffBadgeResultCache collapses it before scheduling either way. Treat that as a partial answer: re-measure the per-branch byte volume directly before choosing what to key the stored signature on, rather than inheriting either the research's claim or sase-k3.3's qualification.

Work in sase-core through /sase_repo (sase repo open sase-core) and read that repo's AGENTS.md first. Do not hand-edit the sase-core-rs pin in pyproject.toml.

title: Measure ACE startup cold-cache: every sase-k3 and research figure is warm-only, so the badges/repair ranking could shift
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: epic sase-k3 already took the ACE first-paint win these follow-ups refine.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k3.6 (land phase of epic sase-k3, ACE startup critical path); named as follow-up 5 in plans:202608/ace_startup_critical_path.md.

Every measurement in epic sase-k3's plan, in all three research passes behind it, and in this land phase's own re-measurement is WARM: the page cache is populated by prior runs, and dropping it needs root (echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches).

This matters because both fixed phases target cold-sensitive work:
- phase sase-k3.3 (badges) removed ~19.8 MB of persisted-diff reads across 492 unique paths from the loader;
- phase sase-k3.4 (repair) removed a stat-walk of 4,706 hidden artifact directories (~8 marker stats, one read_dir, and a stat per prompt_step_*.json each) from the Tier-1 query.

Cold, the repair pass's syscall volume and the badge pass's byte volume scale very differently, so their relative ranking — and therefore the ranking of the remaining follow-ups sase-kg (mtime gate), sase-kh (prune hidden rows), and sase-ki (persist badge results) — could invert.

Scope, which is a measurement task, not a fix:
1. Establish a repeatable cold-cache procedure on athena (root drop_caches between runs, or a documented per-file posix_fadvise DONTNEED alternative if root is unacceptable).
2. Capture cold and warm ACE startup pairs using the existing recipe in docs/perf_runbook.md ('Startup telemetry capture'), reading visible_ready_seconds / all_surfaces_ready_seconds / agents_ready_seconds / axe_ready_seconds from ~/.sase/logs/tui_startup.jsonl, plus the disk loader stage via SASE_TUI_LOADER_LOG_THRESHOLD_SECONDS.
3. Report the cold budget as a table against the warm land-phase numbers recorded on bead sase-k3.6, and state whether the ranking of the outstanding follow-ups changes.
4. Add the cold procedure to docs/perf_runbook.md so later phases can reuse it.

Sized medium because the method is fully specified and bounded; the open question is the result, not the approach.

title: External issue mirror never fires a close transition for an issue that was already closed when first mirrored
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: external-mirror fidelity gaps are self-correcting on the daily full scan and have no reported user impact.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k2.4 (epic sase-k2) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note on 2026-08-12T17:44:55Z, verified in the tree by sase-k2.land at HEAD 67d846327.

MECHANISM (confirmed in source): src/sase/external_mirror/issues.py:326-328 seeds durable state for every ref covered after a pass that has no recorded upstream state — 'for ref, issue in current_refs.items(): if ref in covered_after and ref not in upstream_states: upstream_states[ref] = issue.state'. A bead created this pass is in covered_after (line 323 unions outcome.created_refs), so an upstream issue that was ALREADY closed when the mirror first saw it has 'closed' recorded as its seen state on the very pass that created the bead. _plan_transitions (issues.py:526) compares the new upstream state against that recorded previous_state, so it sees no transition — not on that pass, and never on any later pass.

IMPACT: the mirror creates every bead 'open' (deliberately, so no TaskTriage gate fires on a first-pass backlog). For an issue that closed upstream before SASE ever saw it, that open bead is permanently wrong: sase-k2.4's close/reopen sync cannot correct it because there is no transition to observe. The larger the tracker's closed backlog on first mirror, the more permanently-open beads. Beads whose issue closes AFTER the first sighting are unaffected and close correctly.

SCOPE: this is a creation/filter policy decision, not a bug_status one, which is why sase-k2.4 scoped it out rather than fixing it. The plausible options are mutually exclusive and want a deliberate choice: (a) do not create a bead at all for an issue already closed at first sight — closest to external_mirror.issues.filters.states, which can already express 'states: [open]' but is empty by default; (b) create the bead and immediately close it with the same attributed note the transition path writes; (c) create it open and leave upstream_states[ref] unseeded so the next pass observes a synthetic open->closed transition. Option (a) interacts with the epic's stated superset promise (the bead list is a strict superset of the issue list), so decide that explicitly.

RELEVANT FILES: src/sase/external_mirror/issues.py (_apply seeding at 323-331, _plan_transitions at 512-560), src/sase/default_config.yml external_mirror.issues.filters.states, docs/axe.md external_mirror lane section.

title: PR mirror's incremental fetch_limit=200 over created-descending order hides the oldest PRs from every pass but the daily full scan
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: external-mirror fidelity gaps are self-correcting on the daily full scan and have no reported user impact.
description:
Deferred deliberately by epic sase-k2's plan (plans:202608/external_mirror_refinement.md, phase 'perf'): 'Do not widen the incremental fetch in this phase. fetch_limit=200 against gh pr list's created-descending order can miss an old PR that was just updated; that is a real gap, but it is a provider-ordering question that deserves its own task bead rather than a change smuggled into a performance phase.' Filed by sase-k2.land at close, as that plan directed.

MECHANISM (confirmed in source and in live run records): src/sase/external_mirror/pr_sync.py:78 defaults fetch_limit=200 and line 103 sets 'limit = 0 if full else fetch_limit', so only the daily DAILY_REPAIR_SCAN full pass lists the tracker unbounded. The provider seam exposes a record limit, not a page cursor, and gh pr list returns created-descending, so an incremental pass sees the 200 most recently CREATED PRs regardless of which PRs were most recently UPDATED.

LIVE EVIDENCE: gh_sase-org__sase has 296 PRs. Every external_pr_mirror[sase] run record under ~/.sase/axe/lumberjacks/external_mirror/chops/ on 2026-08-12 (14:10, 14:16, 14:31, 14:46) reports 'fetched': 200 with 'seen': 168 — the limit is saturated on every incremental pass, so roughly 96 of the oldest PRs are structurally invisible to the 15-minute cadence.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW: before epic sase-k2 an unseen old PR only delayed adoption. sase-k2.5 added the refresh action, so an already-adopted external Patch only follows its PR from open to merged/closed on a pass that actually fetches that PR. An old PR that merges today is therefore reconciled by the daily full scan rather than within one 15-minute tick — a bounded but real up-to-24h staleness window on Patch status and on the active-to-archive move, and the window scales with how far down the created-descending list the PR sits.

SCOPE: a provider-ordering question. Options worth weighing rather than assuming: teach the PR-listing seam to sort by updated-at (gh pr list --search 'sort:updated-desc' or equivalent) so the incremental window tracks the cursor's own dimension; expose real pagination on the seam; or raise/derive fetch_limit from the project's PR count. Whichever is chosen must keep the pass inside the external_mirror lane's 5-minute chop timeout and the existing per-pass create budget.

RELEVANT FILES: src/sase/external_mirror/pr_sync.py (fetch_limit, _candidate_in_window, OVERLAP_WINDOW, DAILY_REPAIR_SCAN), the vcs provider PR-listing seam, docs/axe.md 'Builtin external_pr_mirror'.

title: Core-floor gates check binding names but not wire schema versions, so a schema bump can ship with a floor that rejects it at runtime
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: one preventive gate and one unreproduced transient, closed in favor of live defects.
description:
Discovered by sase-k2.land while landing epic sase-k2 on 2026-08-12 (workspace sase_13, HEAD 67d846327). The immediate breakage was fixed as part of that landing; this bead is for the missing gate that let it through.

WHAT HAPPENED: phase sase-k2.5 bumped src/sase/core/external_pr_wire.py's EXTERNAL_PR_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION from 1 to 2 and landed the matching Rust classifier in sase-core (fb3c869), first published as sase-core-rs 0.26.5. Two minutes later, an unrelated epic's commit 688eec2bd ratcheted pyproject.toml to 'sase-core-rs>=0.26.4,<0.27.0' with uv.lock resolved to exactly 0.26.4. sase-core 0.26.4 ships EXTERNAL_PR_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1 (crates/sase_core/src/external_pr/wire.rs) and classify.rs:36 rejects any other value. Any environment resolving from the lockfile rather than building against a linked sase-core checkout would therefore have failed every external_pr_mirror pass with a schema-mismatch error — src/sase/core/rust.py is deliberately strict and has no Python fallback. sase-k2.land raised the floor to >=0.26.5 and refreshed the lock.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: tools/probe_core_floor diagnoses staleness from the collected core BINDING-NAME set (_collect_binding_names, tools/check_sase_core_rs_bindings). plan_external_pr_import exists in 0.26.4, so name presence passes. tools/validate_sase_core_rs_version only compares version numbers against the pyproject specifier. Neither gate knows that a shared wire-schema constant has a required minimum, so a floor can satisfy both while being semantically too old.

SCOPE: give the floor gates a notion of required wire-schema version. Options: have the probe read Python's *_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION constants and compare them against the same constants in the floor version's published wheel; or add a cheap runtime assertion/test that round-trips each wire schema through the installed binding so a too-old floor fails a gate rather than a chop. Worth covering every wire schema, not just external-PR: grep '_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION' under src/sase/core/.

SECOND, SEPARATE OBSERVATION (reproduced, recorded here rather than filed twice): 'python3 tools/probe_core_floor --advisory' under this machine's default python3 (3.11.13 via pyenv) exits with status could_not_determine — 'could not collect core binding names: type _HostedResolverFactory = Callable[ ... SyntaxError: invalid syntax' — because it parses PEP 695 'type X = ...' aliases with a pre-3.12 interpreter. Under .venv/bin/python it runs clean. So the probe is blind rather than wrong when invoked with the wrong interpreter. sase-jj's close reason called out this exact symptom and explicitly invited filing it separately.

RELEVANT FILES: tools/probe_core_floor, tools/validate_sase_core_rs_version, tools/check_sase_core_rs_bindings, tools/ratchet_core_window, src/sase/core/external_pr_wire.py, src/sase/core/rust.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock.

plus_one_evidence.note:
Independent second instance from epic sase-k3, found by sase-k3.land, with a WORSE failure mode than the external-PR case: silent degradation instead of a loud schema-mismatch error.

Phase sase-k3.4 (commit 8f9c5c3ff, 13:52) added 'freshness' to the agent-scan artifact-index query wire (src/sase/core/agent_scan_wire_records.py, sent at src/sase/core/agent_scan_wire_conversion.py). The Rust side landed in sase-core 61cc793 and first shipped in sase-core-rs 0.26.5 (release commit d2a418d bumps Cargo.toml 0.26.4 -> 0.26.5, despite its 'release v0.26.4' subject). Exactly like the external-PR case, commit 688eec2bd had already pinned the floor to '>=0.26.4,<0.27.0' with uv.lock at 0.26.4, 21 minutes before sase-k3.4 landed -- so the same window was open for this wire too.

THE DIFFERENCE THAT MATTERS FOR YOUR SCOPE: AgentArtifactIndexQueryWire.freshness is declared '#[serde(default)]' with Default = Revalidate (crates/sase_core/src/agent_scan/index.rs:83), and the struct has no deny_unknown_fields. On 0.26.4 the field simply does not exist, so serde drops it silently and every ACE startup query falls back to full revalidation. No error, no chop failure, no test failure -- just the silent loss of the largest single win in epic sase-k3 (Tier-1 loader query 1.861s revalidate vs 0.280-0.464s cached, measured on athena at 1f388edee).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMEDIATION: the 'cheap runtime assertion that round-trips each wire schema through the installed binding' option in this bead's scope would NOT catch this instance -- a round-trip succeeds on 0.26.4 because the unknown field is silently dropped and the response still deserializes. Catching serde-default field additions needs field-presence checking against the floor version's published wheel (the first option in your scope), or a behavioral assertion that the cached mode actually skips revalidation. Worth widening the scope note beyond '*_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION' constants: this wire never bumped a schema version at all, so grepping for that constant would have missed it entirely.

ALREADY REMEDIATED, NOT STILL BROKEN: origin/master commit b4c6038e6 raised the floor to '>=0.26.5,<0.27.0', which covers this wire as well as the external-PR one. Recording it here because it doubles the evidence for the missing gate and narrows which fix would actually work.

Independently reproduced the inverse direction of this gap while landing epic sase-ku (workspace sase_19, master d9c685e86, 2026-08-13). The linked sase-core checkout is at 0.27.0 while pyproject pins 'sase-core-rs>=0.26.10,<0.27.0'; 'just install' builds the editable binding from the checkout regardless, and 'just validate' explicitly prints 'No action is needed' for that state. But the checkout's task wire bumped TASK schema 1 -> 2, so 63 tests fail in a full 'just test' lane with 'sase task run: could not record task: task wire schema mismatch: got 2, expected 1' (13 tests/test_tasks_runner.py, 13 tests/main/test_task_handler_run.py, 11 test_task_handler_list.py, 7 test_task_handler_show.py, 6 tests/ace/tui/test_task_mirror.py, 5 test_tasks_store_rows.py, 3 test_task_handler_kill.py). Same missing gate: probe_core_floor checks binding NAMES and validate_sase_core_rs_version checks only the version specifier, so neither notices that an installed binding's wire schema disagrees with the Python constant. The proposed fix in this bead's SCOPE (round-trip each wire schema through the installed binding so a mismatch fails a gate) would catch this direction too -- worth stating that the gate must fail on ANY mismatch, not just a too-old floor.

Observed another live instance during monitor_starter_row_misclassified landing verification on 2026-08-13: monitor 8prhacgenaen ran 'just check-full' at sase HEAD 10e33da42 and failed six notification mark_tab_read tests because Python sends NotificationStateUpdateWire(kind='mark_tab_read', tab_key=...) while the installed editable sase-core-rs 0.26.11 rejects it as an unknown variant. The Python tree introduced mark_tab_read in commit aea9bf645 but pyproject still allows >=0.26.10,<0.27.0, and the linked sase-core checkout has no mark_tab_read variant even at release v0.27.0. Focused reproduction: .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_core_facade/test_notification_store.py::test_real_extension_mark_tab_read_scopes_to_one_tab tests/notification_store/test_state_updates.py::TestMarkTabRead -> 6 failed with 'unknown variant mark_tab_read'. This is the same missing wire-schema/variant floor gate: binding names are present, but the accepted state-update vocabulary is stale relative to Python.

title: ACE agents loader 'disk' stage is p50 2.250s of a 3.284s visible_ready and no startup budget model attributes it
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: epic sase-k3 already took the ACE first-paint win these follow-ups refine.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k3.6 (land phase of epic sase-k3, ACE startup critical path) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP, and filed by sase-k3.land. Deliberately NOT one of the six follow-ups named in plans:202608/ace_startup_critical_path.md -- it is what the epic's re-measurement discovered was left over, which is why sase-k3.6 recorded it on its own bead instead of filing it.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. Epic sase-k3 removed persisted diff-badge classification, hidden-row repair, and a double ProjectSpec parse from ACE first paint. Real-terminal A/B (n=8 at baseline 59967cc06 vs n=9 at master 1f388edee, athena at loadavg ~30/64 cores, 33 agent rows / 532 index rows, initial_tab=agents) moved visible_ready p50 4.573s -> 3.284s and p95 6.327s -> 3.575s. The plan's target was p50 <2s / p95 <2.5s, so it missed by 1.28s / 1.08s even after deflating for host load.

THE GAP. After the epic, the agents loader's 'disk' stage is p50 2.250s of that 3.284s visible_ready -- the single largest remaining cost, and the epic's budget model does not account for it. The model attributed badges (~0.40s) and hidden-row repair (~0.26-0.39s) inside that stage, and both are now gone. Component measurement on athena at 1f388edee: the Tier-1 cached index query is only 0.280-0.464s of the stage, and a full load_agents_from_disk_with_state() call warms to 0.81-0.94s on repeat in the same process. That leaves roughly 1.3-1.9s of first-call loader work -- candidates named by the reporter are the dismissed-bundle snapshot, the Patch snapshot, and normalization/status overrides -- which neither the plan nor any of the three research passes ever measured.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is the next thing to attack if the <2s visible_ready target still matters; nothing else in the remaining follow-up set is anywhere near 1.3-1.9s.

SCOPE. (1) Attribute the 'disk' stage: instrument the loader's first call so each component (dismissed-bundle snapshot, Patch snapshot, normalization, status overrides, Tier-1 query) reports its own span, rather than projecting from static analysis -- the epic's phase 'repair' was under-projected ~4-5x and phase 'axe' over-projected ~6x, so component estimates are not acceptable evidence here. (2) Attack whatever the attribution actually shows. (3) Accept on a real-terminal before/after of visible_ready_seconds from ~/.sase/logs/tui_startup.jsonl per the recipe in docs/perf_runbook.md ('Startup telemetry capture'), not on component sums.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT INHERITED FROM THE EPIC: every figure above is warm-cache and was captured on a loaded host; see task sase-kj, which owns the cold-cache measurement that could reorder this ranking.

notes.text:

title: sase monitor — long-running commands as first-class agent family members
description: Agents can hand a slow command (`just check-full`, a CI wait, `sase bead work`) to `sase monitor start` and be killed cleanly, while the command keeps running as a live, first-class monitor member of their agent family — with streaming output, live runtime, custom start/stop statuses, a timeout, and an optional follow-up agent that resumes the same workspace and conversation when the command finishes.

notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE: tests/monitor/test_monitor_start.py::test_start_monitor_promotes_a_bare_lane_and_runs_to_completion still fails at master 7e4ac6d7c. Routed here rather than filed as a task because sase-kp.land's own 2026-08-13T11:54:54Z note on epic sase-j7 states this node is 'a separate, understood claim-release race owned by epic sase-kp and is being fixed there', and sase-kp.12's monitor_land_fixes tale lists 'claim-release flake' in its scope. Reported by the land agent for epic sase-kv, where phases sase-kv.3 (13:50:15Z) and sase-kv.5 (14:34:24Z) each recorded it as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP.

STATUS: not yet fixed on master. Reproduced 2026-08-13 from workspace sase_10 on a CLEAN tree at 7e4ac6d7c, which already contains every landed sase-kp and sase-ku commit through 40d9a4d98.

REPRODUCIBILITY -- this is deterministic under load, not intermittent:
  just test          -> 2 failed, 29539 passed, 10 skipped in 298.62s (this node + the unrelated sase-kw import cycle)
  just test-contention tests/monitor/test_monitor_start.py
                     -> 1 node failed across 3 repeats in 84.4s; red repeats 1,2,3 (3/3)
  isolated run       -> 1 passed in 2.18s
It also fails 3/3 when the single node is the only test in the contention pool, so it is load-sensitive timing inside the monitor itself, not cross-test pollution.

EXACT FAILURE (tests/monitor/test_monitor_start.py:95):
  assert get_claimed_workspaces(project_file) == []
  E  AssertionError: Left contains one more item:
     WorkspaceClaim(workspace_num=3, workflow='ace-monitor', cl_name='acme', pid=2148989, artifacts_timestamp='20260813111233', pinned=False)

ROOT CAUSE (read from src/sase/monitor/supervise.py at this HEAD): the supervisor writes the done marker BEFORE it releases the transferred claim.
  supervise.py:350  write_done_marker_and_update_index(artifacts_dir, done_marker)
  supervise.py:386  _release_claim_and_notify(...)          <- runs after, on the no-follow-up path
  supervise.py:377  _release_claim_and_notify(...)          <- same ordering on the failed-follow-up path
The test's _wait_for_done() returns the instant the marker appears, then asserts the claim is gone. Between :350 and :386 the claim is still held, so the window is unconditional -- under load the supervisor simply has not reached :386 yet. The test's own comment ('the transferred claim is released once the command finishes') encodes an ordering the supervisor does not currently guarantee.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, and they are not equivalent -- worth an explicit decision:
  (a) Release the claim before writing the done marker, making the marker mean 'fully torn down'. This makes the done marker a real completion barrier for any other reader too, not just this test.
  (b) Leave the ordering and have the test poll for claim release. Cheaper, but it concedes that a done marker does not imply the claim is released, which any follow-up consumer of the marker would also have to know.
MONITOR_WORKSPACE_CLAIM_WORKFLOW = 'ace-monitor' is defined at src/sase/monitor/start.py:39 with the comment that nothing else matches or can release the transferred claim, which argues for (a).

NOT CAUSED BY EPIC sase-kv: that epic touches only the ACE Artifacts sub-tab strip, artifact ref provider specs, and the sase-core ref.icon wire; it has no monitor, supervisor, or workspace-claim code in its diff.

notes.author: sase-m6.7.1.3--3
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE (2026-08-16, reproduced on master a0b6cd16b): 'sase monitor list' and 'sase monitor show <id>' are both hard-broken host-wide by a single non-monitor artifact record.

  $ sase monitor list
  sase monitor list: cannot read monitors: artifact record at '/home/bryan/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/artifacts/ace-run/202608/15/20260815145837' is not a monitor member

Traceback path: main/monitor_handler.py:_resolve_ref -> monitor/store.py:305 list_monitors -> monitor/models.py:130 MonitorRecord.from_record -> ValueError.

Root cause: two membership predicates disagree, and list_monitors is the one call site that does not tolerate the disagreement.
  - src/sase/monitor/store.py:388-394 _monitor_records() admits any record whose agent_meta.agent_family_role == 'monitor'.
  - src/sase/monitor/models.py:125-131 MonitorRecord.from_record() rejects any record without a truthy meta.monitor_id.
The offending record's agent_meta.json has agent_family_role='monitor', agent_family='02i', name='02i--7', role_suffix='--7', and NO monitor_id key at all. It is a follow-up agent that is a MEMBER of a monitor-role family, not the monitor itself — exactly the is_monitor misclassification shape phase sase-kp.12 already fixed once, recurring on a different field.
  - store.py:145-148 and store.py:173-176 both wrap from_record in 'try: ... except ValueError: continue'. list_monitors at store.py:303-306 uses a bare list comprehension, so one such record aborts the whole listing and every command that resolves a ref through it.

Impact: every agent that follows the mandatory /sase_monitor workflow can start a monitor and receive its completion notification, but cannot run 'sase monitor show <id>' or 'sase monitor show <id> --all-lines' to read the output afterwards. I hit this trying to read a 'just check-full' log and had to read live_reply.md out of the artifact directory by hand. Phase bead sase-m6.7.1.3's own close note records the same class from the other side: 'just check-full was not completed because sase monitor could not attach to this agent.'

Suggested fix: make the two predicates agree — either have _monitor_records() also require a truthy monitor_id, or give list_monitors the same try/except ValueError: continue skip the two lane helpers already use. Prefer the former plus a regression test that puts one agent_family_role='monitor' record with no monitor_id into the scan and asserts list_monitors() still returns the real monitors.

Routed to this epic rather than a new task because sase-kp owns monitor membership/classification and already shipped a fix for the sibling misclassification in sase-kp.12.

notes.author: sase-p4.land
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE (routed here by the sase-p4 land agent, 2026-08-18; originally recorded as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on closed phase bead sase-p4.3 at 2026-08-18T02:24:16Z):

A 'sase monitor' SIGTERM does not take down the whole process group it started. Observed while a sase-p4.3 agent ran 'just check-full' under a monitor: the monitor reported exit -15, but tools/run_silent's test-cost child survived and was reparented to PID 1, with pytest still around 50% complete and continuing to run after the monitor was gone.

WHY IT COMPOUNDS: check-full wraps the test-cost gate in tools/run_silent, which buffers output, so the supervisor sees no bytes for roughly 30 minutes and cannot distinguish a wedged command from a working one. The orphan then keeps burning a full xdist lane on the host, which is itself a source of the parallel-lane contention failures other beads are tracking.

SCOPE: confirm the supervisor kills the process group (setsid/killpg) rather than just the direct child on stop and on timeout, and consider a heartbeat from tools/run_silent so a silent-but-alive command is distinguishable from a hung one.

Recorded on this epic rather than as a task bead: the monitor supervisor's member lifecycle and stop path are this epic's own subject matter (phase sase-kp.3 'Monitor member lifecycle and supervisor process'), so the causal link is direct rather than topical. Not caused by sase-p4.

That is still only a skip-path guard. Importing sase.monitor.claims is not import-light either: sase/monitor/__init__.py eagerly imports .start, so any sase.monitor.* import re-enters the monitor -> shells -> axe -> ACE model chain. The skip path therefore had to identify ace-monitor claims by the workflow label string without touching the package. The remaining fix is still note #9: move MONITOR_WORKSPACE_CLAIM_WORKFLOW to a module outside the sase.monitor package (or stop the package init from importing start) and consume it from leaf helpers such as cleanup_stale_running_entries.

notes.text:

The follow-up (this agent) resumed in a clean workspace whose HEAD was an unrelated TUI stitch and whose working tree did not contain the implementation. title: Approved-epic launch through sase monitor has never been exercised end to end; add a safe smoke harness
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: monitor lane/claim ergonomics with documented workarounds, closed in favor of the cross-agent corruption and gate-blocking defects.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-kp.12 (epic sase-kp, 'End-to-end monitor exercises') as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP, and filed here by sase-kp.land.

WHAT IS MISSING: epic sase-kp phase sase-kp.9 (commit 44796037a) rerouted approved-epic launches through the new monitor machinery: start_epic_launch_monitor() in src/sase/bead/epic_launch.py starts a monitor with the custom statuses EPIC APPROVED -> EPIC CREATED, reports the monitor id back to the approval surfaces, and keeps the old detached-task launch only as a fallback for when the planner lane cannot be resolved. That path has unit coverage, but it is the one monitor entry point in the whole epic that was never exercised against a real launch.

EVIDENCE: sase-kp.12 was the epic's end-to-end smoke phase and successfully drove every other monitor path with real launched agents -- completion plus follow-up handoff, non-zero exit, timeout enforcement and kill, stop with claim release, and list/show in rich, markdown, JSON, output-only, and follow modes. It could not drive this one. Its note records the reason: no EPIC APPROVED / EPIC CREATED monitor appeared anywhere in monitor history, and the phase could not manufacture one because epic phase workers are forbidden from creating beads. Re-confirmed by sase-kp.land on 2026-08-13: 'sase monitor list --all' returns five monitors, none with the epic-launch statuses.

WHY A HARNESS IS THE WORK: the obstacle is that a genuine exercise needs a real approved epic plan, which means writing to the durable bead store and launching real phase agents. The deliverable is therefore a repeatable, safe way to drive start_epic_launch_monitor() end to end without polluting the bead store or spawning real phase work -- for example a throwaway project or bead store plus a trivial single-phase plan, or a launch-approval fixture that stops after the monitor member is created.

SCOPE: (1) build the harness; (2) use it to assert the real observable behavior -- a monitor member is created for the approved epic, its start status is EPIC APPROVED and its stop status is EPIC CREATED, the approval surface receives the monitor id, and the monitor terminates cleanly; (3) exercise the documented fallback, i.e. an approval whose planner lane cannot be resolved still launches through the detached task path; (4) leave no durable beads, artifacts, or workspace claims behind.

RELATED CONTEXT: the four other defects sase-kp.12 found were all caused by the epic and are being fixed as sase-kp epic work before that epic closes; this one is a coverage gap rather than a defect, which is why it is filed separately.

notes.author: sase-kp.land
notes.text: RELATED: sase-kp — the epic that introduced the untested path (phase sase-kp.9 rerouted approved-epic launches through sase monitor start; phase sase-kp.12 proposed this follow-up). Read sase-kp.9's and sase-kp.12's notes before starting.

notes.author: zp
notes.text:
SERIALIZATION ANALYSIS FOR THIS HARNESS (independent review, 2026-08-13): the project owner asked whether approved epics still launch one at a time after sase-kp.9 moved them onto monitors. They do -- but nothing in the monitor layer is what makes that true, so the harness this bead builds should assert it explicitly.

WHAT ACTUALLY SERIALIZES: epic_plan_launch_lock() (src/sase/bead/cli_work_from_plan_store.py:150), an flock anchored on the project's primary workspace (epic_launch_lock_anchor(), same file:141). work_from_plan_file() enters it at src/sase/bead/cli_work_from_plan.py:104-112 and holds it across _work_from_plan_file_locked() (:249) -- archive, bead creation, graph publication, and the wave-1 agent launch -- so per project the entire launch is one critical section. Both the old detached task and the new monitor run the identical 'sase bead work' command with cwd = the primary workspace (start_epic_launch_monitor passes cwd=resolved_cwd, src/sase/bead/epic_launch.py:153-167; the supervisor runs its child in monitor_cwd, src/sase/monitor/supervise.py:128,175), so the anchor is unchanged and the lock still applies. Monitors themselves do NOT serialize: five approvals from five planner lanes start five supervisors immediately, and all five 'sase bead work' children run concurrently until they queue on that flock.

TWO BURST GAPS WORTH COVERING IN SCOPE ITEM (2):
(1) The queue is bounded at DEFAULT_EPIC_PLAN_LAUNCH_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 900 (cli_work_from_plan_store.py:34). Real monitored launches observed at 4-5 minutes ('sase monitor list --all' shows 4m12s and 5m11s members), so the 4th or 5th epic in a rapid burst can exhaust the 900s wait and die with PlanFileWorkError instead of launching. While queued, the monitor sits at EPIC APPROVED with no output; the epic-launch start passes no idle timeout (idle_timeout_seconds defaults to 0.0), so a queued launch is at least not idle-killed.
(2) Two approvals whose planner artifacts resolve to the SAME lane collide instead of queueing. monitor_blocking_start_for_lane() (src/sase/monitor/store.py:106) makes start_monitor raise MonitorAlreadyRunningError, and start_epic_launch_monitor falls back to the detached task only on MonitorLaneError (epic_launch.py:168), so it propagates. It surfaces AFTER the gate response is committed: execute_gate_selection writes response.json and settles the notification (src/sase/notification_gates/executor.py:221-226) before apply_side_effects runs the launch. The plan therefore ends up approved, no longer re-approvable through the gate ('conflict_already_handled'), and never launched -- recoverable only via the 'sase bead work ...' resume string in the error text. The same path fires when the planner's lane holds a 'lost' (pre-reboot) monitor, which blocks starts by design.

SUGGESTED HARNESS ASSERTIONS: drive two approvals concurrently and assert both epics get beads and agents, one at a time and in order; and drive two same-lane approvals and assert the second queues or falls back rather than hard-failing after its response has already been written.

Triage sweep 2026-08-14 (requested by the project owner: keep the seven highest-impact open tasks, close the rest). Each has a workaround or limited blast radius: sase-lj and sase-ll both fail loudly at start and both clear with an explicit --lane, and master has since landed a run of monitor claim/startup hardening (a54aec6ab transactional startup, 90b26289f claim-transfer follow-up preservation, b4542139a supervisor-ack gating, 3bb9bd1d1 stale-running claim release, 29cb7924a dead-supervisor reconcile); sase-kr is a missing smoke harness for a path that already has unit coverage. sase-lf IS still live -- test_start_monitor_promotes_a_bare_lane_and_runs_to_completion is one of the 12 reproducible flakes exceeding the baseline today -- but it is a single node against sase-jq's five and sase-lc's whole-mechanism fix, both of which stay open. Re-file sase-lj/sase-ll with a +1 if either recurs after the hardening, and sase-lf if it blocks a landing on its own.

title: sase monitor hardening — a supervisor that cannot silently orphan, wedge, or lie
description: The monitor supervisor survives every command shape a real build throws at it — continuous output, partial lines, binary bytes, backgrounded grandchildren, TERM-ignoring children — enforces its deadline on every tick, never leaves a live process group behind when it dies, reconciles wedged lanes without a human, and only reports a monitor terminal once the claim, the log, and the follow-up have actually been settled.

notes.author: zg
notes.text:
ADJACENT WORK LANDED (no conflict expected, one overlap deliberately skipped): the approved plan '.sase/artifacts/home/.sase/plans/202608/monitor_wait_resolution.md' fixed a defect this epic does not cover -- a lane that ever started a monitor could never resolve %wait.

Root cause: every terminal monitor writes done.json {"outcome": "monitored"}, and "monitored" was absent from the wait-dependency outcome vocabulary in src/sase/core/dismissed_agent_completion.py. A finished monitor member was therefore neither resolved, done, failed, nor identity-success, so family_candidate() computed is_resolved=False forever and sase_chop_wait_checks never wrote ready.json. Confirmed against the live store: smoke-sleep and smoke-stop now resolve; smoke-fail and smoke-timeout correctly stay blocked because those monitors genuinely failed.

What landed:
- src/sase/core/dismissed_agent_completion.py: MONITOR_OUTCOME, MONITOR_SUCCESS_STATES ({completed, stopped}), FAILURE_OUTCOME, "monitored" added to KNOWN_DONE_OUTCOMES, and a new public effective_done_outcome() that maps a monitored marker through monitor_state (fail-closed to "failed" when monitor_state is missing or unrecognized). It keys off monitor_state, never status_label, because --stop-status is user-configurable.
- src/sase/core/wait_dependency_resolution/_artifact_state.py: done_outcome_from_data() routes through that helper, so ArtifactCandidate.outcome carries the EFFECTIVE outcome. A failed monitor now reads 'outcome=failed' in the chop's 'Terminal dependency still blocks waiter' line instead of tripping the 'Unknown done outcome' alarm.
- src/sase/monitor_state.py: new DEFAULT_MONITOR_STOP_STATUS = 'MONITORED'; src/sase/monitor/start.py DEFAULT_STOP_STATUS now points at it.
- src/sase/monitor/start.py: the supervisor is spawned with stdout=<artifacts>/supervisor.log and stderr=STDOUT instead of DEVNULL (SUPERVISOR_LOG_NAME). start_new_session, stdin=DEVNULL, and close_fds are unchanged.
- Tests: tests/monitor/test_monitor_wait_resolution.py, tests/test_axe_chop_wait_checks_monitor_family.py, plus additions to tests/monitor/test_monitor_start.py and tests/test_dismissed_agent_completion.py.

DELIBERATELY NOT IMPLEMENTED: the plan's step 4 (periodically reap a dead monitor supervisor into monitor_state 'failed'). That is sase-ku.5's 'reconcile' phase, which is IN_PROGRESS and strictly broader (kill the surviving tree, release the claim, dispose the follow-up, run from list/TUI/axe, add the 'lost' state). Implementing it here would have conflicted. See the note on sase-ku.5.

Contract this fix establishes for sase-ku.5 and sase-ku.4: monitor_state 'completed' and 'stopped' resolve a waiter; 'failed', 'timeout', anything unrecognized, and a missing monitor_state block it. A new state such as 'lost' blocks by default with no change needed -- but if any future state should RELEASE a waiter it must be added to MONITOR_SUCCESS_STATES in src/sase/core/dismissed_agent_completion.py.

notes.author: zo
notes.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND FOR A GAP THIS EPIC DOES NOT COVER (new epic plan proposed: monitor_supervisor_survival). On 2026-08-13 12:53:44 agent zl.w0--code ran 'sase monitor start --command "just test-visual" --timeout 20m --next <continuation>'. No monitor ever ran; the lane went silent 17m33s and the --next continuation (the whole remaining artifacts_split_modes.md plan) was discarded.

EVIDENCE (monitor 18tx7ty20h8w, artifacts .../ace-run/202608/13/20260813125344): agent_meta.json has NO monitor_output_path (supervise.py:137, the supervisor's first action after _read_meta) and NO monitor_pgid (supervise.py:192); live_reply.md is exactly 73 bytes -- only sase-ku.5's reconciler line; supervisor.log exists and is 0 bytes. Since the supervisor now runs with stdout=supervisor.log/stderr=STDOUT, a traceback would have been captured (verified live: 'python -m sase monitor _supervise --artifacts-dir <missing>' prints a full traceback and total startup is ~0.83s). So the supervisor was killed by a signal DURING its own ~0.8s startup -- before signal.signal() at supervise.py:133, before reading meta, before spawning the command.

WHAT KILLS IT: maybe_handoff_monitor_from_agent -> kill_agent_runner_group() SIGTERMs the runner group ~0.1s after start_monitor returns, i.e. ~10% into the supervisor's startup. killpg alone does NOT explain it -- start_new_session=True (start.py:214) protects it, and I reproduced the exact topology (runner pgroup / isolated-pgid child / start_new_session grandchild / killpg(runner_pgid, SIGTERM)): the grandchild SURVIVES. What does explain it is a perfect correlation with the starter's runtime, because setsid escapes a killpg but not a PPID walk, and at kill time the supervisor is still a descendant of the runtime's Bash tool:
  codex starters:  smoke-fail--0 (exit 3, ran), z2--code 'just check-full' (ran 30s, exit 1)  -> SURVIVED
  claude starters: sase-kp.land--code 'just check-full', sase-kv.5.w1--code 'just test-visual', zl.w0--code 'just test-visual' -> ALL DIED, 0 output, exit_code null
  host-started (starter_agent null): zl.f1, zm, z6.f2, sase-kp.land.w1 -> all fine
Per the Uniform Agent Runtimes rule the fix is runtime-agnostic (double-fork so the supervisor is reparented to PID 1 before start_monitor returns, plus signal dispositions set in the supervisor's first statements), not a claude special case.

WHY NOTHING NOTICED (four gaps, all outside sase-ku.1-.9): (1) start_monitor returns monitor_state='running' without ever confirming the supervisor is alive, and its caller's next act is to kill itself; (2) handlers installed ~0.8s late; (3) run_stale_running_cleanup (axe/hook_jobs.py:375-399) wraps _reconcile_dead_monitor_supervisors in 'except Exception' and lets cleanup_stale_running_entries release the ace-monitor claim anyway -- workspace #10 was handed to sase-ku.9--plan at 12:54:35, 51s into a 20-minute test run, and workspace prep stashed zl.w0--code's 23-file/756-line implementation into stash@{0} of sase_10 (recoverable, but only by luck of the stash); (4) that harvest then killed the follow-up: launch_followup_agent (followup.py:116-133) passes retry_transfer_from_pid=<dead supervisor pid> and failed with 'workspace #10 with pid 3333672 was not found', discarding the --next payload into a done.json string.

CREDIT WHERE DUE: sase-ku.5's reconciler is the only reason this surfaced at all (it moved the phantom to failed at 13:11:17), and sase-ku.3's durable identity is what let it decide the supervisor was dead. This epic hardened the supervisor once it is running; the new plan covers dead-on-arrival. Expected file overlap: monitor/start.py, supervise.py, followup.py, settlement.py, transaction.py, ace/scheduler/stale_running_cleanup.py, axe/hook_jobs.py -- disjoint from sase-ku.10, which commits no source.

notes.text:
COVERAGE GAP IN THIS PHASE'S MATRIX (see the full root-cause note on parent sase-ku, and the proposed epic plan monitor_supervisor_survival). Every monitor path this phase and sase-kp.12 exercised was either host-started (starter_agent=null, cwd=main repo) or started by a codex-runtime agent. The one row never driven is the common real-world one: a monitor started from inside an agent whose runtime tears down its own process tree on handoff. That row is broken today -- 3/3 claude-runtime agent-started monitors on 2026-08-13 (sase-kp.land--code 'just check-full', sase-kv.5.w1--code 'just test-visual', zl.w0--code 'just test-visual') produced a supervisor that died silently during its ~0.8s Python startup: exit_code null, monitor_pgid never recorded, live_reply.md exactly 73 bytes (only the reconciler line), supervisor.log 0 bytes. Meanwhile 2/2 codex-runtime agent-started monitors (smoke-fail--0, z2--code) ran fine, which is why the matrix looked green.

WHAT I SUGGEST ADDING TO THIS PHASE'S MATRIX, if it is still open when you read this: (a) an agent-started monitor per supported runtime, over a command that runs for minutes -- assert the supervised command's output actually reaches live_reply.md and the --next follow-up agent launches into the lane; (b) an assertion that the monitor's workspace is NOT reassigned to another agent while it runs (workspace #10 was handed to sase-ku.9--plan at 12:54:35, 51 seconds into zl.w0--mon's 20-minute run).

ALSO, ON THIS PHASE'S OWN SMOKE RUN just now: sase-ku.10--mon-0 (20260813132048, starter sase-ku.10--mon) failed at start with 'could not claim workspace: workspace #0 with pid 3700673 was not found' -- a monitor started BY a monitor member. I have listed it as out of scope in the new plan (phase 'claim' may fix it incidentally); if it does not, it is worth filing.

HEADS-UP ON WHAT WILL CHANGE UNDER YOU: the proposed plan's 'detach' and 'ack' phases change what a healthy start looks like -- the supervisor is double-forked and reparented to PID 1 before start_monitor returns, and start_monitor blocks on a new .monitor_started acknowledgement and raises MonitorError (CLI exits non-zero, starter agent stays alive) instead of returning a phantom 'running' record. Any exercise that asserts on the supervisor's PPID, on start_monitor returning immediately, or on a monitor member existing after a failed start will need re-running once those land.

notes.author: zg
notes.text:
INPUT FROM ADJACENT WORK -- your phase is now the ONLY thing standing between a dead supervisor and a permanently un-waitable lane.

The approved plan '.sase/artifacts/home/.sase/plans/202608/monitor_wait_resolution.md' proposed its own minimal reaper (settle a monitor whose pid is gone and whose done.json is missing into monitor_state 'failed'). I did NOT implement it: your 'reconcile' phase is IN_PROGRESS and strictly broader. Nothing in that plan's steps 1-3 or 5 touches src/sase/monitor/store.py or src/sase/ace/scheduler/stale_running_cleanup.py, so you should see no conflict there.

What DID land that you should build on (src/sase/core/dismissed_agent_completion.py):
- New public effective_done_outcome(done_data) maps a done marker whose outcome is 'monitored' onto the ordinary wait vocabulary via monitor_state.
- MONITOR_SUCCESS_STATES = {'completed', 'stopped'} resolve a %wait. Everything else -- 'failed', 'timeout', an unrecognized state, or a missing monitor_state -- blocks the waiter and is reported through sase_chop_wait_checks' existing 'Terminal dependency still blocks waiter' path.

Consequences for your phase:
1. store._reconcile_dead_supervisor() already writes {'outcome': 'monitored', 'monitor_state': 'failed'}, which now classifies as a wait FAILURE. Reaping a wedged monitor therefore makes its lane terminally-blocked-and-reported instead of silently unresolved. That is the intended contract; no change needed on your side.
2. Your new 'lost' state buckets as Failed, so it will block a waiter automatically with no edit to MONITOR_SUCCESS_STATES. Only add a state to that frozenset if a waiter should be RELEASED by it.
3. If reconciliation ever settles a monitor WITHOUT a monitor_state field in done.json, the fix fails closed to 'failed' -- deliberate, but it means the marker should always carry monitor_state.
4. Live phantom still present at the time of writing: sase-kp.land--mon (monitor id h8bkkdxmxvzm, artifact .../ace-run/202608/13/20260813083112) reports monitor_state 'running' with dead supervisor pid 3608804 and no done.json. Its lane sase-kp.land still resolves to is_resolved=False and blocks waiters sase-kp.land.w0 and sase-kp.land.w1 -- correctly, since a running monitor must block. Reaping it is what releases them. Good end-to-end fixture for your phase's tests.

title: Circular import between sase.project_aliases and sase.memory breaks test_project_handler_list_show.py collection
close_reason: Fixed on master; the circular import is gone and a regression test pins it.
description:
tests/main/test_project_handler_list_show.py fails at COLLECTION with a deterministic circular import, so the whole module's tests never run.

REPRODUCTION (2026-08-13, workspace checkout at master 829030f97):
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/main/test_project_handler_list_show.py -q
  -> ImportError: cannot import name 'resolve_project_alias_ref' from partially initialized module 'sase.project_aliases' (most likely due to a circular import)

Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to my change by 'git stash'-ing my working tree and re-running on clean master: the identical collection error reproduces.

CYCLE (from the pytest traceback):
  tests/main/test_project_handler_list_show.py:14
    -> src/sase/main/project_handler.py:29  from sase.project_aliases import ...
    -> src/sase/project_aliases.py:23       from sase.project_alias_prompts import ...
    -> src/sase/project_alias_prompts.py:8  from sase.xprompt._fenced_blocks import ...
    -> src/sase/xprompt/__init__.py:34 -> directives.py:48 -> processor.py:41 -> loader.py:28
    -> src/sase/xprompt/loader_memory.py:15 from sase.memory.notes import collapse_description
    -> src/sase/memory/__init__.py:1 -> src/sase/memory/proposals/__init__.py:8
    -> src/sase/memory/read_log.py:35       from sase.project_aliases import resolve_project_alias_ref  <-- closes the cycle

ROOT CAUSE: src/sase/memory/read_log.py:35 imports resolve_project_alias_ref at module scope, but its only use is inside a function body (read_log.py:370). Because sase.project_aliases transitively imports sase.memory (via project_alias_prompts -> xprompt -> loader_memory -> sase.memory.notes), any entry into the cycle that starts at sase.project_aliases finds sase.memory.read_log re-entering a half-initialized sase.project_aliases. src/sase/memory/proposals/paths.py:9 has the identical module-scope import with the same function-local-only use (paths.py:16) and is the second edge of the same shape.

LIKELY FIX: move both imports into their calling functions (deferred import), or hoist resolve_project_alias_ref into a leaf module that neither side's package __init__ pulls in. Then add a regression check that the module imports in a fresh interpreter -- the test that catches this is named test_project_handler_imports_in_fresh_interpreter, so the intent already exists; it just cannot run because collection dies first.

title: sase-core's icon-field requirement for ArtifactRefProviderSpecWire breaks sase's provider specs (unreleased feature ahead of Python support)
description:
sase-core commit 4f8c99e ('feat(artifact-ref): require icon field in provider ref spec wire'), which sits on sase-core's master after the 0.26.7 release tag (8bb76d1) and before commit 87e4a4f (needed for AGENT_SCAN_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION=6, added on sase's side in sase commit dc9da5576), makes the Rust artifact_ref_provider_spec_validate binding reject every ArtifactRefProviderSpecWire dict lacking an 'icon' field. sase's Python side has not been updated to supply 'icon' anywhere a provider spec is built: src/sase/artifact_providers/_builtin.py's builtin_plan_ref_provider_spec(), src/sase/sidecar_ref_config.py's _default_document_spec(), and multiple test fixtures across the suite.

REPRODUCTION (2026-08-13): with sase at master (dc9da5576) and sase-core rebased to its tip (87e4a4f, chronologically after the icon commit), 'just check''s test-scoped run failed 22 tests, all with 'ValueError: spec is not a valid ArtifactRefProviderSpecWire dict: missing field icon': tests/test_artifact_provider_registry.py (4 nodes, including completely generic registry-fixture specs unrelated to any real provider), tests/test_sidecar_ref_config.py (7 nodes), tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py (6 nodes), tests/agents_sync/test_referenced_by_planning.py, and tests/artifact_refs/test_context.py. Checking sase-core back out to 8bb76d1 (last commit before the icon requirement, still inside the sase-core-rs>=0.26.6,<0.27.0 floor) made all 22 failures disappear with no other changes.

IMPACT: any workspace whose sase-core linked checkout advances past the icon-field commit -- including via the documented 'sase repo open sase-core' recovery path that 'just install' itself recommends when it detects a stale wire schema -- will deterministically break the entire artifact-ref provider-spec validation surface, not just artifact refs specifically opted into icons.

SCOPE: add an 'icon' field (with a sensible default such as an empty string, or whatever default sase-core's Rust side treats as 'no icon') to builtin_plan_ref_provider_spec() and _default_document_spec(), and update any inline test-fixture provider specs the new requirement now rejects, so sase's Python side is coordinated with sase-core's icon-field feature before that feature reaches a released sase-core-rs version.

notes.author: z9
notes.text: RELATED: sase-km — same class of sase-core/sase floor-coordination gap (a sase-core change lands without a matching sase-side update/floor bump), though the specific mechanism differs: sase-km is about the floor gate not knowing a required wire-schema minimum, while this bead is about an unreleased sase-core feature (icon field) landing on origin/master ahead of any coordinated Python-side support, so pulling past the floor via 'sase repo open' hits it even though the floor check itself passes.

title: Nested snippet sessions in the prompt input widget
description: Expanding a snippet while another snippet's tabstops are still pending suspends the outer snippet instead of destroying it: the nested snippet's tabstops are visited first, and once they are exhausted `Tab` resumes the enclosing snippet at the stop after the one that was nested into. Tabstop anchors survive arbitrary editing because they are remapped from real document deltas, `Shift+Tab` steps backwards through the visited stops, and the whole session state machine lives in the Rust core so any future frontend gets the same behavior.

title: A monitor an agent starts must actually run
description: A monitor started from inside an agent survives that agent's own runner teardown, and when it cannot, the failure is loud and immediate: `sase monitor start` refuses to return success for a supervisor that is not provably alive, a monitor's workspace is never harvested out from under it, and a monitor's `--next` action is never silently dropped.

notes.author: sase-l1.land
notes.text:
VERIFIED (steps 1-2 of the land workflow).

PHASES. All six children closed `done`. Read every child note and confirmed each against source and the epic's five commits (3bb9bd1d1, d11dfd6eb, 90b26289f, b4542139a, 1b7ce6194), all on master:
- detach (sase-l1.1, d11dfd6eb): src/sase/monitor/supervisor_bootstrap.py double-forks; SIGHUP=SIG_IGN and SIGTERM/SIGINT recorders are installed at module scope before the sase import; start_monitor records the grandchild pid then its identity; _terminate_supervisor signals the grandchild.
- ack (sase-l1.2, b4542139a): supervisor writes .monitor_started; _wait_for_start_acknowledgement blocks on it for MONITOR_START_ACK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=20s while polling supervisor liveness; on failure it terminates the supervisor, hands the claim back to the still-live starter via _undo_workspace_claim (never into the free pool), tears the member down terminal-failed, and raises MonitorError.
- claim (sase-l1.3, 3bb9bd1d1): hook_jobs.run_stale_running_cleanup passes skip_monitor_claims=True whenever _reconcile_dead_monitor_supervisors() raises, and cleanup_stale_running_entries._monitor_claim_is_releasable requires the owning member to be terminal, failing closed on any read error.
- followup (sase-l1.4, 90b26289f): fresh-claim then workspace-0 fallbacks, FollowupLaunchResult/degraded_reason plumbed into three explicit settlement outcomes, prompt persisted as a durable artifact when unlaunchable.
- visibility (sase-l1.5, 1b7ce6194): ACE and CLI badges plus wire plumbing; docs and skill source extended.
- exercises (sase-l1.6): a real claude-runtime agent-started monitor (9yeer0htvj79) survived the handoff, streamed real pytest output, settled timeout/exit -15, and its follow-up ran in the same workspace (sase_10). Only the claude row -- the reported regression -- was driven end to end; the deliberate startup-window kill is covered deterministically by tests instead.
180 monitor/visibility/claim tests pass in this workspace.

INTEGRATION with commits landed since the epic started (3bb9bd1d1..d9c685e86):
- c5935856a ("make monitors notification-neutral", plan 202608/silent_monitors.md) deliberately deleted notify_monitor_complete and the notify_monitor_followup_dropped alarm this epic's visibility phase added -- an intentional owner-directed reversal of visibility item 3, not a regression. It updated no docs, so docs/monitors.md still promised an alarm-tagged notification for a dropped --next. Corrected: that paragraph now states monitors are notification-neutral and names the durable signals instead.
- FIXED, epic-caused defect: the ⚑ flag never appeared for a *degraded* follow-up. docs/monitors.md, the sase_monitor skill, and the code's own comments all promised "did not launch **or launched degraded**", but every check keyed on followup_error, which a launched-degraded outcome never sets (it records monitor_followup_degraded_reason). - Documented the new ⚠/⚑ monitor badges in docs/ace.md's Agent Row Glyphs section (the visibility phase added glyphs without listing them there).
- 2e2facb94 already consumes this epic's outcomes correctly (SUCCESSFUL_MONITOR_FOLLOWUP_OUTCOMES includes launched-degraded). ab7deab66 and 0083d1e10 layer cleanly on the claim/settlement changes; 0083d1e10's sase.monitor.claims leaf module re-exports through sase.monitor.start, which the epic's sweeper still imports and which is covered by an explicit re-export test. 093088abb, the Grok provider commits, and the ACE snippet/SASE-CONTEXT work do not touch monitors.

1. plan-show `plans:`/`plan:` reference spelling failures (sase-l1.1, .2, .4) -- ALREADY FIXED by cbd47ed11 and b5e1ac88c; tests/plan_show/test_resolve.py + tests/sdd/test_hosted_links.py now 49 passed. No task filed.

6. bead event stream lost an event during a concurrent sync (sase-l1.5) -- genuinely distinct and unresolved; filed via /sase_new_task as sase-li (large, ready), with a RELATED note to sase-f0. Not a duplicate of any task bead and not causally linked to any in-progress epic.

With sase-lh.1 (Rust procs rename) closed and sase-lh.2 (Python) still open, the linked sase-core checkout builds task wire schema 2 while this repo pins version 1, so 63 tests across tests/main/test_task_handler_*, tests/test_tasks_*, and tests/ace/tui/test_task*.py fail in every workspace. title: Make sase repo list honor the current workspace's repo config
close_reason: Duplicate: sase-l2.land filed this same repo-list follow-up twice within 43 seconds (sase-l4 at 15:16:01, sase-l5 at 15:16:44) with identical titles, reproductions, and root-cause analysis. sase-l5 is the surviving READY bead; closing this draft so only one triage gate remains.
description: Proposed by phase bead sase-l2.2 while verifying the sase-research-artifacts rename before its SASE wiring commit landed. Reproduction: from a numbered workspace with an uncommitted edit to sase/sase.yml repos.linked, running sase repo list --json still renders the linked rows from the registered primary checkout, so it showed the old sase-research row rather than the workspace-local sase-research-artifacts row. Root cause confirmed on current master: src/sase/main/repo_handler_list.py resolves a ProjectContext for cwd, but then calls collect_repo_inventory(project=ctx.project_name); src/sase/repo_inventory.py rebuilds that project's entries from ProjectSpec WORKSPACE_DIR and read_project_local_config(primary), discarding the current checkout path. Impact: the command's documented current-project/current-workspace default cannot validate repo-config changes before they land. Scope the fix to make current-checkout invocation read the current workspace's config while preserving explicit --project/--all behavior, clone-matrix semantics, and repo open/path consistency; add CLI/inventory regression coverage.

notes.author: sase-l6.6
notes.text:
Re-measured the full budget in a real terminal on athena, workspace sase_11, master HEAD 2b64c5582 (all 5 implementation phases landed), against the same recipe phase `trace` established (tests/perf/bench_detail_header_summary.py --include-home, driving the production tui_trace spans; docs/perf_runbook.md).

PER-RESOLVER COLD/WARM (ms), home_real, 20 non-clan agents, baseline (2026-08-13, sase-l6.1, trace-only) vs after (2026-08-14, all 5 phases):

  resolver              cold_p50  before->after   cold_max  before->after   warm_p50  before->after
  skill_uses              203.2 -> 4.8               232.2 -> 13.3            6.3 -> 8.9
  memory_reads               7.5 -> 7.5              152.6 -> 114.1         145.9 -> 5.8
  artifact_file_paths       92.1 -> 3.4              793.8 -> 81.7           90.5 -> 3.2
  plan_enrichment             0.2 -> 0.1              171.7 -> 1.4             0.2 -> 0.1
  slow_tool_sources           0.2 -> 1.9              123.3 -> 100.8          24.3 -> 1.9
  wait_bead_statuses           0.0 -> 0.0              956.9 -> 0.0             0.0 -> 0.0
  (delta_entries/opened_workspaces/xprompts/linked_delta/bead_display: ~0 both times)

artifact_file_paths breakdown (where the time inside it goes): list_indexed_artifact_files p50 dropped from ~1.7-1.9s (sase-l6.1's own baseline note; the real index had grown past the plan's 7.7MB figure) to 8.5ms in a clean re-run today -- a ~200x reduction, and it is now identical cold vs warm, confirming defect 1 (the one resolver with literally no cache) is fixed. synthesize_default_artifact_files (never touched by this epic, always uncached, does its own done.json/agent_meta.json/plan_path.json reads) measured noisily across runs (6.5ms p50 in a clean 10-agent/3-run pass vs an 80ms outlier in a busier sample taken while this host had a concurrent Rust release build and several other agents running) -- consistent with the load-noise caveat sase-l6.1 already recorded for this host, not a regression.

One new finding outside the epic's three named stores: agent_page_url measured 400-800ms cold AND warm whenever the 20-agent sample includes a page-publishing 'Done' agent (0.0ms in the original baseline only because no such agent was sampled that day). Root-caused and filed as sase-lw (see below) -- an uncached per-call registry snapshot, not something any of sase-l6's five phases touched or introduced.

REAL-TERMINAL VERIFICATION (sase ace --tmux, tmux send-keys/capture-pane, live ~/.sase data, ~46 agents / 3 running):

- First paint: SASE CONTEXT (with whatever lane is free/cached) was present in the very first captured frame after a selection change (~50ms poll), consistent with phase `immediate`'s zero-I/O synchronous cheap-path render -- no separate worker round trip observed for that content.
- Complete section: batch timings read from the live trace confirm phase `stream`'s cheapest-first, coalesced-publish behavior (this land pass's own capture: first-ever cold selection in the process published 3 batches totaling ~98ms; already-warm-in-process selections settled between <1ms and ~40ms per batch). This land pass's own tmux-driven navigation did not cleanly isolate one-key-per-agent transitions to get a clean per-key p50/p95 (the cursor stayed on one clan/tribe container across several key presses), so for the authoritative batch-latency figures I'm relying on phase sase-l6.4's own real-terminal capture, recorded in its close note: batch 1 (free/in-memory lanes) ~0.2-0.7ms, batch 2 (store-backed lanes) 12-41ms warm / 300ms-1.2s cold. That is the honest per-batch number; this land pass corroborates the *shape* (fast free batch, slower store-backed batch) but not independently a tighter number.
- Steady-state enrichment CPU, one stationary selection, 60s real time: build_detail_header_summary parent spans totaled 47 calls / 445ms of duration across the 60s window (0.74% of the window), and only 1 of the 9 possible lanes (bead_display) actually re-resolved on the stationary selection -- the other 8 stayed cached, confirming defect 3 (the old blanket 1s TTL that re-ran all twelve resolvers every repaint) is gone; this is revalidation of one lane, not full recomputation. tui_stalls.jsonl gained 0 new entries during the window. Total process CPU over the same 60s was ~81% of one core (utime+stime), but tracing shows that is dominated by ace.provider_snapshot (456 calls) and widget.agent_list.patch_agent_row (378 calls) -- live agent-list churn from this host's 3 concurrently-running agents with ticking elapsed timers, unrelated to SASE CONTEXT enrichment and out of this epic's scope. Reporting both numbers because the plan asked for "steady-state enrichment CPU" specifically and the raw process-CPU number alone would overstate what this epic controls.

TARGET CHECK: "context content on the first paint" -- met (zero-I/O immediate paint, phase l6.5). "a complete section within roughly 100ms warm" -- met for warm-in-process selections (mostly <40ms per this pass and phase l6.4's own capture); a genuinely cold first selection can still take several hundred ms to ~1.2s on the store-backed batch per sase-l6.4's own cold figures, which is expected (a cold-cache first touch was never the target) and is exactly what follow-up sase-lu proposes to characterize properly since none of this epic's numbers, including these, are cold-OS-page-cache measurements. "steady-state enrichment work that is revalidation rather than recomputation" -- met (see above).

WHICH DEFECTS EACH PHASE ACTUALLY REMOVED (honest read):
1. Three whole-store parses repeated per agent -- REMOVED by sase-l6.2 (stores). artifact_file_paths cold p50 92ms->3.4ms, and critically stopped scaling with agent count (process-wide snapshot cache, not per-agent).
2. All-or-nothing rendering -- REMOVED by sase-l6.3 (lanes, structural) + sase-l6.4 (stream, user-visible). Section now renders partial lanes cheapest-first with a pending affordance instead of waiting on all twelve resolvers.
3. 1s blanket TTL re-running all resolvers every repaint -- REMOVED by sase-l6.3's per-lane freshness policy. This land pass's own 60s stationary-selection trace is direct confirmation: 1 of 9 lanes revalidates, not 9.
4. Nothing survives the panel (show_empty clears everything) -- NOT ADDRESSED (was explicitly deferred to a follow-up in the original plan). Filed as sase-lt.

FOLLOW-UP OUTCOMES (all via /sase_new_task from this land phase):
- sase-lr (new, size large): prune/rotate the three append-only stores. RELATED note added to sase-kh (a same-theme but different-file prune task from epic sase-k3).
- sase-ls (new, size large): move the artifact-file index into sase-core's Rust indexed storage. RELATED notes added to sase-lr and sase-kh.
- sase-lt (new, size medium): scope show_empty()'s cache clear to the deselected agent instead of wiping every agent's resolved lanes.
- sase-lu (new, size medium): measure cold-cache enrichment cost; every figure this epic has (including this land pass's) is warm-page-cache only. RELATED note added to sase-kj (same gap, epic sase-k3).
- sase-lv (new, size medium): audit non-TUI callers of read_artifact_file_index (artifact_cli/prune.py, axe/run_agent_exec_finalize_artifacts.py, artifact_file_reclaim.py) for their own call patterns now that a cache exists to lean on.
- sase-lw (new, size medium; not plan-named, discovered during this land pass's re-measurement): resolve_agent_page_url has no cache and re-scans the whole agent-name registry on every call, 400-800ms whenever the selected agent publishes a page. RELATED to closed sase-c7, which fixed the same get_reserved_family_names()-uncached problem for a different call site (bulk bead-page-association publication) that does not cover this one.
- sase-le (+1 corroborated, not new): phase sase-l6.4's order-dependent test_prompt_panel_header.py flake is an exact duplicate of an already-open task; added independent reproduction evidence.
- sase-lm (+1 corroborated, not new): phase sase-l6.5's 'TaskSubmitError: task wire schema mismatch' (63 failures) is an exact duplicate of an already-open task (sase-core-rs floor lag); added independent reproduction evidence. Not currently reproducing in this workspace (just check passed clean here today), consistent with that task's own finding that it depends on which sase-core-rs build is linked.
- sase-l6.1's stale --epic-symbol whitelist report (bead sase-kz.5, Snippet* symbols) and sase-l6.2/l6.3's symvision unused-public-function report (stream_and_parse_messages_json_output) -- both CONFIRMED ALREADY RESOLVED on current master: grep of Justfile's _lint-symvision recipe shows zero --epic-symbol entries today, and this land pass's own `just check` run passed lint (symvision) clean. No new task needed for either.

VERIFICATION: `just check` (scoped) green today at HEAD 2b64c5582 -- fmt, ruff, mypy, pyscripts, test-waits, changelog, terminology, symvision, toobig, SASE validation, committed-plans, and the scoped test lane all passed with no failures.
