title: Workspace allocator hands a sase_<N> clone to a second agent while another agent is still RUNNING in it
close_reason: Fixed: the implementing work landed and its own follow-up defect is closed too. This bead's child epic sase-lb.1 ('One live agent per numbered workspace — close the monitor claim hole') is CLOSED, and the guard it shipped is live -- _guard_workspace_not_occupied in src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner_setup.py:70, called at lines 133 and 220 and referenced by run_agent_exec_retry.py. The claim-parsing hole later found in that guard (sase-qa: WorkspaceClaimLine::parse dropping rows with unrecognized trailing parts) is fixed in sase-core and closed in this same sweep. No agent was still running against this bead's in_progress reservation. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
Proposed by epic bead sase-l2 (land agent sase-l2.land) during the sase-l2 landing.

REPRODUCTION (observed live, 2026-08-13 ~19:40 UTC):
- Land agent sase-l2.land was allocated /home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_14.
- Concurrently, phase worker sase-l6.1 was RUNNING (duration 426s) with workspace_num=14 in `sase agent list -j`.
- Confirmed not by the ws column alone but directly from the OS: `readlink /proc/2140006/cwd` (PID 2140006 = agent sase-l6.1, status RUNNING) resolved to exactly /home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_14 — byte-identical to the land agent's cwd.
- Both agents are the same project (gh_sase-org__sase), so this is not a per-project numbering coincidence.

IMPACT:
sase-l6.1's in-flight, uncommitted edit to src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/prompt_panel/_agent_display_header_summary.py (tui_trace instrumentation, docstring self-attributed to 'bead sase-l6.1') was visible in the land agent's working tree from the very first git status of its session. This tripped the land agent's post-completion commit finalizer twice (pass 1 of 2 and pass 2 of 2). The finalizer's pass-2 text states the run fails unless the listed changes are committed, so the failure mode this creates is an agent committing another bead's incomplete, unverified, in-flight work under an unrelated landing commit — and racing the owning agent's own commit workflow. The land agent correctly declined, but only because the change happened to self-identify its bead in a docstring; a change without that tell would be far harder to attribute.

SCOPE:
Workspace allocation must not hand a sase_<N> directory to a second agent while another agent is still RUNNING in it. Investigate the allocator's liveness check (a stale-lock/PID-liveness gap, or allocation keyed on something other than 'currently running' is the likely root cause) and decide whether the fix is exclusive leasing, a liveness probe before reuse, or per-agent workspaces. Consider also hardening the commit finalizer so a dirty path that predates the agent's own session is not attributed to it.

title: One live agent per numbered workspace — close the monitor claim hole
description: A numbered `<project>_<N>` workspace checkout is never occupied by two live agents at once. Every process that works inside a numbered workspace holds the RUNNING-field claim for that exact number for as long as it is in there, the claim's PID is always a live process, and any code path that cannot satisfy that invariant fails loudly instead of silently running unclaimed.

title: Flake gate counts audit failures from dirty workspaces, so one agent's in-progress edit blocks everyone's check-full
description:
DISCOVERED while running 'just check-full' for an unrelated TUI change in workspace sase_19 at commit 31b9c62b6805 (2026-08-13T20:03Z). The run's own full pytest lane passed clean (29682 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures), and only 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' failed.

ROOT CAUSE (proved from the durable store, not inferred): reproducible-flake classification consumes full-run records that were recorded from DIRTY workspace trees, so a source-tree audit that an agent's own uncommitted edits legitimately broke is promoted into shared cross-workspace flake debt and then blocks 'just check-full' for every other agent.

EVIDENCE. tests/test_agent_artifact_marker_path_passing_audit.py::test_tracked_marker_path_passing_sites_are_reviewed was flagged as a reproducible flake on exactly two records in ~/.sase/test-selection/gh_sase-org__sase, and BOTH carry changed_files that overlap the very tree the audit walks:
  - 20260812T230235Z-9f93c3d8c0c5-2782438-full-run.json (workspace sase_12, exit 1, 2 failures) changed_files: src/sase/monitor/, src/sase/plan_chain.py, tests/monitor/, tests/test_plan_chain_roles.py
  - 20260813T194513Z-1004f9eb33d6-2320907-full-run.json (workspace sase_16, exit 1, 2 failures) changed_files: src/sase/monitor/supervise.py, src/sase/monitor/settlement.py, src/sase/monitor/start.py, src/sase/monitor/reconcile.py, src/sase/ace/tui/models/_loaders/_workflow_loaders.py, and 7 more

The audit asserts _path_passing_contexts() == set(_REVIEWED_PATH_PASSING_CONTEXTS) (tests/test_agent_artifact_marker_path_passing_audit.py:111), i.e. an AST scan of src/sase compared against a checked-in reviewed inventory whose entries include 'src/sase/monitor/supervise.py:_read_meta' and the monitor start entries. Editing those files without updating the inventory breaks the audit DETERMINISTICALLY in that workspace. That is correct, intended behavior for the editing agent -- it is not a flake, and it is not a break on master. On a clean tree here the file passes in isolation (2 passed in 13.25s).

The sibling node tests/test_agent_artifact_marker_mutation_audit.py::test_tracked_marker_mutation_sites_are_reviewed failed in the same sase_16 record, confirming the class generalizes to every marker-audit node and, more broadly, to any source-tree audit test.

WHY THIS IS NOT sase-hl: sase-hl (closed done 2026-08-08) covered a DIFFERENT false-positive mode -- a node deterministically broken on master that different workspaces report alongside disjoint diffs -- and proposed distinguishing it by checking whether the node fails consistently across ALL full runs after some commit. That remedy does not help here: these are two isolated failures among many passing full runs, so the dirty-tree case still reads as genuine intermittency under sase-hl's proposed rule. Different root cause, different remediation.

IMPACT: the gate is currently blocking 'just check-full' for every landing agent that hits this node, and the 30-day record retention means a single mid-edit run keeps poisoning the shared gate for weeks after the editing agent has landed or abandoned the change.

SCOPE: decide and implement the correct attribution rule in tests/_test_selection_health.py / tools/selection_health -- for example, do not feed a full-run record's failures into reproducible-flake determination when the record's changed_files overlap the sources a failing audit scans, or record tree-dirtiness on the run record and discount dirty-tree records the way max_failures_per_run already discounts catastrophic runs. Add a regression that reconstructs the two records above and asserts the node is not classified as a reproducible flake.

Neither commit is broken alone; the merge is.

SCOPE: decide whether 4d36d6d3d's new code actually needs that symbol. If it calls it, import the private name (`from ._subprocess_claude import _stream_and_parse_messages_json_output`) or re-promote the function to public and drop the sase-ld symvision finding; if nothing in 4d36d6d3d uses it, delete the stale import line. Verified locally that aliasing the private name makes the import succeed and tests/monitor go 119 passed.

notes.author: sase-lh.land--1
notes.text: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: the legacy `tasks.history_limit` config key is parsed but never applied, so the plan requirement "legacy key still honored" is unmet. Root cause: src/sase/default_config.yml always ships `procs.history_limit: 100`, so get_proc_history_limit() (src/sase/config/core.py:328) always takes its first branch and the `tasks` fallback is dead code. Repro: a user config containing only `tasks: {history_limit: 5}` yields 100; the same file with `procs: {history_limit: 7}` yields 7. The deprecation *diagnostic* does work (the user layer reports deprecated_keys=["tasks"], so `sase config layers` / `sase doctor` nudge correctly) - only the value is ignored. Two candidate fixes, both needing an owner decision: (a) make the lookup layer-aware so a user-set legacy key outranks the bundled default but a user-set canonical key still wins, or (b) drop `history_limit` from the bundled default_config.yml and let DEFAULT_PROC_HISTORY_LIMIT be the only default, at the cost of config discoverability. Not fixed in the land phase because the precedence semantics are a design choice.

notes.author: sase-lh.land--1
notes.text: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: homes already migrated by the shipped migration need a repair pass. The land phase fixed _relocate_legacy_logs so future migrations merge legacy logs into an existing ~/.sase/procs/logs, but the marker is one-shot, so a home migrated before the fix keeps its damage. Observed on this real home: ~/.sase/procs_migration.json says {schema_version: 1, completed: true, migrated: true}, yet 12 of 13 rows in procs.jsonl have a log_path under ~/.sase/procs/logs that does not exist, while ~/.sase/tasks/logs still holds 14883 un-relocated files (two of them the missing logs). Separately, stale-Python workspaces recreated ~/.sase/tasks/tasks.jsonl after the marker was written; it now holds 6 proc_id-keyed rows, one still status=running, which the new code cannot see and the one-shot migration will never adopt. A repair needs both a MIGRATION_SCHEMA_VERSION bump (so _marker_is_complete goes stale and the migration re-runs) and a change to the `new_store.exists()` guard in _migrate_legacy_store, which currently short-circuits to migrated=False and would strand those rows on a re-run.

title: Concurrent bead sync can silently delete an event from a shared event stream, wedging every later sync
description:
Discovered by epic phase agent sase-l1.5 (epic sase-l1, 2026-08-13) while landing unrelated monitor-visibility work.

Commit 32edc3208cac352165ab7d7b6d4d6f23d17f6ce6 in the shared beads store ("chore(beads): sync bead state and pages for sase-l3", agent bbugyi200.athena.sase-l3.1) silently deleted the last line of events/streams/sase-l1.jsonl on origin/main -- event 000040, a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note -- and added nothing back. Origin was then missing content present in the merge-base, so every subsequent 'sase bead sync' from that workspace failed with:

  ValueError: validation: cannot merge non-append-only bead event stream sase-l1: theirs missing base event 40

raised from src/sase/bead/conflict_resolver.py:_resolve_bead_conflicts. 'sase bead doctor' reported 11 consecutive failed managed-sync integrations before it was diagnosed by hand.

Two distinct defects:

1. ROOT CAUSE (unknown): whatever produced that 'sync bead state and pages' commit dropped a line from an append-only stream. Reproduce or bound the race in the sync/publish path; a bead event stream must never shrink.

2. DIAGNOSTICS: 'sase bead doctor' reports only the symptom (failed managed-sync integrations). It should detect the actual corruption -- a stream in origin that is shorter than its own history, i.e. missing events present in an ancestor commit -- and name the offending commit, so an agent does not have to run 'git log <base>..origin/main -- events/streams/<id>.jsonl' by hand.

The append-only check itself is behaving correctly: it refuses to silently drop history. Recovery required manually confirming origin added no new content and force-resolving to the local (superset) side before 'sase bead resolve-conflicts' could regenerate issues.jsonl.

title: sase monitor start transfers the workspace claim from the newest lane member's pid, so a lane whose newest member is a settled monitor fails to start a second monitor
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: monitor lane/claim ergonomics with documented workarounds, closed in favor of the cross-agent corruption and gate-blocking defects.
description:
Discovered by epic sase-ku's exercises phase (sase-ku.10) and corroborated by the zo root-cause note on epic sase-ku. Filed by the sase-ku land agent; NOT caused by sase-ku (see root cause below).

SYMPTOM (two independent observations on lane sase-ku.10, 2026-08-13):
  1. 17:21:32Z - after a completed host-style monitor (e9m61z) on lane sase-ku.10, a second start created monitor brgjrd with starter_agent=sase-ku.10--mon and failed with stderr 'workspace #0 with pid 3700673 was not found'.
  2. 17:32:23Z - a retry with an explicit '--lane sase-ku.10' failed the same way: 'workspace #0 with pid 3702168 was not found'.
  3. The zo note on sase-ku records a third: sase-ku.10--mon-0 (artifacts 20260813132048, starter sase-ku.10--mon) failed at start with 'could not claim workspace: workspace #0 with pid 3700673 was not found' - a monitor started BY a monitor member.

ROOT CAUSE: src/sase/monitor/start.py:176-190. start_monitor() reads the NEWEST lane member's agent_meta.json ('raw_meta') and, when inherit_lane_workspace_claim is set and the cwd matches the lane workspace, unconditionally sets transfer_from_pid = raw_meta['pid'] and starter_agent = raw_meta['name']. There is no check that the newest member is a live agent runner rather than an already-settled monitor member. When the newest member is a '--mon' member, that pid is its DEAD supervisor's pid, so transfer_workspace_claim() at start.py:255-264 fails with 'workspace #N with pid <dead pid> was not found', _terminate_supervisor()/_teardown_failed_member() run, and start_monitor() raises MonitorError. The monitored command never runs.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT A sase-ku REGRESSION: git blame attributes 'transfer_from_pid = runner_pid' to b32167c31b ('feat(monitor): add monitor member lifecycle and supervisor process', epic sase-kp) and the surrounding guard to 44796037a5 / 10d3527dd5 - none of them sase-ku commits. sase-ku.4's transactional rewrite preserved the existing semantics.

SCOPE: decide the correct source for the claim transfer when the newest lane member is a monitor member. Options include skipping monitor members when picking the transfer source (walk back to the newest non-monitor member), verifying the recorded pid is alive before attempting a transfer (supervisor_is_alive()/process liveness already exists in src/sase/monitor/identity.py), or claiming fresh instead of transferring when the transfer source is not a live runner. Cover the regression with a test that starts a second monitor on a lane whose newest member is a settled monitor member.

Verified at master d9c685e86 that it did not: start.py:176-190 still has no liveness or member-kind check on the transfer source. sase-l1.4 ('The --next action survives a failed claim transfer', commit 90b26289f) makes the resulting failure less destructive but does not prevent it.

description:
Filed by the sase-ku land agent. These three tests were added by epic sase-ku phase sase-ku.2 (commit afa8178ce, 'fix(monitor): decouple supervisor waits from output reads'). They pass reliably in isolation and in the monitor-only suite but fail intermittently in other agents' full parallel lanes, where they trip 'just check-full''s 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' gate.

EVIDENCE (from ~/.sase/test-selection/gh_sase-org__sase full-run records, 892 records scanned):
- test_run_supervisor_escalates_term_ignoring_chatty_child: 9 failures
- test_run_supervisor_completes_when_grandchild_holds_stdout: 10 failures
- test_run_supervisor_times_out_after_partial_line: 4 failures
All 23 fall between 2026-08-13T16:47Z and 2026-08-13T19:04Z, across workspaces sase_10/12/13/14/16/17 and heads bd6167875cc8, 29cb7924a87d, a7433cfe70a4, 3bb9bd1d1c35, 6d21fbbef36a, cbd47ed11055. Three of those runs failed ONLY these nodes (18:38:31Z ws=sase_16, 3 monitor failures and nothing else; 18:53:53Z ws=sase_16, 1; 19:04:22Z ws=sase_17, 1 plus one unrelated), so they are genuine standalone flakes, not collateral of the SDD/plan_show cluster that was failing in the same window. Corroborated by three independent agent reports on epic sase-ku (2026-08-13T16:51:04Z zl.w0, 17:56:14Z zs, 18:39:23Z zr) and one on sase-l1.3 (18:09:41Z). Every reported failure passed immediately on a serial rerun.

NOT REPRODUCED LOCALLY: at master d9c685e86 in workspace sase_19 the land agent ran the full 'just test' lane (29,721 passed, 10 skipped, 642s, 14 workers) with ZERO monitor failures, plus ~70 targeted attempts -- serial, xdist -n 14, and under 3.3x CPU oversubscription (load average 210 on 64 cores) -- all green. Slowest node under that load was 0.83s against a 5.0s bound.

DIAGNOSTIC NARROWING (hypothesis, not confirmed): all three flaky rows assert 'elapsed < _NO_HANG_TIMEOUT' where _NO_HANG_TIMEOUT = 5.0 (tests/monitor/test_monitor_supervise.py:27), and all three are rows where the output pipe does NOT reach EOF promptly when run_supervisor() closes it -- a lingering grandchild holds the write end, or ~64 KiB is still buffered from a chatty child. BoundedLogPipe.close() (src/sase/logs/pipe.py:74-86) does 'self._thread.join(timeout=5)', i.e. exactly the tests' no-hang budget, so a drain thread that is slow to exit can consume the whole assertion budget by itself. The one sibling row that never flakes, test_run_supervisor_times_out_after_child_closes_stdio, is precisely the one whose child closes stdout/stderr so the pipe EOFs immediately and the join returns at once. A second, independent fragility in the same code: _drain() checks _close_deadline_reached() at the TOP of its loop (pipe.py:91), so a drain thread descheduled across the supervisor's close_drain_seconds=0.5 budget (supervise.py:170) breaks out WITHOUT reading data that is already readable -- silent loss of the tail of a monitored command's output, which also explains the content assertions ('partial', 'parent done') if it is the real cause.

SCOPE: reproduce first (running the monitor supervisor tests concurrently with a full lane in another workspace is the closest known condition), then fix the underlying fragility rather than only widening the bounds. Candidate fixes: drain everything currently readable before honoring the close deadline; decouple the tests' no-hang bound from BoundedLogPipe.close()'s join timeout; and reconsider the 0.2s total-timeout budgets, which race /bin/sh spawn latency under load. Confirm afterwards that the nodes drop out of the reproducible-flake set (see 'just selection-health --explain').

description:
Proposed by epic sase-ku phase sase-ku.10 (End-to-end hardening exercises) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on 2026-08-13T17:31:20Z; filed by the sase-ku land agent. No duplicate found by search or by the one-week task sweep.

SYMPTOM: running 'sase monitor start --command "just check-full" ...' from inside the real agent on lane sase-ku.10, with no explicit --lane, failed before launch with:
  FamilyAttachError: Cannot create agent family `sase-ku`: resolved parent is named `sase-ku.4`
Retrying with an explicit '--lane sase-ku.10' got past this failure (it then hit the separate claim-transfer defect tracked by sase-lj).

IMPACT: the documented ergonomic path -- an epic phase agent handing a long command to /sase_monitor from its own lane -- can hard-fail before the command runs. Every phase agent in an epic family is exposed, and the workaround (always pass --lane explicitly) is not what docs/monitors.md or the sase_monitor skill tell agents to do.

SCOPE: work out how the implicit lane is derived for an in-agent start and why, on an epic-phase lane, it resolves a family parent belonging to a sibling phase (sase-ku.4) rather than the caller's own lane (sase-ku.10). Start from resolve_lane()/the durable-lane derivation in src/sase/monitor/start.py and the family-attach path that raises FamilyAttachError. Decide whether the implicit lane should be taken from the caller's own SASE_AGENT_NAME/artifacts rather than from a lane-wide newest-member lookup, and cover the epic-phase-lane case with a regression test. If the correct answer is that --lane is required in an epic family, that must be enforced with a clear error and documented in docs/monitors.md and the sase_monitor skill source instead of surfacing as FamilyAttachError.

title: sase stitch create's _stage_all_except swept a concurrent agent's uncommitted work into an unrelated commit, already pushed to origin/master

description:
Reproduction in workspace sase_16 (host project gh_sase-org__sase) on 2026-08-13 while
implementing the approved plan
sase/repos/plans/202608/notification_read_current_tab.md. That plan's Python/test
changes were deliberately left uncommitted per the launching agent's instructions ("do
not create a git commit unless the user asks for one").

At 2026-08-13T18:42:15-0400 a commit appeared that this session never requested:

    commit aea9bf645a8e6e1fc7ccff57253f31068eb9f01a
    docs: add Grok Build coverage across provider documentation
    SASE_BEAD=[sase-l3.7]  SASE_TYPE=stitch  SASE_AGENT=[bbugyi200.athena.sase-l3.7]

`git show aea9bf645 --stat` shows its tree includes every file this session had changed
and left uncommitted for an unrelated bead (sase-l3.7, Grok Build docs):

    src/sase/ace/tui/modals/notification_modal.py
    src/sase/ace/tui/modals/notification_modal_action_types.py
    src/sase/ace/tui/modals/notification_modal_basic_actions.py
    src/sase/ace/tui/modals/notification_modal_constants.py
    src/sase/ace/tui/modals/notification_modal_tags.py
    src/sase/core/notification_store_wire.py
    src/sase/notifications/__init__.py
    src/sase/notifications/store.py
    tests/notification_store/test_state_updates.py
    tests/test_core_facade/test_notification_store.py
    tests/test_notification_modal_action_bindings.py
    tests/test_notification_modal_read_tab.py

`git show aea9bf645 -- src/sase/notifications/store.py` confirms the diff is the real
`mark_tab_read()` addition from the notification plan, not a coincidental docs-driven
touch. `git reflog show HEAD` shows this was a fresh `commit:` (not `commit (amend):`),
and the three neighboring commits from the same session window (d9c685e86, 4ff3a4161,
2e2facb94) are clean -- `git show <sha> --stat` for each has zero notification files --
so this is not routine amend misuse, it is a one-off cross-contamination between two
concurrent, unrelated agents sharing one git working tree.
`git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/master` returns true, confirming this
contaminated commit is already pushed/shared history on origin/master, not a local-only
mistake that can be quietly fixed.

Root cause: src/sase/vcs_provider/plugins/_git_commit_dispatch.py:140-147
(`_stage_all_except`) calls plain `git add -A` (repo-wide) whenever the commit payload's
`exclude` list is empty:

    def _stage_all_except(self, exclude: list[str], cwd: str) -> CommandOutput:
        """Stage every change, honoring `exclude` as literal pathspec excludes."""
        if not exclude:
            return self._run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd)
        ...

When a `sase stitch create`-driven commit runs in a workspace/working tree that another
agent is concurrently using for a *different*, still-uncommitted task, this stages and
commits that other agent's in-progress work too, silently. The resulting commit message
and SASE_BEAD trailer describe only the committing agent's own bead, so the bundled
changes are undiscoverable except by reading the actual diff.

Impact: (1) commit messages/trailers become inaccurate audit records; (2) unrelated work
streams get bundled into one pushed commit; (3) "do not commit unless the user asks"
gets silently violated whenever two agents race in a shared working tree, with no error
or warning to either agent. This session's launching agent was never told a commit
happened and only discovered it while investigating an unrelated just check-full
failure.

Not filing a remediation attempt here: fixing the notification-plan history (revert or
split the pushed commit) is a judgment call for the project owner given it is already on
origin/master, so that decision was left to the user in the same conversation instead of
being made unilaterally.

Suggested fix direction: scope `_stage_all_except`'s default (empty-exclude) path to the

title: just test-visual-update rewrites every PNG golden in the suite, silently absorbing unrelated drift
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: PNG-golden drift is contained by the dedicated just test-visual lane and is not blocking the shared gates.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-ky.2 (epic sase-ky, plan @plan:202608/plan_ref_kind_rename.md) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on 2026-08-13T18:23:50Z; filed by sase-ky.land after search and the one-week task sweep found only node-specific snapshot-stabilization tasks (sase-l7/sase-l8/sase-l9/sase-la), not this update-mode defect.

WHAT HAPPENED: sase-ky.2's diff changed fixture text in tests/ace/tui/visual/_ace_prompt_png_snapshot_helpers.py and test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_clan_panel.py, legitimately affecting exactly 5 goldens (prompt_artifact_ref_highlight_120x40, prompt_glossary_highlight_dark/light_120x40, prompt_glossary_wrapped_highlight_dark_120x40, agents_clan_panel_epic_logical_prompt_hints_120x40). An earlier wholesale 'just test-visual --sase-update-visual-snapshots' sweep in that phase rewrote 211 goldens. The agent caught it, reverted the 211 to HEAD, and regenerated only the 5 -- but on inspection at least one of the wrongly-rewritten goldens (changespec_selected_row_120x40.png) had been captured with the footer keybinding-hint text missing entirely, i.e. update mode had blessed a genuinely wrong render as the new expectation. Nothing in the tooling flagged that 206 goldens moved for no reason in the diff.

ROOT CAUSE: tests/ace/tui/visual/png_diff.py:202-204 -- when the update option is set, every snapshot assertion unconditionally does write_bytes(expected_path, png_bytes) and returns before any comparison. There is no scoping to the tests the author intended to update, no diff summary of which goldens changed, and no failure when a golden outside the intended set moves. Justfile:480 ('just test-visual-update' -> 'just test-visual -- --sase-update-visual-snapshots') applies the flag to the WHOLE 669-golden suite, so the documented one-command way to accept an intentional 5-golden change also silently re-blesses every unrelated golden, including any that is currently rendering wrong under host contention, font/renderer drift, or an in-flight bug.

WHY IT MATTERS: goldens are the only record of intended appearance. A wholesale re-bless destroys that record silently and is easy to miss in review because binary PNG diffs carry no visible content. sase-ky.2 only caught it by manually opening the rewritten files. CLAUDE.md documents test-visual-update as the way to accept intentional visual changes, so agents are actively steered into this.

SCOPE: make update mode account for what it changed and refuse to quietly widen. Options, not mutually exclusive: (a) in update mode, record every golden whose bytes actually changed and print/fail with that list at session end so the author must acknowledge each one; (b) make the flag require an explicit selection (node ids / -k expression / an explicit --all opt-in) and refuse a bare whole-suite update; (c) keep writing but report unrelated churn as a distinct non-zero exit so it cannot pass unnoticed; (d) add a guard test that fails when a commit touches goldens whose owning tests are not in the diff's import closure. Also update CLAUDE.md's PNG Snapshot Tests guidance to tell agents to scope regeneration to the affected test files and to sanity-check that unrelated goldens did not move.

title: sase bead doctor --fix-design-refs takes ~2 hours for 456 beads because it updates and flushes one bead at a time
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: single-surface CLI/doc papercuts with narrow blast radius, closed in favor of cross-agent correctness and gate-blocking work.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-ky.3 (epic sase-ky, plan @plan:202608/plan_ref_kind_rename.md) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on 2026-08-13T21:01:10Z; filed by sase-ky.land after search and the one-week task sweep found no duplicate (sase-f9 is about CLEARING stale design/artifact refs, not about the apply path's cost).

REPRODUCTION: running 'sase bead doctor --fix-design-refs' on this machine's bead store to migrate the legacy plans: design-ref spelling to plan: correctly repaired 456 event-backed design references but took roughly two hours of wall clock to do it.

ROOT CAUSE: src/sase/bead/cli_admin.py:99-103 applies the repairs with a per-bead loop -- 'for repair in preview.repairs: mutation.project.update(repair.bead_id, design=repair.new_reference)' -- inside a single bead_store_mutation. Each update writes its own event and flushes its own projection change, so the cost is 456 sequential write/flush round trips rather than one batched write. The existing batch path does not help here: 'sase bead update' accepts several bead IDs but applies the SAME field values to all of them, whereas a design-ref repair needs a different design value per bead.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the supported migration path for legacy design references, and it is the only one. A two-hour foreground run is long enough that an agent will be killed, interrupted, or will work around it, and any future ref-kind or bead-ID migration touching the whole store pays the same cost. sase-ky.3 had to babysit it to completion.

SCOPE: add an apply path that writes N differing per-bead design values in one batched store mutation -- one event append and one projection flush for the whole repair set -- and route --fix-design-refs through it. Note this likely crosses the Rust core boundary: 'mutation.project.update' is the core-backed bead update, so the batched-heterogeneous-update API probably belongs in ../sase-core/crates/sase_core with a new binding and wire, with cli_admin.py as the caller. Confirm first whether an existing core batch primitive can already take per-item field values before adding one. Cover with a test that the repair set is applied atomically and that a mid-run failure leaves no partial projection, and record the before/after timing on a store of comparable size.

title: Grok Build double-loads CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md as duplicate project instructions
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: single-surface CLI/doc papercuts with narrow blast radius, closed in favor of cross-agent correctness and gate-blocking work.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-l3.6 (epic sase-l3, Grok Build LLM provider) and confirmed again by sase-l3.land during epic landing.

ROOT CAUSE: Grok Build reads AGENTS.md natively, so SASE intentionally generates no GROK.md shim (tests/main/test_init_memory_agent_docs.py::test_provider_instruction_shims_do_not_include_grok pins this). But Grok Build 1.0.3 ALSO recognizes SASE's generated CLAUDE.md as project instructions and loads both files, feeding the model the same instruction content twice. Phase sase-l3.6 verified this with a live 'grok inspect' run under a temporary HOME: both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are reported as project instructions. Setting '[compat.claude] agents = false' in Grok's config does NOT suppress the generic CLAUDE.md load.

IMPACT: Every SASE agent run on the grok provider pays double the instruction-token cost for AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md content and risks the model treating duplicated directives as emphasis. The duplication is currently accepted and documented rather than fixed -- see the 'Instruction double-load' section of docs/agent_providers.md.

SCOPE: Find a narrower mitigation than suppressing CLAUDE.md generation under a Grok provider. Simply not generating CLAUDE.md would break any human running 'claude' in the same tree, which is why sase-l3 declined it. Options worth evaluating: a Grok-side config knob that disables generic-CLAUDE.md discovery (recheck against Grok Build releases newer than 1.0.3), making the Claude shim a symlink/pointer to AGENTS.md so a double load costs nothing, or emitting a short CLAUDE.md that defers to AGENTS.md. Update the docs/agent_providers.md 'Instruction double-load' section with whatever posture is chosen.

REPRODUCE: deploy SASE instruction files into a scratch tree, point HOME at a temp dir with an authenticated Grok Build 1.0.3, and run 'grok inspect'; both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md appear as project instructions.

title: Prune or rotate the three append-only TUI stores backing SASE CONTEXT enrichment
close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: epic sase-l6 already landed the SASE CONTEXT enrichment win these follow-ups refine.
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-l6.6 (land phase of epic sase-l6, SASE CONTEXT incremental enrichment); named as follow-up 1 in plans:202608/sase_context_incremental.md.

Epic sase-l6 (bead sase-l6.2, 'stores') added process-wide revalidating snapshot caches for the artifact-file index (~/.sase/artifacts/index.jsonl), the memory-read log, and the skill-use log, so N agents now share one parse per store change instead of paying a full re-read each. That fixed defect 1 (repeated whole-store parses) but the stores themselves remain append-only and unpruned:

  ~/.sase/artifacts/index.jsonl                          7.68 MB / 7,747 rows (2026-08-13 baseline)

  ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/skill_uses.jsonl    3.09 MB / 6,222 rows

Scope: decide and implement a retention policy per store (prune, rotate to cold storage, or age out), consistent with each store's read/write paths in src/sase/core/artifact_file_explicit.py, src/sase/ace/tui/memory_reads.py, and src/sase/ace/tui/skill_uses.py.

title: resolve_agent_page_url has no cache: refreshes the whole family-name registry on every TUI selection (400-800ms)
description:
Discovered during phase bead sase-l6.6 (land phase of epic sase-l6, SASE CONTEXT incremental enrichment) while re-measuring the full detail-header-summary budget on 2026-08-14.

resolve_agent_page_url() (src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_page_url.py:26), one of the twelve resolvers inside build_detail_header_summary, is not one of epic sase-l6's three targeted stores, but it has no cache at all and measured 400-800ms cold AND warm in the land-phase re-measurement (tests/perf/bench_detail_header_summary.py --include-home), whenever the sampled agent set includes a 'Done' agent that publishes a hosted page (agent_publishes_page() is true). The epic's original plan baseline (2026-08-13) sampled 0.0ms for this resolver because no such agent happened to be in that day's first-20-agents sample -- this is real, previously-unmeasured cost, not a regression from this epic's changes.

ROOT CAUSE: resolve_agent_page_url() calls hosted_link_resolver(...).snapshot_agent_name_registry() (src/sase/sdd/hosted_links.py:107) unconditionally on every call. hosted_link_resolver() itself IS process-cached per (repo_root, project, root) (src/sase/sdd/hosted_links.py:365 factory), but snapshot_agent_name_registry()'s own docstring says it exists to 'refresh family-name state once for a batch of agent-link lookups' -- it assumes its caller batches calls and refreshes once per batch. resolve_agent_page_url() is called once per TUI agent selection (not batched), so every selection of a page-publishing agent re-triggers a full get_reserved_family_names() registry scan with no staleness check across selections.

RELATED: sase-c7 (closed) fixed the same underlying get_reserved_family_names()-is-uncached-per-call problem for the bulk bead-page-association publication path, adding a build-scoped snapshot refreshed once per publication build. That fix does not cover this call site: the TUI's per-agent-selection path was never batched, so it still refreshes on every call.

Scope: give resolve_agent_page_url's registry snapshot the same treatment sase-c7 established (cache/bound the refresh, e.g. TTL'd or per-selection-batch rather than per-call), following this repo's Rust-core-backend-boundary convention if the fix belongs in a shared layer rather than the TUI adapter.

plus_one_evidence.note:
Independently reproduced 13 days later at master a7b702863, and the confound this bead
asked to rule out first turns out not to be dischargeable.

REPRODUCTION (2026-08-27, athena, `pytest -s -m slow tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk.py -k
selected_tribe`), selected-tribe fold level 1 against `_SELECTED_TRIBE_P95_BUDGET_MS = 40.0`:

  full-file run: next p50 34.33 / p95 55.12 / max 324.98; prev p50 32.54 / p95 54.57 / max 329.73
  solo run 1:    next p50 32.87 / p95 50.66 / max  52.50; prev p50 34.11 / p95 61.20 / max 257.09
  solo run 2:    next p50 29.38 / p95 54.52 / max 236.03; prev p50 32.56 / p95 51.08 / max 234.46

That is the same non-outlier shape this bead recorded (p50 28-34 ms then, 29-34 ms now):
the median alone is 73-85% of the whole p95 budget, so half of all tribe hops still cost
about two 60 Hz frames. 3/3 runs fail, matching the original 3/3.

THE "RE-MEASURE ON A QUIET ATHENA" CONFOUND IS NOT DISCHARGEABLE AS WRITTEN. The original
report attributed load average ~18 on 64 cores to `yes` processes and a concurrent Rust
build. Today athena sits at load average 18.21 / 17.68 / 20.56 with no such session
running: the top consumers are routine `sase_chop_*` workers plus `sase` itself. Load ~18
on 64 cores (~28% utilization) is this host's ordinary resting state, not an artifact of
the measuring session, so "wait for a quiet athena" is not a step a future agent can
actually complete. Either the bench must tolerate athena as it normally runs, or the
budget has to be justified against a pinned-CPU environment.

A REMEDIATION THAT IS NOW VALIDATED IN THIS EXACT FILE. Epic sase-ug added a sibling
bench (`test_bench_agents_jk_with_and_without_the_link_rail`) and hit the same
instability, so the fix was worked out there and measured:

  - two sequential arms at n=20, p95 compared directly: delta spread -2.7 .. +7.2 ms,
    failing 2 of 8 runs on an unchanged tree;
  - four alternating short arms pooled to n=48 per direction: delta spread -2.8 .. +2.9 ms,
    passing 8 of 8.

Two effects drive that. First, at n=20 the p95 index is the 2nd-highest sample, so one
~250 ms scheduler stall moves it; at n=48 the index sits 2 samples below the top, so the
stall lands in `max` and leaves p95 alone. Second, this host's absolute j/k p50 drifts
between 12 ms and 20 ms across runs as background load changes; two measurements taken at
two different times sample that drift, while alternating short rounds let it fall on both.

`test_bench_axe_jk`, `test_bench_clan_jk_at_each_panel_fold_level`, and this scenario
would all keep their current user-visible budgets under that pooling -- it makes the
measurement robust without weakening the budget, which is what bead:sase-dx asked for.
Note the distinction this bead already drew still holds: axe and clan are the
outlier-p95-over-low-median shape (re-run alone, axe passes and clan reads p95 16.26 vs a
16.0 budget over a p50 of 11.29), whereas selected-tribe fails on its median.

Reported by the land agent for epic sase-ug while verifying that epic's own new bench in
this file. Not caused by sase-ug: this bead predates the epic, the numbers are unchanged,
and the epic's rail composes last (just above the footer) and is `display = False` until
an index has chips, so it occupies no layout row on the tribe path.

title: sase repo open's clean/reset silently destroys untracked files in a linked repo checkout, losing agent-authored work
description:
REPRODUCTION (2026-08-14, host project gh_sase-org__sase, linked repo 'research'):

Research clan research.0i dispatched two agents with the same prompt, which told each to write a report under $(sase repo path research --ensure)/$(date +%Y%m)/. Both chose the same filename.

- research.0i.cdx (codex/gpt-5.6-sol) ran in workspace sase_10 and wrote
  sase_10/sase/repos/research/202608/supergrok_subscription_tiers.md at 12:57:45Z.
- At 13:04:09Z, during its OWN commit finalizer, cdx invoked 'sase repo open research'.
  That command cleans the linked-repo checkout and resets it to origin/main. The report
  was still untracked, so the clean DELETED IT.
- The finalizer then recorded, in
  artifacts/ace-run/202608/14/20260814084958/commit_finalizer_result.json:
  {"changed_files": [], "reason": "clean_after_pass", "status": "finalized"}
- cdx then reported commit 21654c8 as its own. That commit is research.0i.cld's
  (authored [bbugyi200.athena.research.0i.cld][1]). cdx committed nothing.

The work is UNRECOVERABLE. Confirmed exhausted:
- git fsck --dangling / --lost-found: empty (checkout is a fresh clone; the file never
  entered any object store). git stash and reflog: clone-only.
- tool_calls.jsonl records the Write call but only as a summary with
  'content_length: 0' -- no content is captured.
- codex_thinking.jsonl: 0 bytes. No commit_diff.diff for that run. No rendered
  markdown_pdfs/ for that run (only for cld's).

IMPACT
An agent that writes a file into a linked repo checkout and then opens that same repo
(exactly what the /sase_repo skill instructs it to do before committing) destroys its
own uncommitted work, silently, and then reports success. This is not specific to
research clans -- any agent that produces a file in a linked repo and follows the
mandatory /sase_repo workflow before committing is exposed. The failure is invisible:
the finalizer's empty diff looks identical to 'nothing to do'.

SCOPE / DESIGN QUESTIONS FOR THE WORKER
- 'sase repo open' should not silently discard untracked files. Options: refuse to clean
  when the checkout has untracked/modified paths and report them; stash and report;
  preserve untracked files across the reset; or clean only when the caller explicitly
  asks. Pick one and make the default non-destructive.
- The finalizer should distinguish 'clean because nothing was written' from 'clean
  because a reset discarded what was written', and must not let an agent report a commit
  hash it did not author (cdx reported another agent's HEAD as its own).
- Separately, the multi-agent research prompt template points concurrent agents at the
  same output path in a shared linked repo. Even with the clean fixed, two agents writing
  one path race. Consider per-agent filenames or per-agent checkouts.

DISCOVERED BY the lead researcher consolidating that clan's reports; the loss was found
because only one of the two expected reports existed.

DISCOVERED ISSUE (found by sase-n8.land while landing epic sase-n8): the release-core-floor-smoke job fails on every recent CI run, and because it fails early it fail-fasts the whole workflow — lint, test, visual-test, perf-floors, coverage-contexts, docs-build, build-core, ace-page-group-isolation and contention-test all report 'skipped'. Net effect: no CI signal at all on master right now.

Evidence: 'gh run view 31975415240 --log-failed' (head db922adf9, 'chore(master): release 0.17.0', 2026-08-16T22:07Z) ends '52 failed, 399 passed in 31.71s' in the 'Run contract set' step. Every one of the 52 failures is the same error — FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'just' — from tests that shell out to the just binary: all of tests/test_justfile_lint.py, all of tests/test_justfile_sase_core_dir.py, and tests/test_run_pytest_contention.py::test_contention_is_unreachable_from_the_verification_recipes[check|check-full]. The job runs those tests without installing just.

Not a one-off: runs 31975094180 (5bac0d89c), 31974893913 (8652c4a64), 31974723858 (2b30d57c6) and 31974604835 (ac7d973d8) all fail in release-core-floor-smoke with visual-test skipped. Every master-commit run in the same window is 'cancelled' (superseded by the next push at this commit cadence), so the release-please branch runs are the only ones that finish — and they all fail here.

Routed to sase-m4 rather than a standalone task because this epic's charter is exactly 'restore reliable passing CI, documentation, and publication workflows on the sase default branch', its phase sase-m4.1 owns the core release floor ratcheting this job smoke-tests, and its own landing note records that m4.6 final acceptance ('no green master CI run') was never reached — this is a concrete, currently-reproducing instance of that unmet acceptance. Likely fix is adding the just binary to that job's setup (or excluding the just-dependent nodes from the contract set), but the epic owns the call.

Also relevant to this epic: CI's visual-test job cannot currently give signal even when it does run — see the DISCOVERED ISSUE note recorded on epic sase-m6 and the corroboration on task sase-nq, where commit 3c9df1182 renamed ACE keymap labels without regenerating goldens, leaving 41/48 models-panel and 6 base ACE PNG nodes deterministically red on clean master.

title: ACE Patch pane: 'o' is double-booked, so mark_pr_origin shadows cycle_grouping_mode and forward grouping-cycle is unreachable
description:
docs/ace.md:614 and the Patch info panel both promise that 'o'/'O' cycle the Patch grouping mode forward/reverse (BY_PROJECT -> BY_DATE -> BY_STATUS). Only 'O' works. 'o' opens the PR-origin modal instead.

ROOT CAUSE
src/sase/ace/tui/keymaps/metadata.py binds two app actions to the same default key:
  index  27: ('mark_pr_origin', 'Mark PR Origin', False)
  index 154: ('cycle_grouping_mode', 'Cycle Grouping', False)
Both default to 'o' in src/sase/default_config.yml (mark_pr_origin: "o", cycle_grouping_mode: "o") and both have priority=False. build_app_bindings() preserves _BINDING_META order, and Textual's App._check_bindings (textual 8.0.1, app.py:3905-3915) walks key_to_bindings[key] in insertion order and stops at the first binding whose run_action succeeds. mark_pr_origin is enabled on the whole Artifacts tab (_app_action_availability.py:172-174: only blocks current_tab != ARTIFACTS_TAB), so it always wins on the Patch pane and cycle_grouping_mode is never reached. The other two 'o' bindings (beads_open_bug, files_open_external) are pane-gated and correctly inert on Patches.

REPRODUCTION (executed on master e4baf0771, workspace sase_12)
  from sase.ace.tui.keymaps import load_keymap_registry
  from sase.ace.tui.keymaps.bindings import build_app_bindings
  reg = load_keymap_registry({})
  [(b.action, b.priority) for b in build_app_bindings(reg.app) if b.key == 'o']
  -> [('mark_pr_origin', False), ('beads_open_bug', False),
      ('files_open_external', False), ('cycle_grouping_mode', False)]
  [(b.action, b.priority) for b in build_app_bindings(reg.app) if b.key == 'O']
  -> [('cycle_grouping_mode_reverse', False)]

IMPACT
Forward grouping-cycle is unreachable on the Patch pane; users must press 'O' twice to advance one step. action_cycle_grouping_mode's Patch arm (actions/agents/_grouping.py:248-262) is dead code from the keyboard. src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/patch_info_panel.py:198 renders the '[group: <label>]' badge using key_display_name(app.cycle_grouping_mode), so the UI advertises a key that does not work.

SCOPE
Decide which action moves. Options: move mark_pr_origin behind the bang-mode prefix ('!o'), give it a distinct default key, or scope its availability so it only claims 'o' when it is contextually meaningful. Then update src/sase/default_config.yml, docs/ace.md (Navigation and PR Actions tables), the help modal (modals/help_modal/patches_bindings.py:71,251), and add a regression test asserting that no two app-level bindings share a default key while both being enabled on the same tab/pane.

NOTE
Found while researching the Artifacts pane contract unification (sase/repos/research/202608/unified_artifacts_pane_contract.md, section 1.3). Not caused by that work.

notes.author: sase-m6.6.1.5
notes.text:
Steps 1-3 of the 7-step plan (sase/repos/plans/202608/flat_pane_query_migration.md) are implemented, verified, and committed to master:
1. ArtifactsPaneContract now carries a real compiled CompiledQueryProfile (query_schema promoted from empty placeholder), included in presentation digest and explain output, covering healthy/degraded/built-in/synthetic-provider contracts.
2. New host facade src/sase/core/query_profile_corpus_facade.py wraps compile_corpus_with_profile / compile_query_with_profile / evaluate_many / parse_query_with_profile / canonicalize_query_with_profile with immutable ArtifactQueryIndex/ArtifactQueryResult records and an exact (pane_id, generation, profile_digest, canonical_query) cache key. Date literals resolve via the Python reference canonicalizer before Rust sees them.
3. Shared FilterBar widget is now instance-configurable from a compiled profile (key completions, static values, negation, repeatability, free-text hint, completion context).

Also fixed three real correctness bugs this wiring exposed in the already-closed sase-m6.6.1.2/.3 work (all now covered by tests, in both sase and the linked sase-core repo, committed to both):
- Rust's flat matcher always did exact-match on string fields (Patch-only assumption); added exact_match to the field schema (Rust + Python + wire + digest).
- Rust never implemented since/until date-range comparison (was plain string equality, silently zero matches).
- Python's flat canonicalizer fell back to boolean OR syntax for repeated same-key terms, which the flat-only Rust grammar can't parse.

Verified: just check passes clean (lint including symvision -- added --epic-symbol 'sase-m6.6.1.5(...)' whitelist entries in the Justfile for the new facade's symbols that steps 4-7 below will consume) and the full test-scoped suite, modulo two pre-existing flaky tests unrelated to this diff (independently investigated and routed: +1'd sase-lk with a fresh reproduction, and added a DISCOVERED ISSUE note to epic sase-j7 for test_procs_service.py::test_settlement_resumes_after_an_injected_crash).

NOT done -- steps 4-7 remain and this bead should stay in_progress:
4. Row adapters + off-thread index construction for Stitches, Beads, Plans, Files, and provider panes.
5. Migrate each pane's filter session (Stitches, Beads, Plans, Files) onto the shared parse/canonicalize/evaluate path, replacing their bespoke row matchers, while preserving session rollback/selection-restore/coverage/background-load behavior. Stitches does not use the shared ArtifactsSnapshotPane base and needs its own integration; Plans carries deep-archive coverage on top.
6. Enable negation for Files fields/free-text and the closed host predicate atoms, in both Rust and Python, with parity coverage.
7. Extend the Artifacts conformance harness and the artifacts-nav perf benchmark (tests/ace/tui/bench_artifacts_jk.py, which does not yet cover Beads or Files) to cover the migrated panes.

Left in_progress deliberately: closing this bead now would misrepresent an incomplete phase. Per sase_beads.md, sase bead work sase-m6.6.1 can reassign this phase to continue steps 4-7.

notes.author: chop.refresh_docs.sase.4_900125.1
notes.text: DISCOVERED ISSUE: Grouping/fold and relation keybindings are unreachable outside the Patches pane. NON_PRS_ARTIFACT_ACTIONS in src/sase/ace/tui/actions/artifacts.py:40 was not extended when f5dda81f3 (phase .5, shared fold registry) routed h/l/H/L/o/O and a0b6cd16b (phase .3, generalized relation navigation) mounted relation navigation across panes. check_app_action therefore returns False for cycle_grouping_mode, cycle_grouping_mode_reverse, expand_or_layout, hooks_or_collapse, hooks_or_collapse_all, expand_all_folds, start_ancestor_mode, start_child_mode, and start_sibling_mode on every non-Patches Artifacts pane, so Textual skips the binding entirely. Verified against a live AcePage: on Stitches, 'o' leaves the grouping mode at by_date and '<' leaves _ancestor_mode_active False. Net effect: the shared fold registry and host-rendered relation panel both render but cannot be driven from the keyboard, and Files/Beads/Plans silently fall through to their own o/L bindings. No test covers the key path — existing tests call pane.group_cycle_mode() and the action methods directly, which is why this passed. Suggest phase .6 (Conformance, docs, and the relation performance gate) add a conformance check that every declared grouping/relation action is actually reachable per pane. Found 2026-08-16 during the docs refresh; documented as a current limitation in docs/ace.md and docs/artifacts_pane_visual_grammar.md rather than fixed, since that agent was scoped to documentation only.

title: chezmoi just check is not idempotent: pytest_cache/README.md trips fmt-md-check on repeat runs
description: Repo: chezmoi (linked repo, opened via /sase_repo). Reproduction: from a clean chezmoi checkout, run 'just check' once — it passes (fmt-check, lint, test all green). Run 'just check' again immediately without any source changes — it now fails at the fmt-check stage: prettier --check --prose-wrap=always --print-width=88 '**/*.md' reports 'Code style issues found in .pytest_cache/README.md' and 'fmt-md-check' exits 1. Root cause: the 'test-python' recipe runs 'cd home/lib/xfile && ../../../.venv/bin/pytest test', but pytest resolves its rootdir from the repo-root pyproject.toml (not the cwd), so pytest writes its .pytest_cache/README.md at the chezmoi repo root instead of inside home/lib/xfile. That directory is listed in .gitignore (so 'git status' stays clean) but prettier's '**/*.md' glob does not respect .gitignore and still matches it, so any 'just check' run following a prior test run fails deterministically until the cache dir is manually removed. Impact: 'just check' (and thus 'just install'-adjacent CI-style validation) is unreliable for any agent that runs it more than once in the same checkout, which is a common pattern (e.g. run once, fix something unrelated, run again to confirm). Fix options: (1) add .pytest_cache to .prettierignore or pass --ignore-path .gitignore to the prettier invocation in the fmt-md/fmt-md-check Justfile recipes, or (2) pin pytest's cache-dir/rootdir (e.g. -o cache_dir=... or a rootdir override) so the artifact never lands at the repo root. Discovered while validating an approved plan (sase/repos/plans/202608/gemini_37_flash_antigravity.md) that only touched home/bin/executable_tmux_ai_window, home/dot_config/sase/sase.yml, and tests/bash/tmux_ai_window_test.sh in the chezmoi repo — this bug is unrelated to those changes; the first 'just check' run against them was clean, only the second (rerun after 'rm -rf .pytest_cache') failed until cleaned again.

FIX: '.pytest_cache/' added to the chezmoi repo's .prettierignore, which now reads '.luarocks/', '.pytest_cache/', '.venv/'. Option 1 from the bead's scope. Both prettier recipes in the chezmoi Justfile ('fmt-md' at line 63 writes, 'fmt-md-check' at line 81 checks) invoke bare 'prettier ... "**/*.md"' with no --ignore-path, so both pick up the repo-root .prettierignore automatically and stay consistent with each other -- the consistency condition the bead asked for.

VERIFICATION by the land agent on 2026-08-17, reproducing the exact reported regression in the linked chezmoi checkout: planted a deliberately unformatted .pytest_cache/README.md (long lines, irregular spacing -- prettier would rewrite it), then ran 'just fmt-md-check' -> 'All matched files use Prettier code style!'. The directory remains gitignored, so it never reaches git status; only prettier's glob saw it, and that is now handled at the ignore layer.

title: Supervisor-owned procs and the sase shell model

title: CI flake: large publication-queue backlog exceeds 1.0s wall-clock bound
description:
REPRODUCTION: Scheduled master CI run 31870783076 (https://github.com/sase-org/sase/actions/runs/31870783076) for d19d08641246a2b0f9276fded07d93004815d640 failed job test (3.12) (job 94979384829) with exactly one node after 30157 passed / 56 skipped:

  tests/agents_sync/test_commit_publication_queue.py::test_large_backlog_builds_one_inventory_and_publishes_each_hood_once
  AssertionError: assert 1.5754990230000203 < 1.0
  at tests/agents_sync/test_commit_publication_queue.py:249

The same SHA's earlier push CI run 31861402259 had test (3.12) green, so this is load-sensitive rather than a deterministic break on that tip. Functional assertions in the failing node passed: result.error is None, drained == 2000, one integrate call, one inventory build, one publish per hood, 500-key updates, and the acknowledge set. Only the extra wall-clock guard `assert elapsed < 1.0` around `_publish_queued_locked` failed.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is now a required default-branch CI job failure, not only a local contention tally. sase-h8.10.5.3 already recorded this exact node as a 1/3 just test-contention flake (2026-08-08) and routed it to retired umbrella sase-ct / sase-h8. sase-ct's close reason forbids +1 and requires a narrow task.

SCOPE: decide whether `_publish_queued_locked` genuinely got slower on a 2000-item / 4-hood backlog, or whether the 1.0s perf_counter bound is too tight for GitHub Actions / contended hosts. Do not delete the performance contract. Prefer a contention-independent check (call counts already asserted in the test) or a bound calibrated from recorded CI/history, and keep a regression tripwire. Not attributable to stabilization commit 5601920c9 (ancestor; Python 3.12 passed on the same SHA's push run). Not a process-global leak for epic sase-j7.

VERIFY: the node stays green in isolation and under just test-contention, and a loaded CI-shaped run no longer fails only that wall-clock assert.

RELATED: sase-ct (retired umbrella; do not +1), sase-h8.10.5.3 (prior 1/3 contention tally), sase-j0 (separate 3.13 post-pytest cost-gate redness on the same scheduled run).

notes.author: sase-ns.6.land
notes.text:
Fixed by epic sase-ns.6 phase sase-ns.6.2, commit d9b2984a7 'fix(tui): isolate config center state replacement'. Closed by that epic's land agent because the phase worker did not perform its plan-mandated bead bookkeeping.

ROOT CAUSE (not just the symptom): the atomic-save tests monkeypatched config_center_state.os.replace. That attribute is the shared Python 'os' module object, so the patch replaced os.replace process-wide on the pytest-xdist worker for the duration of the test, and any concurrently-running test on that worker that replaced a file hit the test's assertion-bearing stub. That is why the node failed only under the full parallel lane and passed instantly in isolation, and why four unrelated agents reproduced it from diffs that never touched Config Center persistence.

FIX: save_admin_center_tab_history() now calls a module-local _replace_state_file(source, target) wrapper (src/sase/ace/tui/modals/config_center_state.py). The two atomic-save tests patch only that local seam, and the success test additionally asserts 'os.replace is real_replace' so a future regression back to a process-wide patch fails loudly. The atomic-replace assertion is intact and unweakened: the stub still verifies the temporary file holds the new content and the destination still holds the old content at replace time.

VERIFICATION: phase sase-ns.6.2 ran the focused suite 23/23 and SASE_CONTENTION_REPEAT=10 SASE_CONTENTION_WORKERS=8 'just test-contention' on the node (10/10 repeats, 0 failed nodes), and its 'just check' escalated to the full non-visual suite with the node green. title: sase_git_commit blocks in agent-hood rendering after pushing the commit
description: REPRODUCTION: During the post-completion finalizer for commit 5b4d5b3c6 on 2026-08-15, sase_git_commit -M .sase/commit_message.md printed the before-commit hook, reported create_commit completed successfully, warned that prompt archive publication was skipped because raw_xprompt.md was unavailable, and pushed the commit: git status was clean and HEAD matched origin/master at 5b4d5b3c6. The wrapper then stayed alive for several minutes in post-commit tracking while holding /home/bryan/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/repos/agents/.git/sase-agents-sync.lock. ps showed the process in D state with WCHAN folio_wait_bit_common, and Ctrl-C produced a traceback through run_agent_publication_step -> publish_committed_agent_hood -> _publish_queued_locked -> publish_queued_transaction -> _prepare_publications -> hooks.publish_hood -> render_browsing_payload -> render_agent_page -> render_neighbors_section -> relative_page_url -> posixpath.relpath. IMPACT: the VCS commit and push are complete, but the finalizer has to interrupt the wrapper, leaving the commit workflow with exit 130 and no normal cleanup of the temporary message file. SCOPE: investigate and bound/fix agent-hood publication rendering after the primary commit, preserving durable retry and clean commit semantics. This is not the dismissed_bundles/registry scan fixed by closed task sase-cl; the observed stack is in agent page neighbor rendering.

notes.author: sase-mi.land
notes.text: Fixed by epic sase-mi phase 6 (commit 392dcc962). publish_committed_agent_hood in src/sase/agents_sync/commit_publication.py now runs the synchronous drain inside _bounded_publication_drain, a SIGALRM itimer bounded by SASE_AGENTS_PUBLICATION_DRAIN_TIMEOUT (default 120s). The alarm unwinds the same call stack that is already inside bounded_agents_lock's with block, so that existing finally releases sase-agents-sync.lock -- no untracked thread and no abandoned process is left able to mutate the sidecar after the lock is gone, which was the explicit constraint on this fix. A stall is routed through _record_failure, so the request stays in the durable outbox for sase agent sync to retry, the already-pushed primary commit is untouched, and incomplete work is never acknowledged; fast publication and quarantine/retirement semantics are unchanged. The bound is skipped rather than faked when SIGALRM is unavailable or the caller is not the main thread; the commit workflow reaching this path (workflows/commit/workflow_publication.py) runs on the CLI main thread. Verified by the landing agent at HEAD daf933aa5: tests/agents_sync/test_commit_publication_bounded_drain.py covers a blocked render staying bounded with the request retained and a later drain retrying successfully, and the full tests/agents_sync suite plus tests/llm_provider/test_commit_finalizer_bead_publication.py are green in a 381-test focused batch; the phase-5 large-backlog node still passes, so the new boundary reintroduced no per-request or per-hood work.

Reproduced 2026-08-15 ~22:00 EDT from workspace sase_12 on master 117476b7d: 'sase bead +1 sase-mk --note ...' failed and recorded nothing (bead history sase-mk still ends at the 01:48:51Z issue_updated event), and an unrelated 'sase bead note sase-mf ...' failed with the SAME sase-mk error even though its own note event WAS appended locally (bead history sase-mf shows my note_appended at 02:02:13Z) — so writes now land in the worktree but can never be published, and the failure is attributed to whichever stream is dirty rather than the bead being written. 'sase bead doctor' reports 'bead state has uncommitted changes' plus 14 ERROR-level rewritten/short streams already in published history (sase-m5 ev3, sase-m7 ev2, sase-m8 ev2, sase-mb ev6, sase-m4 ev46, sase-md ev2, sase-me ev5, sase-ll ev11, sase-lk ev11, sase-mh ev4, sase-jw ev6, sase-mk ev2, sase-ml ev3, and sase-j7 shorter than its own history missing events 62-63), each naming a first offending commit. Causal link: phase sase-mi.2 'Protect append-only bead event streams' added the commit/push guard (b681d1bc3) that is now, correctly, refusing a store whose history was already rewritten before the guard existed; nothing repairs or quarantines that pre-existing damage, so the guard converts old corruption into a total write outage. Phase sase-mi.7 owns verifying the combined tree and reconciling task beads. Suggested scope for the fix: repair or quarantine the 14 damaged streams, and make the commit path fail only for the streams actually being written (or report every offending stream) instead of aborting an unrelated bead's write. Reported here rather than as a task because filing a task bead is itself blocked by this defect. RELATED: sase-li (concurrent bead sync can silently delete an event from a shared stream — plausible upstream cause of these rewrites); sase-mk (in-progress symvision task whose +1 evidence I could not record because of this).

notes.text:
VERIFIED (step 1). Read the plan (plans:202608/statistics_perf_view.md), all five phase beads and every phase note, and the four epic commits against the actual source.
- sase-mj.1 / core_perf_logs: sibling sase-core has crates/sase_core/src/perf_logs/{mod,sources,aggregate,wire}.rs registered at lib.rs:49/604 and the PyO3 binding py_perf_logs_query at crates/sase_core_py/src/lib.rs:8451 with module registration at 9099, the documented binding list at 262, and the round-trip test at 14192. Wire defaults for max_records_per_source / max_bytes_per_source are serde defaults (wire.rs:7/11/51-54), which is why the Python adapter can omit them. Landed as d0ac555 and published in sase-core v0.27.10.
- sase-mj.2 / stats_facade: src/sase/stats/perf_query.py is a thin adapter (require_rust_binding('perf_logs_query'), six env-overridable log paths, the plan's enumerated telemetry fan-out with grouped variants replacing rather than adding to the ungrouped ones, one store_stats call, never raising on a disabled/empty store); src/sase/stats/_perf_view.py holds the I/O-free frozen view models plus build_perf_view with HealthThresholds-based grading, deltas, and coverage notes; both are exported from sase/stats/__init__.py; load_statistics_view builds PerfView only when view == 'perf' (statistics_pane_data.py:163-165).
- sase-mj.3 / perf_view: 'perf' is last in VIEW_ORDER with Perf/Perf/Prf labels and a description, statistics_view_supports_grouping returns True for perf, the tab-strip thresholds are 123/83, and the help modal has the Perf methodology section. The views.empty bypass includes perf (statistics_pane_rendering.py:113) and the dimmed '· not applied' project chip is at 359-372.
- sase-mj.4 / perf_render: statistics_pane_perf.py holds StatisticsPerfRenderingMixin with the five hero tiles, startup and stalls panels, the grouped latency table, the data-and-instrumentation strip, and every degraded/empty state; _PERF_STACK_BELOW_WIDTH is 108 with the matching on_resize branch; tiles are non-interactive.
- sase-mj.5 / perf_visuals: the three PNG goldens (perf_120x40, perf_90x30, perf_degraded_120x40) exist and docs/perf_runbook.md has the 'Reading the Admin Center Perf view' section with panel/metric mapping, retention caveats, and probe flags.

INTEGRATED (step 2). Reviewed all 21 non-epic commits landed since the epic opened (2026-08-15 20:25). No other commit touched src/sase/stats or any statistics_pane* module, so there were no conflicts, and src/sase/ace/tui/logs/sources.py only registers the same JSONL files as raw Logs-tab tails, which is the separation the plan intends - no duplicated aggregation to fold in.
The one real integration item was this bead's own DISCOVERED ISSUE, filed twice by unrelated agents: pyproject declared sase-core-rs>=0.27.9 while perf_logs_query first shipped in v0.27.10, so the advisory core-floor probe reported stale_actionable. Reconciled with the owning tool, 'just ratchet-core-window', which bumped pyproject.toml and uv.lock from >=0.27.9,<0.28.0 to >=0.27.11,<0.28.0 (0.27.11 is the newest complete published release and contains the binding). This follows the established land-agent precedent (9d9d49959 by sase-mg.land, 4ba7ee812, ca93686a6). The probe now exits clean. That bump broke tests/test_powerful_variables_landing.py, whose floor guard pinned the exact string 'sase-core-rs>=0.27.9,<0.28.0'; since .github/workflows/publish.yml runs the same ratchet automatically on the release branch, that guard would have failed on every future release, so it was rewritten to compare the parsed floor against its intended minimum (0, 27, 9) instead of pinning it.

VERIFICATION RUN. just install, then every check-full gate individually: ruff format, ruff, mypy (3195 + 39 files), keep-sorted, pyscripts, test-waits, changelog, patch/stitch terminology, toobig, sase validate, committed plans (3750 files, 0 errors), and the core-floor probe - all green. just test-scoped escalated to the full suite: 30689 passed, 11 skipped, 2 failed, both pre-existing and unrelated (sase-mp and sase-mv below). Two gates are red on master for reasons this epic did not cause and did not touch: lint (symvision) fails only on FilesQueryIndexResult (sase-mn), and selection-health --fail-on-new-flake fails on the sase-mp and sase-mv nodes.

FOLLOW-UPS ROUTED.
- sase-mj.2 and sase-mj.3 proposed symvision private-cross-file-import failures (models_panel_provider_*, _now helpers): already resolved on this HEAD - just _lint-symvision no longer reports any private-import failure. Tracked by existing task sase-mk. No new bead.
- sase-mj.4 proposed nine unused public symbols: eight (PublicationDrainTimedOut, StreamIntegrityResult, analyze_stream_against_ancestor, clear_agent_page_url_registry_cache, configured_publication_drain_timeout, encode_stream_events, is_event_stream_relpath, parse_stream_text) were fixed by daf933aa5 from epic sase-mi. The ninth, FilesQueryIndexResult, is already task sase-mn; corroborated with an independent reproduction (+4) rather than duplicated.
- sase-mj.4 proposed a flaky test_override_pills_keep_narrow_top_bar_in_bounds. It is not flaky - it fails deterministically in isolation. Already filed as sase-mp with the same root cause I independently confirmed (llm_override_indicator reads peek_active_temporary_override on the render paths while the test patches get_active_temporary_override, first bad commit 233d62463); corroborated with +1 (+2) rather than duplicated.
- sase-mj.3 proposed that a beads close publish was blocked by a stream rewrite of ancestor event 5. Declined as no longer reproducing: every bead mutation in this landing (one create, four notes, two +1s, one status update, this close) succeeded, and b681d1bc3 plus f935acace landed the append-only shrink guards. The class is covered by closed task sase-li.
- NEW, found by this landing: tests/test_config_cache.py::test_owner_snapshot_reuses_parsed_overlay_until_token_changes fails only in the full parallel lane and passes in isolation and under file-scoped contention (3 repeats, 0 failures). sase-ct is a retired umbrella that forbids +1, so per its close policy this became node-specific task sase-mv (large, ready) with RELATED notes to sase-ct, sase-j7, and sase-mp, plus a note widening it to cover the sibling node test_clear_config_cache_forces_reload that the flake gate names.
- No symvision --epic-symbol whitelist entries exist for sase-mj in the Justfile, so nothing expires at this close.

TREE STATE: pyproject.toml, uv.lock, and tests/test_powerful_variables_landing.py carry the uncommitted integration change described above.

description:
DISCOVERED while running the full `just test` suite (not the required `just check` scoped lane) as extra diligence while implementing the approved plan sase/repos/plans/202608/adaptive_models_panel_description_height.md (Launch Control description-height change touching only src/sase/ace/tui/modals/models_panel_display.py, src/sase/ace/tui/styles.tcss, and Models-panel tests). `just test-scoped` (the actual required `just check` test lane) passed 745/745 clean; `just test-visual` passed 684/684 clean. The full `just test` run failed 60 tests, 30545 passed, 10 skipped, all in files unrelated to the diff: tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py, tests/test_gate_cli_act.py, tests/gate_conformance/test_gate_conformance.py (every cli-* and ace-* case), tests/main/test_ops_commands.py, tests/test_special_cases.py, tests/test_partial_launch_cleanup.py, tests/test_prompt_inputs.py, tests/test_multi_prompt_e2e.py, tests/ace/tui/modals/test_snippet_name_modal.py.

ROOT CAUSE (partially diagnosed, reproduced in isolation): re-running two of the failing tests together in isolation (tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py::test_set_types_every_declared_input_field + tests/test_special_cases.py::test_launch_query_from_agent_context_requests_approval) reproduces both failures deterministically. test_special_cases reveals real contamination: the mocked create_launch_approval_request_from_prompt is called with THIS actual live agent session's real prompt text ('#gh:sase The last model in the model pool shown in #sshot is cut off...') instead of the test's own literal input string, proving some code path under test reads real, live host session state (this very running sase agent's own launch/session data) rather than being fully isolated from environment. test_gate_cli_answer fails with `sase.ops.errors.OperationIOError: operation sidecar /home/bryan/.sase/procs/runtime/<real-pid>/operation-request.json has operation 'run.launch', expected 'gate.answer'` -- a real path under the live ~/.sase/procs/runtime tree, not a tmp_path fixture. A second isolated repro (tests/main/test_ops_commands.py::test_patch_status_success_and_failure_results) shows the SAME operation-mismatch error even though that test's result path is a fresh pytest tmp_path (`/tmp/pytest-of-bryan/.../ok.json`) with content `operation: 'run.launch'` -- meaning code under test wrote (or resolved) the wrong sidecar despite an explicit path argument, strongly suggesting a global/env-var-driven operation-context resolution (e.g. a real SASE_PROC_ID/operation-sidecar env var set in this live host shell) that these tests do not fully override via monkeypatch, so under `just test`'s parallel/full-process conditions the tests intermittently observe or write against this live host's actual 'run.launch' operation state instead of their own mocked/fixture state.

This differs from the already-tracked sase-lc (dirty-workspace source-tree audits contaminating the flake-baseline store) -- that bug is about audit tests reading an agent's own uncommitted source edits; this bug is about operation/gate/launch-CLI tests reading real live ~/.sase/procs/runtime state from the actual host session rather than being hermetically isolated, which only manifests when running the full unscoped suite (never observed in `just test-scoped` or `just test-visual`). Searched for existing task beads with 'gate_cli_answer', 'gate_conformance', 'test_ops_commands', 'operation sidecar', 'OperationIOError', 'run.launch' -- none found; also swept task beads created in the last 3 days and found only the related-but-distinct sase-lc.

IMPACT: blocks `just check-full` / plain `just test` from completing cleanly for any agent working from a live, actively-running host session (as opposed to a disposable CI sandbox), even on an otherwise clean diff. Project guidance already routes check-full through `/sase_monitor`, which may avoid this by running out-of-process, but the underlying hermeticity gap in these ops/gate/launch tests should be fixed directly.

REPRODUCTION: from a live sase agent shell, run e.g. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_gate_cli_answer.py::test_set_types_every_declared_input_field tests/main/test_ops_commands.py::test_patch_status_success_and_failure_results -q` and observe the OperationIOError 'run.launch' mismatch; or the full `just test` lane.

notes.text: RELATED: sase-lc — different mechanism (dirty-tree audit contamination of flake-baseline store vs. live ~/.sase/procs/runtime state bleeding into gate/ops/launch CLI tests), but both are examples of a live/dirty agent workspace polluting full-suite test results; a shared fix theme (stronger test isolation from the live host session) may be worth considering together.

The focused regression suite for this change passed 102 tests before the full-lane failure, and this diff does not touch gate/ops CLI sidecar resolution.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE (write direction, durable proof): while root-causing a phantom 'running proc' in ACE on 2026-08-16, found that pytest processes do not merely READ live ~/.sase/procs state — they WRITE rows into the user's real proc store, and those rows persist. /home/bryan/.sase/procs/procs.jsonl contained 21 kind='tui', lifecycle='legacy' rows whose cwd is an ephemeral agent workspace (sase_14, sase_15, sase_16, sase_17, sase_19, sase_20) rather than a real checkout, carrying unmistakable test-fixture payloads: label 'kill my_feature' (the my_feature fixture agent used by tests/test_agent_kill_single_actions.py) and message 'Kill cleanup failed for my_feature: boom' (a test double raising Exception('boom')). One of those leaked rows (proc_id hbw7szt6mnbh, session 20260816T013806Z-2654527, pid 2654527, started 2026-08-16T01:39:49Z) was still status='running' with finished_at=null roughly twelve hours later, its pid long dead. It inflated the live ACE session's top-bar proc indicator to 1 while the Admin Center Procs tab (session-scoped) correctly showed 0 running, and it blocked a completed 'sase update' from restarting ACE, because the restart gate treats any projected running row as a blocker.

MECHANISM: unlike the bead store (assert_bead_store_write_sandboxed) and telemetry (assert_test_state_write_isolated), the proc store has NO write guard. src/sase/procs/store.py resolves proc_store_path() and calls straight into the Rust binding from append_proc/reserve_proc/update_proc/finish_proc with no pytest-sandbox check. tests/_conftest_environment.py isolates SASE_HOME per test via monkeypatch, so any write that lands AFTER fixture teardown — a thread worker or Textual worker still running, e.g. the submit worker _submit_durable_proc spawns at src/sase/ace/tui/actions/proc_actions.py:273 — resolves the REAL ~/.sase and writes there. That teardown-race path exists at HEAD, so this is not confined to the older ACE mirror writer that produced these particular rows.

SUGGESTED REMEDIATION (same boundary this bead needs): give proc state under ~/.sase/procs the fail-closed guard the bead/telemetry stores already have, so a pytest process either writes inside SASE_PYTEST_SANDBOX_DIR or raises. That would have turned this silent corruption of the user's real store into a loud test failure, and it covers both the read contamination this bead reports and the write leak reported here.

IMPACT: silent corruption of the user's production proc store by test runs, plus a user-visible ACE defect (phantom running-proc count, blocked post-update restart). No new task bead created; a separate tale plan covers the ACE-side reconciliation and count-consistency fixes for the symptom.
