One additional failure (tests/test_tui_plan_approval_archive.py) was a real regression in this diff and is fixed separately. This change does not touch ops/gate sidecar resolution.

CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE with a controlled A/B — the leaked variables are SASE_PROC_REQUEST_PATH / SASE_PROC_RESULT_PATH / SASE_PROC_ID (src/sase/ops/models.py:12-15). Independent repro: 'just check-full' via /sase_monitor from a live agent (monitor 563h2j93e61t, 2026-08-16T14:05Z, workspace sase_15 on 78a9130f7) failed 72/30915. My agent shell had SASE_PROC_REQUEST_PATH=/home/bryan/.sase/procs/runtime/kq6tayvcwdkh/operation-request.json with SASE_PROC_OPERATION=run.launch — byte-for-byte the path in every 'OperationIOError: ... has operation run.launch, expected gate.answer' failure. sase/ops/cli.py:85 load_request() -> resolve_request_path() falls back to os.environ.get(REQUEST_ENV) when no -Q/--request-path is given, so the monitor subprocess inherited MY live agent's sidecar. This CONFIRMS the bead's 'strongly suggesting a global/env-var-driven operation-context resolution' hypothesis and names the variables. PROOF (A/B, same tree, same commit): running the 13 failing files with the vars inherited reproduces the failures; 'env -u SASE_PROC_REQUEST_PATH -u SASE_PROC_RESULT_PATH -u SASE_PROC_ID -u SASE_PROC_OPERATION -u SASE_PROC_LOG_PATH -u SASE_PROC_SESSION_ID .venv/bin/python -m pytest <13 files> -n 8' gives 240 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed — and that single remaining failure was a genuine unrelated stale assertion I fixed. So 71 of the 72 failures are 100 percent this bug. NOTE: /sase_monitor does NOT avoid this (the bead speculated it might) — the monitor supervisor inherits the launching agent's SASE_PROC_* rather than scoping its own. SUGGESTED FIX: an autouse conftest fixture that monkeypatch.delenv's every SASE_PROC_* var, so ambient operation context can never reach a test; a targeted workaround for agents needing a clean full suite today is the 'env -u ...' prefix above.

title: test_override_pills_keep_narrow_top_bar_in_bounds fails on master: the pill now reads peek_active_temporary_override but the test patches get_active_temporary_override

Reproduction: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ace/tui/test_top_bar_order.py::test_override_pills_keep_narrow_top_bar_in_bounds -q -p no:randomly  ->  1 failed in ~1.8s. Fails on every attempt, in isolation and under 'just test-scoped' (where it was the only failure out of 30,677).

', line 35/198) because the off-thread default resolve has not completed inside the test app.

Scope: decide whether peek_active_temporary_override is the intended display source (then repoint the test's monkeypatch at it, and check the sibling asserts in the same file that still pass) or whether the widget should fall back to the authoritative read when the peek is cold (then fix the widget). Only the default-model pill is affected; the alias and provider-disable asserts in the same test pass. Re-run the whole tests/ace/tui/test_top_bar_order.py file plus 'just check'.

title: write_event_store rewrites every bead event stream file on every mutation
description:
Discovered 2026-08-16 while root-causing the bead-store wedge that blocked epic launches (fixed in sase-core 2233171, sase 5184f5ab0).

crates/sase_core/src/bead/jsonl.rs:288-306 in the sibling sase-core repo re-serializes and rewrites EVERY stream file on every bead mutation, not just the streams whose events changed. The store currently holds 853 streams, so appending a single note to one bead rewrites all 853 files.

Two concrete consequences, both observed:

1. Blast radius. A single event that is not round-trip stable wedges the ENTIRE store rather than one bead. That is exactly what happened: one 'resolution: null' event in sase-mk.jsonl failed to round-trip, and because every mutation re-emitted that stream, the append-only integrity guard refused every commit, push, and rollback store-wide. Error: 'cannot publish non-append-only bead event stream sase-mk: worktree rewrote ancestor event 5'. Per-stream writes would have confined this to sase-mk.

2. Latency. The failed 'sase bead work' for the primary_workspace_ownership epic reported slow_launch_stage phase_creation elapsed_ms=200901.7 and dependency_creation elapsed_ms=170376.8 -- each stage rewriting all 851 files then.

Verified the writes are currently byte-identical: after the round-trip fix, mutating one bead in a full 853-stream scratch copy changed only that bead's stream plus issues.jsonl, so git sees no spurious diff today. The cost and the blast radius remain.

Scope: make write_event_store write only the streams whose events actually changed, keeping events/manifest.json consistent and without weakening the append-only guard. Cross-repo: the change belongs in ../sase-core.

notes.author: 038.f1
notes.text: RELATED: sase-li — a different root cause (concurrent sync silently deleting an event) in the same event-stream write path; a per-stream write change should be checked against that failure mode too.

notes.author: sase-ns.3
notes.text: Implemented per-stream bead event-store writes in linked repo sase-core. Changes: crates/sase_core/src/bead/jsonl.rs now has write_event_store_changed(), validates all streams before writing, writes only selected streams, and skips byte-identical atomic writes including manifest.json; crates/sase_core/src/bead/mutation.rs now wraps event streams in tracked_streams::TrackedEventStreams so every mutable stream handout records the stream id, loaded event stores start with no changed streams, and legacy JSONL imports mark all streams changed for the first save. Added tests for selective writer/manifest reload, byte-identical write skipping, one mutation touching one stream file, the sase-mk blast-radius regression, and legacy JSONL first-save migration. Verification: focused cargo tests passed for write_event_store_changed_writes_selected_streams_and_reloads, atomic_if_changed_skips_identical_bytes, one_mutation_touches_only_the_mutated_stream_file, sase_mk_blast_radius_regression_preserves_unrelated_stream_bytes, and legacy_jsonl_migration_first_save_writes_every_imported_stream; sase-core just check passed. Scratch-store evidence on a copy of SASE_SDD_BEADS_DIR after the fix: 898 streams before/after, append note to top-level bead sase-10 took 934.129 ms, exactly 1 stream mtime moved (sase-10.jsonl), no streams created/deleted, events/manifest.json mtime did not move, issues.jsonl did move as expected. I did not run a pre-change scratch baseline in this session; the old code path rewrote every stream by construction. In the sase repo, just install succeeded against the linked checkout, then just check failed at unrelated mypy errors for HistoryWordCompletionMetadata in _history_word_rows.py:17 and _prompt_input_bar_completion_panel_labels.py:30; corroborated that existing active-epic issue on sase-n8 rather than creating a task.

title: sase bead doctor reports 14 settled historical event-stream rewrites as permanent ERRORs
close_reason: Premise falsified: the historical rewrite findings are not permanent -- they age out of the doctor's bounded commit window, and the store reports zero today.
description:
Discovered 2026-08-16 after repairing the bead-store wedge.

'sase bead doctor' on a healthy, fully-synced store prints 14 ERROR lines for event-stream rewrites that are already settled history, e.g.:

  ERROR: bead event stream sase-m5 rewrote event 3; first offending commit a2c29f164c6a
  ERROR: bead event stream sase-j7 is shorter than its own history: missing events 62-63 present in ancestor 7e3d27461b3a
  ERROR: bead event stream sase-mk rewrote event 2; first offending commit 4dfa41f5ad5d

These are backward-looking. The guard already settled each one at the time by restoring ancestor bytes, and the store commits and pushes cleanly now: verified by three real mutations (close sase-m9.3.1.5, close sase-mi.6, and the 8-agent epic graph commit for sase-mq) all committing and pushing without incident, and by mutating one bead in a full 853-stream scratch copy and confirming every other stream stayed byte-identical.

The problem is signal quality, not correctness. A doctor that always prints 14 ERRORs on a healthy store trains agents and the owner to ignore its ERROR section, so a genuinely new rewrite will not stand out. That directly cost time during this incident: distinguishing the one live, blocking rewrite from the 14 dead ones required manual event-by-event comparison.

Scope: give settled historical rewrites a distinct, non-ERROR classification (baseline/acknowledged/settled) so ERROR is reserved for rewrites that are currently blocking, and keep the historical set inspectable on demand. Deliberately excludes any history rewrite of the bead store; the committed events stay as they are.

notes.author: 038.f1
notes.text: RELATED: sase-li — that task explains at least one of the 14 (the sase-j7 'shorter than its own history: missing events 62-63' entry is exactly its concurrent-sync deletion defect); classifying the historical set should not hide a recurrence of it.

notes.author: 038.f1
notes.text: RELATED: sase-mr — the same incident's other follow-up; per-stream writes would shrink how often a single bad event can produce store-wide rewrite reports.

notes.author: 04c
notes.text: TRIAGE 2026-08-16 (workspace sase_13, master 630f4ea71). 'sase bead doctor' against the live store now prints ZERO 'rewrote event' / 'shorter than its own history' ERROR lines; the only output is pre-existing WARNING/NOTE lines (beads.db missing, 14 malformed design refs, 14 design-ref owner mismatches, 3 artifact-ref warnings, 454 redundant close events). Root cause of the disappearance: diagnose_event_stream_history (src/sase/bead/_stream_integrity.py:235) sources its records from stream_history_records (src/sase/bead/_stream_integrity_git.py:145), which passes --max-count=_HISTORY_COMMIT_LIMIT to git log over the stream dir. Settled rewrites therefore scroll out of the window on their own as the store commits, which is exactly the self-limiting behavior this bead asked to be engineered. All 14 named streams (sase-m5, sase-j7, sase-mk, sase-m7, sase-lk, sase-me, sase-mh, sase-jw, sase-ml) are gone from the output. Refile with a +1 if a rewrite finding ever persists across the window while the store is otherwise healthy. The related concerns remain tracked: sase-li (concurrent-sync deletion) is closed, sase-mr (per-stream writes) stays open.

title: sase bead work aborts mid-cleanup after already wiping some forced-reuse targets
description:
Discovered 2026-08-16 while relaunching stalled epic phase agents after the bead-store wedge.

Reproduction (observed once, then self-cleared):

  $ sase bead work sase-m6.6.1 -Y
  Existing agents for epic sase-m6.6.1:
    KILL     (WAITING) sase-m6.6.1.7 ...
    KILL     (WAITING) sase-m6.6.1.land ...
    REMOVE   (COMPLETED) sase-m6.6.1.6--code ...
    REMOVE   (MONITORED) sase-m6.6.1.6--mon ...
    REMOVE   (COMPLETED) sase-m6.6.1.6--plan ...
  Error: bead-work cleanup target sase-m6.6.1.6--code is no longer eligible for destructive cleanup

No agents launched. Re-running the identical command immediately succeeded, and its preview then listed only the two KILL targets -- the three REMOVE targets were already gone. So the first run wiped part of the selection, then aborted, leaving the epic with neither its old agents nor new ones. Nothing relaunched it; the operator had to notice and retry.

Root cause: _verify_cleanup_target_still_selected in src/sase/bead/cli_work_cleanup.py:858-901 re-validates each target against a freshly recomputed selection and raises ForcedReuseCleanupError when a target is no longer in destructive_targets. That check runs per target during the wipe loop, so targets already processed stay wiped when a later one fails. The guard itself is right (it is a TOCTOU check); the problem is that its failure is not atomic and not self-healing.

Impact: an epic relaunch can silently leave an epic with no live agents. During this incident that would have gone unnoticed had the retry not been run by hand -- the epic's phase agents simply would not exist.

Scope: make the destructive-cleanup phase all-or-nothing, or make the abort path either roll back or automatically re-drive the launch from the recomputed selection. The sibling error message on line 900 already says 'rerun', which suggests the retry was intended to be the operator's job; at minimum the partial-wipe case should say what was already removed and that the epic now has no agents.

notes.author: sase-ns.6.land
notes.text:
Fixed by epic sase-ns.6 phase sase-ns.6.3, commit 4d8d24eef 'fix(bead): make forced-reuse cleanup all-or-nothing'. Closed by that epic's land agent because the phase worker did not perform its plan-mandated bead bookkeeping.

FIX (src/sase/bead/cli_work_cleanup_apply.py, prepare_selected_bead_work_force_reuse): the verify and wipe passes are now separate loops. Every destructive target is checked by _verify_cleanup_target_still_selected before any target is wiped, so the reported failure mode -- a TOCTOU check firing on a later target after earlier targets were already destroyed -- can no longer destroy anything. The wipe loop additionally tracks wiped_names, and a genuine mid-wipe failure is re-raised as a ForcedReuseCleanupError naming which owners were already wiped and stating that the epic now has no live agent for them until the command is rerun. That matches the sibling 'rerun' guidance in revalidate_bead_work_launch_selection: retry stays the operator's job, but the error is now honest about the state it leaves behind.

REGRESSION COVERAGE: tests/test_bead/test_cli_work_cleanup_apply.py (3 tests) covers verify-before-wipe ordering (a stale later target aborts with zero wipes), the partial-wipe failure message content, and that a first-target failure leaves no stale claim.

VERIFICATION: phase sase-ns.6.3 ran the new tests plus the existing cleanup/confirm suites (17 passed) and a full 'just check' with every lint gate green. Re-verified by the land agent at HEAD 6000a54a1: tests/test_bead/test_cli_work_cleanup_apply.py plus tests/ace/tui/test_config_center_state.py -> 26 passed, and 'just check' exits 0.

RESIDUAL RISK, stated plainly: this does not close the window entirely. A wipe can still fail partway through, leaving earlier targets destroyed; the change converts that from a silent strand into a named, actionable error. Narrowing it further would need rollback or automatic re-drive of the launch, which the bead itself listed as the higher-risk alternative and which was not attempted.

title: BeadUpdateFieldsWire.resolution cannot express clearing a resolution over the wire
close_reason: Fixed in sase-core by 279f0e0 'fix: repair core storage identity contracts', taking the bead's first option. crates/sase_core/src/bead/mutation.rs:114-119 now annotates resolution with deserialize_with = "deserialize_present_option" (imported at line 17 from crate::serde_option), so an explicit JSON null deserializes to Some(None) -- a clear -- instead of collapsing onto the outer None. The round-trip test the bead asked for exists at mutation.rs:5340, update_fields_resolution_preserves_omitted_clear_and_set. Verified 2026-08-24 through /sase_repo.
description:
Found 2026-08-16 during the audit that accompanied the bead-event resolution round-trip fix (sase-core 2233171); filed as follow-up rather than folded into that tale.

crates/sase_core/src/bead/mutation.rs:100-105 in the sibling sase-core repo declares:

  pub resolution: Option<Option<BeadResolutionWire>>,

as a plain derived double option. Serde's derived deserializer maps JSON null onto the OUTER None, not Some(None), so a caller sending {"resolution": null} to mean 'clear the resolution' is silently read as 'leave unchanged'. There is no way to express a clear over this wire, and the misread is silent -- no error, the field just does not change.

This is the same asymmetric-double-option bug class already fixed on the event wire: bead/events.rs's issue_updated resolution field had it, and it produced a non-round-trip-stable event that wedged the whole bead store for hours. The fix there was to pair the field with the presence-preserving deserializer now shared at crates/sase_core/src/serde_option.rs (deserialize_present_option).

Difference in severity: the events.rs field also carried skip_serializing_if, which is what made it non-round-trip-stable and therefore store-wedging. mutation.rs's field has no skip_serializing_if, so it cannot wedge anything -- it can only silently drop a clear request. The audit found no live caller that depends on clearing through this wire, which is why it was filed instead of changed.

Scope: decide whether clearing should be expressible here. If yes, apply deserialize_present_option and add a round-trip test alongside the ones added for events.rs. If no, make the impossibility explicit -- change the type so the unusable state cannot be constructed, or reject an explicit null -- so the next reader does not assume a clear will work. Cross-repo: ../sase-core.

title: test_owner_snapshot_reuses_parsed_overlay_until_token_changes fails under the full parallel lane, passes in isolation
description:
tests/test_config_cache.py::test_owner_snapshot_reuses_parsed_overlay_until_token_changes failed under the escalated full-suite lane on master HEAD 3862288e9 (workspace sase_14, 'just test-scoped' escalated to the whole suite: 2 failed, 30689 passed, 11 skipped in 341.36s). The other failure in that run was the deterministic, separately-tracked sase-mp.

Isolation and narrow-contention evidence, all green:
  - .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config_cache.py::test_owner_snapshot_reuses_parsed_overlay_until_token_changes -p no:randomly -> passed.
  - SASE_CONTENTION_REPEAT=3 just test-contention tests/test_config_cache.py -> 18 passed per repeat; contention tally 0 node(s) failed across 3 repeat(s) in 82.8s, red repeats none.

So the node only fails when the WHOLE suite runs in parallel, not when its own file is put under CPU contention. That points at another test elsewhere in the suite poisoning process-global config state rather than at intra-file contention.

Why the node is fragile: the test patches sase.config.core.CONFIG_DIR, Path.cwd, and _load_yaml_file, then asserts BOTH identity reuse (first is second) and an exact loader call count (calls['count'] == 1) against the process-global memoized owner snapshot. Any other test that leaves the config cache warm, invalidates it mid-test, or perturbs the change token (config mtime/size, machine_name_path, selector stat) breaks either assertion. The fix is likely to isolate the global config cache around this test (or make the assertion robust) rather than to change production caching.

Second independent observation: closed phase bead sase-mj.4 recorded the same node as 'one config-cache flake that passed on retry' in its full-suite run at 2026-08-16T03:46Z, several commits earlier. This bead is filed by the sase-mj land agent, which reproduced it independently at 3862288e9.

Impact: an unpredictable red node in 'just check' escalations and 'just check-full', so agents must hand-triage before landing.

Scope: find the poisoning test (the sase-j7 global-state leak detector from phase sase-j7.2 is the natural instrument), fix the leak or isolate the cache, and re-measure with the full parallel lane plus just selection-health / tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt. Narrow file-level test-contention is NOT sufficient evidence here, because it is already green.

notes.author: sase-m6.7.1.3--3
notes.text:
ROOT-CAUSE CANDIDATE (from sase-m6.7.1.3 verification, 2026-08-16, HEAD a0b6cd16b): the poisoning test is very likely tests/test_config_cache.py::test_current_config_token_refresh_is_single_flight itself, and the mechanism is a timing deadline, not an unrelated distant test.

That test enters 'with patch(sase.config.core.time.monotonic), patch(sase.config.core._compute_current_config_token)', triggers the daemon refresh thread, then asserts 'refresh_started.wait(timeout=1.0)'. Under the loaded full parallel lane the daemon thread can miss that 1.0s window, so the assert fails and the 'with patch(...)' block unwinds WITHOUT ever calling release_refresh.set(). The orphaned daemon thread is still inside the mock's side_effect closure (which survives unpatching); its 'assert release_refresh.wait(timeout=2.0)' then raises, _refresh_current_config_token swallows it via 'except Exception' (src/sase/config/core.py:148-166), and the handler still takes _current_config_token_cache_lock and pushes _current_config_token_cache_deadline forward while leaving the real (unpatched) cached token in place. Every later test on that xdist worker then reads a warm, real process-global token.

That is exactly the observed cascade in this run: gw8 failed, in order, test_current_config_token_refresh_is_single_flight (assert False = wait(timeout=1.0)), then test_clear_config_cache_resets_config_token_time_gate (got a live token tuple (1879, True, '/home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_14', ...) instead of the patched ('token', 1)), then tests/test_config.py::test_legacy_overlay_is_discovered_but_not_a_complete_owner (get_agent_owner_identity() returned a memoized AgentOwnerIdentity(username='bbugyi200', machine_name='athena') instead of None). All three on gw8 in one 'just check-full' (3 failed, 30960 passed, 11 skipped in 666s).

This also explains why file-scoped contention never reproduces it: SASE_CONTENTION_REPEAT=3 'just test-contention -- tests/test_config.py tests/test_config_cache.py' spreads 51 items over 26 workers, so the single_flight test and its victims land on different workers and the leak has nowhere to land (re-confirmed today: 51 passed, contention tally 0 node(s) failed across 3 repeat(s) in 98.5s).

Suggested fix shape, in addition to the autouse cache-isolation fixture the earlier notes propose: make the single_flight test's failure path non-leaky (set release_refresh in a finally/addfinalizer and join the refresh thread before leaving the patch context), and treat the 1.0s/2.0s deadlines as the fragile part. Cache isolation alone will still leave a stray daemon thread racing whichever test runs next.

notes.author: sase-ns.land
notes.text:
Fixed by epic sase-ns phase sase-ns.2 (commit 3a22ff04f, 'fix(config): isolate config cache from test-owned CONFIG_DIR'). The phase agent implemented and verified the fix but did not do this bead's bookkeeping; the sase-ns land agent is recording it here.

ROOT CAUSE (two mechanisms, both process-global): (1) current_config_token() memoized a token without remembering which CONFIG_DIR object it was computed against, so when one test's monkeypatched CONFIG_DIR was restored and a successor test patched its own, the successor read the predecessor's warm token instead of cold-reading its own root. (2) The autouse _clear_config_caches fixture was setup-only, so a test that left the 'sase-config-token-refresh' daemon worker blocked (test_current_config_token_refresh_is_single_flight's 1.0s deadline can be missed under load) let that orphaned worker publish a real host-path token into a later test's cache generation on the same xdist worker.

FIX: bind the cached token to the CONFIG_DIR object it was computed against so rebinding that root is a cache-generation change; make _clear_config_caches a yield fixture that depends on _isolate_sase_home, drains the refresh worker, and clears derived caches before monkeypatch restores host paths; clear cache_clear only on the originally-captured functools helpers so a test's monkeypatched lambda cannot break teardown; and teach the sase-j7.2 global-state leak detector to treat a leftover refresh worker as poisoning.

REGRESSIONS: test_rebound_config_dir_cold_reads_successor_paths, the poisoner-then-victim pytester ordering in tests/test_config_cache_isolation.py, test_drain_config_token_refresh_joins_worker_and_advances_epoch, test_prior_refresh_worker_cannot_publish_after_drain, test_reset_derived_caches_tolerates_monkeypatched_cached_helpers, test_reset_derived_caches_clears_originals_while_names_are_patched.

Mechanism note for whoever fixes this: an orphaned refresh daemon alone cannot install a live token. _refresh_current_config_token (src/sase/config/core.py:147-164) swallows the compute exception, and when the epoch has advanced past its captured cache_epoch it writes only the deadline, never the value. Installing a real token requires some thread to call current_config_token()/load_merged_config() while the value is None (i.e. in the window right after the autouse tests/_conftest_runtime.py::_clear_config_caches fixture clears it) and while CONFIG_DIR is still unpatched. That points at a live non-test background thread that reads config on that worker, not at an orphan left by the single_flight test. A fix that only hardens test_config_cache.py's own deadlines would therefore not cover this instance; isolating the process-global config cache (or making current_config_token refuse to self-populate from non-main threads during tests) would.

description:
Proposed by phase sase-mq.3 (epic sase-mq, Enforce user-owned primary workspace boundaries) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on 2026-08-16T06:16:10Z, and independently reproduced by sase-mq's landing agent at HEAD ec390cdd4 in workspace sase_16 on a clean tree.

ROOT CAUSE (precise): the two entry points that check generated memory drift resolve different template sources for the same generated note, so they give opposite answers for the same file at the same commit.

REPRODUCTION (clean worktree, HEAD ec390cdd4, after just install):

  $ .venv/bin/sase validate
  SASE validation
    ok     init memory --check      <-- GREEN
    ok     init repo --check
    ok     init skills --check
    ok     plan links validate
    ok     agent prompts validate

  $ sase init memory --check --diff
  Needs attention:
    run  init memory  update 2 memory files and provider shims
         ~ update  sase/memory/sase_sizes.md  +5 -4  generated SASE size memory
         ~ update  sase/memory/README.md      +4 -4  memory README

The planned sase_sizes.md rewrite changes the alias wording in both directions of the note:

  -`medium`, `large`, `xlarge`. Size chooses the default work model through the matching
  -`@<size>` built-in alias and decides whether the worker plans before implementing. An
  +`medium`, `large`, `xlarge`. Size chooses the default work model through
  +`@<size>_worker` aliases and decides whether the worker plans before implementing. An

  -Default model aliases are `@xsmall`, `@small`, `@medium`, `@large`, and `@xlarge`. An
  -explicit `model` on a bead or plan takes precedence.
  +Default model aliases are `@xsmall_worker`, `@small_worker`, `@medium_worker`,
  +`@large_worker`, and `@xlarge_worker`. An explicit `model` on a bead or plan takes
  +precedence.

plus a mechanical line/token-count refresh in sase/memory/README.md.

WHY IT MATTERS: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md make 'sase memory init' mandatory after any memory file edit. Following that mandated workflow rewrites sase_sizes.md to the `@<size>_worker` wording, which is what 'just check' then has to accept -- but 'just check' runs 'sase validate', whose 'init memory --check' step is green only on the committed `@<size>` wording. So the required post-edit step is exactly what turns the gate red, and the agent is left choosing between an unrelated 2-file diff in their commit and a red check. Phase sase-mq.3 worked around it by deliberately leaving generated memory at HEAD so validate stayed green, which means the drift is still latent for the next agent.

WHICH SIDE IS WRONG IS UNRESOLVED: grep finds no `_worker` alias anywhere in this repo (src/sase/default_config.yml, src/sase/xprompts/), so the `@<size>_worker` wording appears to come from the home/global (chezmoi) memory template rather than the project template. Determining the authoritative alias names is part of this task; do not assume the generator is right.

SCOPE: reconcile the two check paths so 'sase validate' and 'sase init memory --check' agree on a single template source for a project-scoped generated note, then make the committed sase/memory/sase_sizes.md match whichever alias vocabulary actually exists. Open the chezmoi repo through /sase_repo (never by guessing a path) to inspect the home/global template. Add a regression gate so a project note whose generator output differs from the committed file cannot pass 'sase validate'.

description:
REPRODUCTION (clean origin/master a0b6cd16b, no local changes):

    F601 Dictionary key literal repeated
       --> tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py:292:5

ROOT CAUSE: _REVIEWED_DIR_OPERATION_CONTEXTS contains the key
'src/sase/workspace_provider/reset_replay.py:_clear_owned_paths' TWICE, at lines 279 and
292, with different exemption prose. The second entry was added by b82f21c1b 'test:
register ownership audit coverage' (from the now-closed epic sase-mq) on top of an entry
that already existed. The second entry is also out of keep-sorted order, sitting after
the utils.py key.

IMPACT: this project sets commit_hooks.before: 'just fix' in sase/sase.yml. 'just fix'
runs 'ruff check --fix src/ tests/', F601 has no autofix, so the recipe exits 1 and the
before-commit hook fails. Every 'sase stitch create' / sase_git_commit in this repo
fails for every agent until this is fixed, regardless of what the agent changed. There
is no sanctioned bypass: sase stitch create has no hook-skip flag, the commit workflow
reads no skip env var, and project-local config has the highest merge precedence so a
user-global override cannot neutralize it. Discovered when a documentation-only refresh
could not be committed.

FIX: delete one of the two entries. Note that Python already discards the FIRST one, so
deleting line 279's entry preserves current runtime behavior exactly and is
semantically a no-op; deleting line 292's entry instead CHANGES which exemption the
audit enforces. The two exemptions say materially different things (line 279: 'Clears
only caller-supplied paths after resolving and verifying each path is inside the live
leased checkout...'; line 292: 'Clears only caller-supplied generated paths after
reset-and-replay has authorized a live leased checkout...'), so a human should confirm
which text is authoritative rather than deleting arbitrarily. Restore keep-sorted order
for the surviving entry.

VERIFY: 'just fix' exits 0, and
tests/test_agent_artifact_directory_operation_audit.py::test_artifact_directory_operation_sites_are_reviewed
still passes.

title: Unify approval-time plan publication behind a single writer

description:

title: Auto-disable LLM providers on usage-limit errors
description: When a sase agent fails because its LLM provider reported a usage/quota limit, sase recognizes that failure, temporarily disables just that provider (honoring the reset time the provider itself reported when one is available), stops wasting retries on it, and tells the user what happened with a rich notification. Defaults work out of the box for every shipped provider, and users can extend or replace the patterns and durations from config.

title: Get monitor reconciliation off the ACE startup critical path
description: `sase ace` startup returns to at or below its 2026-08-12 baseline (median `visible_ready` <= 2.8 s, `agents_ready` <= 3.4 s), monitor reconciliation no longer runs synchronously inside the agents disk load, and an operation-count regression gate keeps data-scaled work off the startup path.

notes.author: sase-n7.land
notes.text:
VERIFIED (step 1): read all five child beads and every child note, then read the source and each commit rather than trusting the reports. sase-n7.1 (6d9db4c26) reorders should_reconcile_dead_supervisor so monitor_state/pid reject before proc_shell_owns() — behavior-preserving, all three are pure False-returning predicates. sase-n7.2 (3f3f61d14) adds procs.store.read_proc_snapshot() as the single store-read primitive, threads snapshot= through get_proc/proc_shell_owns/should_reconcile_dead_supervisor/reconcile_dead_supervisors_for_records and list_monitors/_with_proc_projection; get_proc's semantics are preserved because filter_procs with all-default args is a no-op. sase-n7.3 (9fe82045d) gives reconciliation its own _reconciliation_project_records() query (include_active only, active_limit=1000, include_full_history=False, recent_completed_limit=0, only_monitors=True) plus a bounded max_records=0/newest_first fallback scan, and leaves _project_records/list_monitors on full history — no Rust escalation was needed. sase-n7.4 (39bdd6772) removes the sync _reconcile_dead_monitor_supervisors_for_tui() from _load_agents_from_disk_impl and schedules it after the sync, async, and artifact-delta loads, mirroring _run_loader_cleanup exactly (latest-wins coalesce, spawn_pump_free_task, NavigationGate deferral, spawn-fail guard release, trailing pass in finally) with MONITOR_RECONCILE_REFRESH_SOURCE breaking the refresh loop. sase-n7.5 (0ec2018f1) adds tests/perf/bench_agent_disk_load_ops.py, check_agent_disk_load_ops_regression.py, a committed baseline, a pytest gate, and a Just recipe. Grep confirms no synchronous reconcile caller remains on any TUI path; only the background helper and axe/hook_jobs.py call reconcile_dead_supervisors.

MEASURED: 54 tests green across tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py, tests/test_procs_facade.py, tests/ace/tui/test_monitor_reconcile_off_read_path.py, tests/perf/test_agent_disk_load_ops_regression.py. 'just agent-disk-load-ops-check' passes: 1 loader index query, 0 proc-store reads, 0 monitor-reconcile index queries, 0 sync reconcile calls, unchanged between 0 and 250 monitor rows. The plan's own harness on the author's real ~/.sase state now reports disk_load 1.014s / 1.229s / 1.224s for 361 agents with 0 sync reconcile_dead_supervisors calls (was 3.84s for 173 agents with the sync call). The epic's structural goals are met; the plan's absolute median visible_ready <= 2.8 s was NOT re-measured, because a live 'sase ace' launch needs an interactive session and the box was under heavy load. The one post-change tui_startup.jsonl sample (2026-08-16T17:34:13Z) reads visible_ready 3.95 s / agents_ready 4.78 s, down from 5.8-8.1 s before, on a workload that has roughly doubled since the 2026-08-12 baseline (173 -> 361 agents scanned, index_row_count 530 -> 614).

INTEGRATED (step 2): reviewed all seven non-epic commits since 6d9db4c26 (be0e35d81, 23c953bc7, c9ef67510, ddef1f0d4, 1fbc8c0f1, ed39dd0b8, 96b48d0ab). None touch src/sase/monitor, src/sase/procs, or the agents loading path, and none introduce a proc-store or artifact-index N+1 that should adopt read_proc_snapshot(). procs/service.py's reconcile_proc_shells deliberately re-reads after writes and must not be snapshot-scoped. One real integration gap was found and fixed as epic work: the new gate had a Just recipe and a pytest gate but no step in CI's perf-floors job, unlike its siblings launch-perf-check and view-hints-perf-check. Added 'Run agents disk-load operation-count floor' plus its artifact upload to .github/workflows/ci.yml.

FULL VERIFICATION: 'just check' escalated to the whole suite — every lint gate green, 31240 passed, 11 skipped, 2 failed. Both failures are cross-repo drift from other in-flight epics, reproduced in isolation and unrelated to this epic: test_var_integration schema 21-vs-22 (sase-core 5078d26, epic sase-n8) and test_bead_cli_golden_contract[stats] missing the Flags row (sase-core 198a7b4, epic sase-nb).

FOLLOW-UPS from child PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP notes, all five routed: (1) sase-n7.5's Python/Rust index schema 21-vs-22 -> corroborating DISCOVERED ISSUE note on epic sase-n8, which already tracked it and whose phase sase-n8.8 is the natural home; no task created. (2) sase-n7.2's lane-helper N+1 proc-store reads (active_monitor_for_lane, monitor_blocking_start_for_lane) -> DISCOVERED ISSUE note on epic sase-m9, whose phase sase-m9.2.1.4 (8b4635ad1) put the expensive proc_shell_owns() into that guard; no task created. (3) sase-n7.4's get_monitor() full-history query per reconcile candidate -> new task sase-ne (medium, ready), with RELATED notes to sase-n7, sase-m9, and sase-kh. (4) sase-n7.2 and sase-n7.3's tests/test_config.py xdist flakes (test_load_config_layers_overlay_detected, test_load_merged_config_invalid_yaml_skipped) -> +1 on sase-mv, same process-global config-cache root cause and same remediation. (5) sase-n7.3's test_enter_returns_while_xprompt_file_read_is_blocked -> new task sase-nf (large, ready), filed as a narrow node task per sase-ct's retired-umbrella close reason, with RELATED notes to sase-ct, sase-j7, and sase-mv. Nothing was declined.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the gate phase's sase/memory/tui_perf.md rule-9 update. CLAUDE.md requires explicit user permission for memory-file edits and the plan anticipated this; permission was not granted to sase-n7.5 and has not been granted in this landing either, so the memory note still does not record the monitor-reconciliation instance of the settlement-work-on-a-read-path failure mode.

notes.text: POST-CLOSE INTEGRATION (second gap, found while checking the working tree after the close): .gitignore listed an explicit ignore line for every other perf floor-check report — sdd/plans/202604/rust_backend_phase7_floor_check.json, 202605/bead_perf_smoke.json, 202605/agent_launch_regression_check.json, 202607/view_hints_regression_check.json — but not the report sase-n7.5's checker writes. So running 'just agent-disk-load-ops-check' left sdd/plans/202608/perf_artifacts/agent_disk_load_ops_regression_check.json untracked in every agent's tree, which is exactly the dirty-tree state the repo's commit workflow and dirty-tree audits object to. Both edits from this landing — the CI perf-floors step in .github/workflows/ci.yml and this .gitignore line — are in the working tree for the finalizer to commit.

DISCOVERED ISSUE: During finish_m9_proc_closeout verification on master 57c71d17a, just check escalated to the full 14-worker lane and failed both tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py::test_reconcile_dead_supervisors_reads_proc_store_once and ::test_list_monitors_proc_store_reads_do_not_scale_with_record_count. Both passed immediately together in isolation, and the focused monitor/proc lane had already passed 221/221. The local diff only publishes the spawned supervisor PID before start ack; it does not touch store reconciliation. The two assertions count process-global proc-store reads, so their full-lane/pass-isolation shape is credible evidence of a background reconciliation call leaking across test boundaries after this epic moved reconciliation off the synchronous startup path. Please diagnose with the sase-j7 global-state leak tooling or route elsewhere if the recorded call source proves different.

notes.text: ROUTED (post-close, in response to 044's DISCOVERED ISSUE note of 2026-08-16T18:16:52Z): 044's report is correct and this epic caused it. Diagnosis: _count_proc_store_reads (tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py:641) and the inline 'counting' closure in test_list_monitors_proc_store_reads_do_not_scale_with_record_count both monkeypatch the PROCESS-GLOBAL sase.procs.store._call_binding and append every read_procs_snapshot call to a plain list with no thread or task scoping. Phase sase-n7.4 (39bdd6772) then moved _reconcile_dead_monitor_supervisors_for_tui off the synchronous disk load onto a background spawn_pump_free_task, so a concurrently-running ACE TUI test in the same xdist worker can now emit a read_procs_snapshot that these counters attribute to themselves. That is exactly the pass-in-isolation / fail-in-full-lane shape 044 observed. Filed as new task sase-nj (small, ready) via /sase_new_task, with RELATED notes to sase-n7, sase-j7 (the process-global-state-leak epic whose tooling 044 suggested), and sase-ne. title: Record the alias resolution trail and its origin at launch
description: provenance: make alias resolution return the ordered trail of alias hops it traversed, give LaunchSelection that trail plus the origin of the request (directive vs no-directive default vs no alias), and persist `model_alias_trail` and `model_alias_origin` into agent_meta.json and prompt-step markers at every launch, reconcile, re-exec, and follow-up write site.

notes.author: sase-n8.1
notes.text: Contract note for phases core/adapter: the epic pins "model_alias_trail[0] == model_alias". That holds for every alias reference SASE generates (format_model_directive_value always emits @<name>, and _directive_extract only sets directives.model_alias when the @ prefix was present). It does NOT hold for a hand-typed "%model:large" — a known alias written without @ — where directives.model_alias is None but resolution really did traverse @large. The provenance phase records the truthful trail there rather than dropping a real hop; downstream projection/query/adapter key off the trail and alias_position, never off model_alias, so this only makes history more complete. No action needed unless a later phase asserts that invariant literally.

notes.author: sase-n8.1

title: Feature flags whose removal is a bead, a deadline, and a gate
description: SASE has one boolean feature-flag registry resolved through the existing config layer chain, every temporary flag is owned by a dedicated `flag` bead carrying a date-and-release removal threshold, that threshold raises a FlagTriage gate the owner answers with Remove / Extend / Keep / Close, flag beads read unmistakably on every surface that renders a bead, and `sase/memory/sase_flags.md` teaches agents when a flag is warranted and how to retire one.

notes.text:
DESIGN CORRECTION (owner, 2026-08-16) — applies to the memory phase, sase-nb.10:

sase/memory/sase_flags.md must NOT be generated by `sase init`. Feature flags are sase's own registry, so the note that teaches them is local to this repo; a generated note would ship flag teaching into every SASE project's memory tree, including projects that can never own a flag.

Do NOT add `templates/memory-sase-flags.template.md`, a `_GeneratedLongMemorySpec`, or a `_generated_flags_memory_relative_path()` in `init_memory/root_rendering.py:122-145`. Write `sase/memory/sase_flags.md` by hand instead, shaped like the existing project-local Tier 2 notes `symvision.md` and `tui_perf.md`: `type: long`, `parent: AGENTS.md`, and a `description:` naming the decision it settles. Then run `sase memory init` to reindex AGENTS.md, the provider shims, and the memory README. The note's content budget and required coverage from the plan are unchanged. If a phase already landed the generated form, revert the template, the spec entry, and any test pinning the generated-note set (tests/main/test_init_memory_markdown_templates.py, tests/main/test_init_memory_handler_outputs.py).

Revised exit condition: `sase init -c` no longer proves anything about this note, since drift checks cover generated files only. Verify instead that (1) `sase memory list` shows sase_flags.md as a Tier 2 note with its description, (2) the regenerated AGENTS.md Tier 2 listing includes it, and (3) `sase init` in a non-sase project produces no sase_flags.md.

Same mistake one level up: the plan's always-loaded pointer targets `templates/memory-sase.template.md`, which renders sase/memory/sase.md into EVERY project. That pointer must move to a project-local Tier 1 short note in this repo (its own note, or a section in sase/memory/gotchas.md). See the sase variables on this run for the remaining fallout.

notes.author: 042.f0
notes.text:
DESIGN CORRECTION FALLOUT (owner, 2026-08-16) — the rest of what the "local note, not
generated" decision changes. Read together with the correction note above.

1. The Tier 1 pointer is the same bug (sase-nb.10). The plan's "Feature Flags" section
targets `templates/memory-sase.template.md`, which renders `sase/memory/sase.md` into
EVERY project — wider blast radius than the Tier 2 note. Put it in a project-local short
note in this repo instead: a new `sase/memory/*.md` with `type: short`,
`parent: AGENTS.md`, or a new section in `sase/memory/gotchas.md`. Hand-written short
notes are still structure-checked when AGENTS.md is assembled
(`amd/_memory.py::_short_memory_structure_blockers` -> `validate_short_memory_structure`:
exactly one H1 first, no heading deeper than H3), so the shape still matters. The 90-word
budget was priced as text loaded into every project's Tier 1; local text is cheaper, so
keep it tight but treat 90 words as guidance and drop it from the exit condition.

2. Nothing that ships globally may cite the note's path (sase-nb.7, sase-nb.6). The
`sase flag new` scaffold ("the path `sase/memory/sase_flags.md` teaches"), the `flags.*`
doctor messages, and the FlagTriage gate text all reach every install, while the note now
exists only here — strip the path from those strings or make it conditional. This exposes
a scope question the plan never asked: the registry is code under this repo's `src/sase/`,
so `sase flag new` run from another project scaffolds a registry entry with nowhere to
paste it. Gate the `sase flag` group — or at minimum warn — on `is_sase_managed`
(`project_management.py:15,35`; default `false` in `default_config.yml:17`), and say so in
`-h`.

3. Do NOT extend "local" to the glossary or the user docs. `Feature Flag` / `Flag Bead` in
the `glossary:` block of `sase/sase.yml` is already project-local and regenerates
`sase/memory/glossary.md` here only — leave it as planned. `docs/configuration.md` also
stays: `scope: "project"` flags are overridable from any project's local config, so the
config surface is genuinely global even though the teaching note is not. Local memory !=
local config surface.

4. Formatting and validation move to the ordinary gates. The hand-written note loses
`format_generated_memory_markdown` (`init_memory/formatting.py:99`), so run `just fmt-md`;
`just check` runs prettier over `**/*.md` and will fail on unformatted frontmatter or
prose. And `description:` is optional on a discovered note (`memory/notes.py`,
`description: str | None`) — omitting it raises no error, it just leaves a blank hook in
the AGENTS.md Tier 2 listing, so eyeball the regenerated listing.

title: Flaky test_run_noninteractive_timeout_kills_process_group: empty child stdout under full parallel lane
close_reason: Fixed by 569d4257b 'fix: stabilize process concurrency closeout': 'Add deterministic seams for noninteractive subprocess startup.' tests/test_noninteractive_subprocess.py:45-68 now monkeypatches noninteractive_subprocess._start_noninteractive_process with a wrapper that reads the child's pgid off stdout before returning, so the test no longer races an empty child stdout under lane contention. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
tests/test_noninteractive_subprocess.py::test_run_noninteractive_timeout_kills_process_group failed under an escalated full just check (workspace sase_19, 2026-08-16, 6 xdist workers, 31161 items) with:

  IndexError: list index out of range
  at `child_pgid = int(output.strip().splitlines()[0])`

The test runs `python -c "import os, time; print(os.getpgrp(), flush=True); time.sleep(30)"` through `run_noninteractive(..., timeout=0.2)` and expects TimeoutExpired.output to contain the child's process-group id. Under the full parallel lane the captured output was empty, so splitlines()[0] raised. The timeout itself did fire (TimeoutExpired was raised).

This session did not touch `run_noninteractive` or that test file — it only added reserved `lease(...)` RUNNING-field labels. Isolated rerun of the session's own tests passed (38 passed).

SCOPE: reproduce under a contended full parallel lane, then either make the helper reliably capture the first flushed line before killing the group, or stop asserting on stdout that can be lost when the 0.2s budget expires before the child prints.

title: Monitor reconciliation's locked settle path runs a full-history artifact-index query per candidate via get_monitor()
description:
DISCOVERED BY: bead sase-n7.4 during epic sase-n7 ('Get monitor reconciliation off the ACE startup critical path'), recorded as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP and routed to a task by sase-n7.land on 2026-08-16 (workspace sase_17, master HEAD 0ec2018f1).

WHAT IS WRONG: reconcile_dead_supervisor() (src/sase/monitor/reconcile.py:69) takes the lane lock and then calls get_monitor(record.lane, record.monitor_id) to re-read the record under the lock, and _reconcile_dead_supervisor_locked() re-reads through the same callable. get_monitor() (src/sase/monitor/store.py:246) walks _monitor_records() -> _project_records(), which issues an unbounded artifact-index query with include_full_history=True, active_limit=None, recent_completed_limit=None, include_hidden=True over ~/.sase/agent_artifact_index.sqlite, then linear-scans the result for the one artifact_dir it already knows. That is O(archive) work per settled candidate. On the author's real state that query measured 1.51 s per call against a 115 MB index (see the epic plan plan:202608/tui_startup_monitor_reconcile.md, Defect 3), and the index only grows.

WHY IT SURVIVED sase-n7: the epic bounded the query that *selects* reconciliation candidates (_reconciliation_monitor_records(), sase commit 9fe82045d) and moved the whole pass off the synchronous TUI disk load (39bdd6772), so this call is no longer on the ACE startup critical path. It is still archive-scaled work inside the settle path, and it multiplies by the number of dead-supervisor candidates -- exactly the burst case after a reboot, when many monitors need settling at once. The reconcile pass also holds the lane lock across it.

THE FIX ALREADY HAS A HOME: read_monitor_marker(project_name, artifacts_dir) (src/sase/monitor/store.py:257) exists for precisely this shape and documents it -- 'get_monitor() runs a full-history, unlimited, hidden-inclusive index query ... to find one record it already knows the path to'. The reconcile path holds the member's artifacts_dir, so the locked settle and re-read should use the marker helper instead of get_monitor(). Note reconcile_dead_supervisor() takes get_monitor as an injected GetMonitor callable, so the change is at the call sites in src/sase/monitor/store.py (reconcile_dead_supervisors, active_monitor_for_lane, monitor_blocking_start_for_lane) plus any test doubles, not a signature change. Confirm the marker read preserves the semantics the locked re-read depends on (it must still observe a concurrent settle and bail when the record already left 'running'); if it cannot, say so and keep get_monitor() with a bounded query instead.

SCOPE: switch the locked settle/re-read to the path-direct marker helper (or an equivalently bounded lookup), keep settlement semantics unchanged -- a monitor whose supervisor died must still settle, pre-reboot monitors must still reconcile to 'lost' -- and pin the new bound with a test asserting the reconcile pass does not scale its artifact-index queries with candidate count, mirroring tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py::test_reconcile_dead_supervisors_uses_bounded_active_monitor_index_query and ::test_reconcile_dead_supervisors_reads_proc_store_once.

IMPACT: background monitor settlement stays archive-dependent and gets slower as the artifact index grows, and a post-reboot burst pays that cost once per candidate while holding the lane lock. Not user-visible as a startup stall today, which is why it is a task rather than epic work.

title: test_enter_returns_while_xprompt_file_read_is_blocked fails under the full parallel lane, passes in isolation
description:
DISCOVERED BY: bead sase-n7.3 during epic sase-n7 ('Get monitor reconciliation off the ACE startup critical path'), recorded as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP and routed to a task by sase-n7.land on 2026-08-16.

OBSERVATION: tests/ace/tui/test_xprompt_browser_load_keymap.py::test_enter_returns_while_xprompt_file_read_is_blocked failed during phase sase-n7.3's first 'just check', where the scoped lane escalated to the whole suite. The node passed when rerun in isolation, and the phase's second full 'just check' was green. The phase's own diff touched only src/sase/monitor/store.py (a bounded artifact-index query for monitor reconciliation) and tests/monitor/, so the failure is unrelated to the change under test. The same escalated run also failed tests/test_config.py::test_load_merged_config_invalid_yaml_skipped, which was routed separately as a +1 on sase-mv.

CLASS: green in isolation, red only when the whole suite runs in parallel -- the shape sase-ct was retired for. The node exercises the xprompt browser's Enter handler while an xprompt file read is deliberately blocked, so it is timing- and receiver-sensitive by construction, which is the usual signature of process-global state or scheduler contention leaking in from elsewhere in the suite rather than intra-file contention.

SCOPE: reproduce under the full parallel lane (narrow file-scoped 'just test-contention' is NOT sufficient evidence for this class -- see sase-mv, where file-level contention was already green while the full lane was red), identify whether the trigger is a poisoning test or a genuine race in the blocked-read path, fix the leak or make the node robust, then re-measure with the full parallel lane plus 'just selection-health' and tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

IMPACT: an unpredictable red node in 'just check' escalations and 'just check-full', so agents landing unrelated work must hand-triage before landing. Single observation so far; corroborate rather than duplicate if it recurs.

title: Retire dead ACE in-process launch and cleanup bodies
description: On current master 57c71d17a, src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agent_workflow/_launch_procs.py and src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_cleanup_procs.py accept proc_callable only to delete it before submitting the durable argv operation. The in-process launch helpers run_agent_launch_body, run_single_agent_launch_body, _launch_repeat_agents, _launch_bulk_agents, _launch_multi_prompt_agents, and _launch_multi_model_agents therefore have no executable production path even though test doubles still invoke their callables directly; the same ignored seam leaves cleanup worker bodies test-only. This production/test divergence previously hid the stale _prompt_context bug fixed by 2aa8ba26f. Retire both dead in-process body families and both proc_callable parameters, and migrate affected test doubles to exercise the durable submit paths production uses.

notes.author: sase-ng.1.land--1
notes.text:
Delivered in full by child epic sase-ng.1 (closed 2026-08-18, plan 202608/retire_dead_ace_launch_cleanup_bodies.md, commits 97f5b6f03 / f43358dcb / 13e9ccbc9 / 0f7d86a66 / 65b72d43a plus the prerequisite dc4ca2057). Re-verified against this bead's description at master c89e5bbeb before closing:

- Both dead in-process body families are gone. grep over src/, tests/ and docs/ finds no run_agent_launch_body, run_single_agent_launch_body, _launch_repeat_agents, _launch_bulk_agents, _launch_multi_prompt_agents or _launch_multi_model_agents, and the modules that held them (_launch_body*.py, _launch_bulk.py, _launch_multi_prompt.py, _launch_multi_model.py, _launch_repeat.py, _launch_background.py, _launch_history.py, _workflow_exec.py, axe/run_workflow_runner.py) are deleted, along with the cleanup worker closures behind kill, dismiss and save persistence.
- Both proc_callable parameters are gone. Zero proc_callable references remain in src/; _submit_launch_proc (_launch_procs.py:49) and _submit_cleanup_proc (_cleanup_procs.py:34) no longer accept one. The six test files that still spell proc_callable are positional stand-ins for _submit_session_worker's 'body' argument (_proc_action_submission.py:197-200) - a different, still-live production seam this task never targeted.
- Affected test doubles now exercise the durable submit paths: the launch and cleanup harnesses assert on the RUN_LAUNCH / persist-cleanup payloads production submits instead of invoking task["proc_callable"]() directly, which is exactly the divergence this bead was filed to remove (the +1 evidence from the kill_and_edit_force_reuse plan).
- No user-facing capability was dropped on the way: forced name reuse (%id:!name kill-and-edit), VCS-xprompt MRU recording, the unresolved-#ref warning toast, and cleanup-failure recovery were each moved onto the durable path and verified end to end during the epic landing.

Two capabilities the epic plan deliberately scoped out are carried by ready task beads rather than left implicit: sase-p6 (marked-Patch bulk launch fans out one agent instead of N) and sase-p7 (Ctrl+Space replay target not refreshed from the submitted prompt). Both are pre-existing regressions from 0835b38d2, not damage from this retirement.

Verification: just check-full at c89e5bbeb - all lint/mypy/symvision/validation gates green, full suite 32563 passed / 13 skipped / 0 failed; the only failure was tools/check_test_cost_budgets, the standing master-red gate tracked on sase-j0. The trailing flake gate named two of this epic's own pre-fix seam nodes, whose evidence was retired with a '# fixed-at: 2026-08-17T20:21:41Z' block for 13e9ccbc9; the remaining named node belongs to sase-oh (+1 recorded). Full detail is in sase-ng.1's close note.

No parent above this bead.

title: Proc-store read counters in test_monitor_store_reconcile.py are process-global, so background reconciliation from other tests inflates them under the full parallel lane
description:
DISCOVERED BY: agent 044 as a DISCOVERED ISSUE note on closed epic sase-n7 ('Get monitor reconciliation off the ACE startup critical path'), 2026-08-16T18:16:52Z, observed on master 57c71d17a. Root cause diagnosed during the sase-n7 landing.

FAILING NODES (both added by sase-n7.5, commit 0ec2018f1's sibling work in phase n7.2/n7.3):
  tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py::test_reconcile_dead_supervisors_reads_proc_store_once
  tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py::test_list_monitors_proc_store_reads_do_not_scale_with_record_count

REPRODUCTION: During finish_m9_proc_closeout verification, 'just check' escalated to the full 14-worker lane and failed both. Both pass immediately together in isolation, and the focused monitor/proc lane passed 221/221. That pass-in-isolation / fail-in-full-lane shape is cross-module contamination, not a logic error.

ROOT CAUSE: Both assertions count proc-store reads through a PROCESS-GLOBAL monkeypatch with no thread or task scoping.
  - _count_proc_store_reads (tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py:641) replaces sase.procs.store._call_binding with a closure that appends every 'read_procs_snapshot' call to a plain list, then asserts 'reads == ["read_procs_snapshot"]' (exactly one).
  - test_list_monitors_proc_store_reads_do_not_scale_with_record_count builds its own equivalent 'counting' closure inline (same file, ~line 532) and asserts '1 <= small <= 2' and 'small == large'.
Any caller anywhere in the process that touches read_procs_snapshot while the patch is installed lands in that counter.

WHY IT ONLY STARTED NOW: sase-n7.4 (39bdd6772) moved _reconcile_dead_monitor_supervisors_for_tui (src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_loading_disk_support.py:108) off the synchronous agents disk load and onto a background asyncio task via spawn_pump_free_task (src/sase/ace/tui/util/pump_tasks.py:64). Before that change, reconciliation only ran inline on the load path and could not overlap an unrelated test. Now any concurrently-running ACE TUI test in the same xdist worker can emit a read_procs_snapshot that the monitor tests' counters attribute to themselves. The counters were written in the same epic, under the pre-existing assumption that no concurrent caller exists.

SCOPE / LIKELY FIX: scope the counting to the call under test rather than to the process — record the owning thread ident (and/or asyncio task) when the patch is installed and only count reads originating from it, or have reconcile/list_monitors surface their own read count so the assertion does not depend on a global patch. Applies to both the shared helper and the inline closure. Verify under the full parallel lane, not just the focused monitor lane, since the focused lane already passes.

NOT ATTEMPTED HERE: the sase-n7 land agent diagnosed but did not fix this, because a speculative change to a regression gate could not be verified under the 14-worker conditions that produce the failure within that agent's turn.

FIXED BY sase-m9's integration commit ccbcb3557 'perf(monitor): share one proc-store snapshot per lane scan' (SASE_BEAD=[sase-m9], authored by sase-m9.land after this bead was filed). That commit applies exactly the remediation this bead scopes: _count_proc_store_reads (tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py:694) now captures owner = threading.get_ident() and counts a read only when threading.get_ident() == owner, so a background reconcile pass that ACE schedules through asyncio.to_thread can no longer land in the caller's counter. The separate inline 'counting' closure inside test_list_monitors_proc_store_reads_do_not_scale_with_record_count was deleted and routed through the same thread-scoped helper, so both named nodes share one correctly scoped counter.

VERIFIED at master ccbcb3557 by sase-m9.land post-close verification: (1) full-lane 'just test' under the reproduction condition named in this bead -- the same multi-worker parallel lane where both nodes previously failed -- passed both (monitor run k8tezynyarfn, 8m31s, 7 failed / 31353 passed / 10 skipped; neither failure is in this file). The two remaining full-lane failures belong to sase-nk (stale tests/test_file_panel.py assertions) and sase-nb (bead stats-golden Flags row); neither touches proc-store read counting.

No production behavior depended on this bead -- the defect was test-counter scoping only, though ccbcb3557 also removed the underlying N+1 by making active_monitor_for_lane and monitor_blocking_start_for_lane read the proc store at most once per scan and skip it entirely for a lane with no monitor member.

title: tests/test_file_panel.py: 6 tests still assert panel.update.called after the scroll-anchor refactor routed every body render through _update_body
description:
Six tests in tests/test_file_panel.py fail deterministically on clean master, unrelated to any in-flight diff: test_render_static_file_result_renders_content, test_display_linked_diff_renders_banner_and_raw_content, test_live_diff_renders_all_lines_and_posts_line_count, test_live_diff_timestamp_refresh_reuses_cached_body, test_file_panel_pathological_cap_posts_explicit_range, and test_linked_diff_full_rerender_keeps_banner.

Reproduction: '.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_file_panel.py -q -p no:randomly' -> 6 failed, 11 passed. Verified on a clean stashed tree at master ce1ad41a1 and again after rebasing onto master e93da1e91, so it is not workspace- or diff-specific and is not a parallel-lane flake. Also surfaced as 6 of the 7 failures in a full 'just test' run (31307 passed, 7 failed); the 7th is the separate stats-golden drift already noted on the feature-flags epic.

Failure shape: 'assert panel.update.called' -> AssertionError: assert False, where panel is the test's MagicMock body widget (tests/test_file_panel.py:243 for the static-file case).

Root cause: commit ce1ad41a1 'fix(ace): stop the file panel from losing the reader's scroll position' (tale plan 202608/file_panel_scroll_anchor.md) replaced the ad-hoc save/restore calls with a scroll-anchor controller, so every body render now funnels through the new _update_body seam in src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/file_panel/_content.py rather than calling body.update() directly. The tests were not updated and still assert on the old direct-update call.

Scope: update the six assertions to observe the current _update_body seam (or have the mock body satisfy it), preserving what each test actually guards -- rendered content, the linked-diff banner, the live-diff line-count message, cached-body reuse on timestamp refresh, and the pathological-cap explicit range message. Do not weaken the assertions to mere 'was called' checks on a seam that no longer proves content reached the widget, and do not change production behavior: the scroll-anchor routing is the intended fix.

Verified: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_file_panel.py -q -p no:randomly -> 17 passed; just test-scoped -> 468 passed (42 files, including the six named nodes). just check fmt/ruff and remaining lint gates green; just _lint-mypy fails on unmodified HistoryWordCompletionMetadata imports (pre-existing, recorded on sase-ns.4).

plus_one_evidence.note: Independently reproduced by sase-m9.land post-close verification on a NEWER tree than the original report: master ccbcb3557 (the sase-m9 integration commit, two commits past the e93da1e91 rebase cited in the description). Exhaustive lane 'just test' (monitor k8tezynyarfn, 8m31s): 7 failed, 31353 passed, 10 skipped. Six of the seven are exactly this bead's nodes; the seventh is the separate sase-nb stats-golden drift. title: just check can fail after every selected test passes when the pytest-current tmpdir symlink disappears during xdist cleanup
description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-na.1--1 (epic sase-na, plan 202608/word_completion_ranking.md) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP, and carried forward here by sase-na.land because it is unrelated to that epic's word-ranking work.

Reported symptom: 'just check' can exit non-zero after its scoped pytest lane has already reported that every selected test passed. The reporter attributed this to a race in pytest's tmpdir cleanup that runs after xdist workers finish, where the 'pytest-current' symlink under the base temp directory is removed by one process while another is still resolving it, so the run fails during teardown rather than on any test assertion.

Honest state of the evidence: the original note is the only observation. sase-na.land did not reproduce it while landing the epic on master eba0eab73 in workspace sase_12 -- 'just test-scoped' passed 1493 tests cleanly, and several targeted pytest runs over tests/history, tests/ace/tui/widgets, and tests/ace/tui completed without a teardown failure. So this is an intermittent race whose trigger conditions are not yet characterized, not a deterministic defect. The sizing reflects that: the root cause is genuinely unknown and the first real work is reproducing it under load.

Impact if real: a spurious red on the mandatory pre-reply gate is expensive, because the failure appears after a fully green test report and gives an agent no failing node to act on, so the natural response is to rerun the whole gate.

Scope: reproduce the teardown failure (most likely under repeated parallel 'just check' / 'just test-scoped' runs, possibly with concurrent runs from sibling workspaces sharing a base temp directory), capture the actual traceback and exit path, then make the cleanup tolerate a concurrently removed 'pytest-current' link rather than failing the run. If it cannot be reproduced after a bounded effort, close with that finding recorded -- do not paper over it by suppressing teardown errors generally, which would hide real cleanup failures.

Probe: 4207 ambient read(s) from 181 record(s); 150 poisoning; 33 cross-test thread(s); 0 refresh worker(s) still live after origin.

Breaking down the 150 poisoning records: 139 are the asyncio_0..8 Textual/asyncio default-executor thread pool (22 through sase.ace.tui.widgets.llm_override_indicator's run_worker(thread=True) default-resolution path exactly as sase-mv's step-1 probe already named; 117 through a second, previously-unrecorded call site -- asyncio.to_thread(prepare_loaded_agents_worker_boundary, ...) in src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_loading_disk.py (both the async_load and artifact_delta_load paths) calling get_max_running_agents() -> load_merged_config() from _loading_compute.py:404). The remaining 11 are a probe self-artifact, not a real leak: they carry thread names like "Thread-423 (load_merged_config)" that exactly match this plan's own new generation-guard regression tests (test_load_merged_config_discards_build_invalidated_by_concurrent_clear, test_owner_config_snapshot_discards_build_invalidated_by_concurrent_clear, and the token single-flight lambdas in test_config_cache_token.py), whose builder threads are created and joined entirely inside their own test. tests/_config_reader_probe.py keys self._threads purely by native thread_ident and never clears a stale entry (_remember_thread_locked's `if ident in self._threads: return`), so when the OS reuses a just-freed native thread id for one of these short-lived test threads, the probe attributes its origin to whichever unrelated earlier test first used that recycled ident. title: Stop a stale global sase build from silently answering workspace memory-drift checks
description: saseinstall: make it impossible for a bare `sase` resolved from a separate uv tool checkout to silently answer a memory-drift check about this workspace, which is the mechanism behind five phantom-drift reproductions across six agent shells.

notes.author: sase-ns.6.6.6.5
notes.text: TASK NEEDS APPROVAL: two optional complements to the landed in-repo staleness warning are outside this phase's authority and were deliberately not done. (1) Keeping /home/bryan/.local/bin/sase's uv tool install synced with master (e.g. a chezmoi apply hook or a periodic `uv tool install --reinstall -e ~/projects/github/sase-org/sase sase`) is a change to the user's machine / the chezmoi repo. (2) Wording agent instructions (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/sase/memory/*.md) to always name the venv-pinned invocation ('.venv/bin/sase memory init --check' instead of a bare 'sase ...') requires explicit user permission to edit those files. Neither is required for this phase's fix to work: the landed warning is dynamic (compares sys.executable against the invoked project's own .venv/bin/python), so once any future refresh of the global build picks up this commit, it will self-report when a workspace has its own pinned build it isn't using -- no wording change or reinstall is needed for the warning itself to start firing, only for the global build to carry the code that emits it sooner.

notes.author: sase-ns.6.6.6.5
notes.text: Landed option (a)'s in-repo half: sase memory init / sase init memory (both --check and apply) now detect when the running python differs from the invoked project's own <project_root>/.venv/bin/python while that project also carries its own .venv/bin/sase (src/sase/main/init_memory/staleness.py:workspace_pinned_sase_mismatch_warning). When it fires, the check surfaces a Warnings: line naming the foreign interpreter and the exact pinned command to re-run (e.g. '<project>/.venv/bin/sase memory init --check', or 'just check'), without failing the check (InitPlan.warnings, already rendered/propagated by the existing init-onboarding and sase-validate warning plumbing). No warning on the golden path: verified 'just check' runs sase validate's init-memory --check through this workspace's own venv-pinned python with zero warnings. Option (b) (rewording agent instructions) and the durable global-tool-sync route were deferred with a TASK NEEDS APPROVAL note, per this bead's approval boundaries. title: flake-baseline gate keeps failing on historical records for nodes that have since been fixed
description:
`just check-full`'s last gate, `just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake`, currently fails on athena with 13 reproducible-flake node IDs above tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt (window: records after the file's `# effective-after: 2026-08-15T17:22:27Z` marker).

Seven of the thirteen are the config / config-cache nodes that epic sase-ns just fixed in commit 3a22ff04f (`fix(config): isolate config cache from test-owned CONFIG_DIR`):

  tests/test_config.py::test_legacy_overlay_is_discovered_but_not_a_complete_owner
  tests/test_config.py::test_machine_overlays_require_matching_selector_and_keep_ordinary_overlays
  tests/test_config.py::test_selected_overlay_identity_cannot_be_overridden_by_other_sources
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_clear_config_cache_forces_reload
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_clear_config_cache_resets_config_token_time_gate
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_current_config_token_refresh_is_single_flight
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_explicit_invalidation_wins_race_with_background_refresh
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_first_config_token_read_does_not_start_worker
  tests/test_config_cache.py::test_yaml_content_cache_survives_config_cache_clear

The remaining ones belong to other beads (tests/ace/tui/test_top_bar_order.py::test_override_pills_keep_narrow_top_bar_in_bounds -> sase-mp, tests/main/test_var_integration.py::test_var_cli_end_to_end..., tests/test_bead/test_cli_golden.py::test_bead_cli_golden_contract[stats], tests/test_query_profile.py::test_provider_query_schema_derives_fields_from_the_notes_fixture).

The defect: `_flake_evidence_nodeids` (tests/_test_selection_health_correlation.py) flags a node once it fails across two disjoint change sets with an *interleaved* independent pass. Interleaving is evaluated between the two recorded failures, so once that shape exists in the durable store it is permanent: a later green full lane, however many, can never clear it. Every full-run record backing these nine config nodes was written by workspaces running trees that predate 3a22ff04f (newest: ~/.sase/test-selection/gh_sase-org__sase/20260816T230240Z-e50d8a9537a1-1091606-full-run.json, recorded 2026-08-16T23:08:29Z at commit e50d8a953). The fix works -- the evidence simply cannot be retired.

Today the only lever is to hand-bump `# effective-after:` in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt, which is all-or-nothing: bumping it far enough to drop the fixed config nodes also erases the still-live evidence for sase-mp and the var/bead-stats/query-profile nodes, which is exactly what the sase-mj land agent declined to do when it filed sase-mv (see that bead's SCOPE WIDENING note).

Impact: `just check-full` cannot go green on this host for any agent, on any tree, until someone resolves this by hand -- so the gate that exists to catch new flakes is currently a permanent red that every landing agent has to explain away.

Adjacent, already-solved precedent: sase-j5 taught the gate to report renamed/deleted node IDs as *stale* rather than as live flakes (`stale_flake_nodeids`, collectible-node oracle). This bead is the sibling case the same design left open: the node still collects and now passes, but its historical failure evidence is immortal.

Fix directions to weigh: record a per-node 'fixed at <commit>' retirement in the baseline file so evidence older than that commit is ignored for that node only; or treat a run of N consecutive eligible passes after the last recorded failure as retiring that node's evidence; or make `effective-after` expressible per node instead of only file-wide.

Discovered by epic sase-ns's land agent, routed from a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note left on phase bead sase-ns.2 (which explicitly deferred the aging-out decision to the land agent / sase-mv closer).

notes.text: Implemented direction 3's mechanism (per-node '# fixed-at: <UTC timestamp> <nodeid>' baseline directive) carrying direction 1's framing (a human declares a node fixed and names the commit). Rejected direction 2 (N consecutive eligible passes retires evidence) because the still-live sase-mp node (test_top_bar_order.py::test_override_pills_keep_narrow_top_bar_in_bounds) has ~90 eligible passes since its last failure and is dormant, not fixed -- any N that retires the nine config nodes would retire it too, which the bead's exit criteria call a bug. title: Rebaseline 7 stale ACE PNG goldens left by landed UI changes (artifacts split, help filter, models-panel navigation)
description:
Seven ACE PNG snapshot goldens fail deterministically in the dedicated serial visual lane on clean master f8b4ebb11, and no active epic owns the commits that changed them.

REPRODUCTION (workspace sase_14, clean master f8b4ebb11, after a from-scratch 'just install'):
  .venv/bin/pytest -q -n 0 -m visual tests/ace/tui/visual/
  -> 16 failed, 681 passed, 14 deselected in 1506.01s (0:25:06)

Serial (-n 0), so this is not xdist contention.

THE SEVEN NODES THIS BEAD OWNS:
  tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_artifacts_split.py::test_artifacts_split_mode_png_snapshot[narrow-size0-artifacts_split_narrow_120x40]
  tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_artifacts_split.py::test_artifacts_split_mode_png_snapshot[even-size1-artifacts_split_even_120x40]
  tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_artifacts_split.py::test_artifacts_split_mode_png_snapshot[wide-size2-artifacts_split_wide_120x40]
  tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_artifacts_split.py::test_artifacts_split_mode_png_snapshot[narrow-size3-artifacts_split_narrow_80x24]
  tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_help_panel.py::test_help_panel_filter_png_snapshot
