  tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_models_panel_navigation.py::test_models_panel_mixed_builtin_bucket_png_snapshot

The other nine failures from the same run are already owned and are NOT in scope here: four retry-e2e nodes -> sase-dc; one Artifacts Files node -> sase-my (an AttributeError before any PNG comparison, not a golden diff); three Artifacts Beads nodes -> recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on active epic sase-nb; one AXE chop-overrun node -> recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on active epic sase-jx.

EVIDENCE OF SCALE (.pytest_cache/sase-visual/*/summary.txt): help_keymaps_filter_120x40 changed 681/1520532 pixels (0.0448%), all 681 material, expected and actual both 1482x1026. Small, single-label-shaped diffs like this one match the stale-text signature rather than renderer variance.

LIKELY CAUSE: recent UI commits landed without regenerating goldens. Candidates, none owned by an active epic: 3f5378aeb 'feat(artifacts): conform pane contract capabilities' (closed epic sase-m6, phase sase-m6.10) for the four artifacts_split nodes; 83e2ceea6 'feat(ace): unify monitor gear iconography across nodes and the top bar' (tale plan 202608/monitor_gear_iconography.md, no bead) and 3c9df1182 'feat(ace-tui)!: unify the Artifacts keymap across Patch and its siblings' for the help-panel and models-panel-navigation chrome. Note that epic sase-m6's coordinated golden regeneration plus 563a67fb0 already rebaselined the 41-node models-panel drift tracked by the now-closed sase-nq; these two navigation nodes survived that pass and are a later, distinct drift.

SCOPE: for each of the seven, inspect the expected/actual/diff artifacts and confirm the change is confined to intentional text or chrome from a landed commit (no scattered anti-aliasing noise, which would instead indicate renderer variance and belongs with the retired sase-dl class). Rebaseline only the confirmed-intentional goldens with --sase-update-visual-snapshots; investigate rather than accept any node whose diff is not explained by a landed UI change. Do NOT run 'just test-visual-update' broadly -- closed sase-lo records that it rewrites every golden in the suite and silently absorbs unrelated drift. Verify with a serial 'just test-visual' afterward.

IMPACT: contained. The PNG suite is excluded from both 'just test' and 'just test-cost', so 'just check' and 'just check-full' stay green and no landing agent is blocked. This is filed because the cause here is tractable and code-attributable -- stale goldens from identified commits, fixable by a scoped rebaseline -- which is a different class from the renderer/environment variance the owner deprioritized on 2026-08-14 when closing sase-l8 and sase-dl.

DISCOVERED BY: the task-bead triage agent sweeping the sase task backlog on 2026-08-16, while verifying whether sase-np/sase-nq were still reproducible (they were not, and both were closed).

notes.text: Fixed by epic sase-ns.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.5 (commit b6246f1cf). Root cause: the test forked a multiprocessing 'fork' subprocess from a multi-threaded xdist worker to hold the epic plan launch lock -- a fork-after-threads hazard that could inherit a co-resident execnet receiver thread's state, which is why the node accumulated 12 pre-fix records across six workspaces at twelve HEADs. The fork is replaced by _foreign_epic_launch_lock_holder, an in-process context manager that takes fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on _epic_plan_launch_lock_path(anchor) and writes the same holder JSON the production epic_plan_launch_lock writes (pid/op/plan_file/started_at -- verified field-for-field against cli_work_from_plan_store.py:219-227). Because flock ownership belongs to the open file description rather than the process, the holder is indistinguishable from a foreign one; the helper self-checks this by asserting a second open() of the same path is refused with BlockingIOError before yielding. The inflight-launch-holds-anchor assertion is intact: the four patches are byte-identical (including resolve_beads_location's side_effect=AssertionError guarding against sidecar materialization), and start_launch.assert_called_once() plus the 'mon-contended' monitor-id assertion both survive. The one dropped assertion, process.exitcode == 0, tested the deleted harness subprocess rather than the code under test. Full-lane evidence: monitored just check-full swk45sjycf4e (31845 passed, 680.50s) did not name this node anywhere in its output. Land agent retired all 12 pre-fix records (newest 2026-08-17T01:37:59Z, all predating the fix) with a # fixed-at: 2026-08-17T08:54:01Z entry in commit cf7eeee03; just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake no longer names it.

title: Declare fixed-at retirement for already-fixed nodes still red in the flake-baseline gate
description:
Epic sase-ns.6 (task bead sase-nv) added a per-node '# fixed-at: <UTC timestamp> <node id>' directive to tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt that retires only that node's failure evidence recorded at or before the instant its fix landed. It was applied to the nine config/config-cache nodes fixed by 3a22ff04f, and the epic's land agent added the sase-md config-center node fixed by d9b2984a7. Other nodes whose fixes had already landed were never declared, so 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' (the last gate of 'just check-full') stays red on historical evidence for tests that now pass.

MEASURED CASE (do this one first, it is proven):
tests/ace/tui/test_top_bar_order.py::test_override_pills_keep_narrow_top_bar_in_bounds was fixed by commit 981106799 'docs: migrate docs and tests off retired model-alias names' (2026-08-16T04:53:04Z, epic sase-mf phase sase-mf.4). Task bead sase-mp is CLOSED as done on that fix. The durable store holds 12 failure records for the node, the last two at 2026-08-16T05:28:43Z and 05:37:11Z, both from HEAD 6f7052fc9 -- which is NOT an ancestor of 981106799, i.e. stale pre-fix trees, exactly the 'Known limitation' the baseline header documents. Verified on 2026-08-17 at HEAD 6000a54a1 with a probe baseline: adding

  # fixed-at: 2026-08-16T04:53:04Z tests/ace/tui/test_top_bar_order.py::test_override_pills_keep_narrow_top_bar_in_bounds

retires 8 more failures and drops the node out of the gate's report (7 -> 6 exceeding nodes). The node also passes in isolation (-p no:randomly, 1 passed).

REMAINING AUDIT (root cause not yet determined -- do not declare fixed-at without naming a fix commit):
- tests/main/test_var_integration.py::test_var_cli_end_to_end_refreshes_index_and_round_trips_machine_outputs -- 15 failure records, last 2026-08-16T19:55:21Z at HEAD 0ec2018f1.
- tests/test_bead/test_cli_golden.py::test_bead_cli_golden_contract[stats] -- 17 failure records, last 2026-08-16T23:08:29Z at HEAD e50d8a953. Bead sase-na.3 notes the golden fixture was missing a Flags line, which in-progress epic sase-nb may have since supplied.
- tests/test_query_profile.py::test_provider_query_schema_derives_fields_from_the_notes_fixture -- 10 failure records, last 2026-08-16T15:12:02Z at HEAD 95d66f59c.
All three pass in isolation today and none has failed across the 117 full-run records after 2026-08-16T06:00Z, but 'passes in isolation' does not distinguish a fixed node from a live full-lane flake. For each, either identify the fix commit and declare it, or leave it reported and file/corroborate a flake bead.

SCOPE GUARDRAIL (from epic sase-ns.6's plan, 202608/task_backlog_top5.md): do not bump the file-wide '# effective-after:' timestamp as a shortcut, and do not declare a fixed-at for a node you cannot tie to a named fix commit -- that turns the directive into the blanket suppression the baseline file's header forbids ('debt to remove, not suppressions to grow').

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE TASK: epic sase-ns.6's plan explicitly scoped these four nodes out ('The other four belong to live beads and must keep being reported'), written on the belief that all four were still live. sase-mp was in fact already closed as fixed 19 hours before that plan was written. The land agent applied the mechanism only to the node its own epic fixed and filed this rather than silently overriding the plan's stated scope.

title: test_repeat_select_caches_content_read counts process-wide builtins.open, so anything else opening a file in the worker fails it
close_reason: Fixed exactly as scoped: the test no longer counts process-wide builtins.open. tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_prompt_artifact_file_cache.py:98-129 now patches the module-local seam sase.agent.artifact_files_cache._open_text and asserts read_count == baseline == 1, keeping the behavioural assertion that repeat get_prompt_content() calls do not re-read from disk. Landed in 96257e1fb 'fix(test): make cache and flake accounting deterministic'. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_prompt_artifact_file_cache.py::test_repeat_select_caches_content_read failed once under the full parallel lane and passes on a focused rerun.

EVIDENCE: durable selection store ~/.sase/test-selection/gh_sase-org__sase/20260817T011832Z-4819a03141f7-3122359-full-run.json records it in 'failures' at 2026-08-17T01:37:53Z, HEAD 4819a03141f7, workspace sase_22, changed_files ['tests/test_bead/test_flag_gate_response.py'] -- a diff that cannot touch prompt-artifact caching. Reported as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP by phase bead sase-nb.11.4 during epic sase-nb.11. Isolated rerun on HEAD 6000a54a1: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_prompt_artifact_file_cache.py -> 3 passed. This is the only failure record for the node in the whole store, so it is below the flake gate's reproducible bar and is NOT in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

ROOT CAUSE (from the test source, tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_prompt_artifact_file_cache.py:97-124): the test wraps 'patch("builtins.open", side_effect=counting_open)' around three get_prompt_content() calls and then asserts 'open_count == baseline' exactly. builtins.open is process-wide, so any other code executing in that xdist worker during the patched window -- a background thread (config-cache refresh, monitor reconciliation), an atexit/GC finalizer, or lazy module state -- increments open_count and fails the assertion even though the artifact cache behaved correctly. The cache under test is also process-global (sase.agent.artifact_files_cache.get_global_cache()), which the test clears at entry but which nothing prevents another actor from touching.

SCOPE: stop asserting on a process-wide builtins.open count. Count reads through a seam owned by the module under test instead -- the same shape commit d9b2984a7 ('fix(tui): isolate config center state replacement') used to replace a process-wide os.replace patch with a module-local file-replacement hook -- or assert on the cache's own read counters. Keep the behavioural assertion (repeat get_prompt_content() calls must not re-read the prompt body from disk) intact.

title: SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS pins an agent runner to the launcher's flag resolution, so a scope:"project" flag would resolve against the wrong project
close_reason: Obsolete: FeatureFlagDefinition no longer has a scope field and the resolver rejects every local-config flag override, so a scope:"project" flag -- the precondition for this bead's defect -- is no longer representable.
description:
PROPOSED BY: phase bead sase-nb.2 (2026-08-16T16:49:43Z) during epic sase-nb ('Feature flags whose removal is a bead, a deadline, and a gate'); triaged and filed by the sase-nb land agent at close.

PROBLEM: epic decision 7 exports the launching process's fully resolved snapshot into SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS. src/sase/feature_flags/env.py:76 encode_feature_flags_env() serializes every decision's final boolean, and apply_feature_flags_env() writes that string into the child environment. An agent runner launched from ACE therefore inherits the ACE process's resolution -- which was computed against the launcher's config layers, not the agent workspace's project-local config -- instead of resolving for itself.

WHY IT IS DORMANT TODAY: both registered flags are scope:"global" (src/sase/feature_flags/registry.py:34,45), and src/sase/feature_flags/resolver.py:95 rejects a local-config override of a global-scope flag outright ('scope_violation'). So there is currently no flag whose correct value can differ between the launcher and the launched workspace, and the pinning is unobservable.

WHY IT NEEDS A DECISION: the scope field exists precisely so a flag can be overridden per project (docs/configuration.md documents scope:"project" as locally overridable). The first scope:"project" flag makes the inherited snapshot wrong for any agent whose workspace config disagrees with the launcher's, and the failure is silent -- the child never re-resolves, and sase.doctor.checks_flags only flags inherited env values as a warning (src/sase/doctor/checks_flags.py:259).

SCOPE: decide and implement one of -- (a) encode only scope:"global" decisions into SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS and let the child resolve project-scoped flags itself; (b) carry the launcher's project identity alongside the snapshot so the child can tell whether the pin applies to it; or (c) declare the pin intentional and make it explicit (reject scope:"project" flags at registration, or fail loudly when a child's project differs). This must be settled before the first scope:"project" flag ships, not after.

title: tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py still forks epic-plan-launch lock holders from multi-threaded xdist workers
description:
ROOT CAUSE (already proven on a sibling node): forking from a multi-threaded process inherits only the calling thread, so any lock or buffer another thread held at fork time is inherited in an indeterminate state. Under xdist, every worker carries a live execnet receiver thread, so every multiprocessing.get_context('fork') in a test is a fork-after-threads hazard. Epic sase-ns.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.5 proved this is not theoretical: it was the root cause of tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py::test_headless_epic_approval_submits_while_inflight_launch_holds_anchor (task sase-nz), which accumulated 12 full-run failure records across six workspaces and twelve HEADs between 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-17 before b6246f1cf fixed it.

WHAT IS LEFT: tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py carries the identical pattern. Two module-level helpers, _acquire_epic_plan_launch_lock (line 53) and _hold_epic_plan_launch_lock (line 62), are each launched through multiprocessing.get_context('fork') at four call sites (lines 322, 346, 420, 492), guarded by the same wall-clock bounds the fixed node used: acquired.wait(2.0), process.join(timeout=2.0), and release.wait(5.0) inside the holder.

EVIDENCE THAT THE PATTERN IS STILL LIVE: after b6246f1cf, an xdist parallel run (-n 2 --dist=loadfile) of tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py plus tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py emitted the multi-threaded-fork DeprecationWarning naming ONLY the four test_sdd_git_contention.py nodes, and zero from the fixed file. None of these four nodes is a reported flake today, so this is preventive work on a proven-hazardous pattern, not a live red.

THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS AND IS DIRECTLY REUSABLE: b6246f1cf added _foreign_epic_launch_lock_holder to tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py, an in-process @contextmanager that opens the real lock path via the production _epic_plan_launch_lock_path(anchor), takes fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB), writes the same holder JSON the production epic_plan_launch_lock writes (pid/op/plan_file/started_at), and self-checks that a second open() of the path is refused with BlockingIOError before yielding. This works because flock ownership belongs to the open file description rather than the process, so an in-process holder is indistinguishable from a foreign one to the code under test. Port that seam to these four call sites (a shared test helper is the natural home, since two files now want it) and drop the wall-clock waits, which become unnecessary once the contended window is bounded by a with-block instead of a timer.

SCOPE: tests only; no production code should change. Verify with a full parallel lane run and confirm the multi-threaded-fork DeprecationWarning no longer names any node in this file.

notes.author: sase-ns.6.6.6.land
notes.text:
FIXED. tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py no longer forks: 'grep -n "fork|multiprocessing"' now matches only two docstring lines describing what was replaced, and the 'import multiprocessing' is gone.

WHAT LANDED: a _ForeignEpicLaunchLockWorker helper replacing multiprocessing.get_context('fork') at all four call sites (the former lines 322, 346, 420, 492). It runs the target in a daemon thread inside a fresh contextvars.Context. Two independent facts make that a faithful foreign holder: flock ownership belongs to the open file description rather than the process, so a second open() of the lock path from this same process is refused exactly as from a separate process; and the production re-entrancy guard _held_epic_plan_launch_anchors is a ContextVar, so a fresh Context gives the thread the empty set a separate process would start with, preventing a short-circuit past the real flock wait.

DIVERGENCE FROM THIS BEAD'S PRESCRIPTION, DELIBERATE: this bead asked to port _foreign_epic_launch_lock_holder from b6246f1cf and drop the wall-clock waits. I did not, for two reasons. (1) That seam is a contextmanager -- it can hold the lock, but it cannot block-then-acquire. Site 1 (test_epic_plan_launch_lock_blocks_other_process_for_same_canonical_anchor) asserts a foreign party is refused while we hold and succeeds after we release, which inherently needs a concurrent actor, so a with-block cannot bound it. (2) The thread runs the real production epic_plan_launch_lock, so the holder-identity JSON asserted by the expiry test (op, plan_file, started_at) is produced by production code instead of hand-rolled in the test, which is strictly more faithful than the contextmanager's manual json.dump. The waits that remain are therefore load-bearing, not leftover timers. The shared-helper consolidation the bead suggested is not done; tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py keeps its own seam.

ASSERTION CHANGE: 'holder pid {process.pid}' became 'holder pid {os.getpid()}'. Inherent to any in-process seam, including the one this bead prescribed, since the holder JSON records the current pid either way.

VERIFICATION: 19 passed serially in the file; the blocking site measures 0.16s call time, confirming it genuinely waited on the real flock rather than short-circuiting. 41 passed across tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py + tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py run with -W error::DeprecationWarning, so no multi-threaded-fork DeprecationWarning fires -- a stronger check than this bead's 'confirm the warning names no node in this file', since a fork warning requires a fork call site and none remain. The bead's -n 2 --dist=loadfile lane could not run: the SASE pytest worker-token broker was fully subscribed by other agents (one 'scoped' holder had held 14 tokens for ~2.8h), so the xdist form was starved; the static + escalated-warning evidence above covers the same property. title: The global 'sase' on PATH is a uv tool install pinned to a separate checkout, so ad hoc 'sase init memory --check' compares a workspace against the wrong templates
description:
ROOT CAUSE (verified in this environment, not inferred): /home/bryan/.local/bin/sase is a uv tool install -- its shebang is /home/bryan/.local/share/uv/tools/sase/bin/python3 -- editable-installed against a separate checkout at ~/projects/github/sase-org/sase. It is versioned independently of any ephemeral sase_<N> workspace. Proof at the time of filing: the global 'sase --help' prints a flat comma-separated subcommand list with no 'flag' entry, while this workspace's own .venv/bin/sase prints the current grouped help and 'sase flag --help' resolves to 'Inspect the code-owned SASE feature-flag registry and scaffold a new flag plus its dedicated removal bead'. Two different builds, both answering to the name 'sase'.

WHY IT MATTERS: memory-drift checking compares a checkout's COMMITTED memory files against the templates and generator carried by whichever sase build runs the check. just check's validate recipe pins {{venv_bin}}/sase, so it always matches the workspace tree and is trustworthy. But an agent that types a bare 'sase init memory --check' or 'sase memory init --check' -- exactly what the mandatory memory-init workflow invites -- runs the global build instead, comparing this workspace's committed files against a different checkout's templates. Whenever the two checkouts sit at different commits, that reports drift that does not exist in the tree under test (or hides drift that does).

WHY THIS IS PROBABLY THE ANSWER TO A LONG-RUNNING PUZZLE: task sase-n0 collected five independent reproductions across six agent shells between 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-17 of 'sase validate says green but sase init memory --check says drift', and sase-i7 was closed as superseded into it. Epic sase-ns.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.2 then established structurally that no generator divergence exists in source: sase validate's memory step shells out to '<sys.executable> -m sase init memory --check' as a subprocess, so both entry points funnel through the identical chain plan_init_memory -> _memory_root_plans -> plan_memory_root -> memory_root_context -> render_expected_memory_files()/provider_shim_plan(). Two entry points over one generator cannot disagree -- unless they are two different INSTALLS of that generator, which is precisely what a bare 'sase' versus '{{venv_bin}}/sase' gives you. The reported disagreements also match this shape: they were heading-style and memory-README-listing diffs, i.e. template-version skew rather than logic errors.

DECIDE AND IMPLEMENT ONE OF: (a) keep the global tool install synced with master -- a chezmoi apply hook, a post-merge reinstall, or a staleness warning the CLI prints when its own build predates the workspace it is invoked in; or (b) document that bare 'sase' memory-drift checks are unreliable outside just check, and make the mandatory memory-init workflow name the venv-pinned invocation explicitly wherever it appears in agent instructions. Option (a) is the durable fix; option (b) is cheap and immediate. They are not exclusive.

NOTE ON SCOPE: option (a) may reach the chezmoi repo, which must be opened through /sase_repo rather than by path. Editing generated memory files or agent instruction shims to carry option (b)'s wording requires explicit user permission per CLAUDE.md -- leave a TASK NEEDS APPROVAL note rather than editing them unilaterally.

PROPOSED BY: phase bead sase-ns.6.6.2 of epic sase-ns.6.6, as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note on 2026-08-17T08:20:46Z; routed to a task bead by that epic's land agent, which independently re-verified both installs.

LAND-AGENT RE-VERIFICATION on master 5e58fb1c8 (read the source, not just the note): src/sase/main/init_memory/staleness.py::workspace_pinned_sase_mismatch_warning returns None unless both .venv/bin/sase and .venv/bin/python exist and sys.executable resolves to something other than the pinned python -- so it cannot false-positive on a non-workspace checkout or on the golden path. No reinstall or instruction rewording is required for the mechanism itself to work.

DEFERRED, and reported to the user rather than actioned, because both fall outside this phase's authority (recorded as a TASK NEEDS APPROVAL note on the phase bead): (1) keeping /home/bryan/.local/bin/sase's uv tool install synced with master, e.g. a chezmoi apply hook or a periodic 'uv tool install --reinstall -e ~/projects/github/sase-org/sase sase' -- that changes the user's machine and the chezmoi repo; (2) option (b), wording agent instructions (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / sase/memory/*.md) to always name the venv-pinned invocation instead of a bare 'sase ...' -- that requires explicit user permission per CLAUDE.md, which a plan file does not confer. Four of those seven (sase-jg, sase-kc, sase-nm, sase-o4) landed within the last week.

MECHANISM: Symvision's epic whitelist lets an in-progress epic pass '--epic-symbol "<bead>(<symbol>)"' in the Justfile's _lint-symvision recipe to exempt a symbol that is not yet wired up. The exemption is keyed to the bead, and Symvision correctly rejects an entry whose bead is closed: "bead '<id>' is closed. Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry and clean up the symbol." So the gate already detects the condition. What is missing is that nothing does the cleanup at the moment the epic closes. The entries go stale the instant 'sase bead close <epic>' succeeds, and the discovery mechanism is that some unrelated agent's mandatory 'just check' goes red on a clean master tree it did not touch.

COST PER INSTANCE: every agent whose tree reaches the lint gate between the epic's close and the cleanup landing gets a red 'just check' with no relationship to its own diff. sase-o4's reporter confirmed with 'git stash -u' that master itself was red. Each instance then costs a triage sweep, a filed task bead, a TaskTriage gate for the owner, and a worker launch - for cleanup the closing agent was best placed to do, since it is the one that knows why each symbol was exempted.

WHY THE CLOSING AGENT IS THE RIGHT OWNER: the land prompt already tells the land agent to run 'just symvision' AFTER closing the epic, because epic-symbol whitelist entries expire at close, and to remove the stale entries and unused code it reports. That instruction exists and is still being missed often enough to produce four beads in a week, so an instruction alone is not sufficient - the step needs to be discoverable and hard to skip.

SCOPE: make the epic close reliably retire its own whitelist entries rather than leaving them for the next agent. Candidate approaches, to be chosen by the worker:
  (a) give the land step a real command that lists the closing epic's own --epic-symbol entries, so the agent does not have to grep the Justfile and reason about which of the entries are its own (sase-o4's fix had to leave the still-open sase-n4 and sase-n4.5 entries untouched while removing five sase-nb ones);
  (b) have 'sase bead close' on an epic detect remaining entries keyed to that bead and refuse, warn, or emit the exact follow-up work;
  (c) tighten the land xprompt so the symvision pass is a gate rather than a trailing instruction.
Note that the per-symbol resolution is genuine judgment work and must NOT be automated away: sase-o4's precedent resolved its five symbols three different ways (tools/ pragma for two, privatize-and-drop-from-__all__ for two, outright delete plus move the seam into tests/_conftest_runtime.py for one), per the Symvision epic-whitelist policy in sase/memory/symvision.md. The goal is to make the work happen at close time, not to make it mechanical.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing the epic-whitelist policy itself, and the separate transient-lookup defect in closed task sase-it (Symvision briefly failing to find an existing in-progress bead), which is a different failure with a different cause.

VERIFICATION: after the change, closing an epic that still has --epic-symbol entries should surface them at close time. A regression test should cover the discovery path; reproducing the human-judgment cleanup is not required.

notes.author: sase-o8.land--1
notes.text:
Verified all five phases against the plan and the source, checked integration with
everything that landed alongside the epic, and routed every phase follow-up.

VERIFIED BY READING THE CODE AND THE FIVE COMMITS, not just the phase notes:

- o8.1 (555eba0b1) `_ranking_signal_rows.py` owns the score meter, reason chip, age
  formatter, palette and `ranking_signal_legend()`/`ranking_label_width()` behind a
  structural protocol; `_history_word_rows.py` and
  `_prompt_input_bar_completion_panel_labels.py` import them. No second meter
  implementation exists anywhere in `src/` (the `▰`/`▱` glyphs appear only in that
  module).
- o8.2 (ded7f1a5f) `_STORE_VERSION = 2` with `_READABLE_STORE_VERSIONS = {1, 2}`,
  per-entry context bags plus `context_uses`, `prompt_count`/`context_frequency` corpus
  stats, deterministic bag and vocabulary trims that log when they bite, `_add_context`
  excludes an entry's own `<text>` token, `seed_common_placeholders_from_history()`
  upgrades a v1 file in place via `_merge_seed_into_store()` keeping `count`/`last_used`
  authoritative and re-reading under the lock, and `remove_common_placeholder()` leaves
  corpus stats intact.
- o8.3 (577986af5) `prompt_placeholder_ranking.py` implements 0.50/0.30/0.20 weights, a
  14-day half-life, capped lift `log2(lift)/log2(8)` times `hits/(hits+2)` shrinkage
  gated by `RELATION_MIN_PROMPTS = 8`, a deterministic `(-score, casefold, text)` sort,
  the memo on `CommonPlaceholderIndex._ranking_memo`, and fixed-width `last_used` parsing
  with an epoch-0 fallback and age clamping. `prompt_context_tokens()` is shared by
  recording and ranking, so evidence and queries cannot drift.
- o8.4 (68aaa6863) the warm cache holds a `CommonPlaceholderIndex` while
  `common_placeholders()` still returns `list[str] | None` derived alongside it;
  `forget_common_placeholder()` drops the entry from the warm index so Ctrl+D stays
  instant; `build_indexed_placeholder_completion_result()` ranks first, hands texts to
  the Rust engine, and reattaches `PlaceholderRankingMetadata` by exact text;
  `_placeholder_highlight.py` routes through it only when the app exposes an index; and
  `placeholder_ranking`/`placeholder_ranking_signals` land in settings parsing, the JSON
  schema and `default_config.yml` defaulting to smart/true.
- o8.5 (5abf9eb64) `append_placeholder_completion_row()` appends meter then chip and
  degrades chip-first-then-meter by width; `placeholder_label_width()` measures both
  source groups with badge cells so they share one column;
  `placeholder_completion_subtitle()` implements the four-rung ladder; `docs/ace.md` and
  `docs/configuration.md` document the signals, glyphs, degradation and both settings;
  the `placeholder_common_completion_panel_120x40.png` golden was regenerated.
- Plan boundaries honored: no `../sase-core` change was needed or made, and no feature
  flag was created (`sase flag list` shows only the two pre-existing unrelated flags),
  both exactly as the plan required.

INTEGRATION: fourteen non-epic commits landed between the epic's first commit
(555eba0b1) and its last (5abf9eb64), which is HEAD -- nothing has landed since, and the
working tree is clean. Only six paths overlap between the two sets (`Justfile`,
`docs/ace.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `src/sase/config/sase.schema.json`,
`src/sase/default_config.yml`, and the placeholder PNG golden), and because the epic's
own final commit is the newest writer of each, every one was already reconciled at
commit time; the golden's last two writers are 442d8711d then 5abf9eb64 in that order.
The adjacent ACE TUI work (procs/monitors, artifacts rail, notifications, flags CLI)
touches no placeholder-completion, ranking, or history-store code, and nothing in the
tree duplicates what this epic added.

SYMVISION: no `sase-o8` `--epic-symbol` entries remain in the `Justfile` -- the phases
retired their own (o8.3 retargeted `load_common_placeholder_index` off closed o8.2, and
o8.5 dropped `sase-o8.4(PlaceholderRankingMetadata)` when it consumed it). The five
DISCOVERED ISSUE notes on this epic from agents 04i, 04j, 04l, 04o and the
toobig-2x split worker are therefore all resolved; the systemic pattern behind them
stays with in-progress task sase-o7.

FOLLOW-UPS ROUTED (every `PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP:` note on the five phase beads):

1. o8.2's flaky
   `tests/ace/tui/modals/test_snippet_name_modal.py::test_derived_only_collision_returns_composed_template`
   -> new ready task sase-og (large). It is an ACE TUI full-parallel/pass-isolation node,
   so per sase-ct's retired-umbrella policy it became a narrow node-named task rather
   than a +1, with RELATED notes to sase-ct, to sibling-node precedent sase-ke, to
   sase-lh.2 (earliest sighting, 2026-08-14) and to sase-oe (same bounded-wait shape,
   filed the same day).
2. o8.2's and o8.5's flaky
   `tests/fakey/test_usage_limit_e2e.py::test_usage_limit_failure_disables_only_fakey_and_preserves_error`
   -> +1 on ready task sase-ob, which had been filed 31 minutes earlier for exactly this
   one-ULP `TemporaryProviderDisable` comparison. Both epic reproductions (10:55Z and
   13:07Z, on unrelated trees) are recorded there.
3. o8.3's flaky
   `tests/test_config_cache.py::test_drain_config_token_refresh_joins_worker_and_advances_epoch`
   -> +1 on in-progress task sase-mv (now +19): same root cause, sibling node in the same
   file, and the failure mode (`current_config_token()` returning a live process-identity
   key instead of the patched token) matches sase-mv's recorded gw8 ordering exactly. The
   +1 flags in-progress phase sase-ns.6.6.6.1 as the active fix to confirm against.
4. o8.4's "retarget or consume `monitor_row_agent_name`" -> already resolved, no bead
   needed. `sase-o9.4` consumed it at `src/sase/ace/tui/modals/procs_pane_selection.py:64`
   in commit 790cb61ee and deleted the `sase-o9.4(monitor_row_agent_name)` whitelist
   entry; the `Justfile` now carries only unrelated `sase-n4` entries.

Both flake nodes were additionally recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE note on in-progress
epic sase-j7, whose goal is that this class stops failing under the full parallel lane.

prints and commits the pre-relocation bead ID. My create raced the sase-o9 land agent,

+1 on in-progress task sase-j0 (now +18) with the measured numbers, noting that
parser_create, pilot_pause_delay and subprocess_run are new overruns beyond sase-j0's

sase-ns.6.6.6.1, and sase-oh). No test touching placeholder completion, ranking, the

title: Command palette hides grouping-cycle on Artifacts panes that already bind o/O
close_reason: Fixed by 19bdc94db (2026-08-20). src/sase/ace/tui/commands/_app_metadata.py:490-492 now scopes cycle_grouping_mode and cycle_grouping_mode_reverse to CL_AGENTS instead of AGENTS_ONLY, matching the contract-correct availability check at availability.py:267 (PaneCapability.GROUPING). Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
REPRODUCTION
On the Patches, Stitches, or Files pane, o / O cycle the L0 grouping bucket (check_app_action already allows cycle_grouping_mode / cycle_grouping_mode_reverse whenever the active artifacts contract has PaneCapability.GROUPING). Opening the command palette on those panes does not offer "Cycle grouping mode" or "Cycle grouping mode (reverse)".

ROOT CAUSE
src/sase/ace/tui/commands/_app_metadata.py scopes both actions to AGENTS_ONLY:

    ("cycle_grouping_mode", "Cycle grouping mode", "Grouping", AGENTS_ONLY, ()),
    ("cycle_grouping_mode_reverse", "Cycle grouping mode (reverse)", "Grouping", AGENTS_ONLY, ()),

CL_AGENTS already exists in src/sase/ace/tui/commands/_tabs.py for artifacts+agents. Availability.py is already contract-correct; only the palette tab tuple is wrong.

IMPACT
Keybinding and help/footer/badge surfaces agree that grouping-cycle lives on every grouping-capable Artifacts pane. The palette is the odd one out. Predates and is independent of the grouping_cycle_back_to_o key swap (o/O vs B/I).

SCOPE
Change those two APP_COMMAND_META tab tuples from AGENTS_ONLY to CL_AGENTS (or equivalent). Add/adjust catalog tests so the palette lists the actions on Artifacts as well as Agents, and still hides them on AXE. Do not change keybindings or check_app_action.

OUT OF SCOPE
Beads and Plans have no grouping-mode data; the keys are a silent no-op there. Do not invent a grouping capability for those panes just to make the palette row appear.

title: test_usage_limit_failure_disables_only_fakey_and_preserves_error compares TemporaryProviderDisable timestamps at float ULP
close_reason: The agent that fixed this forgot to close the bead.
description:
tests/fakey/test_usage_limit_e2e.py::test_usage_limit_failure_disables_only_fakey_and_preserves_error failed once in an escalated full-suite just check (31872 passed, 1 failed) on an unrelated Artifacts relation-panel-collapse tree.

Failure:
  assert TemporaryProviderDisable(...) == TemporaryProviderDisable(...)
  Differing attributes: created_at, expires_at
  created_at: 1786970847.4598663 != 1786970847.4598665
  expires_at: 1786971747.4598663 != 1786971747.4598665

Reproduction: the test calls disable_provider("claude", 900.0, source="ace") to plant a sibling disable, then after the fakey usage-limit run asserts get_active_provider_disables()["claude"] == sibling. Those objects agree on provider/source/window and differ only at one ULP of the float timestamps — consistent with a serialize/reload or a second time.time() sample, not with a real disable-window mutation.

Impact: one-off full-lane flake; the relation-panel change does not touch fakey or usage-limit disable storage.

Fix: stop comparing the reconstructed disable to the original object with ==. Assert the identity fields (provider, source, duration) and compare timestamps with a tolerance, or freeze time so created_at/expires_at are bit-identical across the store round-trip.

Not a duplicate of sase-nt (Antigravity @small routing) or sase-nh (Launch Control from usage-limit notifications). In-progress epic sase-n4.5.4 is topical (usage-limit landing) but is about first-writer bindings and Antigravity routing, not this assertion.

notes.author: sase-o9.land--2
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE: The checked-in completion snapshot tests/completion/snapshots/cli_spec.json is already stale on master, so tests/completion/test_snapshot.py fails two nodes and holds `just test-cost`/`just check-full` red for every agent on the branch.

REPRODUCTION (workspace sase_13, HEAD c715bacbc, monitor 7r3cvqgwvqtw, 2026-08-17): the full test-cost lane reported `2 failed, 32085 passed, 11 skipped` and the only failures were tests/completion/test_snapshot.py::test_checked_in_snapshot_has_no_drift and ::test_current_structural_view_matches_checked_in_snapshot. Reproduced directly by diffing current_structural_view() against the committed JSON: the entire drift is one missing node, .root.subcommands[bead].subcommands[epic-symbols] (present in the live argparse tree, absent from the snapshot), plus the subcommand-order change that its insertion causes. Nothing else differs.

ROOT CAUSE: `sase bead epic-symbols` was added by commit fa1948437 ("feat(bead): refuse close while leftover --epic-symbol entries remain"), and `git log -S` confirms that is the only commit that introduces the string in src/sase. Phase sase-oc.1's commit 48856bc89 then added cli_spec.json (its only commit in that file's history) generated from a tree that did not yet contain fa1948437 — the two landed one commit apart from parallel workspaces, so the snapshot was correct when generated and stale the moment it landed.

IMPACT: this is a hard, deterministic red gate, not a flake, and it blocks the pytest cost lane for everyone on master until the snapshot is regenerated.

FIX: `just sync-completion-spec` (tools/sync_completion_spec --write), then review the regenerated diff — it should contain only the bead epic-symbols subtree and the reordering.

WHY HERE AND NOT A NEW TASK: routed via /sase_new_task. `sase bead search` over every task status for cli_spec/completion.snapshot/sync-completion-spec/completion spec/epic-symbols and the full --since 1w --status all task sweep found no semantic duplicate (sase-o7 is about leftover Justfile --epic-symbol entries; sase-ny is about stale ACE PNG goldens; neither shares this root cause). This epic has a direct causal link — sase-oc.1 landed the stale snapshot, phases sase-oc.3 through sase-oc.8 remain in progress and own the spec, and the epic's own goal is a grammar that cannot drift from the argparse tree — so it belongs here rather than on a standalone bead. Worth considering as part of the fix: the drift gate cannot catch a snapshot that goes stale via a commit landing in parallel, which is exactly what happened; a regeneration step in the land path (or a CI-side regenerate-and-diff) would close that window.

PROPOSED BY: the land agent for epic sase-o9 (First-class sase monitors on the Admin Center Procs tab), which found it in its landing gate. sase-o9 did not cause it: its five commits (cc805197b, 6bd5d5722, 7202e847b, 790cb61ee, 26fefdab7) touch only src/sase/ace/tui/**, docs/ace.md, tests, and one transient Justfile --epic-symbol line — no argparse parser, no src/sase/completion/**.

notes.author: sase-op.land
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE: `sase glossary show/read` TERM positionals and `sase glossary log -t/--term` have no live-value completion, so <TAB> on a glossary term offers nothing.

EVIDENCE (workspace sase_13, HEAD 6ac274be5, 2026-08-17): the command tree itself IS in the checked-in spec — tests/completion/snapshots/cli_spec.json contains /glossary, /glossary/list, /glossary/log, /glossary/read, /glossary/show — but every term slot carries kind: null (/glossary/read [('term', None)], /glossary/show [('term', None)]). src/sase/completion/kinds.py::ValueKind has no GLOSSARY member and neither src/sase/completion/candidates/catalog.py nor providers.py registers a fetcher for one.

WHY THIS IS ROUTED TO YOU, NOT A NEW TASK BEAD: epic sase-op (`sase glossary` command group, landed today) deliberately left ValueKind.GLOSSARY unset — its plan recorded that no live-value provider existed for term slots at the time — and phase sase-op.6 raised it as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP. sase-oc.5 (Value-kind provider catalog) and sase-oc.6 (Dynamic values wired into every shell) own exactly this mechanism, and the whole `sase glossary` group landed *during* sase-oc's run, so it is precisely the kind of since-the-epic-started command your land agent is meant to integrate. sase-oc.8 (Documentation, polish, and reach) covers the same reach concern.

SCOPING NOTE FOR WHOEVER WORKS IT: the fetcher must list a project's configured glossary terms plus display aliases. The obvious helper, editor_glossary_catalog_for_project() in src/sase/xprompt/glossary_catalog.py, is NOT usable — catalog.py's module docstring forbids sase.xprompt (and sase.ace / sase.main.parser / rich / textual) imports on the candidates fast path. A provider would read the project's glossary config directly through src/sase/glossary_config.py (resolve_glossary_config / GLOSSARY_CONFIG_KEY) and use the project's sase.yml as its source path for cache invalidation, mirroring _memory_candidates. Terms are display strings with spaces (e.g. 'Agent Hood'), so quoting in the zsh/bash/fish emitters needs checking.

notes.author: sase-oc.land
notes.text:
LANDED. VERIFIED (step 1): all 8 phases closed done; read every child note and confirmed each was addressed. The epic's own two DISCOVERED ISSUEs are resolved on master — the stale tests/completion/snapshots/cli_spec.json (missing bead epic-symbols) regenerates clean (tools/sync_completion_spec --check exits 0), and live flag bead sase-om now has its registry definition (src/sase/feature_flags/registry.py, key completion_refresh_on_update), so the feature-flags lint gate is green. Read the source behind the phase claims rather than trusting them: entry.py's pre-argparse guard matches the plan's snippet exactly; build/model/shorten/kinds produce the spec all three emitters consume; emit_zsh writes _arguments -C -s -S with exclusion lists, mutex groups, remainders and :kind:{__sase_candidates ...} actions; emit_bash and emit_fish carry the same alias policy and kind markers; install.py resolves a target, writes atomically, zcompiles, probes _comps[sase] and stamps; checks_completion.py registers completion.install and completion.registration; update_handler.py calls maybe_refresh_installed_completions behind the beta flag. Ran the suites: 235 completion/parser/fast-path/contract tests pass (1 skip: fish absent from this host), and a full-suite 'just check' escalation reported 32630 passed with only the two pre-existing tests/test_force_reuse_launch_seam.py failures, reproduced on clean master with my tree stashed and corroborated on task sase-ot (+1). End-to-end on the real host: 'sase completion install zsh' detects, targets, writes, zcompiles, migrates, stamps and verifies _comps[sase]=_sase; a live interactive-zsh pty confirms 'sase bead sh<TAB>' -> 'sase bead show' and 'sase bead show <TAB>' inserting the live candidates' common prefix.

INTEGRATED (step 2): reviewed every non-epic commit since 48856bc89. Three touched CLI surface. f5565edda's root -f/--enable-feature and -F/--disable-feature already resolve to kind flag. f6d757e2c and a383212a2 landed the whole sase glossary group mid-epic with its TERM slots completing as bare files — sase-op.6 recorded exactly that as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP ('ValueKind.GLOSSARY was intentionally left unset'). Wired it here: ValueKind.GLOSSARY plus PATH_OVERRIDES for glossary show/read TERM and glossary log -t/--term, and a catalog provider that reads the project's memory.glossary node through yaml_safe_load and offers slug-form references (agent-hood) with each term's shortened definition, plus authored aliases described as 'alias of <Term>'. Slug form is deliberate: sase glossary resolves references case- and separator-insensitively, so a slug is the one shape that never needs shell quoting. The kind holds the fast path's import-set and 150ms budget (added to the contract test's parametrization) and the spec snapshot is regenerated. Recorded the outcome on sase-op so its land agent does not redo it. Also gave 'sase completion candidates KIND' the shipped-kind choices it was missing, so the epic's own command completes its own value kinds.

FIXED (epic-caused): resolve_target picked the first writable scanned directory, which on any oh-my-zsh host is an unrelated enabled plugin's own directory — this epic had installed _sase and _sase.zwc into ~/.oh-my-zsh/plugins/z on athena, where the script would vanish from fpath the day that plugin is disabled. Framework plugin trees and cache roots are now never chosen; a framework's completions drop-in directory is preferred and created when the framework ships the fpath entry without the directory (verified: ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/completions registers before compinit on this host, while ~/.zfunc is appended after compinit and does not), home directories beat system-wide ones, and a reinstall removes the script a previous install stamped elsewhere so changing targets never leaves a second copy. The stray plugin-directory files are gone. docs/completion.md documents all of it.

FOLLOW-UPS: filed sase-ou (sase/core/__init__.py eager facade imports inflate the fast-path floor, from sase-oc.4), sase-ov (repo completion cannot see linked/sidecar/external repos because repo_inventory pulls sase.sdd/ACE/rich, from sase-oc.5), sase-ow (measure fish latency; fish is not installed on athena, from sase-oc.8), sase-ox (#/%/@ completion inside sase run's prompt text, plan-deferred) and sase-oy (chezmoi deployment of the generated scripts, plan-deferred). Not filed: sase-oc.1's flaky test_on_alias_edited_offers_commit_when_in_repo is already tracked by sase-oh and sase-oc.6's test-cost budget failure by sase-j0 — corroborating notes added to both; sase-oc.1's stale sase-o8.4 epic-symbol entry and sase-oc.3/.4/.7's chezmoi memory-shim drift are both already resolved on master (Justfile carries no sase-o8 or sase-oc entries, PlaceholderRankingMetadata has a caller, and the SASE validation gate is green); and the plan's third deferred item, a carapace-spec emitter, is recorded in docs/completion.md#deferred but deliberately not filed — SASE targets POSIX hosts and nothing consumes it. NOTED, not fixed: src/sase/completion/candidates/catalog.py is now 729 lines, past the plan's own 700-line split-before-you-grow bar though well inside the toobig gate; splitting it cleanly needs the shared private helpers promoted to a public module, which is not work to start at land time.

GATES: just check exits 0 (fmt, keep-sorted, ruff, mypy, feature flags, pyscripts, test-waits, changelog, patch/stitch terminology, symvision, toobig, SASE validation, committed plans, scoped tests); just fmt-check exits 0; sase bead epic-symbols sase-oc reports no entries.

notes.author: sase-oc.4
notes.text: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: sase/core/__init__.py eagerly imports changespec, patch, clipboard, glossary_facade, paths, shell, and time at package-import time (~19ms measured), so any `sase.core.*` import -- including sase.core.rust, used by every fast path -- pays for all of them. title: Procs pane hints line overflows its width: 'Esc: close' is already clipped at 120 columns, and the conditional monitor token drops three more keys
close_reason: Fixed by 671d27c89 'fix(ace): stabilize responsive pane layout': 'Add explicit overflow affordances for Procs hints ... so compact layouts show omitted shortcuts instead of silently clipping them.' ProcsPane._hints (src/sase/ace/tui/modals/procs_pane.py:186-212) now ends in _fit_hints(tokens, protected={...}), which measures #procs-hints width and drops unprotected tokens rather than letting the line clip. The three config_center_procs_tab goldens were regenerated in that commit. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
PROPOSED BY: closed phase bead sase-o9.5 (2026-08-17); re-measured by the sase-o9 land agent on master 26fefdab7.

DEFECT: `ProcsPane._hints()` (src/sase/ace/tui/modals/procs_pane.py) builds one fixed-width line and renders it into the `#procs-hints` `Static`. Nothing truncates, abbreviates, or wraps it, so the tail is silently cut off and the user loses real keybindings with no ellipsis or any other signal that more exists.

MEASURED (character counts of the rendered string, and the committed PNG goldens):
  - Without the monitor token: 114 chars. At a 120-column terminal the pane affords ~108 columns, so `Esc: close` is already cut to `Esc:`. Visible in tests/ace/tui/visual/snapshots/png/config_center_procs_tab_120x40.png.
  - With sase-o9.4's conditional `⏎: agent` token (+10 chars = 124): the line now cuts at `Tab:`, losing `tab  Esc: close`. Visible in config_center_procs_tab_monitors_120x40.png.
  - At 90 columns with the token, the cut lands right after `': jump`, losing `ctrl+d/u, g/G: scroll  Tab: tab  Esc: close`. Visible in config_center_procs_tab_monitors_90x40.png.

SO: the overflow is PRE-EXISTING (the 120-column clip of `close` predates sase-o9), and sase-o9's conditional monitor token widens the loss by 10 columns whenever a monitor row with a resolvable agent is selected. Both belong to the same fix; neither is worth a separate bead.

SCOPE: give the Procs hints line a width-aware treatment. Candidate approaches for the worker to choose between: render it as a Rich `Text` with `overflow='ellipsis'` so truncation is at least honest; drop lower-value tokens as width shrinks (the pane already knows its own width); or shorten the fixed tokens (`Tab: tab` and `Esc: close` are the least informative characters on the line). Check whether other panes with hints lines share the defect before inventing a Procs-only mechanism.

VERIFICATION: rebaseline the three Procs PNG goldens above and confirm at both 120 and 90 columns that either every token is visible or the truncation is explicit.

title: sase bead create prints and commits the pre-relocation bead ID, so an agent's follow-up commands mutate another agent's bead
close_reason: Fixed: both create surfaces now report the post-relocation ID. src/sase/bead/cli_crud_create.py:222-228 resolves it through resolve_created_bead_id(issue.id, mutation.publication_outcome.bead_relocations) and prints published_id, and the ACE Artifacts Beads create action does the same (_artifacts_beads_mutations.py:258-262). The damaging consequence -- stdout naming another agent's bead so follow-up note/update commands hit it -- is gone. RESIDUAL, deliberately not reopened: the commit subject at cli_crud_create.py:217 is still composed from the pre-relocation issue.id because the commit precedes the relocation; refile if that bookkeeping matters. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-08-17 by the sase-o8 land agent. Two agents created a task bead ~30s apart; both locally minted sase-of. The duplicate-ID relocation machinery from closed task sase-f0 worked correctly and moved the losing bead to sase-og, but nothing downstream of the relocation was updated, so the CLI told me my bead was sase-of.

EVIDENCE (shared beads store, sase/repos/beads):
  dd0f91cf 2026-08-17 09:25:16 'chore(beads): create sase-of' -> adds events/streams/sase-of.jsonl  (agent sase-o9.land)
  8c61b3c3 2026-08-17 09:26:00 'chore(beads): create sase-of' -> adds events/streams/sase-og.jsonl  (agent sase-o8.land, MINE)
My commit message still names sase-of while the stream it writes is sase-og. events/streams/sase-og.jsonl event 000001 has issue_id 'sase-og' from its very first event -- so the relocation landed in the stream but never in the caller's view. Stdout read: 'Created task: sase-of - test_derived_only_collision_...'.

CONSEQUENCE (this is the damaging part): I then ran three 'sase bead note sase-of' calls and one 'sase bead update sase-of --status ready' against what the CLI had just told me was my bead. All four hit the OTHER agent's bead. Three long RELATED notes about a test flake were appended to an unrelated Procs-hints-overflow bead, and only the note command's echoed title ('Noted: sase-of - Procs pane hints line overflows...') revealed it. I restored that bead's notes with 'sase bead update --notes' and left a correction note. Nothing was lost -- 'sase bead history' is append-only -- but a less careful agent would not have noticed, and 'sase bead close' or 'update --description' would have been considerably worse than a stray note.

MECHANISM (src/sase/bead/cli_crud_create.py:160-187): proj.create() returns an Issue whose .id is the locally minted ID. The commit message is composed from that stale id at line 182 (require_mutation_commit_message('create', [issue.id])), and line 187 prints it. The relocation happens later, inside the bead_store_mutation sync/conflict path (sase-f0 added merge_bead_event_streams_with_relocation plus the _RelocationIds allocator in conflict_resolver, which already reports 'relocated duplicate beads: <old> -> <new>' into the resolution message and sync log). So the information exists; it just never reaches the Issue object, the commit subject, or stdout.

SCOPE: make the create path report the ID that was actually stored. Candidate approaches for the worker: have the mutation context surface its relocation map and re-resolve issue.id (and the commit subject) before printing; or allocate IDs so a collision cannot happen in the first place; or, at minimum, print a loud 'relocated to <new-id>' line and exit non-zero-ish/warn so an agent scripting against stdout cannot silently address a stranger's bead. Whatever is chosen must also cover the other create surfaces that echo an id (sase bead work / epic phase minting, the ACE Artifacts Beads create action at src/sase/ace/tui/actions/_artifacts_beads_mutations.py:267).

IMPACT: SASE routinely runs many agents concurrently against one shared bead store, and /sase_new_task tells every agent to create-then-note-then-mark-ready. That is exactly the create-then-mutate sequence this defect corrupts. Two beads minted within 45s collided today with only ~6 tasks filed in the preceding hour.

RESIDUAL AFTER sase-f0: sase-f0 fixed the store-wedging half (duplicate issue_created events used to wedge every later sync for ~30 minutes). Relocation is the fix working. This bead is the reporting half that sase-f0 did not cover.

Size medium: the mechanism and the exact lines are identified above; the open decision is which of the three fix shapes to take.

title: sase-telegram CI: extractions/setup-just@v2 intermittently fails with 'no release for just matching version specifier'
close_reason: Fixed: sase-telegram's .github/workflows/ci.yml:34-37 now pins just-version: '1.58.0' AND passes github-token -- both remedies the bead proposed for the unauthenticated release-resolution failures. Verified 2026-08-24 by opening the repo through /sase_repo: the six most recent CI/Publish runs (through 2026-08-22) are all 'completed success', with no setup-just failures.
description: sase-org/sase-telegram CI (check 3.12 and check 3.13 jobs) intermittently fails at the extractions/setup-just@v2 step with ##[error]no release for just matching version specifier. Reproduced 3 times in a row on the same commit 62ddbda (fix(tests): build the flag_triage test gate through its real factory) across reruns of workflow run https://github.com/sase-org/sase-telegram/actions/runs/32035997991 -- each rerun failed at the identical setup-just step, alternating which of check (3.12)/(3.13) hit the error first (the other job then shows cancelled/skipped). Confirmed via 'gh run view 32035997991 --repo sase-org/sase-telegram --log-failed': the step logs 'Run extractions/setup-just@v2' then immediately errors with 'no release for just matching version specifier' after ~10s, with no other diagnostic. Likely cause: GitHub API rate limiting on unauthenticated requests made by extractions/setup-just@v2 to resolve the 'just' release matching its version specifier, or a release-metadata problem with that action version. This is pre-existing CI infra flakiness, not caused by or specific to commit 62ddbda -- that commit is a correct, locally-verified fix (just check passed: 581 tests, ruff/mypy clean) that is blocked from showing green CI purely by this infra issue. title: test_axe_constrained_width_no_wrap_png_snapshot snapshots the AXE detail pane before its status block renders, so the golden fails under CPU contention
close_reason: Fixed by 72f93fb1f 'fix: stabilize visual closeout and verification gates' (2026-08-21), doing exactly what the bead asked -- wait for the dashboard summary fields rather than accepting the transient. tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_axe_layout.py added _axe_long_label_summary_populated(), which requires 'review_pipeline', 'success', and '1.0s' to be present in the status and output sections, plus _pin_axe_output_top() with an explicit scroll wait, before capturing. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_axe_layout.py::test_axe_constrained_width_no_wrap_png_snapshot is a reproducible visual convergence flake against golden tests/ace/tui/visual/snapshots/png/axe_constrained_width_no_wrap_60x30.png. Found while landing epic sase-o9; NOT caused by it (proof below).

SYMPTOM: every failure has the identical signature -- changed 23145/586500 pixels (3.946292%), 23144 material at threshold 8. Decoding the failure artifact's actual.svg shows the AXE detail pane missing its whole summary block ('Status: * running', 'Interval: 60s', 'Cycles: 12', 'Errors: 0', 'Chops run: 24'); the pane instead starts at 'CHOPS' and grows a vertical scrollbar. The frame is captured before the dashboard summary fields are populated, so this is an unconverged render, not golden drift or renderer variance.

REPRODUCTION (workspace sase_13):
  just test-visual-contention -- tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_axe_layout.py
  -> at the default 26 workers on 2 CPUs, HEAD 26fefdab7: 3 of 4 runs red.
  -> at SASE_VISUAL_CONTENTION_WORKERS=18: HEAD 2 of 2 red; pre-epic base 92934cb04 2 of 3 red.
It also fires in the ordinary lane: the sase-o9 landing gate run (monitor 5fegfcvzqvqs, 2026-08-17) failed exactly this node on gw3, 1 failed / 699 passed / 1 skipped.

PASSES WITHOUT CONTENTION: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -m visual -p no:randomly on the node alone (1 passed) and on the whole file (2 passed); 'just test-visual -- <file>' at 12 workers passed; 'just test-visual -- <node>' passed; three direct '-n 2 --dist=worksteal' runs passed. So an unloaded host hides it, which is why it survives ordinary visual-lane runs.

NOT CAUSED BY EPIC sase-o9: the byte-identical 23145/586500 signature reproduces at 92934cb04, the commit immediately before the epic's first commit cc805197b. sase-o9 touches only proc_observer, procs_pane*, proc_gear_chips, proc_indicator, _member_jump, help_modal/binding_common, docs/ace.md, and the config-center Procs visual helpers -- nothing in the AXE dashboard or its settle path.

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE: the test settles with only 'await page.expect_screen_not_contains("IDLE")' then 'wait_for_visual_idle(page)'. Neither waits on the AXE detail summary block, so under CPU starvation the snapshot wins the race against the status fields. The sibling test in the same file already force-settles the footer by hand before snapshotting, with a comment saying the AXE footer repaint can lag the tab change under xdist -- the same gap, patched narrowly for one widget.

SUGGESTED FIX: wait on a concrete marker of the loaded summary (for example expect the screen to contain 'Chops run:') before ace_png_visual.assert_page_png, or teach wait_for_visual_idle about the AXE detail pane, rather than rebaselining the golden. Do not accept the unconverged frame with --sase-update-visual-snapshots.

VERIFY WITH: just test-visual-contention -- tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_axe_layout.py, repeated, expecting green.

title: tools/validate_sase_core_rs hardcodes agent-stats work-schema version 5, but linked sase-core HEAD ships 6
close_reason: Already fixed on master by epic phase sase-oo.1 (commit 24936ffee 'fix(core): require agent-stats schema 6 and truncation fields', part of the same schema-bump work that caused this). Independently authored the identical fix (tools/validate_sase_core_rs schema_version 5->6) in workspace sase_18 to unblock a commit whose pre-commit hook was failing on this, but sase_git_commit's rebase pulled in origin/master's already-landed, more complete version (which also seeds probe xprompt data and validates new commit-counter fields), superseding my local edit -- confirmed via 'git diff --stat' showing tools/validate_sase_core_rs no longer dirty after the commit/rebase. No action needed; recording for the record.
description:
Reproduction in workspace sase_18 (host project gh_sase-org__sase) on 2026-08-17 while
verifying an unrelated, Python-only change (plan 202608/config_cache_atomic_publication.md,
bead sase-ns.6.6.6.1 -- touches only src/sase/config/core.py, tests/test_config_cache.py,
tests/test_config_cache_token.py, tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt; no Rust or schema
code). `just install` succeeds, but every gate that depends on the shared `_setup` Justfile
recipe (`just check`, `just check-full`, `just lint`, `just test-scoped`,
`just test-contention`, `just selection-health`) fails at `_setup`:

    [validate_sase_core_rs] agent statistics work-schema probe requires schema version 5: got 6
    error: recipe `_setup` failed on line 121 with exit code 1

`tools/validate_test_environment` reports the built `sase_core_rs` as stale (bit 2),
`_setup` rebuilds it from the linked checkout at sase/repos/linked/sase-core (currently
`02a37e9` "fix(agent_stats): correct commit, spec, runner, and xprompt counters", one
commit ahead of the `875309a` "chore: release v0.27.17 (#141)" tag), then
`tools/validate_sase_core_rs`'s `_validate_agent_stats_work_schema` probe
(tools/validate_sase_core_rs:497) calls `agent_stats_query_runs` on the freshly built
extension and asserts `payload["schema_version"] == 5`. The linked checkout's HEAD
commit bumped the real payload to schema_version 6, but the Python-side probe was never
updated to match, so any workspace that builds from that checkout (rather than
resolving `sase-core-rs` from the pinned `>=0.27.15,<0.28.0` PyPI window in
pyproject.toml/uv.lock) hits this hard failure regardless of what Python change is
being verified.

Root cause is precisely located: tools/validate_sase_core_rs:497 hardcodes
`payload.get("schema_version") != 5`. Fix is either (a) bump that literal to 6 once the
schema-6 payload shape is confirmed stable and reflected in the rest of the probe's
assertions (`work`, `xprompts`, `runners` fields further down in the same function), or
(b) this is really floor/version-skew debt of the same shape as closed tasks sase-lm,
sase-kx, sase-jj, sase-hz -- advance the sase-core-rs floor once a release containing
02a37e9 is cut, and treat the literal-5 check as needing to track the release, not the
linked dev checkout.

RELATED: sase-km (closed canceled) proposed a general floor gate that understands wire-
schema versions rather than just binding names/version numbers -- exactly the gate class
that would have caught this. Not reopening it (deprioritized in 2026-08-14 triage, not a
duplicate of this specific occurrence). sase-lm, sase-kx, sase-jj, sase-hz, sase-jw are
prior distinct occurrences of the same "linked sase-core checkout ahead of/behind sase's
pinned expectations" class, each filed and fixed as its own task per established
precedent; this is a new occurrence of that pattern for the agent-stats work-schema
specifically.

title: Replace the remaining multiprocessing-fork and os.fork sites in the test suite with in-process seams
close_reason: Fixed by 569d4257b 'fix: stabilize process concurrency closeout': 'Replace fork-based contention tests with thread or subprocess boundaries that exercise the same production locks without forking from pytest.' Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f: all five named files (test_prompt_artifact_staging, test_procs_supervisor, logs/test_run_log, monitor/test_monitor_proc_facade, agents_sync/test_publication_outbox) match neither get_context("fork") nor os.fork(). The two repo-wide matches left are prose (a test_sdd_git_contention.py docstring naming the retired pattern) and an os.fork() inside a script string that run_bounded_subprocess executes in a fresh interpreter to prove descendant-kill -- a genuine process-boundary case the bead explicitly allows.
description:
Forking from a multi-threaded process inherits only the calling thread, so any lock or buffer another thread held at fork time is inherited in an indeterminate state. Under xdist every worker carries a live execnet receiver thread, so every fork in a test is a fork-after-threads hazard.

This is proven twice, not theoretical. It was the root cause of tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py::test_headless_epic_approval_submits_while_inflight_launch_holds_anchor (bead sase-nz), which accumulated 12 full-run failure records across six workspaces and twelve heads between 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-17 before b6246f1cf replaced the fork with an in-process flock holder. Task sase-o5 then removed the four fork sites in tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py the same way (epic sase-ns.6.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.6.4).

DISCOVERED BY: epic sase-ns.6.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.6.4, which recorded this as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP rather than widening its own scope. Re-verified on master 5e58fb1c8 by the epic's land agent:

  $ grep -rln 'get_context("fork")|os\\.fork\\(\\)' tests/
  tests/test_prompt_artifact_staging.py
  tests/test_procs_supervisor.py
  tests/logs/test_run_log.py
  tests/monitor/test_monitor_proc_facade.py
  tests/agents_sync/test_publication_outbox.py

(tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py no longer matches; a docstring in it names the retired pattern in prose.)

SCOPE: replace each site with an in-process seam that still exercises genuine contention, following the two model fixes:

- tests/test_plan_approval_actions.py::_foreign_epic_launch_lock_holder (b6246f1cf) -- a contextmanager that takes the same flock on the real lock path, writes the same holder-identity JSON production writes, and self-checks that a second open() is refused with BlockingIOError before yielding.
- tests/test_sdd_git_contention.py::_ForeignEpicLaunchLockWorker -- a thread worker that runs the production lock helper inside a fresh contextvars.Context, so the ContextVar re-entrancy guard does not short-circuit the real flock wait, and re-raises the worker's assertion instead of flattening it into an exit code.

Preserve exactly what each test asserts. These tests exist to prove real contention or real process behavior, so a replacement that only pretends to contend would silently retire their value. Some sites may genuinely need a separate process -- spawn-based multiprocessing, or subprocess, is a legitimate answer where the test is really about process boundaries (spawn does not inherit threads and is not this hazard). Where an in-process seam cannot express what a site needs, say so in the bead note rather than weakening the assertion.

VERIFICATION: no 'fork' multiprocessing context or os.fork() call remains in tests/ outside prose; each touched file passes serially, under just test-contention with SASE_CONTENTION_REPEAT=3, and in a full parallel lane; just install && just check green.

title: tests/test_force_reuse_launch_seam.py: 2 tests assert a segment_extra_env kwarg that launch_query only passes when it is not None
description:
Two tests fail deterministically on clean master HEAD 30077550b (verified with `git stash -u`, so no working-tree diff is involved):

  FAILED tests/test_force_reuse_launch_seam.py::test_plain_sase_run_without_request_sidecar_still_rejects_forced_reuse
  FAILED tests/test_force_reuse_launch_seam.py::test_sidecar_without_authorization_still_rejects_forced_reuse
  2 failed, 5 passed in 2.31s

ROOT CAUSE (precise). Both tests funnel through the `_run_launch_query_unauthorized` helper, whose final assertion is tests/test_force_reuse_launch_seam.py:227:

    mock_launch.assert_called_once_with(prompt, segment_extra_env=None)

Production never makes that call. src/sase/main/query_handler/_launch.py:112-115 branches on the value instead of always passing it:

    if segment_extra_env is not None:
        results = launch_agents_from_cwd(query, segment_extra_env=segment_extra_env)
    else:
        results = launch_agents_from_cwd(query)

On the unauthorized path there is no force-reuse plan, so `segment_extra_env` keeps its `None` initializer (_launch.py:82) and the else branch runs. The mock therefore records `launch_agents_from_cwd('%id:!foo\nDo work')` while the test expects the kwarg form:

    E  AssertionError: expected call not found.
    E  Expected: launch_agents_from_cwd('%id:!foo\nDo work', segment_extra_env=None)
    E    Actual: launch_agents_from_cwd('%id:!foo\nDo work')

The five passing tests in the file all take the authorized path, where `segment_extra_env` is a real dict and the kwarg branch runs — which is why the file is only half red.

PROVENANCE: both the assertion and the branch arrived in dc4ca2057 ('fix(agent): restore forced agent-name-reuse launches for Agents-tab `,x` kill-and-edit'), the second-most-recent commit on master.

SCOPE: decide which side is authoritative and make the two agree. Either drop the branch and always pass `segment_extra_env=segment_extra_env` (simplest; `launch_agents_from_cwd` already accepts `None` on the authorized path when a plan carries no segment envs — confirm that first), or relax the helper's assertion to `assert_called_once_with(prompt)` for the unauthorized case. Do not paper over it by asserting on `call_args[0]` only; the point of the assertion is that the untouched, still-`!` prompt reaches child validation unchanged.

IMPACT: every agent's mandatory `just check` is red at the test stage for a diff unrelated to launch seams. Discovered while running the scoped test lane for an unrelated split of src/sase/ace/tui/proc_observer.py.

The emitters now ship __sase_run_prompt_fragment/__sase_run_prompt_embedded (emit_zsh_preamble.py:77-132, emit_fish.py:41, bash equivalent), and docs/completion.md:164-168 documents that inside quoted or spaced prompt text '#' completes xprompt names, '%' prompt directives, and '@' canonical artifact references. The item is also gone from the doc's Deferred section. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
Recorded as deliberately deferred by epic plan sase-oc (plan:202608/cli_completion.md, 'Deferred' section) and filed by that epic's land agent per the discovered-work rule. Also documented for users under docs/completion.md#deferred.

TODAY: 'sase run <TAB>' completes the PROMPT argument as a whole word — native file paths plus stored xprompt names, wired through the RUN_PROMPT_SLOT special case in src/sase/completion/kinds.py and handled explicitly by all three emitters. Completing a reference embedded inside a longer prompt string does nothing.

WANTED: typing 'sase run "do X #co<TAB>"' offers xprompt names, '%<TAB>' offers directives, and '@<TAB>' offers artifact references — the same grammar ACE's prompt input already completes in-TUI.

WHY IT IS NOT SMALL: this is in-word completion, not slot completion. Each shell needs its own current-word introspection (zsh compsys can do it with a custom completer over $words/$CURRENT; bash needs COMP_POINT arithmetic; fish's commandline -ct is the closest), and the candidate sources (xprompt catalog, directive table, artifact index) must stay inside the candidates fast path's import-set and latency contracts. Reuse sase.completion.candidates rather than reaching for ACE's in-process completion code, which imports the forbidden set.

title: Deploy generated shell-completion scripts through chezmoi on SASE-managed machines
close_reason: Fixed by abb80f44a 'feat(completion): support managed shell distribution', which added 'sase completion deploy-chezmoi' (src/sase/completion/deploy_chezmoi.py, wired at main/completion_handler.py:35,119-126). It renders the scripts plus owner-aware stamps (InstallStamp owner=OWNER_CHEZMOI) into the chezmoi source tree, and the interactions the bead flagged are handled and documented at docs/completion.md:34-39,184-188: refresh skips chezmoi-owned stamps, and a local install refuses to take over a chezmoi-owned target without --force. The item is gone from the doc's Deferred section. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
Recorded as deliberately deferred by epic plan sase-oc (plan:202608/cli_completion.md, 'Deferred' section) and filed by that epic's land agent per the discovered-work rule. Also documented for users under docs/completion.md#deferred.

TODAY: 'sase completion install' writes the script on the machine it runs on and stamps ~/.sase/completion/stamp/<shell>.json. Nothing carries that script across SASE-managed hosts, so every new machine needs a manual install, and a script regenerated on one host never reaches the others.

SCOPE: deploy the generated scripts through src/sase/main/_init_chezmoi_deploy.py the way the other chezmoi-managed assets are, so a SASE-managed host gets a current _sase / sase / sase.fish from the dotfiles repo. Decide deliberately how this interacts with the local install path: the stamp, .zwc freshness (a chezmoi-delivered zsh script still needs zcompile on the target host), the doctor checks in src/sase/doctor/checks_completion.py, and the flagged 'sase update' refresh hook (feature flag completion_refresh_on_update, removal bead sase-om) must not fight each other over the same file.

CONSTRAINT: the chezmoi repo is a linked repo — open it with /sase_repo, never by path.

title: test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet fails under the full parallel lane: a Textual worker is still unfinished after AcePage exits

close_history.close_reason: Fixed by b8559f36f 'fix(ace): stabilize async teardown and interaction waits' (2026-08-21), which drains Textual workers during AcePage teardown -- the exact post-exit assertion the bead named (all(worker.is_finished for worker in app.workers)). tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt retires it: '# sase-rm.10 (sase-oz): AcePage now cancels and awaits Textual workers' with '# fixed-at: 2026-08-21T10:03:43Z'. Last recorded evidence is 2026-08-20, before the fix. 'tools/selection_health --fail-on-new-flake' exits 0 on 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.

description:
REPRODUCTION: tests/test_ace_testing.py::test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet failed once under the full parallel lane during a monitored 'just check-full' at HEAD 423669549 (monitor j529c27q5gye, 2026-08-17): '1 failed, 32563 passed, 13 skipped, 70 warnings in 1144.43s'. It was the ONLY failing node in the run, and its failure is what turned 'just test-cost' (Justfile:401) and therefore check-full red.

EXACT FAILURE (tests/test_ace_testing.py:169, the post-exit block after the 'async with AcePage() as page' body):
    assert all(worker.is_finished for worker in app.workers)
    E       assert False
    E        +  where False = all(<generator object ...<genexpr>>)
Every earlier assertion in that test passed, including the in-context structural-quiet assertions and the three post-exit assertions above it (_fs_watcher/_prompt_source_watcher/_stall_watchdog are None, _pump_free_async_tasks empty). So the app tore down its watchers and timers correctly and only a Textual worker was still unfinished when the context manager returned.

NOT REPRODUCED under narrower lanes (this is the useful negative evidence for whoever picks this up):
  - alone: 1 passed
  - whole module, default lane, 5 consecutive runs: 35 passed each time
  - whole module co-run with the bead/chop tests that landed alongside it: 94 passed
  - 'just test-contention -- tests/test_ace_testing.py' (the instrument sase-ct's retirement policy names): 'contention tally: 0 node(s) failed across 3 repeat(s) in 225.7s; red repeats: none'
That last one matters: pinned-CPU starvation restricted to this file does NOT reproduce it, so the trigger is very likely cross-FILE interaction in the whole-suite lane rather than intra-file load. A fix attempt that only soaks this file will look green while proving nothing.

NOT A PROCESS-GLOBAL-STATE LEAK, at least not one the current detector sees: the same failing run's sase global leak detector reported '0 poisoning change(s) across 0 test(s); 30980 warming mutation(s) filtered; 302 cooling mutation(s) filtered; 1122 invalidation(s) filtered'. So this is a worker/task lifecycle race, distinct in mechanism from the config/registry state-leak nodes that dominate this flake class.

STATUS: this node is NOT in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt and 'grep' over the durable flake-evidence store found no prior failure record for it, so 2026-08-17 is its first recorded sighting.

SCOPE: determine which Textual worker is still running when AcePage.__aexit__ returns under the full lane, then either make the harness await/cancel it deterministically before the assertion or fix the production path that leaves it outstanding. Prefer a mechanism fix over baselining the node; if it has to be baselined first, the baseline entry needs this bead named as owner per the header of tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

PROPOSED BY: the land agent for epic sase-on, which is NOT the cause: that epic's six commits touch zero src/sase/ace/** files and zero ACE tests (they touch bead config/triage/stale-cleanup, notification gate wiring, default_config.yml, sase.schema.json and docs), and the co-run above rules out its new tests interfering.

Stand up pyproject.toml/Justfile/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/sase.yml, credentials.py (env-var helpers — no pass), gchat_client.py (subprocess wrapper around the gchat CLI: send/edit/upload/download/list/react with retry+debug log), option_codes.py (out-of-band action encoder, smaller than callback_data.py), and port pending_actions.py/rate_limit.py/pdf_convert.py/pdf_style.css from sase-telegram with paths rewritten to ~/.sase/gchat/.
