close_reason: Fixed: no publication request sits at attempts=0 any more. Every entry is attempted and quarantines on failure, which the existing sase agent sync --retry-quarantined remediation reaches.
description:
DISCOVERED BY: sase-oc.land while committing the epic's landing integration work. NOT caused by epic sase-oc (shell completion) — the requests predate the commit by 31-42 hours and are in the 'research' hood, which the epic never touched.

OBSERVED (2026-08-17, workspace sase_12, athena):
'sase doctor --json' check state.agent_publication_outbox reports WARN. Project gh_sase-org__sase holds 20 requests: 0 quarantined, 0 retired, 3 stalled. The three stalled entries are

  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cdx      age 41.6h  attempts=0  last_error=null
  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cld      age 41.5h  attempts=0  last_error=null
  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.final_3  age 31.3h  attempts=0  last_error=null

each with reasons ['stalled: age >= 1d 0h']. The other two projects (actstat, bob-cli) hold zero requests. state.agent_publication_digest is OK with 0 problems, so this is not digest drift.

THE DEFECT: attempts=0 with last_error=null means the drain path has never once attempted these requests. Because they are never attempted they can never fail, so they can never accumulate attempts, retire, or quarantine either — they are invisible to every existing remediation. 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' does not touch them (it clears quarantined requests, and these are not quarantined); 'sase agent sync --drop-retired' does not either (they are not retired). They simply age indefinitely and hold state.agent_publication_outbox at WARN for every agent that runs 'sase doctor' on this host.

Contrast with the working path: during the same session a real quarantine (19 requests, 'file digest mismatch') was reported by sase_git_commit and 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' cleared it completely — quarantined_request_count went 19 -> 0 and the digest check went to OK. So the quarantine machinery works; it is specifically the never-attempted requests that have no path out.

SCOPE: find why the full-sync drain skips these three requests (a hood-selection or publishability filter that silently excludes them is the likely shape, given attempts stays 0), then either make the drain attempt them — so they succeed, or fail into the existing retry/quarantine/retire lifecycle — or give them a deliberate terminal state. A request the drain refuses to attempt should not be able to sit at attempts=0 forever with no recorded reason.

REPRODUCTION: sase doctor --json, then read checks[] entry state.agent_publication_outbox -> data.problems. Note the check identity lives on the 'id' field; 'name' is absent, so a probe matching on 'name' silently finds nothing.

plus_one_evidence.note:
INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION + ROOT-CAUSE DIAGNOSTIC (sase-op.land, workspace sase_13, athena, 2026-08-17T21:0xZ, master d5ac42693).

Answers this bead's SCOPE question directly. The three stalled requests are NOT skipped by a hood-selection or publishability filter. They are attempted and they FAIL, on hood-level relationship validation:

  could not publish agent hood 'research': invalid hood relationships: duplicate or inconsistent container global name 'bbugyi200.athena.research.h.final'

HOW OBSERVED: 'sase_git_commit' (sase stitch create, create_commit) for the epic sase-op land diff pushed the commit successfully and then printed: 'Primary commit succeeded; agent-hood publication is queued and will retry automatically. Last error: <the message above>'. That commit's drain pass is what finally attempted these requests.

STATE AFTER, from 'sase doctor --json' -> checks[state.agent_publication_outbox].data.problems — same three global_agents this bead names, now with a recorded attempt:

  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cdx      age 41.9h  attempts=1  last_error=<above>  primary_revision d5f2d8fe86c7fd0aeb4743aabc0ad9ebbb78e72a
  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cld      age 41.9h  attempts=1  last_error=<above>  primary_revision e35d3831e1adc005a5cb65c071e947080b1b9693
  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.final_3  age 31.7h  attempts=1  last_error=<above>  primary_revision 9b2560f8689ecf28ccfb0223bc0358418e0974aa

All three still quarantined=false, retired=false, terminal_reason=null, reasons=['stalled: age >= 1d 0h'], remediation_command still the inapplicable 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined'. Project sase outbox moved 20 -> 12 requests (quarantined 0, retired 0, stalled still 3); actstat and bob-cli remain empty.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FIX: the attempts=0/last_error=null state this bead was filed on was a not-yet-attempted state, not a permanently-skipped one — a drain does reach them. The durable defect is narrower and now concrete: every attempt fails identically because agent hood 'research' has invalid relationships (a duplicate or inconsistent container global name 'bbugyi200.athena.research.h.final'), and attempts=1 with a populated last_error still does not advance toward retire or quarantine, so they remain invisible to both documented remediations and hold state.agent_publication_outbox at WARN. Two things to fix: (1) repair or reject the duplicate 'research.h.final' container relationship so the hood can publish, and (2) let a deterministically-failing request escalate into the retry/quarantine/retire lifecycle instead of restalling at the same age reason with a remediation command that cannot apply to it.

NOT CAUSED BY epic sase-op (glossary command); that epic touches src/sase/glossary/**, the Justfile symvision line, and docs only, and these requests predate its land diff by 31-42 hours.

INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION + ROOT CAUSE, 2026-08-18 ~19:30 EDT, workspace sase_14, athena. Discovered by sase-q3.land during sase_git_commit, which warned that the sase project holds quarantined agent-hood publication requests. NOT caused by epic sase-q3 (gate input panel); no in-progress epic has a causal link.

THE THREE REQUESTS THIS BEAD NAMES NOW HAVE A REAL last_error. research.0m.cdx, research.0m.cld, and research.0m.final_3 are no longer at attempts=0/last_error=null. 'sase agent sync --check --json' now reports them under quarantine_diagnostics as:

  publication request bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cdx@d5f2d8fe86c7 quarantined after 3 attempts: could not publish agent hood 'research': invalid hood relationships: duplicate or inconsistent container global name 'bbugyi200.athena.research.h.final'; run 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' to retry

So half of this bead's requested remediation has already happened on its own: the drain DOES now attempt them, and they DO fail into the existing retry/quarantine lifecycle. What remains is that they still never drain, and now we know why.

ROOT CAUSE: the 'research' hood has a corrupt relationship graph — a duplicate or inconsistent container global name 'bbugyi200.athena.research.h.final'. This is a hard data-integrity failure, not a transient one, so 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' can never clear these; they will re-exhaust their 3 attempts and re-quarantine on every retry. That is why the outbox WARN never clears. The fix is to repair or de-duplicate the research hood's container relationships (or give a hood that fails relationship validation a deliberate terminal/retired state) rather than to make the drain retry harder.

BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN THIS BEAD RECORDED. The sase project now holds 52 quarantined requests, in four groups:
  - 12 x 'invalid hood relationships: duplicate or inconsistent container global name bbugyi200.athena.research.h.final' — every research.0m/0o/0p/0q/0r request (cdx, cld, final/final_2/final_3). This bead's defect; permanent, unretryable.
  - ~34 x 'agents sync lock is busy' after 3 attempts — transient contention; genuinely retryable, but the 3-attempt budget is exhausted by lock contention alone on a busy multi-workspace host.
  - 1+ x 'agent-hood publication did not complete within 120s' after 3 attempts — timeout; retryable.
  - 4 x 'file digest mismatch', all on 'agents/bbugyi200.athena.<id>--mon/chat.md' — digest drift confined to monitor-hood chat transcripts, i.e. a --mon hood's chat.md keeps changing after its snapshot is signed. 'sase agent sync --repair-digests' (added by sase-fa.4, used by closed sase-fk for bob-cli) is the existing tool for this half.

IMPACT: state.agent_publication_outbox stays WARN for every agent on this host, and sase_git_commit prints a quarantine warning on every commit telling the agent to run a retry that cannot succeed for the research group.

REPRODUCTION: timeout 180 sase agent sync --check --json, then read projects[] where project == 'sase' -> quarantine_diagnostics (52 entries; group them by the text after 'attempts: ').

Reproduced 2026-08-19T02:5xZ on athena, workspace sase_12, while committing the sase-pv landing. The stalled population has DOUBLED since this bead was filed: 6 entries now, not 3. The original three (research.0m.cdx/cld/final_3, now 59-71h old) are joined by research.0o.cdx, research.0o.cld, and research.0o.final_2 at ~39h. Every one is still attempts=0, last_error=null, quarantined=false, retired=false — so the drain has still never attempted any of them and the set only grows. New evidence separating this from the working path: my sase_git_commit run reported 16 QUARANTINED requests, I ran the advertised 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined', and it cleared all 16 to zero in one pass. Immediately after, state.agent_publication_outbox was still WARN with exactly these 6 never-attempted entries and nothing else. That is a clean A/B on one host minutes apart: the quarantine lifecycle works, and these requests are outside it entirely. Note the entries still advertise remediation_command='sase agent sync --retry-quarantined', which provably does not touch them — the suggested fix is itself misleading.

notes.author: sase-p2.land
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE: plugins.required makes 'just install' hard-fail in any workspace where a required plugin's linked checkout is absent, because the plugin is not published to PyPI.

REPRODUCTION (2026-08-18, workspace sase_13, clean master fd2d71afc): 'just install' completes the sase-core build and the editable sase install, then '_setup-required-plugins' (Justfile:181-199, added by sase-p3.4 in 1e59c50e7) runs install_one for each plugins.required entry. sase-github resolves from PyPI (0.2.4). sase-research-artifacts does not: Justfile:45-46 computes sase_research_artifacts_dir as 'sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts' when it exists else '../sase-research-artifacts'; in a fresh ephemeral workspace neither path exists (sase/sase.yml:229-230 declares the linked repo WITHOUT auto_clone, and the sibling path is a peer workspace dir, not a checkout), so install_one falls back to PyPI and uv fails: 'Because sase-research-artifacts was not found in the package registry and you require sase-research-artifacts, we can conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable.' recipe '_setup-required-plugins' failed with exit code 1, recipe 'install' failed on line 179.

IMPACT: 'just install' is the mandatory first step in every ephemeral sase workspace, so this blocks 'just check' / 'just check-full' outright until the agent independently discovers that it must run 'sase repo open sase-research-artifacts' first. It is also the real root cause of a second symptom already misattributed elsewhere: epic phase sase-p2.4 recorded a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP claiming 'just check' fails on the config.file_hooks doctor check (unknown file-hook provider 'sase-research-artifacts@research-highlights' from the chezmoi-managed user config layer) and concluded the chezmoi dotfiles needed redeployment. The chezmoi config is already correct and plugin-prefixed (~/.config/sase/sase.yml:15 reads 'use: sase-research-artifacts@research-highlights'); the provider was simply not installed in the workspace venv because this install step had failed. After 'sase repo open sase-research-artifacts' + 'just install', install_one takes the linked-checkout branch, sase-research-artifacts==0.1.0 installs editable, and 'just check' goes fully green including SASE validation.

WHY THIS EPIC: sase-p3.4 introduced plugins.required and the PyPI-fallback install path, and sase-p3.11 (Missing-plugin gate offering to install) is the in-progress phase that owns the offer-to-install behavior for missing required plugins. A gate that offers to install a plugin that cannot be installed from any registry has the same gap. Candidate fixes: give the linked repo auto_clone, have install_one materialize the linked checkout via 'sase repo open' before falling back to PyPI, or fail with an actionable message naming the 'sase repo open <name>' command instead of a raw uv resolution error.

REPORTED BY: sase-p2.land while landing epic sase-p2. RELATED: sase-o6 (global 'sase' on PATH is a separate uv tool install, which still logs 'Skipping invalid file hook sase-research-artifacts@research-highlights' for the same missing-provider reason).

notes.author: sase-p8.land
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE (reported by the sase-p8 land agent, 2026-08-18, workspace sase_12): the _setup-required-plugins recipe this epic added in 1e59c50e7 (bead sase-p3.4) cannot repair a BROKEN EDITABLE install of a required plugin, and the fail-closed path then hard-errors every command that loads config.

REPRODUCTION: 'just validate' and '.venv/bin/sase validate' exit 1 with 'Skipping invalid file hook sase-research-artifacts@research-highlights from config layer user: unknown file-hook provider research-highlights'. Every sase CLI invocation in this workspace now prints that line on stderr. Reproduced with all local edits stashed, so it is pre-existing on master c033ca4c4.

ROOT CAUSE: sase-research-artifacts 0.1.0 is installed EDITABLE into .venv, and .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/_editable_impl_sase_research_artifacts.pth points at <workspace>/sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts/src, a directory that does not exist in this workspace (sase/repos/linked/ contains only sase-core). So importlib.metadata still discovers the entry point 'research-highlights -> sase_research_artifacts.provider:RESEARCH_HIGHLIGHTS_HOOK' from the surviving dist-info, but 'import sase_research_artifacts' raises ModuleNotFoundError, so ArtifactProviderRegistry.file_hook_providers_by_id never gains the id and _resolve_file_hook_provider (src/sase/config/file_hooks.py:307) raises.

WHY _setup DOES NOT FIX IT: install_one falls through to the PyPI branch because the linked dir has no pyproject.toml, and 'uv pip install --no-deps sase-research-artifacts' sees the existing dist-info as already satisfying the requirement — the recipe prints '[setup] Installing required plugin sase-research-artifacts from PyPI.' and then 'Checked 1 package in 0.13ms' without replacing the dangling editable install. A satisfied-by-name check is not enough; the recipe needs to verify the module actually imports (or pass --reinstall / --refresh) before declaring the required plugin installed.

SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT IN THE SAME MESSAGE: the remediation text tells the user to 'rerun sase doctor -C config.file_hooks', but that check id is not registered — 'sase doctor -C config.file_hooks' exits with 'unknown diagnostic check or group: config.file_hooks', and 'sase doctor -L' lists no file-hook check at all.

Originally surfaced as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on phase bead sase-p8.5, which confirmed it pre-existing on master via git stash. Recording it here rather than as a task bead because the causal link to this epic's required-plugin work is direct.

notes.author: sase-p2.land--1
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE (second, distinct from the 'just install' note above, same plugins.required root cause): the required-plugin install added by 1e59c50e7 breaks tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_tribe_panel.py::test_tribe_panel_display_config_png_snapshot, which now fails deterministically on clean master fd2d71afc.

FAILURE: at line 256, 'assert "∴" not in research_title.plain' -> AssertionError: assert '∴' not in '∴ @research · 1 [R1]'.

MECHANISM: that test deliberately asserts the 'research' tribe renders UNSTYLED, and carries an explicit comment saying research is a user-owned tribe configured in the operator's own ~/.config/sase/sase.yml, not in sase's bundled defaults, and that tests run against bundled defaults only -- ending with 'do not fix this by re-adding a bundled research entry'. That premise is now false. plugins.required force-installs sase-research-artifacts into the venv on every '_setup', the plugin declares a '[sase_config]' entry point (sase_research_artifacts = sase_research_artifacts), and its own METADATA states its default_config.yml ships 'the research tribe display config'. So a required plugin's defaults now merge into every test run, and the research tribe acquires its ∴ icon and #5FD7AF color from the plugin rather than from user config.

EVIDENCE THAT USER CONFIG IS NOT THE SOURCE: re-running the test with XDG_CONFIG_HOME pointed at an empty directory still fails identically, which rules out the operator's ~/.config/sase/sase.yml and leaves the installed plugin as the only source. The repo CHANGELOG separately records e023e68 'ace-tribes: drop bundled research tribe display config', consistent with the test's premise having been correct before required plugins existed.

WHY IT SURVIVED VERIFICATION: the visual suite is excluded from 'just test', 'just check', and 'just check-full'; only 'just test-visual' covers it.

REPRODUCTION: SASE_PYTEST_WORKERS=1 just test-visual tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_tribe_panel.py::test_tribe_panel_display_config_png_snapshot -- fails in isolation in seconds.

DECISION NEEDED BY THIS EPIC: whether required-plugin config should merge into test runs at all. If it should, this test's premise and comment need rewriting; if it should not, the test isolation needs to exclude plugin-contributed config layers. Either way it is a design call that belongs to plugins.required, not to the test.

Reported by sase-p2.land. Not caused by sase-p2, which touched no config, plugin, or tribe-display file.

notes.author: sase-p8.land
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE, SECOND SURFACE (same reporter, same root cause as the note above): the broken editable sase-research-artifacts install also fails SIX tests deterministically on a clean master tree — tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py::{test_repos_reports_ok_when_sidecar_is_unset, test_repos_reports_ok_for_canonical_bucketed_config, test_repos_reports_leftover_name_field, test_repos_reports_scalar_sidecar_value, test_repos_reports_undescribed_enabled_lazy_custom_entry, test_repos_reports_invalid_sidecar_ref_policy}. Each asserts a specific check_config_repos() status and gets WARN instead. Confirmed via git stash on master c033ca4c4, then reproduced in isolation with -p no:randomly.

CHECK OUTPUT PROVING THE LINK: check_config_repos().data['problems'] contains "Failed to load artifact provider entry point sase_artifact_refs:research: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sase_research_artifacts'" and the identical failure for sase_file_hooks:research-highlights, plus "repos.sidecar.custom.research.ref.use references missing artifact ref provider 'research'".

SECONDARY DEFECT THIS EXPOSES: these tests call check_config_repos() with only the CONFIG monkeypatched (_patch_config), so they still read the real installed artifact-provider entry points. Any host whose plugin set differs from the author's flips them regardless of the diff under test. Even after the install is repaired, the entry-point registry should be isolated in these tests the way config already is.

notes.author: sase-p1.land
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE (corroborating the sase-p2.land note above, from the sase-p1 land agent,
2026-08-18, workspace sase_16, master d4594a416): there is a SECOND, silent variant of the
same plugins.required gap, and it is worse than the hard-fail because `just install` exits 0.

When the workspace venv already carries an EDITABLE dist for a required plugin whose linked
checkout has since been removed, uv considers the requirement satisfied and skips the
reinstall, so `_setup-required-plugins` prints '[setup] Installing required plugin
sase-research-artifacts from PyPI. / Resolved 1 package / Checked 1 package' and returns 0
while leaving a dist-info whose _editable_impl .pth still points at the absent
sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts/src. Every entry point then loads to
ModuleNotFoundError:

  .venv/.../sase_research_artifacts-0.1.0.dist-info/direct_url.json
    -> {"url":"file:///...sase_16/sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts","dir_info":{"editable":true}}
  entry_points(group='sase_file_hooks')['research-highlights'].load()
    -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sase_research_artifacts'

DOWNSTREAM SYMPTOMS I traced to this single cause:
  1. `just validate` -> doctor config.file_hooks ERROR, 'unknown file-hook provider
     research-highlights' (the symptom sase-p1.5/.6/.8 each filed separately).
  2. Six tests in tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py fail, because
     check_config_repos() returns WARN instead of OK with three extra details:
     "repos.sidecar.custom.research.ref.use references missing artifact ref provider
     'research'", plus two "Failed to load artifact provider entry point ...
     ModuleNotFoundError" rows. Those tests assert an absolute status and so are
     non-hermetic with respect to host plugin-install state.

CONFIRMED FIX PATH: `sase repo open sase-research-artifacts` (fast-forwards the linked
checkout), after which the next `_setup` takes the linked-checkout branch
('[setup] Installing required plugin sase-research-artifacts from
sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts'), doctor config.file_hooks goes OK, and the
six doctor tests pass. Full `just test` then reports 32958 passed, 12 skipped.

So a fix should cover both shapes: absent-checkout-and-not-on-PyPI (hard fail, already
described above) and stale-editable-install-with-absent-checkout (silent success, this
note). The install step needs to verify the requirement is actually IMPORTABLE, not just
that a dist with the right name and version is present.

notes.author: sase-p4.land
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE (found by the sase-p4 land agent, 2026-08-18, while running this epic's landing verification on clean master 66b884434 — not caused by sase-p4, whose diff touches no task-type or external-mirror code):

TWO TESTS FAIL ON MASTER
  tests/test_axe_chop_external_issue_mirror.py::test_mirror_chop_creates_beads_and_reports_counters
  tests/test_axe_chop_external_issue_mirror.py::test_mirror_chop_closes_mirrored_bead_and_reports_counter

FAILURE:
  src/sase/external_mirror/_issue_apply.py:48 in _require_github_task_type
  RuntimeError: required plugin `sase-github` is not installed; run `sase plugin install sase-github`

ROOT CAUSE: commit 118a60836 'feat(external-mirror): stamp github task type on new mirrored issues' added _require_github_task_type(), which fails closed unless the slug 'github' is in the live task-type catalog. That slug is expected to come from the sase-github plugin, but the installed sase-github 0.2.4 exposes no sase_task_types entry point at all — its entry-point groups are only sase_config, sase_vcs, sase_workspace, sase_xprompts. Verified directly:

  get_task_type_registry().by_slug == ['bug', 'ci', 'feature', 'flake', 'memory']   (no 'github', diagnostics empty)
  importlib.metadata.distribution('sase-github').entry_points → no sase_task_types group

So the Python side of this epic landed ahead of the sase-github release that provides the type, and the fail-closed guard turns that gap into a hard test failure rather than a skip. The misleading part is the error text: sase-github IS installed, it just does not export the task type.

SCOPE FOR THIS EPIC: either ship/require the sase-github version that registers the 'github' task type (and raise the required floor so the message is true), or make these two tests provide the type via the catalog fixture instead of depending on the ambient plugin. Recorded here rather than as a task bead because the causal link to this epic is direct.

A second run is a clean no-op (exit 0), so it is idempotent. Post-install state: sase-github 0.2.5, sase-research-artifacts 0.2.0, entry_points(group="sase_task_types") == ['github']. `sase bead task-type list -a` shows github (plugin) alongside the five builtins and project-local flag. `sase doctor -C plugins.required` OK, 2 required plugin(s) satisfied. `sase validate` exit 0 with init memory --check and doctor config.file_hooks both ok and no "Skipping invalid file hook" noise. The plan's decision point 6 (auto_clone) was made deliberately and is recorded as a comment at sase/sase.yml:253-258. CI acceptance confirmed independently: run 32183458996 shows "Install dependencies" green on every job with the setup lines succeeding in the log -- the step that failed on all eight jobs before this epic.

PHASE 2 (plugin-config-isolation, 3485cb37d). The autouse _isolate_plugin_config fixture (tests/_conftest_runtime.py:217) sets SASE_DISABLE_PLUGIN_CONFIG=1 unless a test requests real_plugin_config. I proved both halves are real rather than trusting the note: with the plugin genuinely installed, load_merged_config() returns ace.tribes.research = {'icon': '∴', 'color': '#5FD7AF', ...}, and under SASE_DISABLE_PLUGIN_CONFIG=1 it returns None. PHASE 3 (publish-research-artifacts, 155ba102b). plugins.required pins sase-research-artifacts>=0.2.0; the git+https://github.com/sase-org/<repo> fallback is gone (checkout then PyPI only) while import verification and --no-deps are kept. `sase plugin show sase-research-artifacts` now reports "Latest v0.2.0 up to date" instead of the "Latest unknown" the plan recorded. One plan verify criterion is knowingly unmet and is not an install-path defect: a plain resolving `uv pip install sase-research-artifacts` still fails because the 0.2.0 wheel declares Requires-Dist sase>=0.17.0 while PyPI sase is 0.16.0. Phase 3's own full-suite run at 23:07Z (33760 passed, 1 baselined zsh flake) already covered the tree through 155ba102b, so the only genuinely un-integrated commit was 11f78656d (gate input panel styling: TUI widgets and PNG goldens only, no plugin or config surface). title: Commit finalizer stops failing agents whose work actually landed
description: An agent whose work is committed and pushed is never marked FAILED by the commit finalizer's discarded-work guard. Commit provenance survives conflict resolution, the finalizer decides attribution from evidence the run itself owns rather than from commit-message footers alone, and a concurrent agent's activity in a shared clone can no longer be misread as this agent discarding its work.

close_reason: Fixed by 19bdc94db (2026-08-20). _launch_start.py:288 calls _record_submit_time_vcs_replay(prompt) after a successful submit; that helper (lines 73-87) derives the VCS prefix from the prompt actually submitted and feeds record_vcs_xprompt_usage, which already drops the implicit #git:home default and non-launchable projects -- exactly the submit-time refresh the bead specified. description:
`+`/`Ctrl+Space` replays the last launch selection (src/sase/ace/last_agent_selection.py, `save_last_agent_selection_if_launchable`). One of its writers was `save_replayable_vcs_selection()` in `_launch_history.py`, which refreshed the replay target from the VCS ref the user actually cycled to with `<ctrl+p>` before submitting. That helper ran only from the discarded `proc_callable` launch body, so it was already dead in production; it was deleted with _launch_history.py in 65b72d43a (phase sase-ng.1.5).

RESULT: cycling `<ctrl+p>` to a different ref and submitting does not update what `Ctrl+Space` replays -- it keeps replaying whatever the picker/relaunch/quick-launch path last saved. The other writers (`_entry_quick_launch.py`, `_entry_relaunch.py`, `_entry_custom.py`) are all still live, so replay works; it is only the submit-time refresh that is missing.

SCOPE: the save mutates in-memory ACE state, so it cannot move into the spawned `sase run` child (that is why epic sase-ng.1 did not restore it). Do the refresh on the ACE side at submit time -- derive the selection from the prompt actually submitted in `_launch_resolved_prompt`/`_launch_start.py` and call `save_last_agent_selection_if_launchable()` there. Note the existing guards: the implicit `#git:home` default and non-launchable projects must not be saved (see the stale/implicit-default warnings in `_entry_points.py`). title: test_real_zsh_zcompile_and_registration flakes under the full parallel lane: probe_zsh_comps' 5s interactive-zsh timeout returns None, so registered is None instead of True
description:
tests/completion/test_install_zsh.py::test_real_zsh_zcompile_and_registration failed once under the whole-suite parallel lane and passes reliably standalone.

OBSERVATION: 2026-08-17T22:58Z, epic phase sase-p2.1 (project-scoped repo mention catalog, epic sase-p2). 'just check' ran every lint gate green and then the full test suite: 32553 passed, 1 failed, this node the only failure. An isolated re-run of the node passed. The diff under test was src/sase/xprompt/{repo_mention_catalog.py,glossary_catalog.py} plus tests — nothing touching shell completion, install, or zsh. The phase agent recorded it as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; sase-p2.land is filing it.

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE (code path, not yet confirmed against a captured assertion): the test is the repo's only real-zsh test and its last assertion is 'assert result.registered is True'. That value comes from install_completion -> _verify_install (src/sase/completion/install.py:505-535), whose default probe is probe_zsh_comps (src/sase/completion/install_targets.py:282-308). probe_zsh_comps shells out to an INTERACTIVE zsh -- [zsh, '-ic', 'print -r -- ${_comps[sase]:-UNSET}'] -- with timeout=ZSH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5.0 (install_targets.py:21), and on subprocess.TimeoutExpired or OSError it returns None. _verify_install maps a None probe to (None, InstallStep('verify','skip','could not probe ${_comps[sase]}'), hint, verify_failed=False), so result.registered becomes None while result.ok stays True and exit_code stays 0. That is exactly the shape of an intermittent failure that only trips the 'registered is True' assertion: the three preceding assertions (result.ok, script.is_file(), zwc_path(script).is_file()) and the two following (registered, exit_code) would all still pass except 'registered is True'.

Under the full parallel lane this test pays for an interactive zsh startup that sources the fixture .zshrc and runs 'compinit -u' over the entire real fpath in a tmp HOME, competing with every xdist worker for CPU; 5.0s is a fixed wall-clock budget with no attempt bound, which is the classic profile for a load-only flake. This is a timing/wait defect, not process-global state leakage: the test builds its own ZDOTDIR, HOME, fpath, and zcompdump under tmp_path and shares no module-level state.

SCOPE: confirm the signature by capturing the assertion (rerun the node under deliberate CPU oversubscription, e.g. the harness pattern in 'just test-contention'), then either give the probe a bounded-retry/attempt-based wait instead of a single fixed 5s deadline, raise the probe budget for the test via the existing verify_fn seam, or make the test assert on a deterministic seam rather than a live interactive-zsh probe. Do not simply widen the constant for production use without evidence: 5s is a user-facing 'sase completion install' latency budget too.

REPRODUCTION COMMAND: '.venv/bin/python tools/run_pytest default tests/completion/test_install_zsh.py' passes standalone; the failure has only been seen inside the full parallel lane. Requires zsh on PATH (the module is skipped otherwise).

title: In-process family hand-offs in the same wall-clock second share one artifacts directory, so the second successor overwrites the first's agent_meta.json
description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-p8.6 (epic sase-p8, 'sase pipe'), routed here by that epic's land agent. NOT caused by that epic: the defect is in shared artifact-directory creation and predates pipe.

WHAT IS WRONG: create_artifacts_directory() in src/sase/artifacts.py:61 derives the directory name from datetime.now(get_timezone()).strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S') and then calls artifacts_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True). There is no collision suffix, no retry, and no uniqueness check. Two calls inside the same wall-clock second therefore resolve to the SAME path, and the second caller's write_agent_meta_atomic() in create_followup_artifacts (src/sase/axe/run_agent_helpers_artifacts.py:199) replaces the first successor's agent_meta.json rather than creating a sibling. The first successor's identity, role_suffix, relationships, and model metadata are lost.

WHO IS AFFECTED: every in-process family-successor hand-off shares this path, not just pipe — handle_accepted_plan's coder hand-off, handle_questions_marker's follow-up, the plan feedback replan branch in run_agent_exec_plan.py, and handle_pipe_marker all reach create_followup_artifacts. Note the contrast with the detached path: spawn_detached_child (src/sase/agent/detached_child.py:93) reserves a globally unique timestamp via reserve_launch_timestamp_batch(1), so out-of-process spawns are already protected. The in-process path has no equivalent.

REPRODUCTION: observed under the sase-p8.6 end-to-end pipe harness (tests/fakey/test_pipe_e2e.py), which drives two hand-offs back to back with no human latency between them. A human-paced hand-off almost never lands in one second, so this is currently a test-harness and fast-chain hazard rather than a routine user-visible failure — but a scripted chain, a retry storm, or a faster host can reach it, and the failure is silent metadata loss rather than an error.

SCOPE: give the in-process path the same uniqueness guarantee the detached path already has — either route create_followup_artifacts through reserve_launch_timestamp_batch, or make create_artifacts_directory detect an existing directory and allocate a distinct name. Verify with a test that creates two follow-up artifact dirs without advancing the clock and asserts both metas survive.

title: test_candidates_fast_path_wall_clock_budget[patch] and [monitor] fail under the full parallel lane: a wall-clock assertion cannot hold under contention
close_reason: Fixed: the bead's preferred remedy (scope option 1) landed. abb80f44a 'feat(completion): support managed shell distribution' (2026-08-21) renamed test_candidates_fast_path_wall_clock_budget to test_candidates_fast_path_child_cpu_budget and replaced the wall-clock bound with child-process CPU accounting via _run_probe_with_cpu_seconds/getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN); the budget comment now reads 'intentionally ignores scheduler wait and parallel host load'. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f, and 'tools/selection_health --fail-on-new-flake' lists the old [agent]/[monitor] node IDs under 'no longer collectable ... excluded as stale'.
description:
FOUND BY the sase-p8 land agent (2026-08-18) during the epic's landing verification run. Unrelated to that epic's diff (a CLI hand-off command; no completion code touched).

REPRODUCTION: tests/main/test_completion_candidates_contract.py::test_candidates_fast_path_wall_clock_budget[patch] and [monitor] both failed under a full parallel run of 32,922 tests on master c033ca4c4 ('10 failed, 32912 passed, 12 skipped in 601s'), and both passed when rerun in isolation with -p no:randomly, where the same parametrizations complete in about 0.13s each.

WHY IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT INCIDENTAL: this test asserts a WALL-CLOCK budget for the completion fast path. Wall clock on a box running an xdist lane at full width measures scheduler contention, not the code under test — the budget can be blown by any other worker, so the node is guaranteed to be intermittently red at some load, on some host, forever. The other two parametrizations that ran in the same suite ([model], [bead], [workspace], [plan], [repo]) were unaffected in this run, which is itself evidence of load-luck rather than a per-parametrization defect.

SCOPE, IN PREFERENCE ORDER:
1. Replace the wall-clock bound with a deterministic proxy for what the budget is really protecting — a call/IO count, or process CPU time (time.process_time) instead of time.perf_counter — so the assertion measures the fast path rather than the host.
2. If a wall-clock bound must stay, mark the node serial (or exclude it from the parallel lane) so it is measured under known conditions, and state the assumed load in the failure message.
3. Widening the budget is the weakest option: it does not remove the dependence on host load, it only moves the threshold.

NO EXISTING BEAD: 'sase bead search' over task beads for 'wall_clock_budget|fast_path_wall_clock' returns nothing, so this node is not yet tracked.

title: Prompt g-prefix which-key hint panel silently drops its last row when the prompt bar hits its height cap
close_reason: Fixed by 671d27c89 'fix(ace): stabilize responsive pane layout', same overflow-affordance change as the Procs hints line: compact layouts now show that shortcuts were omitted instead of silently dropping the last row. description:
DISCOVERED while landing epic sase-p1 (glossary panel). Surfaced by that epic but the
truncation mechanism is pre-existing and independent of it: sase-p1.7 added one hint row
(`gG  glossary...`) to the prompt `g` prefix table, and in a constrained layout that one
extra row pushed the last existing row off the bottom with no indicator.

still renders 11 rows and `gx  save as xprompt` is simply gone from the frame. The key

always hits the alphabetically-last entries.

scroll, render a `+N more` footer, or flow into columns when rows exceed the budget --
and cover it with a test at a height where the clamp binds. Adding rows to the `g` table

title: just install silently accepts a dangling editable plugin install when the linked repo checkout is absent, so sase validate (and every just check) goes red
close_reason: Required-plugin setup now detects and repairs dangling editable installs; both required plugins import and the doctor check is green.
description:
FOUND BY the sase-p4 land agent (2026-08-18) during that epic's landing verification, in workspace sase_13 (host project gh_sase-org__sase). Unrelated to sase-p4's diff.

SYMPTOM: 'just check' and 'just check-full' fail at the 'SASE validation' gate, which sits before the test lane, so the run aborts and every agent in the workspace gets a red check unrelated to its own diff:

  fail   doctor config.file_hooks
  Skipping invalid file hook 'sase-research-artifacts@research-highlights' from config layer 'user': unknown file-hook provider 'research-highlights'; install a plugin exposing the sase_file_hooks entry point group or remove 'use'
  error: recipe `validate` failed on line 786 with exit code 1
  error: recipe `check` failed on line 648 with exit code 1

The message is misleading: the entry point IS present in the venv metadata.

  importlib.metadata.entry_points(group='sase_file_hooks')
    → research-highlights -> sase_research_artifacts.provider:RESEARCH_HIGHLIGHTS_HOOK

ROOT CAUSE: the distribution's metadata is installed but its module is not importable, so the artifact-provider registry drops the provider and config.file_hooks then cannot resolve it. get_artifact_provider_registry() reports it directly:

  file hook providers: []
  ArtifactProviderDiagnostic(code='entry_point_load_failed',
    message="Failed to load artifact provider entry point sase_file_hooks:research-highlights: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sase_research_artifacts'",
    severity='error', package='sase-research-artifacts', version='0.1.0')

sase-research-artifacts is installed EDITABLE, and its .pth points at a directory that does not exist in this workspace:

  .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/_editable_impl_sase_research_artifacts.pth
    → <workspace>/sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts/src   (No such file or directory)
  direct_url.json: {"url":"file://<workspace>/sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts","dir_info":{"editable":true}}

Only sase/repos/linked/sase-core was materialized in this workspace; the sase-research-artifacts checkout was not.

WHY just install DOES NOT REPAIR IT: Justfile:184 _setup-required-plugins calls install_one, which prefers the linked source tree only when \${dir}/pyproject.toml exists and otherwise falls back to PyPI:

  install_one sase-research-artifacts \"{{ sase_research_artifacts_dir }}\"
  → [setup] Installing required plugin sase-research-artifacts from PyPI.
    Resolved 1 package in 130ms / Checked 1 package in 0.09ms

That reads as success, but sase-research-artifacts is NOT published to PyPI — 'uv pip install --reinstall sase-research-artifacts' fails with 'was not found in the package registry'. The plain install only 'succeeds' because uv sees the requirement already satisfied by the stale editable dist-info and short-circuits without resolving or validating that the target still exists. So the broken state is self-perpetuating across every just install.

REPRODUCTION: in a workspace whose sase/repos/linked/sase-research-artifacts checkout is absent but whose venv still holds the editable install from a previous use: run 'just install' (reports success), then '.venv/bin/sase doctor -C config.file_hooks' → ERROR, or 'just check' → fails at SASE validation. '.venv/bin/python -c \"import sase_research_artifacts\"' → ModuleNotFoundError.

RECOVERY (what unblocked this landing): 'sase repo open sase-research-artifacts -r \"...\"' materializes the linked checkout, the .pth resolves again, the import works, doctor returns OK, and 'just check' reaches the test lane with every lint gate green.

SCOPE: make the required-plugin setup path fail loudly or self-heal instead of silently accepting a dangling editable install. Options, roughly in preference order: (1) after installing, verify each required plugin actually imports and its entry points load, and fail the setup with the recovery command when it does not; (2) when the linked source dir is missing but an editable install already points into it, materialize the linked checkout (the same thing sase repo open does) rather than falling back to PyPI; (3) do not fall back to PyPI for plugins that have no PyPI release — that branch can only ever no-op or fail confusingly.

notes.author: sase-p4.land
notes.text: RELATED: sase-o6 — the same class of stale-install trap on the other side (the global 'sase' on PATH is a uv tool install pinned to a separate checkout). A live symptom of that one is visible in this very workspace: every global 'sase bead ...' invocation prints "unknown file-hook provider 'sase-research-artifacts@research-highlights'" — note the FULL prefixed id, not the bare name the workspace venv reports — because the global tool predates commit 54da09ba5 'feat(config)!: require plugin prefix on every use: field' and cannot parse the new prefixed 'use:' form the user's config now carries. Different root cause from this bead (a stale global tool vs. a dangling editable install), but a fix for either should consider whether the setup path can detect the other.

Same family (a workspace's linked-repo checkout out of step with what the venv expects) but a different root cause: sase-jw is a STALE checkout, this bead is an ABSENT one that leaves the editable install dangling and that just install then reports as satisfied.

notes.author: sase-p3.15.land
notes.text: RESOLVED BY EPIC sase-p3.15 — verification from sase-p3.15.land (2026-08-18, workspace sase_12, HEAD 11f78656d). This bead's exact root cause (uv treats a name-satisfied dist-info as installed, so _setup-required-plugins cannot replace a dangling editable install whose .pth points at an absent linked checkout) was the target of phase sase-p3.15.1, which replaced the Justfile recipe with tools/setup_required_plugins. That tool now spawns the target interpreter to 'import <module>' after every install attempt -- a fresh subprocess, because a newly written .pth is only processed by site at interpreter start -- and on failure forces one 'uv pip install --reinstall-package <name>' and re-checks. Observed firing for real in this workspace, not simulated: 'just install' printed '[setup] sase-github installed from PyPI but import sase_github failed; forcing a reinstall' and repaired it; the immediately following run of the same tool is a clean no-op at exit 0, so the repair is idempotent rather than a reinstall-every-time loop. Post-state: sase-github 0.2.5 and sase-research-artifacts 0.2.0 both importable, 'sase doctor -C plugins.required' OK with 2 required plugin(s) satisfied, and 'sase validate' exit 0 with 'ok doctor config.file_hooks' and no 'Skipping invalid file hook' line on stderr -- the precise symptom this bead reports. The misleading-message complaint is also addressed: when no source works the tool now exits with a message naming the plugin and the exact next command ('sase repo open <name>' for a linked plugin, otherwise the install command) instead of uv's raw resolution error. Two things this bead's description says are no longer true of the code: install_one and the sase_research_artifacts_dir Justfile variable are gone, and phase sase-p3.15.3 additionally pinned sase-research-artifacts>=0.2.0 now that 0.2.0 is on PyPI, so a fresh workspace with no linked checkout resolves from the index rather than needing 'sase repo open' at all. Flagging for triage as fixed rather than closing it myself, since a task bead's close is the owner's call.

notes.author: 08u
notes.text: Verified on clean master b7bdd3185 after just install. tools/setup_required_plugins, introduced by eed1d9a67, completed successfully; sase_github and sase_research_artifacts both import in the workspace interpreter; and sase doctor -C plugins.required reports OK with 2 required plugins satisfied. The tool now verifies imports in a fresh subprocess and performs a forced reinstall when metadata points at a broken editable checkout, which directly addresses the dangling-install mechanism in this bead.

title: Write sase glossary add/del into the invoking checkout's sase.yml
close_reason: This is already fixed.
description: Discovered while implementing glossary workspace-project inference. Inference now resolves a numbered workspace to the correct project, but resolve_project_config_read_path / resolve_project_config_write_path still use record.workspace_dir (the ProjectSpec primary checkout). That is byte-for-byte what sase glossary add -p sase already did from a workspace, so it is not a regression of the inference fix — but it means an agent that adds a term from a numbered workspace still writes the primary checkout sase/sase.yml instead of the workspace tree they will commit. Recommended by the approved plan (glossary_workspace_project_inference.md) as a follow-up feature, not bundled into the inference change.

task_type_fields.proposal: After sase glossary infers the project from a numbered workspace, add/del still read and write the project's primary checkout sase/sase.yml (record.workspace_dir), not the invoking workspace's own copy. Make the invoking checkout's sase/sase.yml the read/write target so an agent's glossary edits land in the tree they will commit from, matching sase flag new and sase memory init. This also needs an explicit decision about -p/--project: today -p sase from a workspace already writes the primary checkout.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The approved glossary workspace-project inference plan (glossary_workspace_project_inference.md) deliberately keeps inference as project-identity only. Changing the write target would also change -p semantics and is a separate product decision, not part of the inference fix.

title: just check fails at lint (symvision) on master: unused public long_memory_entry_path and normalize_long_memory_description_lines in src/sase/amd/_agents_doc.py
description:

  Unused public functions/classes. Make these private if they are used only within the file they are defined. If the functions/classes are completely unused, you should delete them:
    long_memory_entry_path in src/sase/amd/_agents_doc.py
    normalize_long_memory_description_lines in src/sase/amd/_agents_doc.py

Reproduction: 'just install && just _lint-symvision' (or the full 'just check') on a tree whose src/ matches master.

Root cause: both helpers are exported from _agents_doc.py's __all__ but have no non-test importer.
  - normalize_long_memory_description_lines (src/sase/amd/_agents_doc.py:86) has exactly one caller, _agents_doc.py:144, in its own file.
  - long_memory_entry_path (src/sase/amd/_agents_doc.py:147) is called at _agents_doc.py:186 and :217 in its own file; its only outside importer is tests/main/test_init_memory_agents_templates.py, which symvision does not count as usage.
The sibling module src/sase/amd/_memory.py imports only collect_long_memory_entries and parse_amd_agents_document from _agents_doc, so neither flagged symbol is needed publicly. Both symbols were introduced by the Tier-2 memory-rendering commits 538dec9fc and 445afde7c.

Impact: every agent whose tree reaches this gate is blocked by a failure unrelated to their diff. Discovered while verifying a tests-only file split (tests/ace/tui/visual/_ace_prompt_png_snapshot_helpers.py) — the visual snapshots and the scoped test lane both passed; only symvision failed.

Scope: consult sase/memory/symvision.md, then privatize both helpers (rename to _long_memory_entry_path / _normalize_long_memory_description_lines, drop them from __all__, update the in-file call sites) and re-point the test import in tests/main/test_init_memory_agents_templates.py per the note's guidance for test-only consumers.

title: test_memory_plan_renders_glossary_terms_block_in_tier2 fails on master: asserts unwrapped 'Aliases follow in parentheses.' against wrapped Tier 2 output
description:
`tests/main/test_init_memory_glossary.py::test_memory_plan_renders_glossary_terms_block_in_tier2`
fails deterministically on master (HEAD af951d1f9). Discovered while landing epic
sase-p5 (`just test` on the epic's combined tree: 1 failed, 33079 passed, 12 skipped).

Failure:

    assert "Aliases follow in parentheses." in tier2
    AssertionError: ... 'definition plus every term the definition depends on. Aliases follow\nin parentheses.\n\n- Agent Clan (clan)\n- Workspace\n'

Root cause: the rendered Tier 2 glossary block is line-wrapped, so the sentence
"Aliases follow in parentheses." is split across a newline between "follow" and
"in". The test asserts the unwrapped literal substring, which no longer occurs in
the rendered output. Every other assertion in the test (the `### 2.1 Long-Term
Memory Files` / `### 2.2 Glossary Terms` headings, their ordering, the
`sase glossary read` snippet) passes; only this one substring assertion fails.

Introduced by 445afde7c ("feat: Split Tier 2 into 'Long-Term Memory Files' and
'Glossary Terms' H3 sections"), the only commit touching both the assertion and
the rendered source string; the markdown reflow that wraps the sentence arrived
with the same Tier 2 rendering work (see also 28613d6fb, "chore: Format with
prettier"). Neither commit carries a SASE_BEAD footer, so no bead owns this work.

Scope: decide whether the fix is the test (assert against wrap-insensitive text,
e.g. normalize whitespace before the containment check, matching how the sibling
assertions are written) or the renderer (emit the sentence unwrapped). Prefer
making the assertion wrap-insensitive unless the wrap is itself unintended, since
the surrounding template is prettier-formatted and will re-wrap on any width change.

title: Tighten sase stitch create --resume's identity check beyond subject-only matching
description:
`sase stitch create --resume` decides "is HEAD the commit this run is entitled to
finalize?" by comparing HEAD's **subject line only** against the checkpointed
payload (`src/sase/workflows/commit/workflow_resume.py:63-78`). Any commit whose
subject matches passes that gate; the resume then amends and pushes it as this
run's commit.

Proposed by epic sase-p5's plan (plan:202608/commit_finalizer_attribution.md,
phase `restamp` / bead sase-p5.1), which specified this alongside the footer
restamp that phase did implement:

> Also tighten the resume identity check itself. Subject-only matching is what let
> a substantially rewritten commit pass as "the expected commit"; it should
> additionally confirm that `HEAD` is a commit this run is entitled to finalize
> (for example, that `HEAD` is not already pushed to the upstream branch and that
> its tree still contains the checkpointed diff's paths). Keep the check advisory
> enough not to break legitimate conflict resolutions that change content — the
> goal is to stop silently finalizing an unrelated commit, not to force the body
> to be byte-identical.

sase-p5.1 shipped only the restamp (commit 22e5444bf touches
`runtime_tags.py` +14, `workflow_resume.py` +81 for `_restamp_missing_footer_tags`,
and its test), left the subject-only gate unchanged, and recorded no note
descoping the identity work. Verified unimplemented on master at af951d1f9: the
resume path still has no upstream-containment or changed-path check.

sase-p5's landing raised the stakes rather than lowering them: the restamp now
*writes* this run's `SASE_AGENT`/`SASE_TYPE`/`SASE_BEAD` footer onto whatever
commit sits at HEAD (`_restamp_missing_footer_tags`, called before
`finalize_commit`). A HEAD that passes the subject gate but is not this run's
commit is therefore now stamped with this run's provenance and pushed, instead of
merely being pushed unattributed.

Proposed scope:

1. Reject a HEAD already reachable from the upstream tracking branch. Reaching the
   restamp/finalize block requires `"dispatch" not in cp.completed_steps`, so this
   run has not pushed anything yet; a HEAD already on upstream cannot be a commit
   this run created. The `git rebase --skip` resolution (agent drops their own
   commit because upstream already carries an equivalent one) lands exactly here
   with a matching subject.
2. Optionally confirm HEAD still touches the checkpointed diff's paths, kept
   advisory — the motivating sase-p5 incident had the agent legitimately drop a
   whole paragraph during conflict resolution, so this must not force byte or path
   equality.
3. Fail loudly with HEAD unpushed and recoverable, matching how
   `_restamp_missing_footer_tags` already reports its own failures.

Design note for the implementer: SASE has no VCS-agnostic upstream-containment
primitive today. `provider.revision_id()` exists (`src/sase/vcs_provider/_base.py:162`)
but nothing exposes "is revision X reachable from the tracking branch"; the only
upstream logic lives in the git plugin (`_git_query_ops.py:122-130`) and in the
finalizer's git-specific `git_upstream_ahead_count`. Expect to add a primitive
across `_base.py`, `_hookspec.py`, `_plugin_manager.py`, the git plugin, and
`vcs_provider/testing.py` fakes, and to check the Rust-core backend boundary
(`../sase-core`) before implementing it in Python. Fail open when the provider
cannot answer, so an unknown upstream never blocks a legitimate resume.

task_type_fields.proposal: Stop sase stitch create --resume from finalizing a commit it did not create. Today the only identity gate is a subject-line comparison (workflow_resume.py:63-78); add a check that HEAD is a commit this run is entitled to finalize — primarily that HEAD is not already reachable from the upstream tracking branch, optionally that HEAD still touches the checkpointed diff's paths — and abort with HEAD unpushed and recoverable when it is not. task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Specified in epic sase-p5's plan under phase restamp but never implemented, and outside sase-p5's goal statement, which is scoped to the commit finalizer's discarded-work guard no longer failing agents whose work landed. It also needs a new VCS-agnostic upstream-containment primitive across the provider protocol, git plugin, and test fakes, which is more than a landing cleanup.

title: sase flag new makes a flag bead live in the shared store before its definition lands, so every other agent's just check goes red on the orphan_bead rule

close_history.close_reason: I'm re-designing sase flags right now (migrating them to a new "flag" task bead type).

description:
`sase flag new` makes a flag bead live in the **machine-wide, shared** bead store
immediately, but the flag's registry definition only exists on the **one workspace
tree** where the flag was authored, until that tree's commit lands and every other
agent rebases onto it. In that window, the `orphan_bead` rule
(`src/sase/feature_flags/integrity.py:120-136`, surfaced by
`tools/check_feature_flags:581`) compares the shared store against the local
checkout and fails every other agent:

    rule 8: live flag bead 'sase-pk' has no definition (key 'commit_finalizer_shared_clone_exempt')

`just check`'s `lint (feature flags)` gate is red repo-wide for the duration, for a
reason unrelated to any of those agents' diffs.

This is recurring, not a one-off — four separate epics have hit it and each
recorded it only as a note, so no task bead has ever been filed:

- sase-p5 (this epic): `DISCOVERED ISSUE` from agent 05l, 2026-08-18 — an unrelated
  glossary-inference tree at bf7e2bca2 failed `tools/check_feature_flags` on every
  run for flag bead sase-pk (`commit_finalizer_shared_clone_exempt`), created ~33m
  earlier by sase-p5.4. Two consecutive runs failed identically, so not a flake.
- sase-oo.3, 2026-08-17: repo-wide red for sase-om
  (`completion_refresh_on_update`) from the concurrent sase-oc epic; that phase had
  to verify via direct ruff/mypy/pytest runs instead of `just check`.
- sase-oo.2, 2026-08-17: same gate, "flag bead exists but this tree has no matching
  flag definition."
- sase-p3.10, 2026-08-18: same gate for sase-pa (`epic_resume` gate kind), blocking
  a fully green check.

Reproduction: on any workspace, run `sase flag new <key>`; on any *other* workspace
whose tree predates that commit, run `just check` (or
`.venv/bin/python tools/check_feature_flags`). It fails on the orphan-bead rule
until the definition commit reaches that tree. Every instance above self-resolved
once the defining commit landed on master and the other agents rebased.

Scope: decide where the window should close. Candidates worth weighing:

- Do not mark the flag bead live until its definition commit lands (create it in a
  pre-live status that `LIVE_FLAG_STATUS_VALUES` excludes, promoting on the commit
  that adds the definition).
- Keep the bead live but make `orphan_bead` tolerant when the bead was created
  after the checkout's HEAD commit date — the drift is then provably "my tree is
  older than this bead", not a genuine orphan.
- Downgrade `orphan_bead` from `error` to a warning for beads younger than some
  threshold, keeping the error for genuinely abandoned definitions.

Whatever is chosen must still catch the real defect the rule exists for: a live
flag bead whose definition was deleted or never written.

Discovered while landing an unrelated agent-role phase-label rename (docs/ace.md + prompt_panel widgets) via just check-full in workspace sase_13.

REPRODUCTION: tests/completion/test_snapshot.py::test_checked_in_snapshot_has_no_drift and ::test_current_structural_view_matches_checked_in_snapshot both pass in isolation on current HEAD (.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:randomly -q tests/completion/test_snapshot.py -- 2 passed), and 'just sync-completion-spec' (tools/sync_completion_spec --write) produces no diff against the checked-in cli_spec.json. selection-health's durable record store (/home/bryan/.sase/test-selection/gh_sase-org__sase/) holds two recent full-run failure records for both nodes -- 20260818T114432Z-134839e82d2e-650306-full-run.json (recorded_at 2026-08-18T11:50:27Z) and 20260818T120830Z-134839e82d2e-1244116-full-run.json (recorded_at 2026-08-18T12:14:36Z) -- both stamped head=134839e82d2e (a commit that already contains the epic-symbols fix from 1482fc1dc, verified an ancestor via git merge-base --is-ancestor) but tree_dirty=true, i.e. the recording workspace had uncommitted local changes to CLI/argparse surface at the time.

ROOT CAUSE: cli_spec.json is a checked-in structural snapshot of the argparse tree (tests/completion/test_snapshot.py); any workspace with uncommitted CLI-surface changes, or any commit that adds argparse surface without also running 'just sync-completion-spec' in the same commit, makes the node fail there without that being a defect in the node itself. Epic sase-oc (closed) hit and understood the same underlying mechanism for a different drift instance (the .root.subcommands[bead].subcommands[epic-symbols] node from fa1948437 vs phase sase-oc.1's stale snapshot); this is the same class recurring, not a new bug. Phase bead sase-p3.14 independently flagged the same two nodes (plus 3 others already tracked elsewhere) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on 2026-08-18T08:09:50Z, corroborating this is cross-workspace noise, not something caused by this workspace's change.

IMPACT: blocks 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' (the last gate of 'just check-full') for every unrelated change landing while the durable store still holds these dirty-tree records, even though the checked-in snapshot is not actually stale on any clean tree tested.

title: Count monitors and post-handoff family shells against max_running_agents
description: A running sase agent holds exactly one runner slot for as long as any of its shells is alive — including its monitor proc shells and every agent shell launched after a monitor handoff — so max_running_agents is the real ceiling on concurrent agents on this host, and every surface that reports occupancy agrees with the admission gate.

notes.author: sase-ps.land
notes.text:
LANDED. All four phases verified against the source and their commits, integration checked, follow-ups routed.

VERIFICATION (step 1). Read every child note and confirmed each against the code and the epic's four commits (63accbfc9 sase-ps.1, 746c80705 sase-ps.3, f9a1afae7 sase-ps.2, 5bb381f4a sase-ps.4).
- count: src/sase/core/runner_slots/_admission.py has the split exactly as planned. is_runner_slot_user_agent_record is documented as admission-only and unchanged; is_runner_slot_occupying_record ignores lineage and is monitor-aware ("started" is a recorded pid when agent_meta.monitor_id is set, otherwise run_started_at); runner_slot_family_key groups by (project_name, agent_family-or-timestamp); running_agent_slot_count charges one slot per family with any occupying serial member plus one per live parallel member. run_agent_wait_slots.py:235 sources running_count from it and the serial-family early return is untouched. running_root_agent_count has no remaining reference anywhere in src/, tests/, docs/, or the Rust crate -- the rename left no second definition of "how many slots are in use", as the plan required.
- display: agent_runner_slots.py reuses the Agents-tab lane projection (sase_agent_status_counts) rather than a third predicate, with a documented narrow supplement for a sequential container whose display status mirrors a terminal child. running_listing._runner_slot_holder_dirs credits one representative shell per serial family and each parallel member, and _is_visible_runner_slot_child now follows occupancy so a post-handoff shell is never missing from sase agent list. The Statistics methodology row and runners legend state the new rule.
- stats: the Rust half is committed on sase-core master as 769b9bc ("fix(agent_stats): count family shells in historical runner occupancy"), not left uncommitted as the phase note warned. agent_runtime.rs carries is_runner_slot_occupying_record, running_agent_slot_count, merge_family_occupancy_intervals, and occupancy_member_start; both crate changelogs list it under [Unreleased]. The sase-core-rs pin stays >=0.27.18,<0.28.0 on purpose: Justfile:112 documents that dev and CI installs build from the checkout and tools/ratchet_core_window moves the published window on the release branch.
- docs: no "serial family follow-ups do not consume slots" claim survives anywhere in docs/ or src/. configuration.md#max_running_agents, ace.md, xprompt.md, llms.md, getting_started.md, troubleshooting/runner-slots.md, monitors.md ("Runner slots"), and default_config.yml all state the occupancy rule and keep holding-a-slot separate from waiting-for-one. The remaining "do not consume" sentences are the correct ones (dependency/time/fork waiters, and a shell parked at QUESTION).
- No feature flag was added, as the plan directed.

LIVE CROSS-SURFACE CHECK. On a busy host: gate running_agent_slot_count = 10; sase agent list -j runner_slots_in_use = 10 across 31 rows, with 10 distinct runner_slot_holders including the monitor sase-pq.land--mon-0 and a post-handoff shell. The gate and the listing agree exactly, which is the property the epic existed to create.

INTEGRATION (step 2). Reviewed every non-epic commit from 63accbfc9 to a2357e214. The two monitor-rendering commits (9102c9efb amber MONITOR phase label, 845253505 settled-monitor gear count) both landed before the display phase and are rendering-only, so they neither duplicate nor conflict with occupancy. Nothing else touches runner slots. Confirmed no surface still computes occupancy independently: integrations/agent_list_entries.py sums the holds_runner_slot flag that running_listing sets from the shared per-family dedup, and axe/chop_policy.py's agent_runners inhibit provider reads that same flag through list_running_agents(), so both inherit the new rule automatically -- which is what makes configuration.md's claim that agent_runners counts "the same population" true rather than aspirational. Every lineage check left in src/ (naming, editor-helper rosters, child summaries, done-row adaptation) is a family lookup, not an occupancy count.

title: A feature flag is a task bead, not a bead type
description: SASE feature flags stop being a bespoke bead type and become ordinary task beads of a project-local `flag` task type whose required fields force every new flag to record what its two branches do and what has to be true before the losing branch is deleted. The `flag` issue type, `FlagRecord`, and `BeadFlagWire` are gone; only `beta` and `sunset` kinds survive; and the five live flag beads are migrated in place.

notes.author: sase-pv.7.f0
notes.text:
DESIGN CHANGE (project owner directive, 2026-08-18): the `migrate` phase no longer rewrites the five flag bead event streams in place. The plan's `migrate` section considered and rejected close-old-create-new; the owner instead directed create-new + delete-old, and that is what shipped. The original design could not ship at all: `sase.bead._stream_integrity.prepare_event_streams_for_commit` refuses any edit to an already-published event (full analysis in sase-pv.7's BLOCKED note), so `issue_type` is immutable after `issue_created` through every sanctioned path.

WHAT SHIPPED IN sase-pv.7: each old flag bead was deleted with `sase bead rm` and re-created as a typed `flag` task bead through `create_flag_bead`, the same creation path `sase flag new` uses. Title, size, kind, `remove_by_date` and `remove_by_release` are preserved exactly; `when_enabled` / `when_disabled` / `remove_when` are the plan's drafts after per-flag verification against the code. Bead IDs necessarily changed, so `src/sase/feature_flags/registry.py` and `tests/feature_flags/test_consumers.py` were repointed:

  sase-nw -> sase-qe  coder_inherits_planner_chat          beta    medium  2026-11-14 / 0.18.0
  sase-nx -> sase-qf  prettier_enabled                     sunset  medium  2026-11-14 / 0.18.0
  sase-om -> sase-qg  completion_refresh_on_update         beta    small   2026-11-15 / 0.18.0
  sase-pa -> sase-qh  epic_resume_gate                     beta    small   2026-11-15 / 0.18.0
  sase-pk -> sase-qi  commit_finalizer_shared_clone_exempt sunset  medium  2026-11-16 / 0.18.0

Those two files were the only references to the old IDs anywhere in the repo.

CARRY-OVER FOR `retire` (sase-pv.8): `sase bead rm` does not delete a bead's event stream, so five tombstoned streams still carry `issue_type: "flag"` in their `issue_created` payload. `sase-pv.8` has a note with the full analysis; that phase must prune them before `IssueTypeWire::Flag` can be deleted.

notes.author: sase-pv.land--3
notes.text:
LANDED epic sase-pv. All nine phases closed; every phase note re-read and checked
against the source and the epic's nine commits (24ce7e056, 88d2a1582, 98b27e849,
c5a0dcf4a, 65a34b909, 2b2c5edef, a469015dc, a317a2e35, 281f3c197).

VERIFIED (step 1)
- The `flag` issue type is gone, not merely unused. `IssueType` is exactly
  {plan, phase, task}; `FlagRecord`, `BeadFlagWire`, `flag_codec`, `FlagScope`,
  and the `flag(...)` create grammar have no remaining reference in src/ or
  tools/. sase-core shipped the matching wire deletion and it is RELEASED, not
  just committed: v0.29.0 (d80fa83 "feat(bead)!: delete the flag issue type",
  3f4e773 reserved-slug drop, c121e0e task_type_fields on update). The linked
  sase-core checkout is clean at fa7ced2 with no uncommitted work, closing out
  sase-pv.4's "still uncommitted" caveat.
- Only `beta` and `sunset` kinds survive and `default` is derived from `kind`.
  `sase flag new` requires --when-enabled/--when-disabled/--remove-when (each
  accepting @<path>), offers -k {beta,sunset}, and has no --scope.
- The seven-field `flag` task type is declared in this project's sase/sase.yml
  with glyph U+2691, accent #FF875F, agent_creatable false, triage
  min_plus_ones 0, and the committed sase/task_types.json snapshot agrees.
- The five live flags are typed task beads: sase-qe, sase-qf, sase-qg, sase-qh,
  sase-qi. `sase bead list -T flag` shows all five with their preserved sizes
  and countdowns (88d/88d/89d/89d/90d, all v0.18.0); `sase bead show sase-qe`
  renders the typed FLAG block plus the rendered body template and its
  PROVENANCE note naming sase-nw.
- sase-pv.7's CARRY-OVER is discharged: the five tombstoned flag event streams
  (sase-nw, sase-nx, sase-om, sase-pa, sase-pk) are gone from the store, so
  nothing still carries issue_type "flag".
- `just _lint-flags` green; `sase bead doctor` reports nothing flag-related
  (its remaining warnings are pre-existing and unrelated).
- The epic's own DISCOVERED ISSUE note (three deterministic failures at
  a2357e214: the completion-spec drift and the demo_flag(default=...) integrity
  test) was fixed inside sase-pv.6 and is confirmed dead: tests/feature_flags,
  tests/completion, tests/task_types, and tests/test_bead/test_flag_fields.py
  run 287 passed, 1 skipped.
- Memory and docs are regenerated: sase/memory/sase_flags.md and
  feature_flags.md describe two kinds and the Off-branch removal rule, and no
  doc, memory note, or AGENTS.md text still calls a flag an issue type.

INTEGRATED (step 2)
- Real gap found and fixed. sase-pv.8 added
  `require_rust_binding("bead_needs_drop_flag_type_migration")` and
  `..._drop_flag_type_migration_sql")`, which exist only in sase-core 0.29.0,
  but pyproject.toml still declared `sase-core-rs>=0.27.18,<0.28.0`. The window
  excluded every release that has them, so CI's release-core-floor-smoke leg
  (`tools/check_sase_core_rs_bindings` against the exact declared floor) would
  have failed and a published install would have crashed on the first bead
  read. This is precisely the skew that gate was written for. No phase could
  have caught it: sase-core-rs 0.29.0 was not uploaded to PyPI until
  2026-08-19T00:50:15Z, after sase-pv.8 closed. Fixed with the sanctioned tool,
  `tools/ratchet_core_window`, taking the window to `>=0.29.0,<0.30.0` and
  regenerating uv.lock. `tools/probe_core_floor --advisory` went from
  "stale_actionable: missing 11 capability(s)" to clean; it had named this
  epic's d80fa83 for two of the eleven. The other nine belonged to the
  task-type and workspace-occupancy epics and are fixed by the same ratchet.
- That ratchet exposed a second defect it had to fix to land:
  tests/test_powerful_variables_landing.py hardcoded the ceiling
  (`,<0\.28\.0$`) in _CORE_FLOOR_RE, so any window move made the guard fail
  with "sase-core-rs dependency is missing from pyproject.toml". That defeats
  the guard's own documented intent ("Compare rather than pin ... an
  exact-string guard would fail every ratchet"). The regex now accepts any
  ceiling and still compares the floor.
- Reviewed every non-epic commit since 24ce7e056 for conflict or duplication.
  Nothing else needed rework: `sase flag new`'s @<path> support already routes
  through the shared `sase.cli_file_values.read_at_path_value` added by
  771454166 rather than duplicating it; 509170484's flake triage bump does not

  entries sase-pv.1 and sase-pv.5 had re-keyed to sase-pq and sase-pw are gone,
  resolved by a3765f857 and 8437cfd9c.

FOLLOW-UPS (step 3) - both phase proposals routed, no new bead created
- sase-pv.8's flake, test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet: duplicate

  test_cross_navigation_and_escape_surface_disabled_workspaces: duplicate of

- Every other PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP across the nine phases was already resolved on
  master and needed no bead: the glossary/render.py mypy failure (959d205ca),

  symvision unused-publics (a3765f857, 8437cfd9c; `just _lint-symvision` is
  green), and tests/_suite_gate.py exceeding the toobig limit (bbd3bf212, filed
  and closed as sase-q7).

`sase bead epic-symbols sase-pv` reports no entries. All whole-repo lint gates
pass on the landed tree: fmt (python, markdown), keep-sorted, ruff, mypy,
changelog, toobig, pyscripts, test-waits, patch/stitch terminology, symvision,
SASE validation, and committed plans.

FOLLOW-UP (step 3, third outcome) - corroborated, no new bead
- The `lint (feature flags)` gate went red on the landed tree at 2026-08-19T01:45Z
  with `rule 8: live flag bead 'sase-qq' has no definition (key
  'plugin_catalog_scoped_latest')`. Not this epic's: sase-qq was created
  2026-08-19T01:21:12Z by sase-qn.2 (still RUNNING at the time) and its registry
  definition is on neither this HEAD nor origin/master. It is the known shared-store
  race already filed as task sase-pp, which had been closed `canceled` on

  reopened by a +1 on 2026-08-18T22:47:22Z. I corroborated it with `sase bead +1
  sase-pp` (now +2), contributing what no earlier report could: the first instance
  observed AFTER this redesign landed, plus proof the redesign left the defect
  untouched - `_LIVE_FLAG_STATUSES` in src/sase/feature_flags/beads.py is the same
  five-status set before (88d2a1582~1) and after this epic, and `create_flag_bead`
  still mints the bead at `open`. So the cancel reason is spent and the bead's own
  "create pre-live, promote on the definition commit" option is still the live
  candidate. Closing this epic does not resolve sase-pp and must not be read as
  resolving it.
- Consequently the lint-gate claim above reads: every whole-repo lint gate passes on
  this tree except `lint (feature flags)`, whose single finding is that external

FINAL VERIFICATION (2026-08-19, three monitored runs)

notes.author: sase-pv.7
notes.text: BLOCKED: the plan's in-place event rewrite (rewrite issue_created payload issue_type flag->task + re-mint event_id, per the migrate phase text) is rejected by the bead stores own append-only integrity guard (sase.bead._stream_integrity.prepare_event_streams_for_commit / analyze_stream_against_ancestor, called from _commit_bead_state on every sase bead commit). That guard diffs local vs ancestor by event_id: an edited event either (a) keeps its old event_id -> classified "rewrite", reverted to ancestor + BeadStreamIntegrityError raised, or (b) gets a new event_id (re-minted, as the plan instructs) -> the old id is now "missing" from local, so the guard "restores" it by prepending the original ancestor event back, corrupting the stream into two issue_created events for one bead. I verified this live: staging the correctly-migrated event content for all 5 beads and running any sase bead commit (note/close/pages refresh) never actually committed the rewritten event-stream files across 13 attempts; a direct call to prepare_event_streams_for_commit confirmed the restore-superset corruption on all 5 files. There is no --force/bypass flag for this guard anywhere in the CLI, and no BeadIssueUpdateEventFieldsWire field exists for issue_type or task_type (only task_type_fields values, e.g. remove_by_date/remove_by_release via -b/--remove-by, are updatable post-creation) -- so issue_type is architecturally immutable after issue_created through every sanctioned mutation path. I fully reverted all exploratory changes: the beads-store workspace clone (sase/repos/beads) is hard-reset to origin/main, the canonical checkout at /home/bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase/sase/repos/beads is untouched, and the linked sase-core checkout is clean (a temporary Rust unit test used only to discover/confirm this finding was reverted, never committed). No data was changed; the 5 flag beads are still issue_type=flag. This phase needs a design revision from the epic owner: either (a) a real, no-workaround mechanism for changing issue_type is added to sase-core (a new event/mutation with matching integrity-guard support, which is Rust core work outside D9's slug/retire boundary), or (b) the migrate phase is redesigned around close-old-create-new despite the plan's D-section rejecting that approach, or (c) some other route the epic owner prefers. Recommend the epic owner revisit the migrate phase design before this is reattempted.
