title: Delete the `flag` issue type end to end
description: retire: remove the flag issue type, `FlagRecord`, and `BeadFlagWire` from the Rust wire, the Python model, the storage codecs, the create grammar, and the compatibility mirror schema.

notes.author: sase-pv.7.f0
notes.text:
BLOCKER FOR THIS PHASE, found while migrating in sase-pv.7: `sase bead rm` does not delete a bead's event stream. It appends an `issue_removed` tombstone and drops the row from `issues.jsonl`, leaving the original `issue_created` event -- including `"issue_type":"flag"` and the `flag` object -- in `events/streams/<id>.jsonl` permanently. After the migration, five such streams remain in the store: sase-nw, sase-nx, sase-om, sase-pa, sase-pk. `issues.jsonl` and the compatibility mirror have zero flag rows; only the raw streams are affected.

WHY IT BLOCKS: `read_store_issues` routes to `read_event_store_issues` whenever the event store is present (crates/sase_core/src/bead/read.rs:64-75), and `MutableStore::load` does the same (bead/mutation.rs:2382-2384), so `read_event_store` (bead/jsonl.rs:223) parses every stream file on every read and every mutation. Deleting `IssueTypeWire::Flag` from the wire therefore does not just orphan those five beads -- serde will reject their files and the whole store load will fail.

TWO CONSTRAINTS ON ANY FIX:
- Deleting a stream file outright is already publishable. `prepare_event_streams_for_commit` skips a changed path when `not (repo_root / path).is_file()`, with the comment "Removing the file is a store-level mutation (bead rm), not a truncated append-only stream" (src/sase/bead/_stream_integrity.py:92-95). Editing the events inside such a file is not publishable; that is what blocked the original migrate design.
- `events/manifest.json` carries `stream_count`, and `read_event_store` errors on `manifest.stream_count != streams.len()` (bead/jsonl.rs:238-242), so a prune must rewrite the manifest in the same mutation.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (owner's call): a one-time store migration in sase-core that drops the event streams of removed beads whose `issue_created` payload is flag-typed and rewrites `manifest.json` -- structurally the same `needs_*` / `*_sql` shape this phase already owes the compatibility mirror, and it can land alongside it. Making `sase bead rm` prune streams in general is a larger, separate decision. Keeping a deserialize-only `flag` variant would defeat the epic's purpose and is not recommended.

title: just check mypy fails: glossary render passes Console.color_system as str | None
description:
`just check`'s `lint (mypy)` gate fails on an untouched file:

    src/sase/glossary/render.py:74: error: Argument "color_system" to "Console"
    has incompatible type "str | None"; expected
    "Literal['auto', 'standard', '256', 'truecolor', 'windows'] | None"  [arg-type]

Discovered while implementing the approved `@<path>` bead free-text tale. That tree
does not touch `src/sase/glossary/`. Reproduced twice: whole-repo `just check` and
direct `.venv/bin/mypy`. The six files from the `@path` change type-check clean.

Root cause: `_print_rich_without_trailing_whitespace` copies `console.color_system`
onto a new `Console`. Rich types `Console.color_system` as `str | None` but the
constructor parameter as a Literal union. Introduced by 88fa6e949 ("feat(glossary):
fail batched reads all-or-nothing and shrink render bytes"), which added this
capture-and-rstrip helper. That commit's `SASE_PLAN` is
`202608/glossary_batched_reads.md`; no in-progress epic still owns it.

Fix is a one-line type narrowing or cast at the `color_system=` argument so mypy
accepts the passthrough. Until then every agent's `just check` is red at mypy.

title: pip install sase-research-artifacts cannot resolve until sase 0.17.0 ships on PyPI
close_reason: That is to be expected.
description: The sase-pt epic plan (plan:202608/research_artifacts_first_release.md, phase 'verify', step 3) explicitly required filing this as a task bead via /sase_new_task; the phase worker (sase-pt.4) deliberately deferred that to the land agent instead of creating it itself. Verified still true by sase-pt.land (2026-08-18) at the time of filing: PyPI's sase package is 0.16.0 (both on PyPI and in this repo's pyproject.toml), while the published sase-research-artifacts==0.2.0 wheel declares Requires-Dist sase>=0.17.0. CI and 'just install' work around this today with an --overrides file pointed at a source checkout (see tools/setup_required_plugins and the install-smoke workflow job), so this does not block internal development, only an outside user's plain 'pip install sase-research-artifacts'. This is deliberate per a comment in sase-research-artifacts' pyproject.toml, not a mistake -- the task is to revisit it once sase 0.17.0 actually ships to PyPI, not to lower the floor now.

notes.author: sase-p3.15.land
notes.text: MECHANISM UPDATE from sase-p3.15.land (landing epic sase-p3.15, 2026-08-18). This bead stays closed-canceled -- the owner's 'That is to be expected' still holds and epic phase sase-p3.15.3 independently hit the same wall, so no new task was filed. One factual correction for whoever revisits this once sase 0.17.0 ships: this description says CI and 'just install' work around the floor 'with an --overrides file pointed at a source checkout (see tools/setup_required_plugins ...)'. That is no longer how it works. The only --overrides file in this repo is Justfile:_core-overrides-arg, which lifts the published sase-core-rs window and has nothing to do with this plugin. tools/setup_required_plugins passes --no-deps on every install, so the wheel's Requires-Dist sase>=0.17.0 is never resolved and PyPI sase 0.16.0 is never consulted; sase-p3.15.3 also removed the git+https://github.com/sase-org/<repo> fallback the tool briefly had. Verified live in workspace sase_12 at HEAD 11f78656d: 'just install' with no linked checkout installs sase-research-artifacts 0.2.0 from PyPI and 'import sase_research_artifacts' succeeds, while a plain resolving 'uv pip install sase-research-artifacts' still cannot resolve. So the blast radius is exactly what this bead says (outside users only), but the internal workaround is --no-deps, not an overrides file.

task_type_fields.impact: Blocks any outside user (not using this repo's source-checkout --overrides trick) from installing sase-research-artifacts via a plain 'pip install'. README.md and docs/configuration.md in sase-research-artifacts already document the floor; once sase 0.17.0 ships on PyPI, confirm the install resolves naturally and update those docs if their wording assumed the blocker was still open.

notes.author: sase-q0.land
notes.text:
LANDING (in progress, sase-q0.land): steps 1-2 done. Verification and follow-up triage below; the epic is NOT closed because step 2 found unfinished in-scope work (see "REMAINING EPIC WORK").

VERIFIED (read the source and each commit, not just the phase notes):
- sase-q0.1 / 725cdb11d — src/sase/logs/workspace_claim_ledger.py appends a record for every mutation of all five helpers in running_field/_operations.py (claim_workspace, release_workspace, hold_workspace_claim, transfer_workspace_claim, claim_next_axe_workspace), inside the lock, with before/after claim rows for the affected workspace, actor pid/ppid, claim pid, outcome, error, and a caller tag; record_running_field_mutation swallows every exception, so a ledger write can never fail a claim. read_ledger_records + ledger_path are real, filtered readers.
- sase-q0.2 / 75e1db1ef — claim_deferred_workspace now claims via claim_next_axe_workspace BEFORE materializing and releases the slot when materialization throws (_claim_next_deferred_workspace); the family-attach pin is a single-shot checked claim that names the occupant and exits (_claim_pinned_deferred_workspace + _describe_workspace_occupant). Re-ran the sweep the plan asked for: the only surviving get_first_available_* callers in this repo are ace/operations.py:46 and ace/tui/actions/agent_workflow/_ref_resolution.py:57, and both are documented read-only previews.
- sase-q0.3 / 7a2906e13 — .sase/occupant.json written on the launcher-preclaim/transfer path (agent/launch_spawn.py:326) and the deferred path (axe/run_agent_phases.py:154), cleared at the three release funnels; .sase/ is in SASE_GIT_INFO_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS so git clean cannot remove it. decide_workspace_occupant_conflict lives in sase-core (crates/sase_core/src/agent_launch/mod.rs:2054, commit 35c09db, pushed and in sync with origin/master) with 7 unit tests; occupancy_guard.ensure_workspace_not_occupied cross-checks the marker against the RUNNING row and raises WorkspaceOccupiedError. Guard runs before prepare_workspace at run_agent_runner_setup.py:133 and :215 and before both retry re-preps at run_agent_exec_retry.py:349 and :397. Retry-spawn children skip prep entirely (retry_handoff early return), which is what covers the plan's "retry-chain parent is the same lineage" case.
- sase-q0.4 / 716e9de98 — workspace.occupancy_conflicts doctor check registered at doctor/checks_workspace.py:63, report-only, three conflict shapes, annotated from the ledger; concurrency + incident-shape tests present.
- Gates: just install && just _lint-symvision is GREEN on 716e9de98 ("All public/private classes/functions are used properly!"), and sase bead epic-symbols sase-q0 reports no --epic-symbol entries. The 146 tests across the epic's 11 test files all pass.

INTEGRATION (commits since 725cdb11d, excluding the epic's own): only daa095ec3 (restart.py split) and ea31a2b5b (kill-and-edit identity) touch src/sase/agent/**, and neither claims, releases, or prepares a workspace — grep for claim_workspace/release_workspace/prepare_workspace/occupant over restart.py, relaunch_prompt.py and the six new _restart_*.py modules returns nothing. No integration edits were needed in this repo.

REMAINING EPIC WORK (why this epic is not closed): the atomic and guard sweeps covered only the sase repo. The sase-github linked plugin holds the workflow steps the epic plan names by name — gh__setup / gh__prepare / gh__checkout — and they were never converted:
- sase_github/scripts/gh_setup.py: the n=None branch is a textbook check-then-claim (get_first_available_axe_workspace -> ensure_workspace_checkout materializes -> claim_workspace) AND discards the claim result, so a losing racer proceeds inside the winner's workspace; the n=<num> branch claims a pinned number with no availability check and no result check. No caller_tag, so these mutations are unattributable in the ledger, and no occupant record is written.
- sase_github/workspace_plugin.py ws_submit_changespec (~:539): still the get_first_available_axe_workspace -> get_workspace_directory_for_num -> claim_workspace pattern, while its sibling src/sase/workspace_provider/plugins/bare_git_submit.py:159 was converted to claim_next_axe_workspace_dir by phase sase-q0.2. Its provider.checkout is unguarded.
- sase_github/xprompts/gh.yml: the prepare step runs `git stash push --include-untracked` + `git pull --rebase` and the checkout step runs provider.checkout + pull, both against a checkout that may hold another live agent, with no ensure_workspace_not_occupied; the release step passes no caller_tag and never clears the occupant record.
This resolves the sase-q0.3 PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP that asked the land agent to confirm the gh__* reading: those hooks are real, they just live in the sase-github plugin rather than in this repo, so the phase's "coverage is equivalent" conclusion holds only for agent launches (which take the SASE_GH_PRE_ALLOCATED branch and skip claiming) and not for direct #gh invocations or ACE submit. Swept the other plugin repos too — sase-telegram, sase-nvim and sase-research-artifacts contain zero claim/release/prepare call sites.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP triage (every entry from all four phase beads):
- glossary/render.py mypy (sase-q0.1, sase-q0.2): already fixed upstream by 959d205ca. No action.
- unused public project_accent/project_accent_map + stale --epic-symbol "sase-pw.8(project_accent_map)" (sase-q0.2, sase-q0.3, sase-q0.4): already fixed upstream by a3765f857 and 8437cfd9c. Confirmed green. No action.
- tests/completion/test_snapshot.py drift and tests/feature_flags/test_integrity.py::test_kind_mismatch_when_default_disagrees_with_kind (sase-q0.2, sase-q0.3): both now pass on 716e9de98 (9 passed). No action.
- RUNNING rows dropped for unrecognized artifacts-timestamp shapes (sase-q0.2): confirmed and materially worse than reported — WorkspaceClaimLine::parse discards the WHOLE row for any unrecognized trailing part, and the already-claimed guard in plan_claim_workspace_from_content parses through the same function, so it fails open into double allocation. Filed as task sase-qa (small), per this plan's own instruction to file rather than widen the epic.
- tests/_agent_cleanup_proc_helpers.py ModuleNotFoundError on standalone collection (sase-q0.1): confirmed still reproducing; root-caused to the sys.modules stub at tests/ace/tui/conftest.py:134 covering for proc_queue.py, deleted in 8c4840458. Filed as task sase-qb (small).
- gh__setup/gh__prepare/gh__checkout discrepancy (sase-q0.3): NOT a follow-up — it is the remaining epic work above.
- centralize occupant.json write/clear inside running_field/_operations.py so all ~60 release paths clear it (sase-q0.3): DECLINED, no bead filed. It has no demonstrated defect — every release funnel that is not already wired kills or outlives the agent first, so the occupant pid is dead and the guard already treats that as a legitimate takeover; and the one residual shape (a live occupant whose claim was released elsewhere) refuses the next agent's prep, which is the correct fail-safe direction. The proposed fix would also have running_field derive checkout paths from workspace numbers, pulling workspace-provider path resolution into the claim layer. Revisit only if a real false refusal or a real missed clear is observed.
- Additionally found while sweeping prep sites: sase workspace open-clean (main/workspace_handler_list.py:377) cleans and hard-resets without the new guard. Outside the four sites the plan named and explicitly user-initiated, so filed as task sase-qc (small) rather than pulled into this epic.
- Also closed ready task sase-q5 (the epic's own unused ledger symbols), resolved by 716e9de98.

title: Extend the workspace-exclusivity guarantee to the sase-github plugin
description: The sase-github plugin acquires workspaces the same way the rest of SASE does: every gh__setup and GitHub-submit allocation is a single atomic claim whose result is checked and whose ledger record names its caller, a pinned n=<num> target that a live agent holds fails with that agent named instead of being taken, and no gh workflow step stashes, pulls, or checks out inside a checkout another live agent occupies.

notes.author: sase-q0.5.land
notes.text:
LANDING (sase-q0.5.land): epic complete and closed. Verified both phases against the source and their commits in the sase-github linked repo (both pushed, origin/master in sync).

VERIFIED (read the code and the commits, not just the phase notes):
- sase-q0.5.1 / 61dd36f "feat: claim GitHub workspaces atomically" — gh_setup.py's unpinned branch now calls claim_next_axe_workspace(caller_tag="gh-setup") first and materializes second via _materialize_or_release, which release_workspace()es the slot when ensure_workspace_checkout or materialize_sdd_store raises. The pinned n=<num> branch is a single-shot claim_workspace whose result IS checked; on failure it prints the occupant (name, pid, liveness, workflow, artifacts timestamp, via _describe_workspace_occupant/_format_workspace_occupant copied from run_agent_phases.py) to stderr and sys.exit(1) without materializing. No claim result is discarded on any branch. The pre_allocated branch is untouched, as the plan required. workspace_plugin.ws_submit_changespec was converted to claim_next_axe_workspace_dir(..., caller_tag="gh-submit") inside try/except WorkspaceClaimError, dropping the get_first_available_axe_workspace + get_workspace_directory_for_num + claim_workspace trio, and its finally: release_workspace now carries caller_tag="gh-submit". gh.yml's release step carries caller_tag="gh-release".
- sase-q0.5.2 / 51347d4 "feat(workspace): guard gh workflow steps against occupied checkouts" — gh_setup.py writes .sase/occupant.json via new_occupant_record/write_occupant_record for real numbered workspaces only (workspace_num > 1, matching claim_deferred_workspace's guard), and calls ensure_workspace_not_occupied before printing _chdir, on the claimed and pre_allocated branches alike, so one guard covers gh__prepare's `git stash push --include-untracked` and gh__checkout's provider.checkout, which both run in that directory immediately afterwards. ws_submit_changespec guards ws_dir before provider.checkout(); its refusal returns (False, "Refusing checkout: ...") from inside the try, so the finally still releases. gh.yml's release step calls clear_occupant_record(setup.workspace_dir).
- Confirmed the pre_allocated pid identity the guard depends on: claim_deferred_workspace writes the RUNNING row and the occupant record with os.getpid() of the axe runner; run_execution_loop calls execute_workflow in that same process, and _execute_python_step runs each step as a direct child, so gh_setup's os.getppid() is that same pid and decide_workspace_occupant_conflict's pid comparison recognises the caller's own lineage instead of refusing every pre-allocated #gh run.
- Confirmed the occupant record gh_setup writes is reachable by the rest of the system: the plugin's ws_get_workspace_directory hook resolves through the same ensure_workspace_checkout(primary_workspace_dir, num), so stale_running_cleanup._clear_stale_occupant_record and the workspace.occupancy_conflicts doctor check resolve to the same directory. `sase doctor --check workspace.occupancy_conflicts` is OK.
- Swept the plugin for leftovers: no get_first_available_* callers remain, no unchecked claim results, no unguarded destructive prep.

FIXED DURING LANDING (99a6277, this epic's own defect): gh_setup claims before it guards, so a WorkspaceOccupiedError left the RUNNING row held — a failed `setup` step means gh.yml's `release` step never runs, because its `if: {{ setup.should_release }}` condition cannot evaluate once setup's outputs are missing, so the slot stayed claimed for the lifetime of the executor process until stale-claim cleanup reaped it. The guard call is now wrapped so a refusal releases the slot it just claimed, mirroring _materialize_or_release; the pre_allocated branch releases nothing, since the launcher owns that claim. Two regression tests added (test_setup_releases_its_claim_when_the_guard_refuses, which fails without the fix, and test_pre_allocated_guard_refusal_releases_nothing).

INTEGRATION (commits since this epic's first commit 61dd36f, excluding its own): sase-github had none. sase-core had none since 35c09db. The sase repo landed five, of which two touch this epic's surface and neither needed an edit here: 893fb2352 split running_field/_operations.py into per-operation modules — verbatim moves behind the same sase.running_field facade, so every name gh_setup.py and workspace_plugin.py import (claim_workspace, claim_next_axe_workspace, claim_next_axe_workspace_dir, release_workspace, get_claimed_workspaces, WorkspaceClaim, WorkspaceClaimError, ClaimResult) still resolves; 7563372f1 added the same ensure_workspace_not_occupied guard to prepare_opened_checkout for `workspace open --clean` (task sase-qc), which complements rather than duplicates this epic. No sase-repo docs name the gh call sites or the caller tags, so nothing there went stale.

title: A wedged pytest run holds its worker-token grant forever: the suite gate bounds waiters but never bounds holders
description:
The pytest suite gate reclaims a token only when the holding process *dies* -- `flock` on `token-NNN.lock` does that for free. There is no bound on how long a *live* process may hold a grant, and no health, age, or progress check on a holder. One wedged run therefore removes its whole grant from the host pool permanently, and the only recovery is a human noticing and killing the process.

Observed live on athena: a `tools/run_pytest scoped` run (pid 1172645, workspace sase_12) has held 14 of the host's 32 tokens continuously for over 27 hours. A scoped run normally finishes in minutes.

The gate already computes and prints each holder's `age` in its waiting and timeout messages (`_format_holders` / `_holder_identity_and_text` in `tests/_suite_gate.py`), so the diagnostic signal exists; nothing consumes it.

Worth deciding as part of the fix, rather than assumed here: whether a holder past some age is *reported* (loudly, e.g. in the waiting message and `just doctor`), *reclaimed* (its tokens stolen back into the pool), or *killed*. Stealing tokens from a process that is merely slow rather than wedged would oversubscribe the host, so a progress heartbeat written alongside the existing `started` field is probably the honest signal, with a generous age cap as the backstop. `sase-ib.6` ('Fair worker allocation when agents run in parallel') built the fair-split behavior this would extend.

FOUND BY the sase-ps land agent (2026-08-18) while running `just test-visual` and `just test` as part of that epic's landing verification; sase-ps (runner-slot occupancy) touches nothing in the pytest suite gate. Checked against the in-progress epic list: no active epic owns the suite gate -- sase-j7 is process-global state leaking between tests, sase-q0 is workspace claims, sase-m4 is GitHub Actions -- so this is filed as a standalone task rather than attached to an epic.

notes.author: sase-q2
notes.text: Live holders are now bounded. Decision: report + reclaim, not process-group kill. Holder metadata gained heartbeat/progress/starttime; pytest collection and completed calls write a progress sidecar (and refresh token files when this process holds the FDs). A holder-side watchdog self-releases if SASE_TEST_GATE_STALE (default 30m without progress) or SASE_TEST_GATE_MAX_HOLD (default 4h even with heartbeats) fires; a waiter SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs a still-held reclaimable PID after starttime identity check, skipping self. Waiting/timeout messages print age, heartbeat age, and reclaim reason. After execv, configure_suite_gate adopts inherited FDs only when LEASE_PID matches (xdist workers and nested pytest do not unlock the controller). Verified: 57 tests/test_suite_gate.py under xdist -n 4; 5 tests/test_suite_gate_integration.py; ruff + mypy clean. Live reclaim on this host: acquire signaled pid 1172645 (the original 27h 14-token tools/run_pytest scoped holder) for max-hold and the pool admitted a 12-worker suite. just check passed fmt/ruff/mypy/flags/pyscripts/test-waits/changelog/terminology and failed only lint (symvision) on pre-existing Justfile --epic-symbol sase-pw.8(project_accent_map); recorded as DISCOVERED ISSUE on in-progress epic sase-pw, not caused by this change.

Gate printed: 14 tokens pid 1172645 grant 14 age 101633s argv 'tools/run_pytest scoped', plus three other live scoped holders (6/4/8 tokens). Visual suite sat blocked with 0 tokens available below the floor. Same wedged holder described in the original report; age has grown past 28h. Did not kill the process.

task_type_fields.impact:
Every agent on the host, for as long as the wedged run survives. The stuck grant is
44% of the pool (14/32), so the effective host-wide test capacity is silently almost
halved. With three other legitimate runs active, the pool hit zero and new runs got
nothing.

Concretely, during this epic's landing verification a `just test-visual` run sat
blocked for roughly five minutes before capacity freed, and the follow-up `just test`
run was still parked at 0 available tokens minutes later. Neither run did anything
wrong; the only reason they eventually proceeded is that *other* runs finished. The
45-minute `SASE_TEST_GATE_TIMEOUT` then turns a starved wait into a `pytest.UsageError`
rather than a test result, so `just check` and `just check-full` fail for a reason that
has nothing to do with the tree under test -- which is exactly the misattribution
`sase-lc` (dirty-workspace flake attribution) already had to fix once for a different
cause.

Nothing surfaces the condition either. The wedged holder is visible only to whoever
happens to read a waiting message and notice a five-digit `age`, so the pool can stay
half-consumed for a day, as it has here, before anyone looks.
task_type_fields.repro:
On athena, 2026-08-18, observed directly in the live token directory:

    $ cat /tmp/sase-pytest-tokens-1000/pool.lock
    {"capacity": 32, "explicit": false, ...}

    $ for f in /tmp/sase-pytest-tokens-1000/token-0*.lock; do head -c 200 $f; done
    token-000..token-013: {"argv": "tools/run_pytest scoped", "budget": 32,
      "granted": 14, "lease_id": "1172645-1786980248731743991", "pid": 1172645,
      "started": 1786980248.73 ...}

    $ ps -p 1172645 -o pid,lstart,etime,stat
        PID                  STARTED     ELAPSED STAT
    1172645 Mon Aug 17 11:24:07 2026  1-03:17:32 Sl

One `tools/run_pytest scoped` run in workspace sase_12 has held tokens 000-013 --
14 of the host's 32 -- continuously since 2026-08-17 11:24 EDT, over 27 hours. It is
alive (state `Sl`), so `flock` never releases its tokens, but a scoped run completes in
minutes; this one is wedged and will hold its grant until someone kills it by hand.

Any run that then asks for tokens sees the pool exhausted and stalls:

    $ just test
    Waiting for a SASE pytest worker-token grant of 4-7 worker tokens; 0 tokens were
    available below the floor. Current holders: 14 tokens: pid 1172645, grant 14,
    age 98251s, argv 'tools/run_pytest scoped'; 6 tokens: pid 173872, grant 6,
    age 167s, argv 'tools/run_pytest visual'; ...

The waiting message already prints `age` for every holder, so the gate has the exact
signal it needs and simply does not act on it.

ROOT CAUSE: `WorkerTokenLease.acquire` in `tests/_suite_gate.py` bounds only the
*waiter* -- `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 45 * 60`, overridable via
`SASE_TEST_GATE_TIMEOUT` -- and never bounds a *holder*. Reclamation is entirely
implicit in `flock`: `_try_acquire_token` takes an exclusive lock on
`token-NNN.lock`, so the kernel frees the token when the holding process dies. That
covers a crashed or killed run and covers nothing else. A live-but-wedged process
holds its full grant forever, and `_scan_active_holders` reads holder metadata
(including `started`) purely to render the waiting/timeout message.

title: Model/pool-alias resolution silently falls back to launch-default model, breaking 6 tests in test_workflow_executor.py and test_pooled_alias_single_consumption.py
close_reason: All six deterministic repro nodes now pass on freshly installed current master; the intervening model-routing work made this report obsolete.
description:
Six tests across two files fail deterministically on master, unrelated to any
in-progress epic, with a shared root cause: model/provider resolution silently
falls back to the launch-default model instead of honoring `%model:` directives,
pooled-alias cursor state, or gh-wrapper provenance.

Failing node IDs (all reproduce standalone with `-p no:randomly`, not just under
the full parallel suite):

- tests/test_workflow_executor.py::TestShouldHitl::test_inherited_model_override_beats_step_model_directive
  (`%model:pro` on a workflow step is ignored; `directives.model` comes back
  `'sonnet'` instead of the inherited `'gemini-3-flash-preview'` override)
- tests/test_workflow_executor.py::TestShouldHitl::test_prompt_step_chat_history_includes_step_metadata
  (`metadata_model` comes back `'sonnet'` instead of `'o3'`)
- tests/test_pooled_alias_single_consumption.py::test_two_consecutive_default_launches_alternate_pool_members
  (pool cursor never advances; both launches select the same member)
- tests/test_pooled_alias_single_consumption.py::test_explicit_large_directive_and_default_alias_share_pool_cursor
  (same symptom: selected member does not match the frozen pool cursor)
- tests/test_pooled_alias_single_consumption.py::test_root_metadata_step_marker_and_chat_agree_with_invoked_model
  (`agent_meta.json` is missing the `model_alias_trail` key entirely --
  `KeyError: 'model_alias_trail'`, not merely a wrong value)
- tests/test_pooled_alias_single_consumption.py::test_root_metadata_reconciles_after_gh_wrapper_display_rename
  (wrong provider entirely: `('claude', 'sonnet')` instead of the expected
  `('codex', 'gpt-5.6-sol')`)

Likely area: the pooled/size-alias launch-selection and provenance-recording
machinery built by epics sase-mf ("Simplify built-in model routing", phase
sase-mf.2 commit 2fcca46eb "feat!: replace role model aliases with size launch
settings") and sase-n8 ("Agent history for a model alias in Launch Control",
phase sase-n8.1 "Record the alias resolution trail and its origin at launch",
commit 96b48d0ab), plus follow-up 9568dd475 "fix: preserve anonymous workflow
attribution after rename" -- all closed 2026-08-15/16. Task sase-ks ("Thread
authoritative load-balanced alias selections into follow-up metadata") covered
an adjacent but distinct race-condition symptom in the same subsystem and was
closed 2026-08-14 as "superseded in substance" by commit 9df15dbe2; these
failures suggest that reconciliation has since regressed, but the exact
defect differs from sase-ks's race-condition framing (these fail
deterministically, single-threaded, with no concurrent cursor movement), so
this is filed as a new, related task rather than a +1 on sase-ks.

Discovered while landing epic sase-pq (task-type gate presentation) during
`just check-full`/`just test-cost` verification.

notes.author: 08u
notes.text: Re-tested all six exact nodes from this bead on clean master b7bdd3185 after a fresh just install. Both workflow-executor cases and all four pooled-alias/provenance cases pass in one focused run; together with three header parametrizations the command reported 9 passed in 3.11s. Current routing honors the inherited model directive, advances the shared pool cursor, records model_alias_trail, and preserves gh-wrapper provider provenance. The deterministic current-master failure described at filing is no longer present after the intervening model-routing changes.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake:
Reproduces deterministically, not intermittently: ran each failing node twice
in isolation with `-p no:randomly` (disabling pytest-randomly reordering) and
got the identical wrong value both times -- e.g.
test_inherited_model_override_beats_step_model_directive always resolves
`'sonnet'` instead of `'gemini-3-flash-preview'`, never intermittently
succeeding. Also reproduced identically at commit 3df5c321b4 (the commit
immediately preceding epic sase-pq's first commit, i.e. before sase-pq
started, in a separate worktree sharing this checkout's .venv), ruling out
both test-order pollution from the full parallel suite and any sase-pq change
as the cause.

title: A RUNNING claim row with any unrecognized trailing part is silently dropped by WorkspaceClaimLine::parse, so the allocator hands that workspace to a second agent
close_reason: Fixed in sase-core. crates/sase_core/src/agent_launch/mod.rs:4408-4426: the trailing-part loop no longer returns None on an unrecognized part -- it pushes WorkspaceClaimSuffixPart::Unknown and keeps the row, so a RUNNING claim can no longer be silently dropped. is_timestamp_part (line 4530) also now accepts the 15-char YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS shape the bead reported as rejected, alongside the 14-digit and 13-char YYMMDD_HHMMSS forms. Verified 2026-08-24 by opening sase-core through /sase_repo.
description:
Found by the sase-q0 land agent (epic "Guarantee one agent per workspace") while verifying that epic. Originally proposed as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on phase bead sase-q0.2.

`WorkspaceClaimLine::parse` in sase-core (`crates/sase_core/src/agent_launch/mod.rs`) drops an ENTIRE RUNNING-field claim row whenever any trailing pipe-separated part is neither the literal `PINNED` nor a shape `is_timestamp_part` recognizes:

```rust
for part in parts.iter().skip(4) {
    if *part == "PINNED" { pinned = true; }
    else if is_timestamp_part(part) { artifacts_timestamp = Some(...); }
    else { return None; }        // <-- whole row silently discarded
}
```

`is_timestamp_part` (same file, ~line 2276) accepts exactly two shapes: 14 bare digits (`20260818120000`) and 13 chars `YYMMDD_HHMMSS` (`260818_120000`). It rejects the very similar `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS` (`20260818_120000`), which is the format `%Y%m%d_%H%M%S` produced elsewhere in the sase repo.

This fails OPEN, which is the dangerous direction:
- `list_workspace_claims_from_content` omits the row, so `allocate_and_claim_workspace_from_content` sees that workspace number as free.
- `plan_claim_workspace_from_content`'s "workspace #N is already claimed" guard also parses through `WorkspaceClaimLine::parse`, so it does not reject the second claim either.

Net effect: one unparseable claim row hands a live agent's workspace to a second agent. That is exactly the failure mode epic sase-q0 exists to prevent, and it matches the epic plan's explicit open anomaly ("Either a row was lost from the ProjectSpec file ... or the interleaving differs from the reconstruction"). The epic plan put ProjectSpec-format work out of scope and directed that this be filed as a task rather than widening the epic.

No producer in the sase repo is known to emit a non-conforming trailing part today (all writers go through the Rust `to_line()`), so this is currently latent — but a hand edit, a plugin, or a future field addition turns it into silent double allocation with no error anywhere.

SUGGESTED FIX (judgment needed, not a blind change): make an unrecognized trailing part non-fatal — keep the row, preserve the unknown part verbatim on rewrite, and ignore it for semantics — so an unparseable extra can never make a claimed workspace look free. Optionally widen `is_timestamp_part` to accept `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS`. Add Rust unit tests that a row with an unknown trailing part is still returned by `list_workspace_claims_from_content` and still blocks `plan_claim_workspace_from_content`.

title: Three test modules import the deleted sase.ace.tui.proc_queue and only survive via a tests/ace/tui/conftest.py stub, so they fail to collect in a scoped run
close_reason: Fixed by b76f53b99 'fix: repair guardrails for provider docs and proc imports'. The tests/ace/tui/conftest.py stub is gone, replaced by an explicit tests/ace/tui/_compat_proc_queue.py, and tests/ace/tui/test_deleted_proc_queue_imports.py now guards both that sase.ace.tui.proc_queue is unimportable and that no test imports it. description:
Found by the sase-q0 land agent while verifying that epic; originally proposed as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on phase bead sase-q0.1.

`src/sase/ace/tui/proc_queue.py` was deleted in 8c4840458 ("feat(ace): observe durable procs read-only", bead sase-m9.3.1.4, plan 202608/readonly_ace_proc_observer.md). Three test modules still import from it:

- `tests/_agent_cleanup_proc_helpers.py:25` — `from sase.ace.tui.proc_queue import ProcInfo`
- `tests/_plan_approval_tui_helpers.py:11` — same import
- `tests/ace/tui/test_agent_cleanup_procs.py:24` — `from sase.ace.tui.proc_queue import ProcInfo, ProcQueue`

They only work because `tests/ace/tui/conftest.py:129-134` builds a fake module and does `sys.modules.setdefault("sase.ace.tui.proc_queue", _proc_queue_module)`. That conftest is only loaded when something under `tests/ace/tui/` is part of the collection, so importability of those three modules depends on collection ORDER and on which directories the run happens to include.

Why this matters beyond tidiness: `just check`'s diff-scoped lane (`tools/select_tests`) picks a subset of test files from the import-graph closure of the diff. A diff touching only `src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_dismiss_persistence.py` can select `tests/test_agent_dismiss_persistence.py` without anything under `tests/ace/tui/`, and the whole scoped run then dies at collection with `ModuleNotFoundError`, not with a real test failure. Epic sase-q0's own phase sase-q0.1 modified exactly that source file and that test file.

The full suite is currently green because `tests/ace/tui/` is always collected there, which is precisely what makes this hard to notice.

SUGGESTED FIX (judgment needed): point the three test modules at the real post-migration types (`sase.ace.tui._proc_observer_models` / whatever now owns `ProcInfo`/`ProcQueue`), then delete the `sys.modules.setdefault` compat shim from `tests/ace/tui/conftest.py`. Alternatively move the shim to the top-level `tests/conftest.py` if the compat surface is still wanted — but that keeps a fake module for a deleted API, so retiring it is preferable.

title: sase workspace open-clean cleans and hard-resets a checkout without the sase-q0 occupancy guard, so a wrong workspace number destroys a live agent's work
description:
Found by the sase-q0 land agent ("Guarantee one agent per workspace") while sweeping every destructive workspace-preparation call site.

Epic sase-q0 added `sase.core.occupancy_guard.ensure_workspace_not_occupied` and wired it in front of every destructive prep site the epic plan named:

- `prepare_workspace_if_needed` and `prepare_linked_repo_workspaces_if_needed` (`src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner_setup.py`)
- both retry re-prep sites in `handle_workflow_error` (`src/sase/axe/run_agent_exec_retry.py`)

One further `prepare_workspace` caller was not in the plan's list and is still unguarded: `prepare_opened_checkout(..., preparation="runner")` in `src/sase/main/workspace_handler_list.py:377-386`, reached from `handle_open_clean` (`sase workspace open-clean <N>`). It runs `prepare_workspace(path, clean_label, VCS_DEFAULT_REVISION, backup_suffix="workspace-open", ...)`, i.e. `git clean` plus a hard reset to the default revision, on workspace `N` of the given project, with no check of the RUNNING field or of that checkout's `.sase/occupant.json`.

`sase repo open` is NOT affected — `src/sase/main/repo_handler_open.py:119` passes `preparation="none"`.

The command name says "clean", so a human running it against their own idle workspace is doing exactly what they asked for. The hazard is a mistyped or stale workspace number: today that silently destroys a live agent's uncommitted work, which is the same data loss the epic's guard was built to make impossible. The epic already supplies the machinery, so guarding this site is a small, self-contained change.

SUGGESTED FIX: call `ensure_workspace_not_occupied` (with an `OccupancyCaller` for the invoking process) before the `preparation == "runner"` branch runs `prepare_workspace`, and fail with the occupant named. Decide deliberately whether an explicit `--force` escape hatch is wanted for the "I know it is stale, clean it anyway" case; the epic's own guard deliberately has none because a dead recorded pid is already treated as a legitimate takeover.

description: The Projects tab of the SASE Admin Center says which project is current — in the project's own accent color, the same one the top-bar `+<project>` chip uses — and one configurable keypress on any row makes that project current, everywhere, at once.

One real integration gap found and fixed: the top-bar chip's tooltip still said 'Launch an agent on a project to make it current', the same claim this epic retired everywhere else; it now names both routes (launch an agent, or press c on the Projects tab), with docs/ace.md and the indicator tests updated to match.

One epic-caused regression found and fixed. sase-qd.3 filed its flake as pre-existing while naming sase-qd.2's own code as the cause, and it was independently filed as sase-qo. It is this epic's: _apply_current_project_display repainted via a bare _refresh_options(), which prefers the session bookmark over the live OptionList.highlighted. Because OptionHighlighted only reaches the pane after bubbling out of the option list's queue, a resolve can overtake it and snap the selection back to row 0 — on mount, on R, and after a successful c, so it is user-facing, not just a test artifact. Fixed by routing both resolve paths through _repaint_for_current_project(), which pins the live highlight the way the inventory worker's completion already does. Added a deterministic regression test that drives the seam directly; confirmed it fails on the pre-fix tree (highlighted == 0, expected 1) and passes with the fix.

title: test_process_group_kill_reaps_grandchildren_and_resistant_children races a non-atomic pid-file write: exists() is true before the digits land, so int('') raises under the parallel lane
close_reason: Fixed exactly as the bead diagnosed: the pid-file write is now atomic. tests/test_procs_supervisor.py:130-133 writes to a per-pid temp sibling and then os.replace(tmp, path), so grandchild_pid.exists() can no longer be true before the digits land and int('') cannot raise. Landed in 569d4257b 'fix: stabilize process concurrency closeout'. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
PROPOSED BY closed epic phase sase-p3.12 (epic sase-p3, plugin-extensible task bead types) at 2026-08-18T04:58:57Z: "tests/test_procs_supervisor.py::test_process_group_kill_reaps_grandchildren_and_resistant_children failed once in the escalated suite with ValueError empty int, then passed on rerun — flaky, not caused by this phase." Routed here by sase-p3.15.land while resuming sase-p3's interrupted landing. Every other follow-up that epic left open already had a bead (sase-jb, sase-pr, sase-pg, sase-oz, sase-oh); this node did not, and unlike those it is not carried in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt, so nothing absorbs it today.

ROOT CAUSE, read directly out of the test at HEAD 11f78656d — this is a non-atomic-write race in the test itself, not scheduler contention:

```python
deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
while time.monotonic() < deadline and not grandchild_pid.exists():
    time.sleep(0.05)  # sase-test-wait: poll grandchild pid file
gpid = int(grandchild_pid.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))   # tests/test_procs_supervisor.py:138
```

The subprocess writes the grandchild pid with `pathlib.Path(...).write_text(str(child))`, which is `open()` + `write()` + `close()`, not an atomic replace. `Path.exists()` flips to True the instant `open()` creates the inode, which is strictly before the digits are written. If the poll observes the file in that window, `read_text()` returns `""` and `int("")` raises `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''` — exactly the reported signature. Under the full parallel lane the writer is descheduled between create and write far more often, which is why this only ever shows up in the escalated suite.

Two smaller defects in the same block, worth fixing in the same pass:
1. The loop has no post-condition assertion. If the 10s deadline expires with no file at all, the failure surfaces as a bare `FileNotFoundError` from `read_text()` rather than a message naming the timeout, so the two distinct causes are indistinguishable in a CI log.
2. `is_process_running(gpid)` on the next line would be handed a garbage pid if a partial write ever produced a short-but-parseable number. A partial numeric read is possible in principle for a multi-digit pid, and would make the test assert against an unrelated process.

SCOPE: make the handshake atomic and the wait explicit. Preferred fix is to have the subprocess write to a temp path in the same directory and `os.replace()` it onto the final path, so `exists()` implies fully written; alternatively, poll for parseable content instead of mere existence (read, strip, retry while empty) and assert the deadline was met before parsing. Do not simply widen the 10s deadline — the deadline is not what fails here.

This is a test-only defect. src/sase/procs/spawn.py:193 does its own `int(payload["pid"])`, but that reads an already-parsed JSON payload, not a racing file, and is not implicated.

notes.author: sase-p3.15.land

title: Six tests in tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py assert an absolute doctor status while reading the host's live plugin entry points, so they pass or fail on installed-plugin state rather than on the tree
close_reason: Fixed: the file is hermetic again. tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py now parametrizes disable_plugins and toggles SASE_DISABLE_PLUGINS explicitly (landed in b76f53b99 'fix: repair guardrails for provider docs and proc imports'). Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f by running the bead's own reproduction, which previously gave 15 passed vs 6 failed/9 passed: '.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py' -> 19 passed, and the same command under SASE_DISABLE_PLUGINS=1 -> 19 passed. That is the bead's stated verification criterion (passes identically with and without the flag).
description:
PROPOSED BY the sase-p8 land agent on 2026-08-18 as the "SECONDARY DEFECT THIS EXPOSES" clause of a DISCOVERED ISSUE note on epic sase-p3, and re-verified and routed here by sase-p3.15.land while closing that epic. The primary defect in that note (a dangling editable sase-research-artifacts install) is fixed and is tracked separately on sase-pj; this is the independent hermeticity defect it uncovered, which no fix to the install path can address.

THE DEFECT: tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py isolates the CONFIG the check reads but not the PLUGIN ENTRY POINTS it reads. Its only isolation helper is

```python
def _patch_config(monkeypatch, config):
    monkeypatch.setattr("sase.config.core.load_merged_config", lambda: config)
```

so check_config_repos() still resolves artifact-ref and file-hook providers out of the live interpreter's importlib.metadata entry points. Six tests then assert an ABSOLUTE status ("OK", or a specific problem list) that silently depends on which plugins happen to be installed on the host running pytest.

REPRODUCTION at HEAD 11f78656d, workspace sase_12, with a fully healthy plugin install (sase-research-artifacts 0.2.0 importable, sase doctor -C plugins.required OK):

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py
15 passed

$ SASE_DISABLE_PLUGINS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py
6 failed, 9 passed
```

The six that flip are exactly the six sase-p8.land named: test_repos_reports_ok_when_sidecar_is_unset, test_repos_reports_ok_for_canonical_bucketed_config, test_repos_reports_leftover_name_field, test_repos_reports_scalar_sidecar_value, test_repos_reports_undescribed_enabled_lazy_custom_entry, test_repos_reports_invalid_sidecar_ref_policy. Each fails as `AssertionError: assert 'WARN' == 'OK'` (tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py:298 for the first), because check_config_repos().data["problems"] gains rows like "Failed to load artifact provider entry point sase_artifact_refs:research: ModuleNotFoundError" and "repos.sidecar.custom.research.ref.use references missing artifact ref provider 'research'".

SASE_DISABLE_PLUGINS is used here only as a cheap, deterministic stand-in for the real trigger, which is any host whose installed plugin set differs from the author's: a workspace where a required plugin failed to install, a contributor without the sase-org plugins, a CI leg that installs a different set, or a future plugin whose provider registration changes. Note that the default test fixture's existing SASE_DISABLE_PLUGIN_CONFIG isolation (tests/_conftest_runtime.py, added by sase-p3.15.2) does NOT cover this: it suppresses plugin default_config.yml layers only, and leaves the entry-point registry live on purpose.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: before plugins.required existed, a missing plugin was the common case and these tests were red for the same reason (that is how sase-p8.land found them). Today they are green because the install path was repaired, which means the defect is latent rather than gone -- the suite has simply stopped telling anyone that six of its doctor assertions are a function of the host rather than of the committed tree.

SCOPE: isolate the artifact-provider registry in these tests the way config already is -- patch or fake get_artifact_provider_registry / the entry-point lookup so each test declares the providers it expects, and clear whatever registry cache backs it -- then confirm the file passes identically with and without SASE_DISABLE_PLUGINS=1. While in there, check whether other doctor check tests that call a check function directly with only _patch_config have the same shape; check_config_repos is the one with proven exposure, but the pattern is what should be fixed.

notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE: tests/ace/tui/test_plugins_browser_pane_detail.py::test_plugins_pane_lazy_fetches_highlighted_latest_when_flag_on fails reproducibly on clean master (17592d904), not a flake: 3/3 serial isolated runs failed under '.venv/bin/python -m pytest <node> -q -p no:randomly', and it also failed inside a full 'just check' run. It fails on a stashed, unmodified tree, so it is not caused by the in-flight test-file split that found it.

Symptom: the lazy worker does run (the test's wait_for on 'calls' passes), but pane._entry_by_name('nvim').latest is still LatestInfo(checked=False, version=None) instead of the fetched '2.0.0'.

Root cause: phase sase-qn.2 (664180532) added _apply_plugin_latest in src/sase/ace/tui/modals/plugins_browser_latest.py, which rewrites self._catalog and self._grouped with the enriched entry. Phase sase-qn.4 (41d9f9141) then added the name-keyed identity map self._plugin_entry_by_name, built only in _rebuild_plugin_identity_maps (src/sase/ace/tui/modals/plugins_browser_rendering.py:212-231) and read by _entry_by_name (line 587). _apply_plugin_latest never refreshes that map, so the map keeps the pre-enrichment entry.

Impact is user-visible, not test-only: _current_entry -> _entry_by_name (line 585) feeds _render_detail_now, so the Updates > Plugins detail panel re-renders from the stale entry after a lazy fetch completes and never shows the fetched latest version while the plugin_catalog_scoped_latest flag is on. Fix belongs with phase sase-qn.5's close-out: have _apply_plugin_latest update _plugin_entry_by_name (and any sibling identity map keyed on the replaced entry) alongside _catalog and _grouped.

description:
`tests/ace/tui/modals/test_project_inventory_subtabs.py::test_cross_navigation_and_escape_surface_disabled_workspaces` failed once under the parallel scoped/`just check` lane and passed on a serial rerun of the same tree.

OBSERVED on 2026-08-18 while implementing the Current Project glossary term (sase.yml + generated instruction files only; no ACE/TUI, Projects-tab, or current-project code touched). `just check` in workspace sase_13 escalated to a 33832-item parallel run (`pytest -n 10 --dist=worksteal`): `2 failed, 33830 passed, 13 skipped, 72 warnings in 538.48s`. This node ran on gw0.

EXACT FAILURE (tests/ace/tui/modals/test_project_inventory_subtabs.py:294):
    pane.query_one("#projects-list", OptionList).highlighted = 1
    await pilot.press("w")
    workspace_pane = pane.query_one(WorkspaceInventoryPane)
    assert pane._active_subtab == "workspaces"
    assert workspace_pane.project_filter == "beta"
    E           AssertionError: assert 'alpha' == 'beta'

notes.author: sase-qd.land
notes.text: Root-caused and fixed during the sase-qd epic landing; the hypothesis in this report (first-open seed racing the highlighted row) was close but not the mechanism. Real cause: sase-qd.2 (commit ec048b168) replaced the seed-only current-project worker with a display resolve whose completion handler called ProjectsPane._refresh_options() with no preferred project. _refresh_options prefers _session_state.projects.identity (the bookmark) over the live OptionList.highlighted, and OptionHighlighted reaches the pane only after bubbling out of the option list's own message queue -- so a resolve posted straight to the pane can overtake it and repaint from the stale bookmark, snapping the highlight back to index 0 (alpha). This is a real user-facing regression, not only a test artifact: the same window exists on mount, on R, and after a successful c set. Fix: _apply_current_project_display now repaints through _repaint_for_current_project(), which passes preferred_project=self._selected_project_name(), mirroring what the inventory worker's completion handler already did. Verified: the node failed 4/12 serial runs before the fix and passed 15/15 after; added tests/ace/tui/test_projects_pane_current_project_seed.py::test_resolve_repaint_keeps_a_row_the_bookmark_has_not_caught_up_to, which fails on the pre-fix tree (highlighted 0 != 1) and passes after; also stubbed resolve_current_project in this module's _patch_inventory_data so the suite no longer reads the developer's real MRU. No baseline entry was needed.

title: test_fresh_heartbeat_is_not_reclaimed fails under the full parallel lane: a 0.2s stale window cannot survive holder starvation
close_reason: Fixed by 569d4257b 'fix: stabilize process concurrency closeout' (2026-08-20), which removed the mechanism entirely: the test no longer runs a starved subprocess heartbeat loop against a 0.2s stale window -- it writes heartbeat=90.0 into the token metadata and passes stale_timeout=30.0 (tests/test_suite_gate_reclaim.py:197-222). tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt records '# sase-qp: retired by sase-rm.11 ... injected deterministic clock' with '# fixed-at: 2026-08-20T19:59:23Z'. The one later +1 is a forwarded sase-ri.4 observation from a pre-fix tree. 'tools/selection_health --fail-on-new-flake' exits 0 on 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
`tests/test_suite_gate.py::test_fresh_heartbeat_is_not_reclaimed` failed once under
`just check`'s escalated parallel lane and passed five consecutive serial reruns on the
identical tree.

OBSERVED on 2026-08-18 while landing epic sase-qd (Projects-tab current project) in
workspace sase_15. The diff under test touched only
`src/sase/ace/tui/modals/projects_pane.py` and two ACE test modules -- nothing in
`tests/_suite_gate*.py` or the pytest gate machinery. `just check` escalated to a full
parallel run: `1 failed, 33845 passed, 13 skipped, 72 warnings in 452.92s`.

FAILURE: `tests/test_suite_gate.py:745` -- `AssertionError` (the run reports it
truncated as `Asse...`); the test wraps its acquire in
`pytest.raises(pytest.UsageError, match="heartbeat")`, so the failure is that the
competing acquire did NOT raise, i.e. the holder was reclaimed when the test asserts it
must not be.

NOT REPRODUCED SERIALLY: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:randomly -p no:xdist -q
tests/test_suite_gate.py::test_fresh_heartbeat_is_not_reclaimed` passed 5/5 on the same
tree (4.06s, then 2.57s / 2.43s / 2.48s / 2.46s).

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE (read from the test, not measured): the test spawns a subprocess that
holds a `WorkerTokenLease` and calls `record_lease_progress('session')` in a `time.sleep(0.02)`
loop, then asserts a competing
`_lease(tmp_path, budget=1, timeout=0.35, stale_timeout=0.2).acquire(...)` raises rather
than reclaiming. The negative assertion only holds while the holder's heartbeat stays
fresher than a 200 ms stale window. Under a ~33.8k-test `pytest -n <N> --dist=worksteal`
run the holder subprocess can be descheduled past 200 ms, its grant looks stale, the
waiter reclaims it, `acquire` succeeds, and no `UsageError` is raised. The 20 ms
heartbeat cadence leaves only a 10x margin against CPU starvation, which a saturated
host erases.

INTRODUCED BY: f7e6acbf6 "fix(tests): reclaim wedged suite-gate worker-token grants"
(closes sase-q2), the commit that added heartbeat-based reclamation and this test.

SUGGESTED FIX: make the negative assertion independent of wall-clock scheduling --
drive the staleness decision from an injected clock or an explicitly written heartbeat
timestamp rather than a real 0.2s window, or widen `stale_timeout` far enough that a
descheduled holder cannot cross it. Prefer that over baselining: this node guards a real
safety property (a live holder must never be reclaimed), so a baselined entry would hide
regressions in the reclaim rule itself.

VERIFY WITH: `just test-contention -- tests/test_suite_gate.py`, repeated, expecting
green; then a full `just check-full`.

notes.text: LANDING RECONCILIATION (epic sase-qn, 2026-08-19): the flag stays kind=beta / default off, and this is a recorded decision, not an oversight. The scoped O(installed) eager-enrichment path and the lazy highlighted-row fetch are fully implemented and tested in both states; tests/perf/check_plugin_catalog_scale_regression.py enforces the scoped curve (fetch_calls = installed_count = 5 at n=1000 and n=2000, and a linear enrich scan_work ceiling) through 'just plugin-catalog-scale-check' and the CI perf-floors job. Phase sase-qn.5 proposed converting beta -> sunset so scoped enrichment would be default-on; the land agent verified that is not currently possible: 'sase bead update' exposes only -b/--remove-by for a flag bead (no kind mutation), the registry-derived default is not independently settable, and flipping only the registry would fail sase.feature_flags.integrity with code=kind_mismatch. No separate task bead was filed for that conversion because this bead already owns the outcome: FlagTriage's Remove branch (delete the Off branch, make the On branch unconditional) achieves default-on scoped enrichment directly, which is the same end state. Until then the default remains the pre-scale full-eager path, so a 1000+ entry catalog still issues one PyPI probe per uninstalled entry unless a user opts in.

title: test_launcher_qualifies_research_swarm_per_dispatch fails deterministically after tests/test_launch_planned_agent_name.py in the same process
close_reason: Fixed by 569d4257b 'fix: stabilize process concurrency closeout' (2026-08-20): 'test name-registry cache resets across isolated SASE_HOME roots.' The leaked process-global state the bead hunted is now cleared by reset_name_registry_caches_for_tests() (src/sase/agent/names/_registry.py:426-435), which clears _CACHE_PATH/_CACHE_SIGNATURE/_CACHE_DATA plus the registry scan caches, the freshness token, and the config cache; test_launcher_qualifies_research_swarm_per_dispatch calls it at line 324. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f by running the bead's deterministic two-file repro: '.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_launch_planned_agent_name.py tests/test_multi_prompt_launcher_xprompt_groups.py -p no:randomly -q' -> 15 passed in 4.10s.
description:
`tests/test_multi_prompt_launcher_xprompt_groups.py::test_launcher_qualifies_research_swarm_per_dispatch`
fails deterministically whenever it runs in the same process after
`tests/test_launch_planned_agent_name.py` or `tests/test_launch_planned_bead_work.py`.
The second `#!research_swarm` dispatch keeps allocating `research.0` instead of
advancing to `research.1`, so `launch_agents_from_cwd` raises
`AgentNameLaunchCollisionError: Agent name 'research.0.cdx' is taken.`

The test writes a real agent for `research.0.cdx` between the two dispatches and clears
`sase.agent.names._registry._CACHE_PATH/_CACHE_SIGNATURE/_CACHE_DATA`, so some *other*
process-global cache consulted by the `{@1}` swarm-index allocation still holds a view
in which `research.0` is free after one of those two files has run. That state survives
into the tmp `SASE_HOME` the test installs, which is the leak to find.

Found while splitting `src/sase/main/project_handler.py` into modules: that diff changed
only which tests the diff-scoped lane co-schedules, and the failure reproduces on a
clean `master` tree (e395acd4c) with the two-file command, so it is not caused by that
change.

notes.text: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: bug (high severity, pre-existing, unrelated to this phase) — sase-core v0.29.1 (commit 6169e0e "feat(provider_disable): add hard/soft mode to the disable wire") inserted a new `mode: str = "hard"` positional-or-keyword parameter before `duration_seconds`/`now` in provider_disable_set_relative, provider_disable_set_until, provider_disable_try_set_relative, and provider_disable_try_set_until, and bumped PROVIDER_DISABLE_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION 1->2. src/sase/llm_provider/provider_disable.py still calls these bindings with the old positional argument order (disable_provider_until:174, try_disable_provider:193-199, try_disable_provider:154 via disable_provider) so a float/None now lands in the "mode" slot and every call raises `TypeError: argument mode: ... cannot be converted to PyString`. notes.author: sase-qy.1
notes.text: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: Justfile _refresh-sase-core-checkout (line ~837) SASE_ALLOW_STALE_CORE=1 guard is a no-op -- each @-prefixed recipe line runs as its own subshell in just, so the guard's `exit 0` only ends that one line, not the recipe; the fetch+fast-forward on the next line always runs regardless of the env var. Reproduced directly: `env SASE_ALLOW_STALE_CORE=1 just _refresh-sase-core-checkout` still fast-forwards the linked sase-core checkout. Same broken pattern is duplicated at rust-install (~868-877) and rust-dev-install (~929-936). Workaround used during this phase: check out the linked sase-core repo as a detached HEAD (refresh_clean_linked_checkout skips detached checkouts) instead of relying on the env var. Fix: restructure each guard into a single shell invocation, e.g. `@if [ \"${SASE_ALLOW_STALE_CORE:-}\" != 1 ]; then just ... _refresh-...; fi` on one line, so the skip actually short-circuits the recipe. Discovered while investigating a since-independently-fixed provider_disable wire-schema-2 break (commit 4d945b1cd already landed for that separate issue).

title: Separate create-refusal text from when_to_use for non-agent-creatable types
close_reason: Fixed: task-type specs now carry explicit create_refusal copy that wins over when_to_use. _agent_create_refusal_message (src/sase/task_types/fields.py:73-87) prefers spec['create_refusal'] and only falls back to when_to_use, and the builtin feature type supplies one (src/sase/task_types/_builtin.py:158). The contradiction the bead reported -- an invitation printed after 'cannot be created by agents' -- can no longer occur for feature. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
`resolve_created_task_type()` in `src/sase/task_types/fields.py` appends the type's `when_to_use` after "cannot be created by agents" when `agent_creatable` is false.

That reads as a contradiction for a type whose `when_to_use` is an invitation (the builtin `feature` type: "File one when you discovered a product or capability idea..."). `flag` avoids the contradiction only because its `when_to_use` is deliberately written as the refusal explanation.

Discovered while implementing the approved plan `sase/repos/plans/202608/feature_task_type_scoping.md`, which suppresses `feature` with `agent_creatable: false` for every non-sase project. An agent that ignored its instruction note and ran `sase bead create -T task(feature)` would then see the invitation text after the refusal.

Out of scope for that plan: improving the message means giving the spec a separate refusal field, which is a larger schema-and-wording change.

task_type_fields.proposal: Give a task-type spec an optional refusal field (separate from `when_to_use`) and have `resolve_created_task_type()` print that text after "cannot be created by agents". Keep `flag`'s current when_to_use-as-refusal behavior as the fallback so existing types do not break.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The approved feature-scoping plan only disables creating `feature` beads outside the sase project. Changing the create-refusal message needs a new spec key, Rust validator/digest work, and wording for every type whose when_to_use is an invitation rather than a refusal.

description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-qv.1 (epic sase-qv, "Required custom monitor statuses with
deterministic pair colors"), routed here by that epic's land agent. Not caused by
sase-qv: the diff under test was src/sase/monitor_status.py + src/sase/palette_hash.py
plus monitor read paths; nothing in it touches linked-repo setup or workspace occupancy.

OBSERVATION (2026-08-19T13:58:08Z, phase sase-qv.1): three nodes in
tests/test_run_agent_runner_setup_linked_repos.py failed together in an escalated
parallel full suite with WorkspaceOccupiedError naming workspace #0 as "occupied by this
agent", then all three passed on a serial rerun of the same tree:

  - test_prepare_linked_repo_workspaces_uses_default_revision_sentinel
  - test_prepare_linked_repo_workspaces_prepares_retained_sidecar
  - test_prepare_linked_repo_workspaces_failure_names_workspace

ROOT CAUSE (identified by code reading during sase-qv landing, 2026-08-19):
prepare_linked_repo_workspaces_if_needed (src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner_setup.py:157)
declares primary_workspace_dir: str = "" and workspace_num: int = 0, and after
materializing each repo it calls the production occupancy guard
_guard_workspace_not_occupied(checkout_dir=primary_workspace_dir, ...) at
run_agent_runner_setup.py:215. These three tests call the function with only
resolution= and cl_name=, and they patch sase.linked_repos.materialize_linked_repo_workspace
and sase.axe.run_agent_runner_setup.prepare_workspace -- but NOT the guard. So the guard
runs for real with checkout_dir="" and workspace_num=0.

Path("").resolve() is the process cwd, which under pytest is the agent's own sase_<N>
workspace checkout. Verified live on 2026-08-19 from workspace sase_14:

  Path("").resolve() -> /home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_14

so ensure_workspace_not_occupied() reads the live host occupant marker for the very
workspace the test process is running in, and workspace_num=0 is where the "#0" in the
error text comes from. Whether these tests pass therefore depends on ambient host
occupancy state at the moment they run, not on the tree under test. That also explains
the serial-rerun pass: the host's occupant record for that checkout differed by then.
The same probe run today returns no conflict, which is why the nodes are green right now
(12 passed in 3.11s for the whole file).

WHY THIS IS NEW: WorkspaceOccupiedError / ensure_workspace_not_occupied landed recently
(7a2906e13, the sase-q0 "guarantee one agent per workspace" work, ~2026-08-18). Before
that guard existed this call path had no ambient-state read, so these tests were
hermetic. This is a fresh test-isolation regression, not the process-global-state-leak
class that epic sase-j7 owns: nothing leaks between tests here, the test reads real host
state directly.

title: test_workflow_step_has_no_kind_heading[parallel] fails: cheap header omits Step line

description:
## CI failure

- **Node:** `tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_agent_display_kind_headers.py::test_workflow_step_has_no_kind_heading[parallel]`

Failed twice on the same tree: once in an escalated full `just check` lane (34921 passed, 1 failed) and again in isolation with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_agent_display_kind_headers.py::test_workflow_step_has_no_kind_heading -q --tb=short`. The `bash` and `python` parametrizations pass; only `[parallel]` fails.

The cheap header for a parallel workflow child is `Name: unassigned\nPatch: test_cl\nTimestamps: ...` and does not contain `Step: do\n`. `_append_project_fields` in `src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/prompt_panel/_agent_display_header_metadata.py` emits the Step line only when `agent.step_type in {"bash", "python"}`. Parallel children fall through to the Patch/Name branch. The test parametrizes `["bash", "python", "parallel"]` and asserts `"Step: do\n"` for all three.

Either include `parallel` in that Step-line guard, or drop `parallel` from the parametrization if cheap parallel headers are intentionally patch/name-only. Unrelated to the Memory panel split that triggered the check.

title: Justfile SASE_ALLOW_STALE_CORE guard is a no-op across recipe lines
close_reason: Fixed by b76f53b99 'fix: repair guardrails for provider docs and proc imports'. Justfile:810-816 now joins the SASE_ALLOW_STALE_CORE early-exit and the refresh_linked_checkout call into one continued recipe line, and rust-install (840-842) gates the _refresh-sase-core-checkout delegation on the same variable instead of relying on a cross-line exit. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
description:
## Bug

- **Location:** `Justfile` recipe `_refresh-sase-core-checkout` (around the
  `SASE_ALLOW_STALE_CORE=1` guard), with the same broken pattern duplicated in
  `rust-install` and `rust-dev-install`.

Each `@`-prefixed recipe line runs as its own subshell in just, so

```just
@if [ "${SASE_ALLOW_STALE_CORE:-}" = "1" ]; then \
    exit 0; \
fi
@"{{ venv_bin }}/python" .../tools/refresh_linked_checkout ...
```

does not skip the fetch. The `exit 0` only ends that one line. Reproduced

actually short-circuits the recipe.

notes.author: sase-v2.land
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE: root cause for the missing .venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp reports on this epic (notes #2, #3, #4, #5, #6). Justfile's `rust-lsp-install` recipe builds with a bare `cargo build --release -p sase_xprompt_lsp` that does NOT pin CARGO_TARGET_DIR, so on any host whose ~/.cargo/config.toml sets `[build] target-dir` the binary lands there instead of under the checkout. The recipe then copies from the hard-coded `{{ sase_core_dir }}/target/release/sase-xprompt-lsp`, which never exists on such a host. Because that recipe body chains with ';' rather than '&&', the failed cp does not stop the recipe: it still prints '[rust-lsp-install] installed <dest>' and exits 0, so `just install` reports success while .venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp keeps whatever stale copy was there.

REPRODUCED 2026-08-28 in workspace sase_26 while landing epic sase-v2. `just install` printed:
  cp: cannot stat '<ws>/sase/repos/linked/sase-core/target/release/sase-xprompt-lsp': No such file or directory
  chmod: cannot access '<venv>/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp.tmp.2820361': No such file or directory
  mv: cannot stat '<venv>/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp.tmp.2820361': No such file or directory
  [rust-lsp-install] installed <venv>/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp
and still exited 0. Evidence: ~/.cargo/config.toml has `[build] target-dir = "/mnt/poseidon/cargo-target"`; `<ws>/sase/repos/linked/sase-core/target` does not exist; the freshly built binary is at /mnt/poseidon/cargo-target/release/sase-xprompt-lsp (mtime 2026-08-28 10:51, this run); .venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp was left at its stale 2026-08-26 08:27 copy. A fresh workspace with no prior copy is exactly the missing-binary case reported in notes #2-#6.

CONTRAST: the sibling `rust-dev-install` recipe does not have this bug — it exports CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$sase_core_abs/target/uv-tool-lsp" before building, so its cp source is correct by construction.

SUGGESTED FIX: pin CARGO_TARGET_DIR in `rust-lsp-install` the way `rust-dev-install` does (or resolve the real path with `cargo metadata --format-version 1`), and chain the cp/chmod/mv with '&&' so a failed install cannot report success. Not caused by epic sase-v2; routed here because this epic already owns the xprompt LSP install-path issue. No standalone task created.

description:
## CI failure

- **Node:** `src/sase/telemetry/catalog.py`

`just check` fails at `lint (ruff)` with F601 (`Dictionary key literal "sase_finalizer" repeated`) on HEAD `f355faa96`. This is a static duplicate dict key, so it fails on every tree that contains both insertions; it is not timing- or order-dependent.

Two closed-phase landings independently added the same catalog mapping:

- `980bedfea` (`sase-rr.1`) inserted `"sase_finalizer": "Finalizers"` into `_PREFIX_TO_SUBSYSTEM` and `"Finalizers"` into `SUBSYSTEM_ORDER`.
- `f4fde13df` (`sase-ru.5`) inserted the same key and the same `SUBSYSTEM_ORDER` label again at the end of each collection.

Python keeps the last dict entry, and both values are identical, so runtime grouping is unchanged. Ruff F601 has no autofix. This project sets `commit_hooks.before: just fix`, and `just fix` runs `ruff check --fix src/ tests/`, so every `sase stitch create` fails until the duplicate key is removed.

`SUBSYSTEM_ORDER` also lists `"Finalizers"` twice (not an F601, but the same double-insert). Delete the later copies from `f4fde13df` and keep the `sase-rr.1` placement.

### Repro

```bash
.venv/bin/ruff check src/sase/telemetry/catalog.py
```

title: Glossary "Proc Shell" still says a proc shell belongs to an agent, but sase-s6 shipped stand-alone xprompt-proc proc shells
description:
The `Proc Shell` glossary definition still says a proc shell belongs to a sase agent.
Epic sase-s6 (`typed_launch_units`, phases sase-s6.5 and sase-s6.7) made that false.

Current definition, in `sase/sase.yml` under `glossary.terms.Proc Shell` (the canonical
source that `sase memory init` renders into `sase/memory/glossary.md`):

> A proc shell is a named supervised proc belonging to a sase agent, with durable
> output and lifecycle state. A family-attached proc shell is a monitor and may carry
> timeout, workspace-claim, and follow-up policy.

What shipped instead: a `%proc` launch unit is stored as lifecycle `proc-shell` with
origin `xprompt-proc` (`src/sase/agent/launch_proc_runtime.py`,
`src/sase/procs/service.py`). It belongs to no agent, is never nested under a family,
allocates no agent runner or agent artifact, and is projected into the Agents tab as its
own row kind counted separately from agents
(`src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_proc_shells.py`; the Agents-tab header renders
`N agents · M procs`).

Verify with:

```bash
sase glossary read "Proc Shell" -r "check whether stand-alone proc shells are covered"
grep -n "belonging to a sase agent" sase/sase.yml
grep -rn "XPROMPT_PROC_ORIGIN" src/sase/procs/ src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_proc_shells.py
```

Proposed change: reword the definition so it covers both an agent-owned proc shell (the
monitor case, which keeps the family-attached sentence) and a stand-alone
`xprompt-proc` proc shell dispatched by a `%proc` launch unit, or split the two into
related terms. Keep `Sase Monitor` accurate as the family-attached specialization.

Closing this requires explicit user permission for the memory edit, then editing
`sase/sase.yml` and running `sase memory init` to regenerate `AGENTS.md`, the provider
instruction shims, and `sase/memory/glossary.md`; `sase memory init --check` must be
clean afterwards.

PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-s6.8 (epic sase-s6). Not edited during the epic because no
explicit user permission for a memory-file edit was given in those conversations.

task_type_fields.proposed_change: Reword the "Proc Shell" glossary definition (or split it into related terms) so it covers both agent-owned monitor proc shells and stand-alone xprompt-proc proc shells that belong to no agent, then run sase memory init.

description:

Agent `sase-s9.2` (run `20260823120149`) implemented its phase in full, then never

monitor and returned. Six consecutive "I'll wait for the background task" replies

This is not caused by epic sase-s9 (procs tab query filtering); it is a general

title: Give the conflict-repair turn the same recovery evidence brief
description:
## Feature proposal

Give the conflict-repair turn (`src/sase/finalizers/commit_repair.py`) the same
host-authored evidence brief that declaration recovery now receives: original prompt
head, response tail, dirty-path provenance from the run-start baseline, and the
`tool_calls.jsonl` write list. The repair turn currently invokes the provider the same
context-free way (fresh session, empty window). Conflict markers in the files make it
more self-orienting than declaration recovery was, but it still has no original prompt,
no response, and no provenance.

This is the same structural blind spot as plan:202608/finalizer_recovery_evidence.md,
