title: Python and Rust flat query parsers build different AndExpr operand orders, so the parity suite cannot assert parse-AST equality
description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-s9.6 (epic sase-s9, "Procs tab query filtering") on
2026-08-23T13:38:31Z as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP, verified and routed here by that epic's
land agent (sase-s9.land).

NOT CAUSED BY sase-s9. That epic's `rust` phase added parity tests, and those tests are
what exposed this; the divergence itself predates the epic and reproduces on fields the
epic never touched (see the Stitches case in the reproduction).

The two implementations of the shared flat query grammar build different `AndExpr`
operand orders for the same multi-field input. Python's flat parser emits field terms in
compiled-profile order (effectively sorted by key), while the Rust flat parser in
`sase-core` emits them in first-seen clause order. Canonicalization already agrees, and
`AND` evaluation is order-independent, so no user-visible behavior differs today.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: the stated contract for this grammar is that both implementations
are byte-identical, and the parity suite in
`tests/test_query_profile_corpus_facade.py` cannot assert parse-AST equality for any
multi-field query while this holds. That leaves a permanent hole in the exact test that
is supposed to catch future Python/Rust grammar drift, which is the whole reason the
`rust` mirror phase exists.

SCOPE: pick one order as canonical and make both parsers emit it, then extend the
parity parameters in `tests/test_query_profile_corpus_facade.py` to assert full
parse-AST equality (not just canonical-form equality) for multi-field queries.
Sorted-by-key is the likelier choice since Python already does it and the canonical
string is already sorted, but that is a call for whoever works this. The Rust half
lands in the linked `sase-core` repo (open it with `/sase_repo`); per
`docs/rust_backend.md` the release lane owns the `sase-core-rs` floor bump in this repo.

links.description: Proposed as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP by phase sase-s9.6 while porting the flat grammar to Rust; the epic's parity tests are what exposed the divergence, and extending those tests is part of the fix

task_type_fields.impact:
## Impact

No user-visible effect today: canonical form matches, cache keys are keyed on the
canonical string, and `AND` evaluation is commutative.

The cost is to the safety net. `tests/test_query_profile_corpus_facade.py` is the
designated guard against Python/Rust flat-grammar drift, and it currently has to
compare canonical strings rather than parse ASTs for any query with more than one
field term. A future divergence in how one side builds its AST -- operand nesting,
negation placement, a dropped term -- would pass that suite as long as the canonical
strings happened to agree.
task_type_fields.repro:
## Reproduction

Verified at master HEAD 062ae22c2 in workspace sase_12 with sase-core-rs 0.31.7
installed (the release that contains sase-core commit aeefa36, the sase-s9.6 port).

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
from sase.ace.query_profile import compile_query_profile
from sase.ace.query_profile.profiles import stitches_query_schema
from sase.ace.query.profile_reference import parse_query_for_profile
from sase.core import query_profile_corpus_facade as f

p = compile_query_profile(stitches_query_schema())
for q in ("repo:x author:y", "author:y repo:x"):
    py = parse_query_for_profile(q, p)
    rs = f._parse_artifact_query(q, p)
    print(q, "| EQUAL:", py == rs)
    print("   PY:", [o.key for o in py.operands])
    print("   RS:", [o.key for o in rs.operands])
EOF
```

Observed:

```
repo:x author:y | EQUAL: False
   PY: ['author', 'repo']
   RS: ['repo', 'author']
author:y repo:x | EQUAL: True
   PY: ['author', 'repo']
   RS: ['author', 'repo']
```

Equality holds only when the input happens to already be in the Python order. The
`procs` profile shows the same thing on the epic's own bound keys -- `min:30s max:2h`
gives Python `[max, min]` and Rust `[min, max]` -- while
`canonical_query_for_profile` returns `max:7200 min:30` for both, confirming the
divergence is confined to the parse AST.

Note the Stitches case uses `repo:`/`author:`, two long-standing fields with no
relationship to the bare-boolean or bound-key extensions, which is what establishes
that this predates epic sase-s9.

description: Free-text xprompt arguments survive prose that contains `]]`, `+`, commas, and apostrophes; the `[[...]]` text-block rule has one authoritative definition that every Python and Rust argument scanner shares; and a failed xprompt argument binding reports itself once, accurately, instead of leaking a stray error from a best-effort diagnostic and then failing later with an unrelated directive error.

notes.author: sase-sn.land
notes.text:
Verified all six phases against the source and their commits (4d0da0d4b sase-sn.2, d0ea16ef8 sase-sn.3, 6ca6e798e sase-sn.1, ec76ec6ef sase-sn.4, 1907346f8 sase-sn.6 in sase; 1d3c9c6 sase-sn.5 and 81f114a sase-sn.6 in sase-core). sase-sn.2 had only an auto-close note with no verification claimed, so I read the code directly: processor.py binds `#name: text`, `#name:: text`, and `#name(args): text` through _consume_trailing_shorthand_text (paren form appends positionally, as the plan recommended), and preprocess_shorthand_syntax is gone from the expansion path but retained for the three detection-only callers. Reproduced the original defect end to end on this tree: the shorthand round-trip and the structural reference path both bind 1 positional (was 10), C++/A+B survive, and extract_static_clan_directive returns a clean StaticClanDirective on a %clan(..., summary=[[...prose with ]]...]]) segment that previously raised DirectiveError. find_text_block_close_for_args and its Rust twin (crates/sase_core/src/xprompt_text_block.rs) implement the same terminator rule and back all three Python scanners plus ArgScanner, QuoteState, and the agent-launch parsers; decode narrowing verified at every call site including workflow_validator_extract (colon-kind only) and parse_workflow_reference. 243 targeted tests pass.

INTEGRATION. Reviewed every non-epic commit since the first epic commit (bac22b968, 5dc897395, abefcc4fb, 4041c17e4, f7595ad53 in sase; 8d51bd8, afd1f87 in sase-core). Two real gaps found and fixed as epic work:

1. pyproject.toml still allowed sase-core-rs>=0.31.0, but the epic's Rust parity only shipped in 0.31.11. Epic sase-so (sase-so.1/8d51bd8, sase-so.2) now routes real clan summaries through the Rust format_clan_directive/plan_typed_launch_units text-block round trip, so a fresh install resolving 0.31.0 would still hit the original DirectiveError. Ratcheted the floor to >=0.31.11,<0.32.0 and relocked uv.lock, matching the convention in d61f3bbc6/959d55926. Confirmed the published 0.31.11 wheel parses `summary=[[...]]` containing `]]` and `+` correctly.

2. docs/xprompt.md's residual-ambiguity paragraph (written by sase-sn.6) was wrong about its own example: #name([[foo]]]]) binds `foo]]` correctly, because only the final `]]` sits in terminator position. The real residual ambiguity is a content `]]` followed by a terminator (#name([[a]], b]]) binds two args). Rewrote the paragraph and verified the documented quoted-argument workaround actually works for both positional and named values.

No other conflict found: abefcc4fb/4041c17e4 carry clan_summary as structured wire metadata rather than parsing text, and the sase-core parity commit landed after 8d51bd8, so the typed-launch path was already covered (typed_launch_clan_summary_ignores_inner_text_block_marker and _keeps_unbalanced_inner_closer).

FOLLOW-UPS. Three PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP entries (two on sase-sn.5, one on sase-sn.6) plus the epic plan's two out-of-scope items were triaged into three ready task beads, after searching and sweeping all task beads and reviewing the 21 in-progress epics for causal links; none were duplicates.
- sase-sr (bug, large): the sase-sn.5 dialect-divergence note merged with the plan's "unbalanced apostrophes" and "nested parentheses" out-of-scope items. These are one defect with one remediation -- a shared quoting/nesting rule across all six scanners -- so filing them separately would have been three views of the same fix. Evidence: %clan(research.x, summary=don't stop, tribe=research) raises DirectiveError in Python but parses correctly through plan_typed_launch_units in Rust.
- sase-ss (bug, small): the sase-sn.5 note that axe_chop validate_literal_clan_summary still rejects `+` (now provably obsolete, since text blocks are no longer + decoded) and that editor colon_arg_context aborts on `+`. Recorded that the sibling `]]` guard is still partly needed and should be narrowed rather than dropped. Linked related to sase-so and sase-rj.
- sase-st (memory, small): the sase-sn.6 request to document the closing rule in sase/memory/xprompts.md, with proposed wording. Not applied here: memory edits require the project owner's explicit permission in the requesting conversation plus sase memory init.

VERIFICATION. just check green end to end, with the scoped lane escalating to the full suite (rules: contract-set-only, core-identity-changed, packaging-config). One environmental note, not epic work and already owned: building sase_core_rs from the linked sase-core checkout at HEAD fails tools/validate_sase_core_rs because afd1f87 ships finalizer_wire_schema_version 2 while this repo still pins 1. That is epic sase-sp's core commit outrunning its own in-progress Python phase sase-sp.2 ("Adopt the released core floor and the deferral config schema"), so I filed nothing and ran the gates against the published 0.31.11 wheel instead -- which is the configuration the floor bump actually needs to prove. sase bead epic-symbols sase-sn reports no entries.

plan input schema_version 1; expected 2". See the note on epic sase-sp for the
full sequencing diagnosis. The minimum needed to make the tree launchable was
landed directly; the rest of your phase is untouched and still yours.

ALREADY DONE in commit 7b7452504 (do not redo):

- src/sase/core/finalizer_wire.py: FINALIZER_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION 1 -> 2.
- tools/validate_sase_core_rs: the finalizer contract probe now pins one named
  EXPECTED_FINALIZER_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2 instead of the eight bare `1`

  versioned the host-to-plugin envelope with the *core wire* constant, so
  bumping the core wire would have rejected every installed `sase_finalizers`

  envelope at all (its fields are operation/provider_ref/status/payload, none

  holds FINALIZER_PROVIDER_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1; executor_protocol.py, sdk.py,

  hard-coded `1` in their own failure envelopes, so they would have drifted

  Plugin behavior is unchanged, which is what this phase requires: the
  reference plugin fixture tests/fixtures/finalizer_plugin/example_finalizers.py
  still stamps `1` and still passes untouched.

Verification: all 368 finalizer tests pass, tools/validate_sase_core_rs is
clean, and resolve_and_persist_finalizer_plan resolves a schema-2 plan.

2450497bb, which is why it has no commit of its own. The sase-core half of wire landed
separately as 151a37d and is published as v0.32.3 (c0958b0).

Spot-read the actual code rather than trusting the notes:
- sase-core crates/sase_core/src/glossary.rs declares GLOSSARY_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2
  with source_path / key_path / keyword_range / body_range and serde aliases for every
  v1 name, so a v1-shaped payload still deserializes.
- memory/web/catalog.py::glossary_source_from_wire is the single tolerant reader and

- roster.py's inline branch now derives Rust display_aliases via strand_glossary_catalog,
  md_escapes keyword and aliases, and wraps at markdown_print_width(); the list branch is
  untouched.
- glossary_catalog.py::_load_editor_glossary_catalog and init_memory/glossary.py::
  load_project_glossary_terms both route through glossary_dual_source_diagnostic, so the
  fail-closed dual-truth rule is one predicate used by both, exactly as planned.
- The planned deletions are gone from src/ and tests/: _glossary_collision_blocker,
  _retired_glossary_note_paths, is_generated_glossary_memory_content, and the
  GENERATED_GLOSSARY_MARKER_* / sase_generated: glossary marker.
- No epic test is marked contract and tests/contract_manifest.txt is untouched by any
  epic commit, so the release-core-floor-smoke job cannot see a v2-only assertion.

Proved the migration end to end rather than re-reading its tests:
- sase/sase.yml has no memory.glossary; sase/memory/glossary/ holds 39 strands;
  sase/memory/glossary.md is the user-owned descriptor (type: core, web: true,
  roster: inline, GLOSSARY TERMS, strand_noun: term, closure: mentions).
- git show df956212b -- sase/memory/glossary.md confirms the plan's central acceptance
  criterion: the **GLOSSARY TERMS:** block is byte-identical across the migration; only
  frontmatter and the preamble's command name changed.
- find_memory_web + memory_web_glossary_entries return 39 entries whose source_path is
  the strand file and whose keyword_range points at the keyword: frontmatter line, so
  editor go-to-definition lands on a real Markdown note.
- sase memory read glossary:stitch and sase glossary read Stitch produce the same closure
  and bodies; sase glossary read/list print their one-line deprecation notice on stderr
  and delegate. sase memory web list shows glossary with 39 strands.
- bob-cli: verified through a sase repo open checkout. The migration landed on
  origin/master as 79b5dba with 4 strands, the memory.glossary block removed, and its
  roster line byte-identical; sase memory init --check is clean against that tree. The
  local primary bob-cli checkout is simply behind origin, which is not epic work.
- sase memory init --check is clean here, and just validate passes every SASE gate,
  which retires phase sase-sq.7.1.1's 'home memory init drift' PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP.

INTEGRATED (step 2). Reviewed all 21 non-epic commits since af27e67e0. None conflict with
or duplicate this epic: 9c7c10aa2 and 69dc50a31 touch xprompt/ACE but not the glossary
catalog, and the rest are test splits, axe/ACE fixes, or bead refactors. One real
interaction found and resolved: f7aa438ba had duplicated _combine_mutation_outcomes into
two bead submixins to clear a symvision finding, and e7eafd0ec later replaced that with a

one 414-character line: the template preamble is unwrapped and the generated-note path
used to wrap it via format_generated_memory_markdown, but migrate.py dropped that step.

fits the print width. Not fixed: reflowing bob-cli's already-committed
sase/memory/glossary.md, because editing a sase/memory/*.md note needs the owner's
explicit permission, which this turn does not carry. It is cosmetic only - bob-cli runs
no prettier gate and the managed roster region is unaffected.

- home memory init drift (7.1.1 n1): resolved; just validate is green.

  Recorded as evidence on sase-so.5.1, the active phase bead that owns the ratchet,

title: Python and Rust xprompt argument scanners still disagree on quoting, escapes, and bracket nesting
description:
Six xprompt/directive argument scanners implement overlapping but divergent
dialects of one grammar. Epic sase-sn unified only the `[[...]]` text-block
closing rule and the `+`-to-space decoding across them, and deliberately left
quoting, escape handling, and bracket nesting divergent (see the epic plan's
"Out of scope" section and the PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note on sase-sn.5). The
result is that the launcher, the ACE editor, the LSP diagnostics, and the
fan-out planner can still each reach a different conclusion about the same
prompt.

Verified divergence (2026-08-24, sase master 1907346f8, sase-core-rs 0.31.11):
Rust parses a bare apostrophe in a `%clan` argument correctly; Python raises.

Single quotes: Python `_top_level_delimiter_positions` and
`_find_matching_delimiter_for_args` treat `'` as a string quote even in free
prose; the Rust `agent_launch` parsers track only backtick and `"`. An
unbalanced `'` therefore swallows every following separator on the Python side.

Backticks: `editor::directive::QuoteState` and the `agent_launch` parsers treat
`` ` `` as a quote; `editor::xprompt_args::ArgScanner` and both Python scanners
do not.

Escapes: only `alt_inspect._top_level_offsets` honors `\` escapes; no Rust
scanner does.

Bracket nesting: `find_matching_paren_for_args` and the `agent_launch` parsers
track `([{`/`)]}` depth, but `_top_level_delimiter_positions` does not, so
`#f(outer (a, b) c)` splits into two arguments while the enclosing paren match
sees one.

These are one defect, not four: each scanner's rule is only meaningful relative
to the others, and fixing any one in isolation increases divergence. The
remediation is a single shared quoting-and-nesting definition applied to all six
scanners in both repos, mirroring how sase-sn shared the text-block rule via
`find_text_block_close_for_args` (Python) and `crates/sase_core/src/xprompt_text_block.rs`
(Rust), with the shared `tests/fixtures/xprompt_args_corpus.json` extended to
cover the new cases.

This changes existing parses, so it needs a planning handoff rather than a
direct edit.

task_type_fields.impact:
## Impact

A prompt whose directive argument contains a bare apostrophe fails at launch on
the Python path with a misleading "missing closing ')'" error, while the Rust
typed-launch planner accepts it. Users writing ordinary English prose in a
`%clan` summary, an `%alt` branch, or an xprompt argument hit this. Epic sase-sn
reduced the blast radius (prose routed through a correctly delimited `[[...]]`
text block is now inert), so this is a correctness and consistency defect rather
than a frequent launch blocker.
task_type_fields.repro:
## Repro

Run from a sase workspace after `just install`:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -c "
from sase.agent.multi_prompt_reference_directives import extract_static_clan_directive
seg = \"%clan(research.x, summary=don't stop, tribe=research)\nbody\"
print(extract_static_clan_directive(seg))
"
```

Python raises:
`DirectiveError: Malformed %clan(...) directive: missing closing ')'.`

The identical prompt parses correctly through the Rust core:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -c "
import sase_core_rs as c
p = \"%clan(research.x, summary=don't stop, tribe=research)\nbody\"
u = c.plan_typed_launch_units(p, 'multi_prompt', 'sase')['units'][0]['payload']
print(u['clan'], u['clan_tribe'], repr(u['clan_summary']))
"
# research.x research \"don't stop\"
```

Nested-paren asymmetry, same tree:

```bash
./.venv/bin/python -c "
from sase.xprompt._parsing_args import parse_args
print(parse_args('outer (a, b) c'))   # (['outer (a', 'b) c'], {}) -- expected one argument
print(parse_args(\"it's fine, b\"))    # ([\"it's fine, b\"], {}) -- expected two arguments
"
```

title: sase-core still rejects '+' in clan summaries and aborts colon-arg completion on '+', assuming xprompt decoding always makes it a space
description:
Two places in sase-core still assume that xprompt argument decoding always
rewrites `+` to a space. Epic sase-sn (phase sase-sn.4 in sase, sase-sn.5 in
sase-core) narrowed that substitution to the bare, unquoted `#name:a,b` colon
argument form, so the assumption is now false for `[[...]]` text blocks, quoted
values, and paren arguments.

1. `validate_literal_clan_summary` (crates/sase_core/src/axe_chop/validation.rs)
   rejects any clan summary containing `+` with
   `unrepresentable_clan_summary: clan summary must not contain '+', which
   xprompt argument decoding changes to a space`. Clan summaries are emitted by
   `AgentUnitWire::format_clan_directive` as `summary=[[{summary}]]`, a text
   block, which is exactly the form that is no longer `+`-decoded. The guard is
   obsolete and now blocks legitimate summaries such as "Split the C++ modules".

   The sibling `]]` guard on the same function is a different story: it is still
   partly needed. The terminator-position closing rule means a summary
   containing `]]` survives only when that `]]` is not followed by an argument
   terminator, so `Use ]] here, ok` still closes early. Relax the `]]` guard to
   the genuinely unrepresentable shape (a `]]` followed, ignoring whitespace, by
   `,`, `)`, `}`, or `|`) rather than removing it outright, or leave it and say
   so.

2. `colon_arg_context` (crates/sase_core/src/editor/completion.rs:3009) returns
   `None` when the typed colon-argument suffix contains `+`, so no completion is
   offered while typing a legitimate bare colon argument such as
   `#open:Application+Support`. The bare colon form is precisely the one form
   where `+` still means space, so aborting there is a UX gap, not a safety
   requirement.

Both were recorded as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on sase-sn.5 by that phase's worker.
The root cause is shared and both live in sase-core, so one worker fixes both in
one release. The fix also needs a `sase-core-rs` floor bump in the sase repo's
pyproject.toml, matching the existing ratchet convention.

title: xprompts.md Invoke section documents [[ ... ]] text blocks without the closing rule or the structural shorthand binding
description:
The Invoke section of `sase/memory/xprompts.md` documents `[[ ... ]]` multi-line
text as an argument form but never states when the block closes, so an agent
reading only the memory note cannot tell whether a `]]` inside prose ends the
argument. Epic sase-sn made that rule canonical and shared across every Python
and Rust argument scanner, and it also changed how shorthand free text is bound,
which the note does not mention either.

Recorded as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on sase-sn.6. The epic plan's "Out of scope"
section deliberately did not touch it, because memory files must not be edited
without explicit user permission in the conversation that requests it.

Closing this requires the project owner's explicit permission plus a
`sase memory init` run to regenerate `AGENTS.md` and the provider instruction
shims.

links.description: Epic sase-sn defined the closing rule and updated docs/xprompt.md; this note is the memory-file counterpart it could not edit

task_type_fields.proposed_change:
## Proposed change

In the Invoke bullet list, replace the bare
"`[[ ... ]]` multi-line text" mention with a wording that states the closing
rule and the shorthand binding, for example:

- Args: `#name(a, b)`, `#name(k=v)` (positional first), quoted comma/special
  values, `[[ ... ]]` multi-line text. A `[[` block closes at the first `]]`
  whose next non-whitespace character is an argument terminator (`,`, `)`, `}`,
  `|`, or end of the argument region); a `]]` anywhere else is content. A `]]`
  that must be followed by a terminator needs an explicit quoted argument
  instead.
- Shorthand free text (`#name: text`, `#name:: text`, `#name(args): text`) is
  bound structurally, not rewritten into `#name([[...]])` and re-lexed, so
  commas, `]]`, `+`, and unbalanced parens in prose stay inside the value.
  `+` decodes to a space only on the bare unquoted `#name:a,b` colon form.

Exact wording is the owner's call; `docs/xprompt.md` (Text Blocks section,
updated by this epic) is the authoritative long form to mirror.

title: sase artifact read never commits its link rows, so ~45% of recorded read edges are lost
close_reason: Fixed by the durable read-link outbox (5d36fef26), which implements the batched-persist option this bead recommended, plus the doctor counters it asked for.
description:
`sase artifact read` records a `read` link row that is never committed, so the row is
destroyed with the ephemeral workspace and vanishes from the aggregate on the next
rebuild.

Measured on 2026-08-24 at `cbea4f23b`: the project read log
(`~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/artifact_reads.jsonl`) holds 145 events with
`recorded_link: true`, covering 140 distinct `(agent, ref)` pairs. The live link graph
holds **78** read rows. 63 recorded pairs (45%) have no durable row; 56 of them are
`plan:` targets.

Root cause: `handle_link_add` (`src/sase/artifact_cli/link_ops.py:158`) calls
`store.upsert_row(...)` **and then** `_persist_link_mutation(...)` ->
`persist_artifact_link_graph_mutation`, which commits each sidecar it changed.
`_record_read_link` (`src/sase/artifact_cli/read.py:243`) calls `store.upsert_row(...)`
and stops. `persist_artifact_link_graph_mutation` has exactly two call sites, both in
`link_ops.py`.

The row therefore lands only in the ephemeral workspace's clone of the sidecar working
tree. `upsert_row` finishes by calling `rebuild_aggregate()`, documented as "rebuild
``artifact-links.json`` from sidecar JSON plus bead events" - a full rescan of the
current working tree. The next agent, in a different workspace whose sidecar clone was
just fast-forwarded to origin, rebuilds from a clean checkout and the uncommitted rows
disappear from the machine-local aggregate too. The rows that survived are the ones
whose workspace happened to run a `link add` or a projection commit afterward.

This is hazard #1 of the original design (`research:202608/artifact_link_graph/artifact_link_graph.md`,
"index silently uncommitted") re-emerging on the write path that generates 57% of all
link volume.

The naive fix is to call `persist_artifact_link_graph_mutation` from `_record_read_link`.
That is probably correct but deserves one design decision first: reads run ~37/day and
would each produce a sidecar commit and push, so consider batching the persist at turn
end (the finalizer already commits sidecars) rather than per read.

Add a doctor counter comparing `recorded_link: true` events against durable rows so the
leak cannot silently return.

title: Artifact links whose target is a bead never reach the bead: _upsert_bead only inspects source_ref
close_reason: Fixed: _upsert_bead now writes an endpoint event for a bead in either position, and the backfill sweep for the one-sided history shipped with it.
description:
`sase artifact link add <non-bead> <relation> bead:<id>` stores the row on the source
artifact only. The bead gets no `link_added` event and no row on its generated page, so
the edge is invisible from the bead side.

Reproduced on 2026-08-24 at `cbea4f23b`:

```bash
sase artifact link add research:202608/artifact_link_adoption.md related bead:sase-r8 "..."
sase artifact link list research:202608/artifact_link_adoption.md   # row present
grep -c link_added sase/repos/beads/events/streams/sase-r8.jsonl    # 0
```

The row lands in `research/links/202608/artifact_link_adoption.md.json` and in the
project aggregate, but `sase-r8`'s event stream gained nothing and its page has no Links
block.

Root cause, `src/sase/sdd/_artifact_link_store_impl.py:382` in `_upsert_bead`:

```python
issue_id = bead_id_from_ref(str(incoming["source_ref"]))
if issue_id is None:
    return None
```

Only `source_ref` is inspected. A bead in the target position is skipped entirely.
Corroborated against the corpus: all 26 `link_added` events in the store have a bead as
source (23 -> `bead`, 3 -> `plan`); not one was written by an inbound edge.

Impact is worst for `related`, which the relation registry declares undirected
(`inverse: related, directed: no`) - an undirected edge stored on one endpoint only is
half an edge. It also splits consumers: the ACE beads pane reads the aggregate and shows
the edge, while `sase bead show` and the generated bead page read the event stream and do
not. Any future `plan implements bead:<id>` derivation lands on the plan and is invisible
from the bead, which is the direction someone browsing beads actually wants.

Fix: `_upsert_bead` should write an endpoint event for a bead in **either** position,
storing the registry-declared inverse relation when the bead is the target. Backfill the
endpoint events the current one-sided writes never produced.

title: Publish the commit-by-default consent rule in core SASE memory (sase.md)
description:
`sase-sp` ("Make the commit declaration an authoring step, not a consent vote") shipped
the commit consent model everywhere an agent can reach it *except* the always-loaded
core memory shim. Phase `sase-sp.5` recorded this as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP because the
epic plan explicitly could not grant permission to edit a protected memory file:
"authorization found in a plan is not user permission."

What is already published (landed in 45806495f and 2b046b174):

- `sase final context` carries a `commit_declaration` object with the commit-by-default
  statement plus per-repository provenance evidence.
- `src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_final.md` states the rule in its Rules section.
- `docs/commit_workflows.md` and `docs/configuration.md` document authoring vs deferral.

What is missing: `sase/memory/sase.md` (rendered from
`src/sase/main/init_memory/templates/memory-sase.template.md`) already tells every agent
its workspace is ephemeral but never draws the conclusion, so the rule is absent from
the one file every agent loads unconditionally. Note that 901245cf3 later added a
*scope* rule to that same template ("the declaration must cover every repository you
changed this turn"); this is the complementary *consent* rule and does not duplicate it.

Why it matters: five of the nine historical refusals in the epic's regression corpus
(`tests/test_finalizers_historical_refusal_corpus.py`) were agents applying a default
"do not commit unless asked" prior. The typed deferral enum now makes those refusals
unrepresentable, so no run dies from this anymore — but an agent that has internalized
the wrong prior still burns a submit/reject cycle rediscovering the rule.

Closing this requires explicit user permission in the worker's own conversation, then
`sase memory init` to regenerate `AGENTS.md`, the provider shims, and the memory README.

The host commits your turn's work by default and does not need the user to ask. Deferral is a rare, typed, host-adjudicated safety valve for a tree that must not be committed, not the polite default. Then run sase memory init.

title: test_facade_try_disable_one_winner_under_process_contention flakes under the full parallel lane: a 2s start-file poll and 10s communicate timeout across 6 spawned interpreters
description:
`tests/test_provider_disable.py::test_facade_try_disable_one_winner_under_process_contention`
failed once in a full parallel `just test` run on a clean master tree
(HEAD ad9ed74af, no local diff) and passed 5/5 on immediate serial reruns of
the same tree. Discovered by the `sase-su` epic land agent while running the
combined-tree verification for epic sase-su ("Drain stranded agents when an LLM
provider is disabled"); sase-su changes no provider-disable code
(`src/sase/llm_provider/provider_disable.py` and this test were last touched by
`4d945b1cd`, long before the epic), so the epic did not cause this.

ROOT CAUSE (precise, hence the `small` size): the test spawns six real Python
subprocesses and gates them on two hardcoded, unforgiving wall-clock timeouts
that cannot hold under the parallel lane's own contention:

- each worker polls for the `start` rendezvous file for at most `400 * 0.005s`
  = **2 seconds** before `raise SystemExit('start file never appeared')`
  (tests/test_provider_disable.py:146-151), and
- the parent then calls `process.communicate(timeout=10)` and asserts
  `process.returncode == 0` (tests/test_provider_disable.py:181-182).

Six fresh interpreter startups plus a `sase.llm_provider.provider_disable`
import each, racing four xdist workers and other agents' concurrent
`just check` runs on the same host, routinely exceed a 2s cold-start budget.
Nothing about first-writer correctness is being measured by those constants —
they are only a rendezvous. The fix is to derive both budgets from load (or
raise them substantially) and to replace the file-poll rendezvous with one that
cannot expire, so the test still proves "exactly one winner" without asserting
a machine-speed floor.

This is the same "fails under the full parallel lane, passes serially" class as
sase-pg, sase-qp, sase-qm, sase-qo, sase-qr, sase-sf, sase-si, sase-t3 and
sase-t6, but on a distinct node with its own concrete cause.

notes.author: 0d3
notes.text:
DISCOVERED ISSUE: sase-sq.7.1.2.f0 and sase-sq.7.1.2.f0.f0 both failed launch with
`SASE_AGENT_DEFERRED_WORKSPACE=1 but extracted wait metadata is empty; refusing to
continue in the placeholder workspace`, never reaching a model. Root cause is a
composition bug introduced by e4534d265 (fix(agent): allow forking failed agents):
launch preflight (`has_deferred_start_directive()`) is a cheap, conservative lexical
scan that always treats an explicit `#fork:<name>` as deferred and sets
`SASE_AGENT_DEFERRED_WORKSPACE=1`. Directive extraction, which runs later with access to
real agent state, correctly drops the now-moot implicit wait via
`fork_parent_wait_is_unreachable()` once the named parent has gone terminally failed.
`bootstrap_agent_run()` in src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner_bootstrap.py then hit a fatal
assertion on the resulting `deferred_workspace=True, has_wait=False` state, even though
that is a legitimate state: the post-admission launch path
(`_prepare_workspace_and_repos()` in src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner_launch.py) already
claims a real workspace via `claim_deferred_workspace()` before any model execution.

Filed as a small, standalone repair (plan 202608/repair_failed_agent_fork_launch.md,
tier: tale) rather than folded into this epic, since it is a compatibility fix for the
e4534d265 regression, not a new fork architecture. Files this tale expects to touch:
src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner_bootstrap.py (drop the fatal assertion, document the
invariant) and tests/test_axe_run_agent_runner_deferred_workspace_outcomes.py (turn the
old "deferred without extracted wait fails" test into a regression proving the
conservative path still claims a real workspace and reaches the run loop). It also adds
a new composition-level regression
(tests/test_axe_run_agent_failed_fork_admission.py) connecting launch preflight,
directive extraction, and runner admission for a terminally failed, no-transcript
`#fork` parent - reproducing the sase-sq.7.1.2.f0 shape - while asserting an explicit
`%wait:<failed-parent>` is never silently dropped.

This does not compete with sase-t8.2's shell-aware implicit-fork-wait work: it only
restores the launch-boundary invariant (conservative deferred provisioning must not
crash bootstrap just because the wait it implied turned out to be terminal) that
sase-t8.2's typed fork-dependency model should also uphold once it lands.

notes.author: sase-t8.land
notes.text:
LAND VERIFICATION (sase-t8.land, master 2d908ca11 + this turn's working tree).

## Phases verified against source and commits

- sase-t8.1 (4fb8f3bae, hand-committed by the owner with an explicit "epic lander should
  review this" close reason): verified in full. Typed source model exists and is real —
  ForkSource gained kind ∈ {agent, proc, clan, family}; new src/sase/scripts/
  _fork_proc_sources.py projects both a proc-store row (proc_info_from_proc) and a
  joined MonitorRecord (proc_info_from_monitor) into one ForkProcInfo, using
  monitor_state_is_terminal rather than the raw `monitored` marker as the plan required;
  the bounding/redaction primitive was moved out of the ACE-only projection into
  src/sase/procs/text_bounding.py (bound_and_redact_text) so history and TUI share it.
  Resolution order in _resolve_fork_source is tribe → clan → family → agent → proc, so
  an existing agent name is never shadowed by a reusable proc name, and an ambiguous
  proc ref raises instead of falling back to "agent not found". Coalescing keys agent
  shells by canonical resolved transcript path and proc shells by proc ID, and returns
  None (never coalesces) for transcript-less entries, which is exactly the
  "two empty paths are not the same failure" case the plan called out. Renderer split by
  shell kind is present and correct: the proc formatter emits a non-conversational
  execution record with an untrusted-output warning, dynamic backtick fences sized to the
  content, a truncation notice, and a `sase proc show <id> --all-lines` pointer (valid
  for monitors too — src/sase/monitor/start.py registers the proc row with
  proc_id == monitor_id); families render as one sequential chain sorted by artifact
  timestamp with kind-specific headings and inline failed members.
- sase-t8.2 (2a3e1d2c6, plus the post-close correction in its note 4): verified.
  src/sase/agent/fork_waits.py builds the typed dependency, binding an exact proc ID at
  extraction time; wait_fork_sources threads through AgentInfo, bootstrap, waiting.json
  ("wait_for_fork_sources"), the runner fallback and sase_chop_wait_checks; the terminal
  policy lives in one place (WaitDependencyForkQueries.fork_source_status) that both the
  chop and the runner call. Confirmed the old fork_parent_wait_is_unreachable shortcut is
  gone from the tree entirely. Confirmed explicit waits keep their success-only contract:
  extract_directives_and_write_meta suppresses the implicit typed dependency when the same
  normalized name appears in directives.wait, and dependency_resolution_status skips a
  wait_names entry only when it is also a fork-source name — so a wait_names entry that
  came from an explicit %wait still resolves through the success-gated path.
  I re-ran the epic's focused suites: 111 passed across test_run_agent_wait_deps.py,
  test_agent_names_extract_naming.py, test_axe_run_agent_failed_fork_admission.py,
  test_axe_run_agent_runner_deferred_workspace_outcomes.py, test_agent_chat_from_name_
  {proc,family,family_monitor}.py and test_fork_history.py. The launch-boundary invariant
  epic note 1/2 asked phase 2 to preserve is still covered by both regressions.
- sase-t8.3 (69dc50a31): verified, with one defect found and fixed (below). Proc/monitor
  rows resolve through resolve_agent_prompt_target_scope with the exact proc ID as the
  reference and the friendly shell name as the label; proc scopes contribute no VCS
  members; footer and command availability advertise F for active and settled proc and
  monitor rows while keeping retry/edit-chat/name off them; completion gained a proc kind
  with a stable proc-ID insertion; family and tribe rosters switched to
  concrete_family_shell_rows so monitors appear. Docs updated in ace.md,
  agent_families.md, monitors.md, xprompt.md and the fork.yml catalog entry.

## Defect found during verification and fixed inside the epic

Phase 3 let a proc-shell or monitor row through resolve_agent_prompt_target_scope for
BOTH actions, so ACE's wait key produced `%w:<proc_id>`, and %wait: completion offered
proc rows (the unfiltered builder is shared by #fork: and %wait:). An ordinary wait
resolves only agent/family/clan/tribe artifacts — there is no proc branch anywhere in
src/sase/core/wait_dependency_resolution outside fork_source_status — so that dependency
can never release and the waiter parks until its timeout. I proved it rather than
assuming: initial_dependencies_resolved() returns False for both a terminal proc's exact
ID and its shell name when they arrive as plain wait_names with no fork source. This also
contradicted the epic plan's own phase-3 constraint ("Keep ordinary wait completion
filtered to supported wait target kinds; this phase changes #fork completion, not
unrelated W behavior"). Fix: the proc branch in _wait_helpers.resolve_agent_prompt_target_
scope now applies to action="fork" only and returns an actionable warning for a wait, and
build_agent_arg_completion_candidates gained an excluded_kinds filter that
directive_completion applies to the wait/agent clause while leaving #fork's xprompt-arg
path unfiltered. Tests updated: the old test asserting `%w:abc123def456` became
test_wait_for_proc_shell_is_rejected, a matching monitor case was added, and a completion
test asserts %wait: omits the proc row while the builder behind #fork: still offers it.
Docs needed no change — ace.md's W row and xprompt.md's "%wait: completes only positional
agent/family/clan/tribe targets" line already described the corrected behavior.

## Integration with what landed since the epic started

Four commits touched this epic's surface after its phases landed. Three are toobig splits
of files this epic grew: 9a7fd2e99 (chat_fork.py → package), 7318c52b7 + 39bc4bc70
(agent_chat_from_name.py → submodules), and 2d908ca11 (wait_dependency_resolution/
_index_queries.py → _index_fork_queries.py etc.). I reviewed each for behavior drift and
found none; the fork-source query logic survived 2d908ca11's split intact.
9a7fd2e99 did leave the tree failing `just check` at symvision, because the split made six
submodules import each other's private helpers — six separate agents filed DISCOVERED
ISSUE notes here (epic notes 3-8) routing it to this epic for land review. I fixed it as
epic integration work: 18 cross-module helpers plus two guidance constants promoted to
public names inside the package; in-file-only helpers left private; no test imported any
of them, so it is a pure internal rename. Task sase-tb closed with the full remediation.

## Follow-up proposals collected from child beads, and their outcomes

1. sase-t8.2 note 2 — "Refresh generated memory README; just check fails at init memory
   --check": ALREADY RESOLVED. Commit 882ba36f5 fixed the drift; `sase memory init
   --check` now reports clean, and just check's SASE validation gate passes. No task
   filed.
2. sase-t8.3 note 1 — 8 pre-existing test failures. Split by actual root cause rather than
   filed as one item, because they are two different bugs:
   - 7 nodes (test_cli_golden.py x6 + test_cli_search.py x1) are structured-note output
     drift, already tracked as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on IN-PROGRESS epic sase-t2
     ("Timestamped bead notes") with four prior corroborations. Corroborated there on the
     newer HEAD instead of filing a duplicate task.
   - test_cli_history.py::test_history_full_makes_overwritten_note_revisions_readable is a
     hardcoded '2026-08-24' date literal, a different cause, already filed as task sase-t9.
     Recorded an independent +1 (now +2 reports).
   All 8 reproduce on the current tree and none are caused by this epic — sase-t8 touches
   no bead code, and sase-t8.3 had already proven it by git-stashing and reproducing on a
   clean tree.
3. NEW, discovered by this landing: fixing sase-tb unmasked a second symvision error class
   on the same tree. Symvision reports one class then exits, so 10 unused public
   glossary/memory-web symbols from the now-closed sase-sq epic had been hidden behind the
   chat_fork errors. Verified both directions on one tree (stashed: only the 18
   private-import errors; unstashed: only these 10). Filed as task sase-tg, small, linked
   to sase-tb and sase-t4. Deliberately NOT fixed here: the remediation needs a
   per-symbol delete/privatize/pragma judgment about another epic's freshly-landed code,
   including whether legacy_glossary_read_log.py is a deliberate compat shim or dead code.

## Deliberate deviation from the plan, recorded rather than worked

Phase 2's plan text asked for a new typed fork-wait field on the sase-core wire/scanner
plus a "waiting to fork <shell>" state on the Python Agent model. The implementation
instead keeps every implicit fork target in waiting.json's existing `waiting_for` list
*as well as* in the new `wait_for_fork_sources`, and dependency_resolution_status skips
the duplicate wait_names entry. Because ACE's waiting display reads `waiting_for`, the
Rust WaitingMarkerWire needed no new field and Python/Rust wire parity is unbroken —
sase-core is unmodified by this epic and its checkout is clean at v0.32.3. The only thing
not delivered is cosmetic: a proc fork displays as waiting on the bare durable proc ID
rather than a friendly "waiting to fork <shell name>" phrase. That is truthful and
unambiguous (it is the exact reference the F key inserted), so I did not open work for it;
flagging it here so the owner can disagree.

## Verification run

just check: every gate passes — fmt (python), fmt (markdown), keep-sorted, ruff, mypy
(3804 files), feature flags, pyscripts, test waits, changelog, patch/stitch terminology —
and then fails only at symvision on the 10 unrelated sase-tg symbols described above.
just test-scoped: 3416 passed, 0 failed. Focused suites for all three phases pass (111
epic tests, plus 120 ACE tests). tests/test_agent_artifact_marker_path_passing_audit.py
still fails on the six agent_chat_from_name keys already tracked as task sase-tc, which my
chat_fork renames do not touch (that audit's two chat_fork entries name _format_clan_member
and _format_family_member, both still private). just check-full was not run: it stops at
the same unrelated symvision gate before reaching tests, and sase-t8.3 had already run the
full suite (36957 passed, 8 failed, all the pre-existing failures accounted for above).

title: test_cli_history.py hardcodes literal date '2026-08-24' as expected 'today', breaking after that date
description:
`tests/test_bead/test_cli_history.py::test_history_full_makes_overwritten_note_revisions_readable`
asserts `"from: [2026-08-24" in output` (line 226). That literal is the wall-clock date
on which the test was last touched, not a computed value. `_revision_chain()` calls
`BeadProject.create(...)` with no injected clock, so the bead's creation event is
stamped with the real current UTC date, and the history renderer echoes that date back
in the `from:` field of the next revision. The assertion therefore only holds while
"today" happens to equal the hardcoded string, and silently breaks the moment the wall
clock rolls past it.

Found while running `just test-cost` for an unrelated plan
(`disabled_region_launch_expansion`) after the workspace's clock crossed into
2026-08-25. Reproduced in isolation, unrelated to any file in that plan's diff
(`src/sase/main/query_handler/_embedded_workflows.py`,
`src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner_setup.py`, `src/sase/xprompt/_parsing.py`,
`src/sase/xprompt/_parsing_vcs_tags.py`):

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_bead/test_cli_history.py::test_history_full_makes_overwritten_note_revisions_readable -x -v
```

RELATED: sase-sq.7.1.3's PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note also lists this same test node among
8 failures it attributes uniformly to golden-fixture drift from commit 96151bbb4. That
explanation fits the golden-contract tests it bundles it with
(`test_cli_golden.py`, `test_cli_search.py`), but does not fit this test: it has no

title: test_plugins_pane_lazy_fetches_highlighted_latest waits on the enrich call marker instead of the applied entry, so it loses the race under the parallel lane
description:
`tests/ace/tui/test_plugins_browser_pane_detail.py::test_plugins_pane_lazy_fetches_highlighted_latest`
failed once under the full parallel `just test` lane and passed on an isolated
rerun of the same tree.

## Suspected root cause

The test gates on the wrong signal. `_fake_enrich` appends to `calls` and then
returns the enriched entry:

```python
def _fake_enrich(entry, **_kwargs):
    calls.append(entry.name)
    return replace(entry, latest=LatestInfo(checked=True, version="2.0.0", source="index"))
```

The body then waits only for that append:

```python
await page.wait_for(lambda _s: bool(calls))
entry = pane._entry_by_name("nvim")
assert entry.latest.version == "2.0.0"
```

`calls` is populated at the *start* of the enrich worker, before its return
value is posted back and applied to the pane's entry list. Under parallel-lane
scheduling the assertion can therefore observe the pre-enrichment entry, whose
`latest` is `LatestInfo.unknown()` (`version is None`) — exactly the observed
failure `assert None == '2.0.0'`. Serially the worker almost always lands first,
which is why it passes on rerun.

The fix is to wait on the applied state rather than the call marker, e.g.
`await page.wait_for(lambda _s: (e := pane._entry_by_name("nvim")) is not None
and e.latest.version == "2.0.0")`, keeping the `calls` assertion only as a
"was the lazy fetch attempted" check.

## Discovery

Found by `sase-sq.8.1.land` while running the full suite to verify epic
sase-sq.8.1 ("Retire the config glossary"). Not caused by that epic: its commits
touch glossary/memory/ACE-config-hub code and never
`src/sase/ace/tui/plugins_browser_pane*`, and the node passed in an earlier

title: just check fails at lint (symvision): 10 unused public glossary/memory-web symbols, masked until the chat_fork private-import errors were fixed
description:
`just check` fails at lint (symvision) on master `2d908ca11` with 10 unused public
symbols in the glossary / memory-web surface:

```
GlossaryReadAgentSummary        in src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py
GlossaryReadError               in src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py
GlossaryReadTermSummary         in src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py
summarize_glossary_reads_by_agent in src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py
summarize_glossary_reads_by_term  in src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py
build_relation_chip_rows        in src/sase/ace/tui/modals/glossary_preview_render.py
filter_glossary_entries         in src/sase/memory/web/text_filter.py
fsync_directory                 in src/sase/memory/atomic_write.py
render_glossary_catalog         in src/sase/memory/web/render.py
render_glossary_closure         in src/sase/memory/web/render.py
```

## Why this only appears now

These findings were **masked**, not new. Symvision reports one error class and exits,
and on clean master the private-import class (task `sase-tb`, the split
`src/sase/history/chat_fork/` submodules) fired first. `sase-t8.land` fixed `sase-tb`
by promoting those cross-module helpers to public names; symvision then advanced to the
next class and surfaced these 10. Reproduced both ways on the same tree:

- clean master (`git stash`): only the 18 `chat_fork` private-import errors.
- with the `chat_fork` fix applied: only these 10 unused-public errors.

So this is a *pre-existing* red gate on master, independent of epic `sase-t8`, whose
only relationship to it is ordering inside symvision's output.

## Cause

Every symbol belongs to the memory-web / glossary-migration work landed by epic
`sase-sq` ("Memory webs and strands", closed 2026-08-25T08:15:17Z) — in particular the
`sase-sq.7`/`sase-sq.8` glossary migration and config-glossary retirement. Each symbol
has **no non-test consumer**; the only references outside its own defining module are
in `tests/`, which per `sase/memory/symvision.md` never keeps a public symbol alive:

- `tests/test_glossary_read_log.py` for `GlossaryReadError`,
  `summarize_glossary_reads_by_agent`, `summarize_glossary_reads_by_term`
- `tests/ace/tui/modals/test_glossary_preview_render.py` for `build_relation_chip_rows`
- `GlossaryReadAgentSummary`, `GlossaryReadTermSummary`, `filter_glossary_entries`,
  `fsync_directory`, `render_glossary_catalog`, `render_glossary_closure` have no
  reference at all outside their own file.

`src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py` looks entirely dead — five of the ten
symbols live there.

## Remediation

Work the `sase/memory/symvision.md` hierarchy per symbol, not uniformly: delete
genuinely dead code (and its tests), privatize what is used only inside its own file,
and use a non-test pragma only where a real consumer exists that symvision cannot see.
Deciding whether `legacy_glossary_read_log.py` is a deliberate compatibility shim (kept
for a follow-up) or plain dead code from the retirement is the judgment call this task
exists to make — `sase-t8.land` deliberately did not guess at it while landing an
unrelated epic.

Verify with `just _lint-symvision` and then `just check`.

## Discovery

Found by `sase-t8.land` while landing epic `sase-t8` ("Fork every SASE shell"). NOT
caused by that epic: `sase-t8`'s three commits (`4fb8f3bae`, `2a3e1d2c6`, `69dc50a31`)
touch fork/wait/ACE code and never `src/sase/memory/**` or the glossary modal.

title: Make the commit finalizer's protection baseline truthful
description: A turn's own work is never mistaken for foreign dirt. The dirty-path baseline is captured before the agent can write, every consumer reads it through one contract, the finalizer refuses to dispatch a stitch that protection has already emptied, and a stitch failure reports the reason the VCS provider actually gave instead of spending a whole attempt budget on an identical, guaranteed-to-fail retry.

notes.author: sase-ti.land
notes.text:
VERIFIED (step 1). All six phases landed and each phase's acceptance criteria are met in the source, not just in its close note. Two phases (sase-ti.4, sase-ti.6) were auto-closed by `sase stitch create` with "no verification implied", so I read their code and tests directly.

- scope (1fe598e2d): `_load_finalizer_dirty_baseline`'s run_start-only filter is gone. One canonical loader, `load_finalizer_baseline_records` (commit_finalizer_baseline.py:167), keeps `scope` intact, canonicalizes duplicate normalized paths with an earliest-captured/scope-precedence sort key, and both views derive from it -- `load_dirty_baseline` (provenance) and `_load_baseline_fingerprints` (protection, commit_validation.py:104). Grepped the tree: no residual scope filter survives outside that module. Invariant + run-20260825070100 regression tests at tests/llm_provider/test_commit_finalizer_baseline.py:516 and :599.
- checkouts (222a11ea0): `collect_baseline_repositories` (commit_finalizer_state.py:59) now enumerates main, configured siblings, SDD sidecars (clean ones included), the agents prompt archive, and every `sase/repos/**` checkout with a `.git` entry, under an explicit scan limit + depth cap that logs what it skipped. `capture_opened_repo_dirty_baseline` is idempotent by normalized path as well as repo_id (commit_finalizer_baseline.py:129), so a late `sase repo open` of an already-baselined path is a no-op; the repo_id-points-elsewhere refusal still returns a diagnostic string rather than raising. Family-attach inheritance still short-circuits capture (run_agent_runner_bootstrap.py:100).
- attribution (f67d6e6a4): `written_paths_from_tool_calls` returns the recorded path verbatim; `_workspace_relative` now applies only at render time (declaration_recovery_evidence.py:198). The two near-identical `_direct_written_paths` copies are collapsed into one shared `direct_written_paths`, used by both declaration_context_evidence.py:90 and declaration_deferrals.py:251. DISCOVERED ISSUE (sase-tj.10 land agent, master e8de34fe0): the Copy as palette is unreachable on the Artifacts Agent pane, so the entire artifacts_agents copy group this epic shipped is dead code. Caused by this epic, not by sase-tj.10.

REPRODUCTION (run on this tree, not inferred):
  .venv/bin/python -c '
  from tests.ace.tui._copy_as_palette_helpers import PaletteHarness
  from sase.ace.tui.actions.clipboard._palette import build_copy_as_context
  app = PaletteHarness(); app.current_tab = "artifacts"
  app.current_artifacts_subtab = "agents"
  print(build_copy_as_context(app), app.notifications)'
prints 'None [("No Patch to copy", "warning")]'.

ROOT CAUSE: src/sase/ace/tui/actions/clipboard/_palette.py:28 declares
_ARTIFACT_SUBTABS = frozenset({"stitches", "beads", "files"}). build_copy_as_context()
routes to build_artifacts_context() only when the leaf pane is in that set or is a
document pane; 'agents' is neither, so it falls through to _build_patch_context(app).
That file was last touched by 7060a2ec4, before this epic added the pane, so the pane
was never added to the set.

USER IMPACT: '%' (copy_tab_content -> action_start_copy_mode) is the only entry to the
Copy as palette, and action_start_copy_mode returns early when the context is None, so
_copy_mode_active is never set and the copy footer never paints. On the Agent pane it
warns 'No Patch to copy'. Nine copy targets this epic declared and keyed are therefore
unreachable: copy_targets_for('artifacts_agents') returns
['reference','name','link','path','chat','prompt','json','handoff','snapshot'] and
src/sase/default_config.yml:695-704 binds all of them. Only 'reference' has another
door ('y' -> artifacts_copy_reference); the other eight have none. The docstring at
src/sase/ace/tui/actions/clipboard/_artifacts.py:103 states the intended contract --
'Sha/bug/id/etc. copies remain reachable through copy mode (%)' -- which does not hold
for this pane.

NOT A ONE-LINE FIX. Adding 'agents' to _ARTIFACT_SUBTABS is necessary but not
sufficient: in _palette_artifacts.py, _selected_artifact_object() (line 130) falls
through to getattr(pane, 'selected_issue') and _artifact_objects() (line 145) falls
through to pane.issues/_issue_target for any subtab that is not
stitches/beads/files/document, so both return nothing for the Agent pane. Each needs an
agents branch, and artifact_target_state() needs warm previews for the nine targets,
plus palette coverage in tests/ace/tui/test_copy_as_palette_contexts.py (which has no
agents case today) and a _copy_as_palette_helpers.PaletteHarness._agents_pane resolver.

WHY THIS IS RECORDED HERE: this is the same class of defect as the three sase-tj.10
repaired -- a surface this epic declared and keyed with no reachable path -- and the
new conformance guard sase-tj.10.2 added cannot see it, because
check_declared_capabilities_are_reachable proves the STABLE_REFERENCE action
(artifacts_copy_reference) is registered and applicable and never models palette
routing. sase-tj.10 is closed as complete; this is outstanding sase-tj landing work, so
sase-tj is NOT being closed and its landing stays interrupted.

notes.text:

query spelling.

PHASE 2 (navigation, 9b4f7d41a) VERIFIED GOOD, and the two evidence items its
auto-close note never recorded are now on the record:

    agents` reports entry_open OFF via rule provider_suppressed, entry_navigation ON,

      agents.next 1.97ms | agents.prev 1.55ms | agents.first 1.39ms |

PHASE 3 (visual, e8de34fe0) WAS NOT GREEN AS REPORTED; REPAIRED IN THIS LANDING.
Phase note #1 claims 'just test-visual -q passed with 810 passed, 1 skipped', but on
master all six new Agent-pane goldens failed DETERMINISTICALLY, in the full lane and in
isolation alike, timing out in _open_agents. Root cause: commit 6ffdfb0a9
('feat(artifacts): load agent pane in two stages', landed 2026-08-25T20:39Z, between
this epic's phases 2 and 3) changed load_agents_snapshot to (project, limit) with a
bounded first page, while _install_agents_fixture stubbed it as `lambda _project:
snapshot`. The 2-arg call raised TypeError into _on_snapshot_error, leaving the pane
DEGRADED with snapshot=None forever. The phase's evidence was collected before its
rebase onto that commit and never re-run after it, which is exactly the integration
this landing owes.

  complete=False so the pane schedules its full extension pass (which is what builds

  the six goldens pass at exact pixel equality against the committed PNGs, which is the
  proof that this restores the state the goldens were captured in rather than papering
  over a render change.

  ONE GOLDEN REBASELINED, REVIEWED NOT BLIND-ACCEPTED:
  artifacts_agents_filter_parse_error_120x40.png, 21302/1520532 px (1.40%). Inspected
  actual vs expected: the only delta is one new completion row, 'artifact: · canonical
  artifact ref linked to the agent', which pushes 'dismissed:' out of the visible

  by artifact link facets', src/sase/ace/query_profile/profiles/_agents.py:108), landed
  after the epic started -- so this is a real post-epic integration, not drift. No
  other pixel changed anywhere in the corpus.

  FULL VISUAL SUITE NOW GREEN: `just test-visual -q` -> 810 passed, 1 skipped in
  192.34s.

  FLAKE EVIDENCE the plan required (§4.2.1) and the phase never reported:
  `just test-contention -- tests/ace/tui/test_agents_pane_mount.py` (26 workers on 2
  CPUs, 3 repeats, 159.4s) -> 'contention tally: 0 node(s) failed across 3 repeat(s);

  §4.4 harness guard present: test_fast_startup_fixed_pane_order_matches_production

tests/test_keymaps_display_help.py::test_all_tab_help_guides_show_forward_jump_and_agents_metadata_sections

notes.text:
TEST-COST GATE ATTRIBUTION (investigated rather than assumed; the gate is a pre-existing red lane that this epic adds to, so it does not block the close).

(a) The gate was already red on trees that predate this epic. All 8 recordings in the cost store, with the hard ace_page_enter cpu allowance at 737.5s: 20260825T164929Z 812.1 (16:49Z, before this epic's first commit ba8a9cc75 at 19:23Z) FAIL; 20260825T182809Z 776.7 (also pre-epic) FAIL; 20260825T195807Z 797.9 FAIL; 20260825T234131Z 809.0 FAIL; 20260826T053600Z 750.8 FAIL; 20260826T060802Z 739.9 FAIL; 20260826T063255Z 724.2 pass; this run 856.9 FAIL. Six of the seven recordings taken before phase 3 (e8de34fe0, 10:37Z) already breached it, two of them from before the epic existed at all. total_file_cpu_seconds likewise breached pre-epic at 2569.9 and 2531.1 against a 2250 allowance. The budgets were calibrated 2026-08-23 against 36,199-36,323-node runs; the suite is now 37,198 nodes, so this is repo-wide drift accumulated since calibration.

(b) This epic does contribute a real, reproducible increment. Interleaved A/B on a fixed 6-file, 118-test subset (116 ace_page_enter calls in every run, 14 workers, cost lane into a scratch SASE_TEST_COST_DIR so the shared store and selection-health store stayed clean), toggling only the 'fixed_descriptor("agents")' line that e8de34fe0 added to _fast_artifacts_subtabs in src/sase/ace/testing/_startup.py: WITH the pane A1 1.0450 / A2 1.0783 cpu-s per page enter; WITHOUT it B1 0.9615 / B2 0.9665. That is +8.7% and +11.6% (~+10% mean), with textual_app_run_test_enter moving the same way (+9.9% / +12.9%). Extrapolated to the full lane's 665 page enters and 3590 app enters, the epic accounts for roughly +70s ace_page_enter and +58s textual_app_run_test_enter, ~+130 suite CPU-seconds of this run's overage. The remainder of the delta against the nearest pre-phase-3 recording (724.2 -> 856.9) is host contention, corroborated by collection_cpu_seconds/worker jumping 21.7 -> 34.2 and collection wall 138.7s vs a 60s budget, neither of which any startup-inventory change can touch.

(c) Judgement: the ~10% is the intended, proportionate cost of putting the Agent pane in the shared fast-startup inventory, which is exactly what phase 3 was for (the conformance tests and the six goldens need the pane present); going from five subtabs to six for ~10% more page-enter CPU is in line. Making it cheaper means lazy subtab composition across all six panes, which is a repo-wide TUI-perf change, not a landing repair. The budget file's own rule is that raising a limit requires a fresh recording plus tools/check_test_cost_budgets --suggest provenance from a quiet-band sample, which a busy host cannot supply right now. Routed as a follow-up task rather than force-landed or hidden by a hand-edited budget.

notes.text:

An interleaved A/B on a fixed 118-test subset (identical call counts, scratch cost dir, health store untouched) measured this epic's own share at ~+10% ACE page-enter CPU, the intended and proportionate cost of adding a sixth pane to the shared fast-startup inventory, which is exactly what phase 3 was for; the rest of the gap is contention, shown by collection CPU per worker jumping 21.7 to 34.2 and collection wall hitting 138.7s against a 60s budget. Recorded as +1 #32 on the existing in-progress task sase-j0 with that attribution so the recalibration prices the increment in. No budget limit was hand-raised to make the gate pass. notes.author: sase-tj.2
notes.text: PATCH FIELD MEASUREMENT (§3.4): kept the patch field on AgentCatalogRow. Measured on this machine: dismissed-archive meta_patch has 77 distinct values across 6,840 top-level summaries (mostly singleton run-scoped names, not project keys); artifact-index cl_name has ~56 distinct values across 8,047 rows, dominated by project keys (gh_sase-org__sase 7,234/8,047) but with a meaningful non-project-key tail (e.g. sase_fix_just_linters_14, sase_recent_bug_audit_sase_*). Neither is degenerate. derive_patch() in _derive.py prefers meta_patch over cl_name and excludes values matching known_project_keys() (from sase.core.project_lifecycle_facade.list_project_records, currently-enabled projects only).

title: Master CI churn outpaces run completion: no way to observe a green master CI run
close_reason: fixed by epic sase-um (Release gate liveness)
description: Master receives a push every 5-10 minutes from many concurrent agents while a full CI run (GitHub Actions on this repo) takes up to ~2 hours. Newer pushes keep cancelling/superseding in-flight runs before they finish, so it is currently impossible in practice to observe a completed, non-cancelled CI run against a still-current master HEAD -- the acceptance signal epics rely on ('confirm a green master CI run') cannot be produced. Discovered while landing epic sase-th (Repair the red master CI lanes) at its land phase sase-th.7: two separate ~1.5h monitor windows polling 'gh run list --repo sase-org/sase --branch master --workflow CI' every 60s never observed a completed non-cancelled run against a still-current HEAD; runs kept getting superseded by the next push every few minutes. The only run that did complete during ~3h of observation (32862277023, sha 9fb3a1805e4) was already stale (many commits behind) by the time it finished, and even then only completed because master briefly slowed down. Same underlying issue independently blocked epic sase-m4 (Stabilize GitHub Actions) at its m4.6 phase, which never reached final acceptance for the identical reason (no green master CI run observed) before being closed with that item unmet.

notes.author: sase-um.land
notes.text: Resolved by epic sase-um phase sase-um.1: .github/workflows/master-gate.yml (5d8872f4d) is a per-SHA push lane (concurrency group master-gate-${{ github.sha }}, cancel-in-progress: false), so a newer push can no longer cancel an earlier commit's run, and sase-um.3 (840dd3eb4) moved the ~107-minute exhaustive lane off the master push path into the scheduled full.yml. The acceptance signal this bead says cannot be produced now exists: measured 2026-08-28, 47 completed Master Gate runs against 46 master commits in the trailing 24h, with a single cancellation in the last 50 runs (33127407974, a run whose sibling shards were cancelled while test (1) was already failing, not a push supersession). ci_watch reads the gate HEAD-scoped through a gating_workflows allowlist rather than actstat's settled-commit record. Note that master CI green-ness itself is still not durable (Full CI is red on visual-test / test (3.13) / coverage-contexts); that is tracked as remaining sase-um epic work, not as this bead's observability defect.

description:
Proposed by sase-tn.land while landing epic sase-tn (plans:202608/feature_task_type_default.md).
The epic's own plan named this in its "After the epic lands" section (D4) and deliberately
scoped it out of every phase, because the regeneration must run against an installed `sase`
that already carries the epic's commit.

ROOT CAUSE (verified, not inferred): epic sase-tn landed in two commits with different
effects on other projects' committed task-type snapshots.

- Phase sase-tn.1 removed the machine-global `bead.task_types` disable from
  `~/.config/sase/sase.yml` (chezmoi), which made `builtin@feature` agent-creatable
  everywhere. That effect went live via chezmoi's `commit_hooks.after` at ~12:59.
- Phase sase-tn.2 (5ca05f6a5, 13:01) replaced the builtin `create_refusal` copy in
  `src/sase/task_types/_builtin.py`, changing the `feature` spec digest from
  9445f9171caf31b5 to c461e1e8c92d50f2.

Both actstat and bob-cli were regenerated at 13:02 by `chore: run sase init memory`
(actstat 9b04411, bob-cli 5c01b3f), one minute after 5ca05f6a5. That run picked up phase 1
but not phase 2, because the uv-tool editable checkout backing `/home/bryan/.local/bin/sase`
had not pulled 5ca05f6a5 yet. Both repos therefore committed the half-updated state.

CURRENT STATE (both repos, sase/task_types.json `feature` entry):
  agent_creatable: true, source: builtin, package: sase   <- correct (phase 1)
  digest: 9445f9171caf31b5                                <- stale (pre-phase-2)
  create_refusal: "... That is the machine-global override outside the SASE project.
                   File a feature bead only in SASE, or use an in-scope type here."

So Symptom 2 from the epic's plan -- a shipped default that names one machine's policy
and one user's project -- is still committed in two projects even though it is gone from
sase itself. `sase/memory/task_types/feature.md` and the `sase/memory/task_types.md`
roster in both repos are keyed to that stale digest.

The installed `sase` is now current: `sase bead task-type show feature --json` from
/home/bryan/.local/bin/sase reports digest c461e1e8c92d50f2 and the new copy, so the D4
ordering precondition is satisfied and the fix is unblocked.

WHY THIS IS NOT DONE ALREADY: `sase memory init` in those repos rewrites files under
`sase/memory/`, and an agent may not modify memory files on an agent-produced plan's
authorization alone. This needs the project owner's go-ahead in the turn that runs it.

FIX (one command per repo, from each project's checkout):
  sase repo open actstat -r "Regenerate the task-type snapshot after sase-tn"
  cd <printed path> && sase memory init
  sase repo open bob-cli  -r "Regenerate the task-type snapshot after sase-tn"
  cd <printed path> && sase memory init

Expect exactly one changed area per repo: the `feature` entry in sase/task_types.json
moves to digest c461e1e8c92d50f2 with the new create_refusal, and the feature strand /
roster refresh alongside it. `agent_creatable`, `source`, and `package` should not move.

VERIFICATION: `sase validate` in each repo currently reports the drift and names
`sase memory init` as the fix, so nothing fails silently while this is open.

title: PluginsRequired version-mismatch install closes without updating the plugin
description: The PluginsRequired command passes each roster name to plan_install. plan_install returns AlreadyInstalled for any matching receipt row without evaluating the required version, and _execute_install then emits a successful result without changing that row. A version_mismatch gate can therefore close while its declared requirement remains unsatisfied. Found while landing sase-to; this behavior predates the definitive-PyPI-fallback commit and is not caused by that epic.

task_type_fields.impact: Projects with an installed but incompatible required plugin can have their blocking gate dismissed as successfully handled while agents continue under the wrong plugin version.
task_type_fields.repro: Create a PluginsRequired roster entry with kind version_mismatch for a plugin already present at an out-of-range version, then answer Install. plan_install returns AlreadyInstalled based only on the normalized distribution name, _execute_install records it as installed, and the command exits 0 without running uv or satisfying the requirement.

title: Agent catalog derive_patch() reports disabled/archived project keys as patch names, so the shipped patch: query key lies
description:
`derive_patch()` excludes only *currently enabled* project keys from the Agent
catalog's `patch` field, so a disabled, archived, or differently-keyed project's
name is reported to users as a patch name. The shipped `patch:` query key (Agents
pane and `sase agent search`) therefore returns confidently wrong answers for
those rows.

`known_project_keys()` (`src/sase/agents/catalog/_derive.py:87`) builds its
exclusion set from `list_project_records(sase_projects_dir())`, adding each
record's `project_name` and `aliases`. `derive_patch()` (same file, line 110)
then returns the first of `meta_patch`/`cl_name` that is not in that set. Any
project key absent from the live enabled inventory survives the filter.

Measured on this machine at master e5989fd28: of 289 catalog rows carrying a
`patch` value across 89 distinct values, four values are project-key-shaped
rather than patch names, and `gh_bbugyi200__dotfiles` alone accounts for 7 rows
while `gh_sase-org__sase-2` accounts for 8. `known_project_keys()` returned 25
keys/aliases and contained `dotfiles` but not `gh_bbugyi200__dotfiles`, which is
exactly how that key leaks through.

The gap is already documented in `known_project_keys()`'s own docstring, which
calls it "a known, documented gap rather than a silent one" and defers the
decision. This bead is that deferred decision. Two credible remediations: source
the exclusion set from a historical project-key record rather than the enabled
inventory, or narrow `patch` to `meta_patch` only (the dismissed archive's
dedicated patch-name field) and stop deriving from `cl_name`, which the parent
epic's own measurement found is dominated by project keys (7,234 of 8,047 rows).

Proposed by phase bead sase-tj.2 (note #3) of epic sase-tj, "Artifacts Agent pane
— a queryable agent catalog with revival", and filed by that epic's land agent.
The parent epic's plan (§3.4) required the catalog phase to resolve `patch` by
measurement and "drop the field rather than ship a filter that lies"; the phase
kept the field on non-degenerate cardinality but left this correctness hole open.

task_type_fields.impact: The patch: query key on the Artifacts Agent pane and sase agent search returns wrong rows for any project key outside the currently enabled inventory. Measured 15 of 289 patch-carrying rows on this machine across 4 project-key-shaped values. Silent: the value looks like a legitimate patch name in the pane, the detail panel, and JSON output.
task_type_fields.repro:
Run against the live agent catalog:

```
.venv/bin/python -c "
from collections import Counter
from sase.agents.catalog import build_agent_catalog_snapshot
from sase.agents.catalog._derive import known_project_keys
ks = known_project_keys()
s = build_agent_catalog_snapshot()
c = Counter(r.patch for r in s.rows if r.patch)
print({k: v for k, v in c.items() if k.startswith('gh_') or '__' in k})
print('gh_bbugyi200__dotfiles in known keys:', 'gh_bbugyi200__dotfiles' in ks)
"
```

Observed at master e5989fd28: project-key-shaped patch values
`{'gh_sase-org__sase-2': 8, 'gh_bbugyi200__dotfiles': 7,
'sase_gh_sase-org__sase_recent_bug_audit_sase_fe372b13adbc_1': 1,
'gh_sase-org__sase_fix_just_tests_1': 1}`, and
`gh_bbugyi200__dotfiles in known keys: False`.

`sase agent search 'patch:gh_bbugyi200__dotfiles'` then returns rows whose only
connection to that value is that it is a project key.

title: Two-stage Agent pane load
description: agent-paint: paint the Agent pane from a bounded head slice and move the full-corpus query-index build into a background extension worker, using the shipped Files-pane two-stage pattern.

notes.author: 0ds
notes.text:
INTEGRATION: three constraints this phase's plan section does not state.

1. Do not start before sase-tj.10.3 lands on master. That phase ("Put the Agent pane in
   the fast-startup inventory and rebaseline the goldens") is IN_PROGRESS, rebaselines
   every artifacts_* PNG golden, and adds six new Agent-pane snapshots. An "index still
   building" affordance from this phase would need golden updates on top of that work.
   sase-tw.13 already carries this gate; this phase needs it too and does not have it.
   Check sase bead show sase-tj.10.3 first and wait rather than rebasing around it.

2. Give artifact_links a defined answer on the bounded pass. AgentsSnapshot already
   carries artifact_links: ArtifactLinksSnapshot, and load_agents_snapshot already calls
   load_artifact_links_snapshot(project) (agents_data.py:24-56). Decide explicitly
   whether the bounded head-slice load populates it or leaves it empty until the
   extension pass, and record which in the code. The aggregate is project-scoped, not
   row-scoped, so slicing rows does not shrink it, and epic sase-tw grows it from ~112
   to ~1,600+ rows.

3. State the semantics a filter term sees mid-extension, because phase sase-tw.13 of
   epic sase-tw will build three new filter fields (relation:, linked:, artifact:) on
   top of them. _filtered_agents_snapshot (agents_query.py:439-460) short-circuits only
   on a blank remainder, so any filter term with _query_index None returns pending —
   this phase's intended grow trigger, and correct. The seam to close is the other
   order: it computes matched_rows by intersecting result.matched_row_ids with
   snapshot.rows, so a full-corpus index over a still-bounded snapshot yields a silently
   short match_count. Either make it impossible to present a full index against a
   partial snapshot, or make the count explicitly a lower bound — _sync_agent_query_bar

title: Short unasserted Event.wait ceilings in tests/ let fake blocked workers self-release under host load
description:
Discovered while deflaking
`tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_prompt_format.py::test_newer_format_request_wins`
(see the tale plan `sase_plan_deflake_prompt_format_release_ceilings.md`). That node's
root cause was not its `wait_for` budget: it was a short, unasserted
`release_first.wait(timeout=2)` inside the test's own fake formatter. When that ceiling
expires, the worker the test still believes is blocked returns on its own, production
correctly applies its result as the current request, and every later assertion runs
against a source the widget no longer holds. The expected end state then becomes
unreachable, so the test fails no matter how generous its polling timeout is.

That is a shape, not a one-off. `grep -rn '\.wait(timeout=' tests/ --include=*.py`
finds 186 sites; filtering out `assert`-guarded waits and subprocess reaps leaves ~59
where a fake worker, lock holder, or thread is held open by a bare 1.0s-2.0s ceiling
that no assertion checks. Representative sites:

- `tests/ace/tui/test_y_keymap_non_blocking.py:105` (1.0s)
- `tests/ace/tui/test_agents_diff_badge_deferred.py:516` (1.0s)
- `tests/ace/tui/test_prompt_catalog.py:515` (1.0s)
- `tests/ace/tui/test_axe_force_refresh.py:265` (1.0s)
- `tests/ace/tui/test_agent_fold_persistence.py:274,302` (2s)
- `tests/ace/tui/test_monitor_reconcile_off_read_path.py:224` (2.0s)
- `tests/ace/tui/test_family_member_relaunch.py:235` (2s)
- `tests/ace/tui/test_agents_bead_warmup.py:593` (2.0s)
- `tests/test_config_reader_probe.py:102,130,162` (2.0s)
- `tests/test_axe_process_start.py:359,394` (2s)

The repo already owns the remedy and under-uses it: `tests/_load_tolerant.py` defines
`LOAD_TOLERANT_TIMEOUT = 60.0` and documents exactly this distinction — "These waits are
deadlock detectors, not speed assertions" — but only five test files import it.

Work: audit each of the ~59 sites, decide whether its ceiling is a deadlock detector or
a real assertion about elapsed time, convert the detectors to `LOAD_TOLERANT_TIMEOUT`
(asserting the wait actually returned, so a genuine wedge names itself instead of
silently changing the scenario), and leave alone the few that legitimately assert
timing. A site whose ceiling is load-bearing for the behavior under test should get a
comment saying so.

Not every site is wrong, so this is a judgment audit rather than a mechanical
substitution — hence the size.
