title: ACE TUI holds 2.3-2.5 GB RSS while idle on the Agents tab
description:
PROPOSED BY: epic sase-v2 ("Fix ACE TUI freezes and prompt-input lag"), plan:202608/tui_freeze_regression.md. Its "Out of scope" section names this explicitly and directs filing it as a separate task bead: "The ~2.5 GB RSS observed in the reproducing process. It is suspicious and worth its own investigation, but nothing gathered here ties it causally to the freezes, and this plan should not grow to chase it. File it as a separate task bead." Routed here by the sase-v2 land agent on 2026-08-28.

OBSERVED: during the live forensics that produced epic sase-v2, one `sase ace` session on the reporter's 64-core host was measured at 2.3-2.5 GB RSS and 24 threads while sitting idle on the Agents tab (`ps`, same process the py-spy sample and the tui_stalls.jsonl window came from, 2026-08-28 08:38-08:45). That is one to two orders of magnitude above what a terminal UI process should hold.

NOT CAUSED BY sase-v2: the epic's six phases only removed work from hot paths (prompt-panel visual/anchor memoization, countdown activity gate, config-token refresh cadence, prompt-completion project-lookup caching, artifact-link target index). None of them allocates a new long-lived cache large enough to explain gigabytes, and the epic's own evidence explicitly declined to attribute the RSS to the freezes. Note that the epic's caches (per-generation/width section anchors, process-level project workflow-type/changespec-name caches, the per-load known-target index) are all small and bounded, but a footprint audit should still confirm that rather than assume it.

SCOPE: measure first, do not guess. Reproduce with a long-lived `sase ace` on a populated fleet, then attribute the heap before changing anything -- e.g. `tracemalloc` snapshots at intervals, `objgraph`/`gc` type histograms, or a memray run against the live TUI -- and check the obvious suspects the forensics already put in view: retained Textual `Strip`/`FIFOCache` render caches across many widths, the agent/artifact snapshot models kept per refresh, the artifact-link and link-index snapshot caches (`src/sase/ace/tui/relations/`), and anything keyed by a value that grows with session length rather than being replaced. Distinguish steady-state high-water from unbounded growth over time: a leak and a large-but-flat working set need different fixes.

VERIFICATION: a documented attribution of where the RSS goes, and either a bounded/reduced steady-state footprint on the same fixture with the number recorded, or a written finding that the footprint is expected with the evidence that says so.

title: Add a shell: filter token (shell:gate, shell:proc) to sase agent search
description:
Give `sase agent search` (and the ACE Artifacts Agent pane, which shares the profile) a
`shell:` filter token — `shell:gate`, `shell:proc` — so a family shell can be selected by
its kind rather than by string-parsing a member suffix.

Proposed by phase bead sase-ud.8 (gate-fork-cli) while landing epic sase-ud, which risk
R6 required to check whether `sase agent search` needs a `shell:gate` token and either
handle it or file a task. sase-ud.8 verified the shape of the work rather than doing it:

- The `agent_artifacts` SQLite table (sase-core `crates/sase_core/src/agent_scan/index.rs`,
  CREATE TABLE around line 1982) has no `shell_kind` / `agent_family_role` / `gate_id`
  column. Those fields live only in the `record_json` blob, which the Python catalog
  deliberately never reads (`src/sase/agents/catalog/_sources.py`: "Only the columns the
  catalog's kind/attribute derivation actually needs. Never SELECT *").
- A real token therefore needs sase-core to add a `shell_kind` column via
  `ensure_agent_artifacts_column`, populate it on INSERT, bump the index schema version,
  and rebuild bindings; then, in this repo, `agents/catalog/_sources.py`
  (`_ARTIFACT_INDEX_COLUMNS` + `ArtifactIndexRecord`), `_models.py` (`AgentCatalogRow`),
  `_build.py` (`_build_row`), `_query.py` (`agent_catalog_query_entry`), and
  `ace/query_profile/profiles/_agents.py` (`QueryFieldSpec`) all need additions.

First decide whether the column is worth it: `role:gate` already works today with zero
code changes, because `role` is derived by string-parsing the member suffix
(`acme--gate` -> `role=gate`). That may be sufficient, in which case the right outcome is
documenting `role:` as the supported spelling instead of adding a cross-repo column.

title: rust-lsp-install copies sase-xprompt-lsp from the checkout-local target dir and exits 0 after cp/chmod/mv fail
description: just install reports a successful sase-xprompt-lsp install while actually copying nothing, because rust-lsp-install hard-codes the checkout-local cargo target directory and its single-line install step never propagates a copy failure. Found twice while landing epic sase-um (phase notes sase-um.3 and sase-um.4).

notes.author: sase-um.land
notes.text:
Reproduced live on 2026-08-28 in workspace sase_12 at master 52327ed78, during the sase-um land turn that filed this bead (same reporter, so recorded as a note rather than a +1). `just install` exited 0 and printed `[rust-lsp-install] installed .../.venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp` immediately after these three lines:

    cp: cannot stat '.../sase/repos/linked/sase-core/target/release/sase-xprompt-lsp': No such file or directory
    chmod: cannot access '.../.venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp.tmp.2738280': No such file or directory
    mv: cannot stat '.../.venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp.tmp.2738280': No such file or directory

`.venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp --version` then reported `sase-xprompt-lsp 0.32.6` while the same `just install` had just built and installed `sase_core_rs` 0.32.12 from the linked checkout.

task_type_fields.impact:
Every agent whose host sets a cargo `target-dir` (this one does, globally) silently
keeps a stale `sase-xprompt-lsp` in its workspace venv while `just install` reports
success. Nothing downstream can notice: the recipe's exit code is 0, so `just install`
is green and no gate re-checks the installed binary's version. Agents then debug
xprompt LSP behavior against a binary that does not match the tree they are editing.
task_type_fields.repro:
`just install` runs `rust-lsp-install` (Justfile:998). Its build step is

    cd "{{ sase_core_dir }}" && cargo build --release -p sase_xprompt_lsp

and its install step (Justfile:1015-1022) then copies from a hard-coded path:

    dest="{{ VENV }}/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp"; \
    src="{{ sase_core_dir }}/target/release/sase-xprompt-lsp"; \
    tmp="$dest.tmp.$$"; \
    trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT; \
    cp "$src" "$tmp"; \
    chmod +x "$tmp"; \
    mv -f "$tmp" "$dest"; \
    printf "[rust-lsp-install] installed %s\n" "$dest"

Two independent defects compound:

1. `src` assumes cargo wrote to the checkout-local `target/`. This host's
   `~/.cargo/config.toml` sets `target-dir = "/mnt/poseidon/cargo-target"`, so the
   binary is actually at `/mnt/poseidon/cargo-target/release/sase-xprompt-lsp` and the
   `cp` reads a path that does not exist. `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, a workspace
   `.cargo/config.toml`, and `build.target-dir` are all equally unhandled.

2. The whole install step is one `@`-prefixed, `;`-separated shell line with no
   `set -e`. A failing `cp` therefore does not stop `chmod` or `mv`, and the recipe's
   exit status is `printf`'s, which is 0. So the recipe prints cp/chmod/mv errors,
   prints `[rust-lsp-install] installed ...`, and exits 0.

REPRODUCE:

    grep -n 'target-dir' ~/.cargo/config.toml     # target-dir = /mnt/poseidon/cargo-target
    just install                                   # prints cp/chmod/mv errors, exits 0
    .venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp --version           # stale version, not the one just built

Observed twice while landing epic sase-um: phase sase-um.4 recorded `just install`
building `sase-xprompt-lsp` under `/mnt/poseidon/cargo-target/release`, trying to copy
from the checkout-local target, printing cp/chmod/mv failures, and still exiting 0.
Phase sase-um.3 independently recorded the same shape with a concrete version skew:
`.venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp --version` reported 0.32.6 after `sase_core_rs` 0.32.8 had
been built in the same `just install`.

title: Record an immutable decision record for CI's two-speed split (Master Gate vs Full CI)
description: Epic sase-um changed a real project policy -- CI no longer runs everything on every master push -- and plan 202608/release_gate_liveness.md section 9 calls for an immutable decision record alongside decisions:two-speed-verification. No such record exists. Proposed by the sase-um land agent from PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note 4 on phase bead sase-um.8.

task_type_fields.proposed_change:
Add an immutable decision record for CI's two-speed split, alongside the existing
`decisions:two-speed-verification` record it generalizes.

The claim: **CI is no longer the thing that runs everything on every push.** As of epic
sase-um, a push to master runs `Master Gate` (`.github/workflows/master-gate.yml`) --
per-SHA, never cancelled, the whole fast suite in six balanced shards plus the lint
gate, budgeted at ~8 minutes -- while the exhaustive matrix (3.12/3.13/3.14,
`visual-test`, `coverage-contexts`, `perf-floors`, the contention harness) moved to
`Full CI` (`.github/workflows/full.yml`), a scheduled caller of `ci.yml` that runs every
two hours off the push path. `ci_watch` then gates the release on both: the fast gate
proves *this commit* is sound (`gating_workflows`), and a green `Full CI` inside
`heavy_max_age_hours` proves the exhaustive suite was recently green.

Why over the credible alternatives, all of which the plan measured and rejected:
`queue: max` on the master group, per-SHA concurrency on the full `ci.yml` (~62% of the
account's daily job-minutes, and the tip still settles only ~14% of the time), deleting
the master concurrency block, `cancel-in-progress: true`, a GitHub merge queue, bigger
or self-hosted runners, verifying every Nth commit, and a diff-scoped selector in CI
(backtesting showed 10 of 10 measurable master commits escalate to the full suite, and
`tests/test_github_actions_ci_workflow.py` deliberately forbids CI ever running the
scoped lane).

Cost: a regression only the heavy lane can catch is learned up to two hours late, and
heavy-lane failures do not page through `ci_watch`'s notification path while the tip
they attach to is unsettled.

Reopen condition: if the fast gate's p50 wall stops fitting the commit cadence, or if
the heavy lane catches regressions the gate misses often enough that a two-hour
detection lag is not acceptable.

Source: plan `202608/release_gate_liveness.md` section 9 explicitly defers this record
and directs that it be proposed as a memory task bead rather than written by an agent,
because SASE memory must not be edited without the user's explicit approval.

title: Cut the Full CI heavy-lane cost outliers: just test-cost (73 min) and coverage-contexts (38 min)
description: Full CI takes ~1h43m against a two-hour schedule, leaving no headroom before ci_watch's heavy_max_age_hours freshness window starts holding the release shut. Two jobs dominate: just test-cost at 73 min for the same suite just test runs in 29, and coverage-contexts at 38 min. Deferred as R7 by plan 202608/release_gate_liveness.md section 9; proposed by the sase-um land agent from PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note 5 on phase bead sase-um.8.

task_type_fields.proposal:
Cut the two heavy-lane cost outliers so `Full CI` finishes well under its two-hour
schedule interval, instead of the ~1h43m it takes today.

Measured while planning epic sase-um (2026-08-26, per-job wall on one master `ci.yml`
run):

| Job                              | Wall   | Runs                    |
| -------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------- |
| `test (3.13)` (`just test-cost`)  | 73 min | same suite as `just test` |
| `coverage-contexts`               | 38 min | fast suite + per-test contexts |
| `test (3.12)` (`just test-cov`)   | 45 min |                          |
| `test (3.14)` (`just test`)       | 29 min |                          |

`just test-cost` runs 73 minutes against `just test`'s 29 for the *same* suite -- a 2.5x
multiplier paid entirely by the cost plugin. `coverage-contexts` is 38 minutes for a
baseline whose artifact is retained 14 days.

Concretely: attribute where `test-cost`'s 44-minute overhead goes and either bound it,
sample it, or move it to its own less frequent schedule; and decide whether
`coverage-contexts` needs to run on every two-hour heavy-lane tick or on a slower
cadence of its own, given the baseline it publishes is consumed by
`just refresh-contexts-baseline` and tolerates being hours old.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
This is heavy-lane budget, not gate budget: after epic sase-um these jobs run on a
schedule off the master push path, so they cost wall-clock on `Full CI` and org runner
minutes, but they do not sit between a commit and its gate result. The epic's own
acceptance criteria are about the fast gate's latency and the release opening, and none
of them move if `test-cost` gets cheaper. Plan `202608/release_gate_liveness.md` section
9 records R7 as explicitly deferred out of that epic and directs that it be filed as a
task bead.

It is worth doing separately because a heavy lane that takes 1h43m against a two-hour
schedule leaves almost no headroom: one slow run and the next scheduled tick either
overlaps (serialized by `full-ci` concurrency) or the newest green `Full CI` run ages
past `ci_watch`'s `heavy_max_age_hours` window and holds the release shut.

title: Give ci_watch a watched-workflow notification list so heavy-lane failures page while their SHA is unsettled
description: After epic sase-um moved sase's exhaustive suite onto the scheduled Full CI lane, a red Full CI run never reaches ci_watch's notification path: the ~1h43m run keeps its master tip unsettled in actstat, and actstat only emits a commit once every run attached to that SHA completes. Named as required follow-up by plan 202608/release_gate_liveness.md phase heavy. Proposed by the sase-um land agent.

task_type_fields.proposal:
Give `ci_watch` (in `bbugyi200/bugyi-chops`) a `watched_workflows` notification list: a
config var naming workflows whose failures must page through the chop's SASE
notification path regardless of whether the SHA they attach to has settled in actstat.

Today `classify_repo` / `decide_repo` drive notifications from actstat's settled-commit
record, and `select_settled_commits` (sase-core `src/github.rs`) only emits a commit
once *every* workflow run attached to that SHA has completed. Epic sase-um's `Full CI`
attaches a ~1h43m run to whatever master tip is current when its two-hour schedule
fires, so that tip stays unsettled for the whole run and a heavy-lane failure never
reaches the notification path.

Shape it like the `gating_workflows` allowlist sase-um.2 already added: evaluate it from
`GitHubReader`'s own bounded queries rather than from the actstat sweep, keep it empty
by default so every other repo the chop watches is unaffected, and reuse the existing
per-incident dedupe so one red `Full CI` run does not page every five-minute tick.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
Plan `202608/release_gate_liveness.md`, phase `heavy`, records this as an accepted cost
of moving the exhaustive lane off the push path and directs explicitly: "Enable GitHub's
native workflow-failure notifications for the repository, and file a task bead (via
`/sase_new_task`) to extend `ci_watch` with a watched-workflow notification list." It
was deliberately kept out of that epic because the epic's release gate does not read the
notification path at all -- it reads `gating_workflows` and the heavy-lane freshness
condition -- so nothing in sase-um's acceptance criteria depends on this, and it lands in
a different repository on its own release cadence.

title: referenced-by write-back reports a TypeError instead of the git failure: _pull_rebase_if_remote builds an undecoded bytes issue message
description:
`_pull_rebase_if_remote` builds its failure detail from an undecoded `subprocess`
result, so a failing `git pull --rebase` produces a `bytes` issue message that later
crashes the string join in the drain path.

`sase.sdd.referenced_by_refresh._pull_rebase_if_remote` calls
`run_sdd_git(["remote", "get-url", "origin"], ...)` and
`run_sdd_git_write(["pull", "--rebase"], ...)` without `text=True`, and
`run_sdd_git` defaults to `text: bool = False` (`src/sase/sdd/_git.py:40`). When the
pull fails, `detail = result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip() or "git pull
failed"` is therefore `bytes`, and it is stored verbatim as
`ReferencedByRefreshIssue.message`.

`sase.agents_sync.referenced_by_publication.drain_referenced_by_requests` then runs
`"; ".join(issue.message for issue in report.errors)` at line 64 and raises
`TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, bytes found`.

Two consequences beyond the crash:

1. The real `git pull --rebase` failure is never reported. The caller
   (`sase.agents_sync.prompt_archive.publish._drain_referenced_by_after_prompt_publish`,
   line 318) catches every exception and reports only
   `referenced-by write-back failed: <TypeError text>`, so the operator sees a Python
   type error instead of the git error that actually stopped the write-back.
2. The outbox is never advanced. The `TypeError` is raised on line 64, *before*
   `update_referenced_by_requests(...)` on line 65, so the escaping exception skips
   both the acknowledge and the failure-recording paths. Those requests keep their
   old attempt count, never reach `quarantine_threshold`, and retry forever with the
   same undecoded failure.

Suggested fix: pass `text=True` to both `run_sdd_git` calls in
`_pull_rebase_if_remote` (or decode `detail` before constructing the issue). A
regression test should assert that a failing pull yields a `str` message and that
`drain_referenced_by_requests` records the failure on the outbox rather than raising.
Consider also hardening line 64 to coerce non-`str` messages, so a future undecoded
message degrades to a bad diagnostic instead of an escaping exception that strands
the outbox.

links.description: Both are defects in sase.sdd callers of run_sdd_git (src/sase/sdd/_git.py:32); sase-u9 hits its unbounded per-ref subprocess loop, sase-va hits its text=False default leaving stderr as bytes

task_type_fields.impact:
## Impact

Hits every agent whose commit finalizer publishes a prompt archive while a sidecar
pull fails. The primary commit still lands, so no work is lost, but:

- the operator-facing warning names a Python `TypeError` instead of the git failure
  that caused it, which makes the condition effectively undiagnosable from the
  message alone;
- the referenced-by outbox requests are neither acknowledged nor failure-recorded, so
  they never increment attempts and never quarantine — they retry indefinitely and
  keep producing the same useless diagnostic on every subsequent publish.
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/sdd/referenced_by_refresh.py:_pull_rebase_if_remote (detail from run_sdd_git without text=True); crash site src/sase/agents_sync/referenced_by_publication.py:64
task_type_fields.repro:
## Reproduction

Observed live on 2026-08-28 on `sase` master at `bcd6813d2`, while resuming a paused
commit in the `research` sidecar:

```bash
sase stitch create --resume
# ⚠️ The primary commit succeeded, but prompt archive publication was deferred and
# will retry with agent publication: referenced-by write-back failed: sequence
# item 0: expected str instance, bytes found
```

The trigger is any failing `git pull --rebase` inside a sidecar that has an `origin`
remote, while a referenced-by outbox request is pending for that role.

Direct unit-level reproduction of the root cause:

```python
from sase.sdd.referenced_by_refresh import _pull_rebase_if_remote
# In a sidecar checkout with an origin remote and a pull that fails
# (e.g. diverged history with rebase disabled), the returned issue's
# .message is bytes, not str:
issue = _pull_rebase_if_remote(repo_root)
assert isinstance(issue.message, str)  # fails: it is bytes
```

Then `"; ".join(issue.message for issue in report.errors)` in
`referenced_by_publication.py:64` raises the `TypeError` above.

title: Index active tier keeps dead agents forever and starves windowed DONE rows
description:
The persistent agent artifact index treats a row as active whenever it has no done marker (`has_done_marker = 0` or `workflow_status` not in the terminal set). Agents that die without writing `done.json` stay in that tier forever.

Measured on this machine's `~/.sase/agent_artifact_index.sqlite` (10,426 rows) while diagnosing Agents-tab completed-row starvation (`plan:202608/agents_window_completed_starvation.md`):

- 3,180 rows match the active predicate
- 590 of those are not dismissed
- ACE's `_filter_dead_pids` later drops any non-terminal row whose PID is gone, so 588 windowed records normalize down to ~14 live agents

The windowed index read used to budget completed candidates as `requested_limit - active_candidates.len()`. With 590 active candidates against a 126 viewport, the completed budget saturated to 0 and the Agents tab showed no DONE history after a TUI restart.

This tale repairs the budget math without terminalizing those rows. Terminalizing rows that still carry `workflow_state.json` or a waiting marker needs its own liveness design; getting it wrong hides a live agent.

## Bug

- **Location:** `crates/sase_core/src/agent_scan/index.rs` (`active_where` / `has_done_marker`)

Query the live index for rows with `has_done_marker = 0` (or `workflow_status` not terminal) whose runner PID is gone. On this host that is thousands of rows, hundreds of them still visible. A cached windowed `load_tiered_agents(..., requested_limit=126, index_freshness="cached")` then reports `active_candidate_count` in the hundreds against a two-digit viewport.

The Agents tab's first paint after `sase ace` restart lists only live rows plus DONE children hanging off them. Header counts, tribe summaries, and clan grouping are computed over that partial set until an unwindowed read arrives.

Do not "fix" this by widening `AgentsViewport` or making ACE's normal refresh unwindowed. The liveness rule must not hide a still-running agent.

task_type_fields.impact: After sase ace restart, the Agents tab's first paint lists only live rows; header counts, tribe summaries, and clan grouping omit recent DONE agents until an unwindowed read arrives.
task_type_fields.repro: On a live ~/.sase/agent_artifact_index.sqlite, count rows with has_done_marker=0 (or non-terminal workflow_status) whose runner PID is gone. Cached load_tiered_agents(..., requested_limit=126, index_freshness='cached') then reports hundreds of active candidates against a two-digit viewport.

title: Revalidating Tier-1 index reads re-stat every hidden row and take minutes
description:
A revalidating Tier-1 artifact-index read runs `repair_stale_rows_for_query`, which re-stats every `hidden = 1` row. On this host that is 4,507 hidden rows.

While diagnosing Agents-tab completed-row starvation (`plan:202608/agents_window_completed_starvation.md`), the recovery load `source=tier1_index_revalidate` in `~/.sase/logs/tui_agent_loads.jsonl` on 2026-08-28 took **137 s** of disk time (`agents=316`). A cached unwindowed read of the same visible set is ~500 ms; the extra minutes are the hidden-row restat, not the absence of a window.

ACE arms this revalidate after each cached Tier-1 load and fires it 2 s after input goes quiet (at most every 300 s). After a TUI restart that is the path that eventually restores DONE history — and why the missing rows "reappeared while I was typing".

The starvation tale now takes one cached unwindowed prefix-completion read instead of waiting on this revalidate. The 137 s hidden-row restat remains.

## Bug

- **Location:** `crates/sase_core/src/agent_scan/index.rs` (`repair_stale_rows_for_query`)

Restart `sase ace` on a home dir whose index has thousands of `hidden = 1` rows. After first paint, wait for `source=tier1_index_revalidate` in `~/.sase/logs/tui_agent_loads.jsonl`. On this host that load restatted 4,507 hidden rows and ran for 137 s.

The Agents tab stays on a bounded prefix (or waits minutes) for a revalidate that is supposed to be a quiet background freshness pass. Typing during the restat is how the missing DONE rows used to reappear.

Do not fix this by skipping revalidate entirely or by making every ACE refresh unwindowed. Cached reads must stay read-only; the defect is restatting hidden rows on the revalidate path.

task_type_fields.impact: The post-startup revalidate that is supposed to be a quiet freshness pass blocks disk for minutes; DONE history used to reappear only when that 137s load finished.
task_type_fields.repro: Restart sase ace on a home dir with thousands of hidden=1 index rows. After first paint, wait for source=tier1_index_revalidate in ~/.sase/logs/tui_agent_loads.jsonl. On this host that load restatted 4507 hidden rows and ran 137s.

description: Add AgentArtifactCache in src/sase/agent/agent_artifacts_cache.py keyed by (agent identity, artifacts_dir, file path, mtime_ns, size, attempt, view mode, terminal width). Caches: prompt-file selection, prompt content, raw xprompt, response content, chat response, timestamped reply chunks, live-reply tail, prebuilt Rich renderables where safe. Live-reply uses TailCache(path, size, offset, text) reading only appended bytes when size grows; resets on shrink. Lazy/capped Rich Syntax: SYNTAX_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_BYTES=64_000, SYNTAX_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_LINES=1_500; above cap render plain Text with notice; optionally schedule highlight after idle if selection stable. Diffs: highlight only visible/trimmed range first. Apply in widgets/prompt_panel/_agent_display.py, widgets/file_panel/_display.py, widgets/axe_dashboard.py. Diff worker dedupe + cache in widgets/file_panel/_diff.py: DiffCacheKey = (agent_identity, workspace_path, vcs_provider_name, worktree_fingerprint) (workspace + .git/index mtime/size + 2s TTL fallback for active agents). _inflight_diff_tasks: dict[DiffCacheKey, Worker]. Acceptance: re-select same agent doesn't re-glob prompts; 5MB response paints immediately as plain text; re-select active agent with unchanged worktree doesn't call diff_with_untracked() again.

title: Phase 7 — Event-Driven Auto-Refresh + Small Wins
description: Event-driven auto-refresh in actions/event_handlers.py + util/fs_watcher.py: track _dirty_changespecs, _dirty_agents, _dirty_axe, _last_full_sanity_refresh; watcher events flip dirty flags; auto-refresh only does refreshes whose flag is set + slow FULL_SANITY_REFRESH_SECONDS=60 floor. Falls back to existing polling on non-Linux. AXE list rendering disk-free: widgets/bgcmd_list.py + actions/axe_loaders.py — parent option formatting uses precomputed counts (len(lumberjack_names)), no load_axe_config() during row render. ANSI parse cache for AXE output keyed by (source_id, mtime_ns, size, tail_hash) in widgets/axe_dashboard.py — append-only logs parse only new tail; 500-line tails reuse cached parse on hash match. Saved-query cache: SearchQueryPanel.render no longer calls load_saved_queries(); actions/startup.py loads once into self._saved_queries; invalidated only on save/delete. Idempotent footer: widgets/keybinding_footer.py stores _last_bindings_signature, _last_status_signature; skips on match; caches child widget refs in on_mount. Lazy startup data: defer xprompt snippet loading and custom keymap resolution until first use. Acceptance: watcher-active + no FS changes → no full load_agents_from_disk; BgCmdList.update_list() no disk reads; unchanged AXE refresh never calls Text.from_ansi; cold startup first paint independent of snippet loading.

notes.author: bryanbugyi34@gmail.com
notes.text:
Phase 6 final summary — sibling-integration consistency pass.

User-visible changes (across plugin repos):
- retired chat plugin README.md and docs/inbound.md: dot-commands tables updated
  to include the .help, .retry/.r, and the no-arg .kill picker landed
  in phases sase-x.1 / sase-x.2.
- sase-telegram README.md and docs/inbound.md: corrected to describe
  agent management as slash commands (/list, /listx, /kill, /resume,
  /xprompts) — the docs had a stale "dot-commands" reference even
  though the inbound script always dispatched on / -prefixed commands
  and registers them with set_my_commands.

Notable technical changes: none — code/tests in both plugin repos were
already consistent and correct after phases 1-5. The drift was purely
in user-facing docs.

Verification:
- retired chat plugin: just check → 265 passed.
- sase-telegram: just check → 219 passed (after re-running `just install`
  to refresh stale .venv state — sase entry-points for sase_llm
  providers were missing from the previously-installed metadata).
- No changes to sase_100 were required.

Commands compared (by design after phases 1-5):
| Command set     | gchat (dot-commands) | telegram (slash commands)              |
| --------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| List running    | .list                | /list                                  |
| List done       | .listx               | /listx                                 |
| Kill picker     | .kill                | /kill (inline keyboard)                |
| Kill named      | .kill <name> ...     | /kill <name>                           |
| Resume targets  | .resume              | /resume (inline copy buttons)          |
| Retry           | .retry <name> / .r   | 🔄 Retry callback button on launch /kill |
| xprompts catalog| .xprompts            | /xprompts                              |
| Help            | .help                | (Telegram's set_my_commands UI)        |

Intentional divergence preserved per the plan: "Google Chat should lean
on threads and dot commands; Telegram should keep button-heavy
workflows." The Telegram retry path is button-driven; the gchat retry
path is typed.

Deferred follow-ups documented in retired chat plugin/ROADMAP.md:
- Reactions on plan approvals (gchat-only UX)
- Streaming / draft API limitations (Google Chat platform constraints)
- .retry polish — no-arg .retry list, recovered-prompt preview
- Dot-command argument hints (e.g. --filter <substring>)

No equivalent ROADMAP exists in sase-telegram and none was added in
this phase — the gaps relative to gchat are deliberate platform-specific
divergences, not parity debt.

notes.author: bryanbugyi34@gmail.com
notes.text:
Phase 3 skipped — no source changes.

Decision: Phase 2 (sase-y.2, commit 959eb3dd) validated that 'sase search -f markdown' and 'sase search -f plain' are sufficient for the sase_changespecs skill across the representative agent workflows (exact lookup, project/status, ancestor/dependency, error/running-state, archive lookup). The only regression-coverage gap — that '&name' is exact and not substring — was filled by tests/test_query_property_filters_name_sibling.py in that commit.

Per this bead's own description ('If existing search is sufficient, document the skip decision and close this phase without source changes'), the optional 'sase changespec show <name> -j / --raw' and 'sase changespec list -q <query> -j' surface is not needed and is intentionally not added. Phase 4 should refine the skill against the existing 'sase search -f markdown/plain' command surface.
